issues.title: Every build check fails in two seconds since 02:10 on 25 September: GitHub stopped running Actions over billing, so nothing can be merged
issues.body:
**Order:** 18 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** find out, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

.github/workflows/build.yml · GitHub Actions for EvilPatrick06/Thornswood · the repository's Billing and plans

## What is known

FOUND 25 SEPTEMBER. From run 859 (main at 19082f1, 02:10 UTC) on, every Launcher builds job has failed within two or three seconds: run 859 on main, run 860 for #343 (re-run once, same again), run 861 for #350. Read through the API: each job has runner_id 0 and no runner name, no steps, and no log (the log download answers 404), and the run's billable Windows time is 0 ms. So no runner ever picked a job up, and nothing on any branch is being tested. Launcher builds is the one required check and enforce_admins is on, so no pull request can be merged by anybody until jobs run again. The usual cause of exactly this shape on a private repository is the month's Actions minutes or spending limit (a Windows runner minute counts double), and the run page says which in a banner at the top. Not confirmed: the banner cannot be read through the API. Waiting on it: #343, #348 (green on dc9ecd6 before the outage), #350. Also waiting on it since: #351 and #352, opened the same night. THE CAUSE, READ BY PATRICK off the run page the same night: "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased. Please check the 'Billing & plans' section in your settings". So it is the account, not GitHub being down and not the code: either a payment failed, or the month's included Actions minutes are used up and the spending limit is 0. A Windows runner minute counts double against the included minutes, and this workflow is Windows only. Nothing runs again until the payment or the budget is fixed, or the billing month rolls over. CHECKED BY HAND MEANWHILE, 25 September: every step and harness the build check runs was run on Linux for main and for #348, #350, #351 and #352 and compared. Main: 166 pass and 32 fail, all 32 needing Windows (the csc, C:\ paths, Windows PowerShell). #348 adds one pass (its own test); #350, #351 and #352 match main apart from their own Windows-only tests. The launcher's C# compiled against the same references gives the same errors on every branch as on main. That is not the build check: Check-Controls and the real Build-Launcher only run on Windows, and Ship runs the build itself. MERGED 25 SEPTEMBER without the build check, by Patrick's decision ("I told you to do the checks and than merge the PRs"): he turned enforce_admins off, the seven open pull requests were merged one at a time on the local checks, each brought up to date with main and its script index rewritten first, and enforce_admins goes back on after. In order: #352 (934686a), #348 (5c9bb42), #350 (25783df), #351 (c38352d), #353 (8449520), #354 (07a6605), #343 (565d629). What did not run on any of them: the launcher window check, the real Build-Launcher, and the 32 harnesses that need Windows; Ship builds the launcher with the Windows csc before it publishes anything. Still open: the Actions budget or the month's reset, so the check runs again, and enforce_admins back on. MAIN CHECKED HERE AFTER THE MERGES, 25 September, with the build check's own steps and harnesses on Linux: every step passes; 169 harnesses pass. Of the 35 that fail, 34 need Windows (the csc or C:\ paths), the three new downgrade tests among them. The other was real: test-repo-docs.js, because #354 gave tools\signing a README the front README did not name. Fixed in #355. The Windows half was covered by the dev Ship of 1.1.94.3, which compiled the launcher from main with the Windows csc.

## Steps

- [x] Open a failed run and read the banner at the top of the page. (patrick)
- [ ] If it names billing or the spending limit: raise the Actions budget or fix the payment in Billing and plans, or wait for the month to roll over. It costs money, so it is Patrick's call. (patrick)
- [x] It did not name an incident, so there is nothing to wait out on GitHub's side. (patrick)
- [ ] Once it runs again: a smaller bill from here on. A newer push to a pull request cancels the run it replaces, and a change that only touches .md files skips the Windows steps inside the job, so the required check still reports. (claude)
- [ ] Once jobs run again, the build check on main, since tonight's merges never had one. (claude)
- [ ] Turn enforce_admins back on. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh api -X POST repos/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/branches/main/protection/enforce_admins
  ```

## Done when

A Launcher builds job runs its steps again, and #343, #348 and #350 have a real result.

## Traps

Do not take the required check off main to merge around it: it is the only thing between a branch and a Ship that stops at the build step. A red check here says nothing about the code, so read the job, not the colour.

## Links

- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/actions/runs/36086031917 run 861, one of the failed runs, with the banner
- https://www.githubstatus.com/ GitHub's status page

issues.title: Downgrade types into Steam's console when Steam's window belongs to steamwebhelper, and the clipboard fallback says there are three parts
issues.body:
**Order:** 19 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools/app/Downgrade.cs (TypeIntoConsole about :460-530, BringToFront :542, ForegroundIsSteam :621, MainWindow :636, the per-part loop :214-364, TryClipboard :662)

## What is known

PATRICK, 24 September, with a tester's screenshot on the main build (launcher 1.1.91, Thornswood in S:/Thornswood, Skyrim 1.7.104): "downgrader still isnt working, its not going into the console by itself its going to your clipboard and it only give you the fiurst one to yuor clipboards and not all of them". The screenshot shows Steam's window open behind the launcher on its CONSOLE tab, the launcher's Downgrade card at "Part 1 of 3: 7,145 MB down so far", and the launcher's line "Steam's window would not come to the front, so nothing was typed. The command is on your clipboard: click in the Steam console's command line, press Ctrl+V and Enter." So the paste worked and part 1 was downloading. MEASURED FROM THE CODE: (1) The launcher looks for Steam's window only among processes named steam (MainWindow) and counts Steam as in front only when the foreground window's process is named steam (ForegroundIsSteam). The current Steam client draws its main window from steamwebhelper.exe, not steam.exe, on at least some machines; there, MainWindow finds nothing usable and ForegroundIsSteam is never true, so every part falls back to the clipboard. It worked for Patrick and Djinn on 17 September, so which process owns the window varies; nobody has measured the tester's machine. (2) The three parts go one at a time: each part's command is typed or put on the clipboard only when the part before it is done, replacing the one before on the clipboard. Nothing on screen says so, so the person reasonably believes only the first command was ever given. WHAT TO BUILD: (a) MainWindow and ForegroundIsSteam treat steamwebhelper as Steam too (both names; steamwebhelper belongs only to Steam), with MainWindow still choosing the biggest visible window, and the log saying once which process and window it found. (b) The clipboard fallback says which part of three it is and that the next part's command will be put on the clipboard when this one is down, in the log line and in the status line that stays on the card, for example: 'Part 1 of 3 is on your clipboard: click in Steam's console command line, press Ctrl+V and Enter. Parts 2 and 3 follow here when it is down.' When a later part falls back, its status line says so plainly and the launcher window is brought forward or flashed (FlashWindowEx on the launcher's own window is fine) so the person notices there is something to paste. (c) Nothing else about the download, the watching, the markers or the apply changes. IN HAND 24 September: a branch is being written and reviewed for this (patrick/downgrade-finds-steamwebhelper). Close this when it has merged and gone out. DONE ON MAIN AND READY TO GO LIVE, 24 September. (1) The window: #315 merged. Steam's window is found under steamwebhelper as well as steam, and keys go only to the window that was brought forward (measured on Patrick's machine: the window titled Steam, class SDL_app, 2308 x 927, belongs to steamwebhelper.exe). (2) A SECOND CAUSE, found by checking ours against the Skyrim Downgrader Tool Patrick downloaded and against two open downgraders for the same depots (Mosalah992/Skyrim-downgrader, JackifyGameDowngrader): Downgrade listened for Steam in the wrong log. It read content_log.txt alone and took depot_489831 as the start. Both other tools read console_log.txt, and one keeps the real lines from 24 August: 'Downloading depot 489832 (26 files, 7260 MB) ...', 'Depot download complete : ...depot_489832 (manifest 8042843504692938467)', 'Depot download failed : ... (Content unavailable)'. So a part that finished was never seen to finish and the next was never asked for, which is the tester's 'it only give you the fiurst one' more exactly than the clipboard was. #316 merged: both logs are read, the start line or a folder that appeared after the command counts as the start, Steam's failure line stops the part at once with Steam's words, the downloaded SkyrimSE.exe is checked before anything is replaced (as the Downgrader Tool does; it was only checked after the copy), and the manual path says Windows+R, steam://open/console instead of Ctrl+Shift+D. Depots and manifests match all three tools. test-downgrade-steam-log.ps1 51 pass and 7 fail on the old code; test-downgrade-steam-window.ps1 82. NOT MEASURED ON A REAL DOWNLOAD: neither Steam log on Patrick's machine has a depot line since 10 September, so the first log from a person who runs it is the proof. (3) HOTFIX 1.1.94 is built on hotfix/1.1.94-downgrade: live 1.1.93 plus these two fixes and the version bump, pushed and level with GitHub, compiles as 1.1.94, the full sweep of 42 harnesses passes. Nothing else from main goes with it. Patrick gave the word on 24 September ('where is the downgrader main build hot fix so we can get that rolling'). The session's permission check refused the live Ship as a production deploy, so it is his to run, from the hotfix folder. The Downgrader Tool itself is the same manual process with Copy-Item -Force, which writes through Vortex's hard links, so it is not something to hand testers. SHIPPED LIVE 24 September 18:10 as launcher 1.1.94, release 20260924-1810 on Thornswood-Releases, from hotfix/1.1.94-downgrade once Patrick had switched the session out of auto mode. The site news has it, the game server gave everybody five minutes, and it is posted to #news. The installer zip is now three releases behind (built 23 Sep 07:47); anybody installing fresh takes those updates on first launch, and Package-Thornswood.ps1 rebuilds it in about twenty minutes. WHAT IS LEFT is the proof from a real run: a launcher log showing Part 1 of 3 is down, then Part 2 of 3 asked for. AND THEN, THE SAME EVENING, ON 1.1.94: "the dowgrader this time didnt even upon the steam console let alone put the commands in for you" (Patrick, a tester), and "Keizaal Onlines downgrader tool does this so it is possible", "they have a progress bar of it in the launcher". No log from the tester yet. Read from the code: every request to Steam was a bare Process.Start(steam://...) inside catch { }, so where Windows cannot open a steam:// link it failed in silence and Steam was never asked; every early stop wrote to the launcher log alone, so the card kept its old words and the button looked dead; and with Steam in the tray and no window the console was asked for once. BUILT on patrick/downgrade-says-why-and-shows-progress (a3c3aca), under adversarial review: AskSteam tries the link and then steam.exe with the arguments Windows registers, every stop says why on the card, Steam with no window is asked again, and the card has a progress bar from the size Steam gives each part. test-downgrade-says-why.ps1 46 pass, 18 fail on main. The tester is being fixed by hand meanwhile. LEFT: the tester's launcher log, to say which of these it was. 25 SEPTEMBER, A NEW TESTER. Patrick: "his skyrim wasnt downgraded so he downgraded than hit enter after and it gave him the wrong files he just reraun and its working normally", and he had old installer zips in his Downloads folder. MEASURED FROM THE CODE: the only step anywhere that copies files after a person presses Enter is Setup-Thornswood.ps1:328, "Press Enter here once all three have finished", inside the half that runs only for a payload with no collection.txt. Package-Thornswood has written collection.txt since 16 September (5b1ee05), so today's installer never shows that prompt: the Skyrim Together era zips of 10 to 15 September do. That half checks only that each depot folder exists (307-313), which Steam makes the moment it starts, then copies whatever is there with robocopy's exit code ignored (333-337) and checks SkyrimSE.exe only afterwards, so an early Enter copies truncated archives and passes, and a rerun after Steam finishes copies the whole files over them: exactly "wrong files, then works". So this report is the same incident as the new entry below about the installer taking an old zip from Downloads, and #340 is its fix. PULL REQUEST #343 is patrick/downgrade-says-why-and-shows-progress (a3c3aca), pushed from Patrick's machine on 25 September; its first review did not survive the session and it was reviewed again here: nothing blocking in the code, no C# 6 syntax (compiled at C# 5 with a control that catches all five banned features), no UI touched off the Dispatcher, the button always comes back as Try again, the bar never passes 100, and the steam.exe fallback starts at most once per call. It touches Shell.cs, so it needs a line in #dev before it merges. Main merged into it on 25 September (5aab28b) with its harness in the script index, so it is ready the moment that line is posted. Not blocking: the bar reaches 100 when the third part finishes and then drops to 0 for the copy (Downgrade.cs:421 then :457); the steam.exe fallback only fires when opening the link throws, so a steam:// link that belongs to another program gets no fallback; and it does not touch any of the wrong-files paths. FOUND ON THE WAY, not fixed, each small and none in a protected file: F1, today's Setup-Thornswood.ps1 counts a wrong game build as a failed check, so the window shows [MISS] Game 1.6.1170 and never opens the launcher, and line 183 tells people to use Steam's Betas list rather than the launcher's Downgrade button; count it as next and open the launcher, about five lines. F2, Package-Thornswood.ps1:304-307 only warns when there is no Vortex record, which is how a payload without collection.txt gets built. F3, the launcher's Downgrade stops part way on a file it cannot replace, and when SkyrimSE.exe was already copied the card and its Try again button go (Shell.cs 1793); copying SkyrimSE.exe last keeps them. F4, the 20 minute fallback takes a part as done when Steam stops writing, and checks only the exe's size before copying; #343 already reads the size Steam announces for each part, so waiting for that is one condition. 25 SEPTEMBER, A TESTER ON LIVE 1.1.94 STOPPED AFTER PART 1. Patrick: "it correctly put the first command in it finnished and than it redid the open console command and stopped". His screenshot: Steam's console shows download_depot 489830 489831 typed, "Depot download complete" for 489831, then ExecCommandLine steam://open/console and nothing after it; the card read "8,169 MB down so far (Steam shows the rest in its console)". READ IN THE LIVE CODE (hotfix/1.1.94-downgrade, Downgrade.cs): that second steam://open/console is part 2's TypeIntoConsole, and nothing typed means Steam's window did not come to the front or the keys went somewhere else. Depot 489832 is 7,260 MB at 1.6.1170, so a folder of 8,169 MB was already there from an attempt at another build before Steam was asked anything. With it there, three things went wrong. The 45 second check for whether Steam took the command passed on the folder alone, so the second try at the console never ran. ProgressLine shows the clipboard instruction only while nothing is down, so the card showed the old folder's size where it should have said "Part 2 of 3 is on your clipboard now". And Steam fills a depot folder without emptying it, so the other build's files would have gone over the game with the 1.6.1170 ones. #343 changes none of this. FIXED AS #350 (claude/downgrade-leftover-depot, e1f2738): ClearLeftover removes a depot folder without this build's marker before the part starts, and stops with the reason on the card when it cannot. tools/test-downgrade-leftover.ps1 fails on main. NOT YET KNOWN: why Steam's window would not come forward for part 2. BringToFront attaches to Steam's input thread, which only helps when Steam is already in front; the foreground belongs to whatever window is in front, and a launcher nobody has touched for twenty minutes cannot hand it on. That is the likely cause; the tester's launcher.log would confirm it by saying "Steam's window would not come to the front" and naming the window it found. THE TESTER FINISHED ALL THREE PARTS BY HAND AND GOT IN (Patrick, the same night), so nothing is owed to him; the fix is for the next person. Patrick: "I still want the fix in for the future". ON DEV 25 SEPTEMBER AS 1.1.94.2: GitHub would not run the build check (entry 18), so #350, #351 and #352 were checked here instead, each against main with the same harnesses the build check runs, and each matched main apart from its own new test, which needs the Windows compiler; the Linux copies of those tests pass. They went out together from claude/dev-downgrade-and-potions (85f6f2f), which Patrick shipped to dev; the dev feed reads 1.1.94.2 with the full note. Main still waits for the build check to run again. ALL THREE ON MAIN, 25 September: #350, #351 and #343 merged (see entry 18 for how). On the merge of #343, #350's ClearLeftover was changed to stop through #343's Stop, so a folder that cannot be removed hides the bar too; test-downgrade-leftover.ps1 checks it, and it was forced on Linux with an immutable file. #343's card and bar are on main and not yet on dev: 1.1.94.2 has #350 and #351 only. #343 ON DEV AS 1.1.94.3, 25 September, shipped from main after the folder move: the card's bar, the stop line under the button, and steam.exe asked directly when steam:// links do not open. Dev now has all three downgrade pull requests.

## Steps

- [x] The window fix, #315, merged into main. (claude)
- [x] The Steam log fix and the check before anything is replaced, #316, merged into main. (claude)
- [x] Hotfix 1.1.94 built from live 1.1.93 plus both, pushed, full sweep clean. (claude)
- [x] The live Ship from the hotfix folder, with the game closed. Patrick said go; it is his to run because the session may not ship live. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\tw-hotfix94; .\tools\Ship.ps1 -NoPause "The Downgrade button works on its own again."
  ```
- [x] Post the release to #news from the main folder, since the webhook file lives only there. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo; .\tools\Publish-Discord.ps1
  ```
- [ ] Read the first launcher log from somebody who runs it: 'Part 1 of 3 is down' then 'Part 2 of 3, depot 489832'. That is the proof the finish line is heard. (patrick)
- [ ] Rebuild the installer so a fresh install starts on 1.1.94 rather than three releases back. Optional; about twenty minutes. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1
  ```
- [ ] Get the tester's Profile\launcher.log lines from pressing Downgrade, to say which stop it was. (patrick)
- [x] Land patrick/downgrade-says-why-and-shows-progress after its review, dev Ship it, and a hotfix to live once Patrick says. (claude)
- [x] #343 approved in #dev (Patrick, 25 September) and merged. It goes to dev with the next dev Ship from main. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "Downgrade says why it stopped and shows a progress bar"
  ```
- [ ] F1: today's installer opens the launcher when only the game build is wrong, and points at the Downgrade button rather than Steam's Betas list. (claude)
- [ ] F3 and F4 in Downgrade.cs: copy SkyrimSE.exe last, and take a part as done only at the size Steam announced. (claude)
- [ ] If the tester still has it, his Profile\launcher.log from this run, from the line 'Part 2 of 3, depot 489832' on: it says whether the window would not come forward, and which window was taken for Steam's. (patrick)
- [x] #350 and #351 on dev as 1.1.94.2 (from claude/dev-downgrade-and-potions); merged into main once the build check runs again. (claude)
- [x] BringToFront also joins the thread of the window in front, the one that holds the foreground: #351 (claude/downgrade-foreground, 32526d0), and the log names the program in front when nothing is typed. (claude)
- [ ] Dev first. A hotfix onto 1.1.94 only if Patrick says so. (patrick)

## Done when

1.1.94 is live, and a launcher log from a real run shows all three parts asked for and down, the exe checked before the copy, and Skyrim on 1.6.1170.

## Traps

C# 5 only. Downgrade drives another program's window with synthetic input: never type or click unless Steam's window is really in front, exactly as now, because keys sent to the wrong window go somewhere else on the person's desktop. Do not open or focus Steam, run steam:// links, or send any input on this machine while testing: harness the decisions (which window, which process, what the lines say) with stand-ins, and read the real window list only if Steam's window is already visible. This ships in a launcher release; the tester is on the main build, so whether it goes live is Patrick's call.

issues.title: The machine that ships trusts newer game files over the launcher's kept copies (developer.flag), so it never repairs the way a tester's launcher does
issues.body:
**Order:** 20 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** merge it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools\Go.ps1 (Update-KeptCopies) · tools\Publish-Update.ps1 (wrote the flag) · tools\app\Keep.cs (reads it, unchanged) · C:\Thornswood\Profile\developer.flag and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Profile\developer.flag · #356 (claude/no-developer-flag)

## What is known

DECIDED BY PATRICK, 25 September: "let's remove the flag it will make testing easier". Publish-Update wrote Profile\developer.flag on the machine that ships, and Keep then let a newer game file win over its kept copy. So Patrick's launchers never did the repair a tester's launcher does. Both his installs have one: C:\Thornswood since 17 September and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild since 16 September, per the listing he sent the same day. The flag existed because Go.ps1, which Ship runs to copy the plugins and overlays in, never refreshed the kept copies. Without the flag, every Play would have put the previous plugins back. #356: Go.ps1 now makes each file it installs under Data\Platform\UI, and each plugin script, the kept copy. It drops the kept copy of anything it takes out, and adopts nothing else. Publish-Update no longer writes the flag. Keep.cs is not touched: it still reads the flag, and nothing writes one. tools\test-go-keeps.ps1 has 20 checks and fails against the old Go.ps1. Local run of every harness: 171 pass, and the 34 that fail are the ones that fail on main on Linux. Publish-Update.ps1 is one of the #dev files: Patrick approved it in chat, and the #dev line is still owed. #356 MERGED 25 September (16e4684), with the admin bypass. Left: the pull and the one time command on Patrick's machine, and the #dev line. PULLED AND RUN, 25 September: the one time command brought 17 kept copies up to date in C:\Thornswood-DevBuild (four plugins, thirteen UI files) and none in C:\Thornswood, and Test-Path says False for both flags. enforce_admins is back on. Left: the next dev Ship printing The launcher's kept copies, and the #dev line.

## Steps

- [x] Merge #356 with the admin bypass, while GitHub Actions cannot run. (claude)
- [x] On Patrick's machine: git pull, then the one time command. It brings each kept copy up to date from a newer game file, then deletes the flag, in both installs. (patrick)
- [ ] At the next dev Ship, Go.ps1 prints a section called The launcher's kept copies with a count. (patrick)
- [ ] A line in #dev: Publish-Update no longer writes developer.flag, and Go.ps1 refreshes the kept copies. (patrick)

## Done when

Neither install has Profile\developer.flag, a dev Ship refreshes the kept copies, and Play on Patrick's machine does not put an older plugin back.

## Traps

Deleting the flag without the adopt half first means the next Play puts back any kept copy older than the game file, which is whatever Go.ps1 put in since the last Play. The one time command does the two in that order. After the next Ship it no longer matters, because Go.ps1 refreshes every file of ours.

issues.title: Main still says launcher 1.1.92 while live is 1.1.94, so a plain Bump-Version makes the next main release one nobody takes
issues.body:
**Order:** 23 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools/app/Updater.cs (Version) · tools/Bump-Version.ps1 · tools/Publish-Update.ps1:1247-1262 (the launcher version it records)

## What is known

FOUND 25 SEPTEMBER in Deploy-DevGamemode's build stamp: 'launcher 1.1.92, feed 1.1.92.6'. The two hotfixes, 1.1.93 and 1.1.94, moved Updater.cs only on their hotfix branches, and main's tools\app\Updater.cs still says Version = "1.1.92". Bump-Version.ps1 with no -To adds one, so the next main release would be 1.1.93. Publish-Update records whatever it is given and warns only when the number is unchanged, not when it is lower, and the updater takes a launcher only when Updater.IsNewer says the feed's is newer: everybody on 1.1.94 would keep 1.1.94 and never get main's launcher, with nothing said. TO DO NOW: the next main bump is .\tools\Bump-Version.ps1 -To 1.1.95. TO FIX: Bump-Version reads the live feed's launcherVersion out of Thornswood-Releases\version.json and refuses, or starts from, anything not above it; or Publish-Update refuses a launcher version lower than the feed's, which is a protected file and needs a line in #dev. ALSO FOUND 25 SEPTEMBER, reading the two dev posts of 24 September: dev went from 1.1.92.6 at 14:36 to 1.1.94.1 at 19:51. That is Ship's own rule and right: a dev number is the higher of the branch's Updater.cs and the live feed's launcherVersion, plus .n, and live went 1.1.92, then 1.1.93 (after 15:58), then 1.1.94 (18:10), with no dev Ship while 1.1.93 was live. It means a main release at 1.1.93 would also be ignored by every dev launcher, because a main release resets dev to match main. BUILT: #348, Bump-Version reads the live feed's launcherVersion from Thornswood-Releases\version.json (where Ship reads it), starts one above it when Updater.cs is behind and says why, and refuses a -To at or below it. tools/test-bump-version-live.ps1: 13 pass, 6 fail on main. #348 MERGED 25 September (5c9bb42): Bump-Version.ps1 now reads the live feed beside the repository and starts above it, so a plain bump on main proposes 1.1.95, and -To 1.1.93 is refused.

## Steps

- [ ] The next main release: bump with -To, not the default. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Bump-Version.ps1 -To 1.1.95
  ```
- [x] Merge #348 once green. (claude)

## Done when

A main release cannot be given a launcher number at or below the one live launchers already have.

## Traps

The dev channel reads its number off main's published feed, so fixing main's number moves dev's too; say so in #dev.

issues.title: The join card counts arrivals properly, and its background is the Thornswood banner
issues.body:
**Order:** 24 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools/discord/bot.py (on_member_join, about :452-480: number = member.guild.member_count) · tools/discord/card.py (BACKGROUND = assets/join-card.png, render, _ordinal) · tools/discord/assets/join-card.png · the Thornswood art already in tools/discord: server-banner-960x540.png, server-banner-animated-960x540.gif, invite-splash-1920x1080.jpg · tools/discord/redraw.py and backfill.py (read what they do with the number) · tools/Install-Bot.ps1 (what -CodeOnly sends)

## What is known

The screenshot: 'Daggerio (Deceased) came up the road', card 'The 28th to walk in', yesterday 19:41; then 'VENUS came up the road', card 'The 28th to walk in', yesterday 22:45. So one departure between two joins gives the second arrival the first one's number again, and it can repeat for ever. The background is a fixed image, assets/join-card.png, a plain starfield, not Thornswood's art. WHAT TO BUILD: (1) An arrival number that only ever goes up. Keep a small record on the bot's side beside bot.py (for example joins.json: the last number given and each member id's number). Seed it so it cannot hand out a number already on the cards: start from the higher of the stored last number and the current member count, and read backfill.py and redraw.py for anything they already know about past arrivals. IN HAND 24 September: a branch is being written and reviewed for this (patrick/join-card-count-and-banner). Close this when it has merged and gone out. MERGED as #318, 24 September. issues.title: The character select window keeps its cursor however long somebody sits on it, and the two minute cap closes every window it takes the keyboard from
issues.body:

## Where it lives

tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js: the menu phase loop that holds the select page up and focused (about :637-712), applyFocus and MANUAL_FOCUS_MS (about :948-1010), the claims and claimedAt arbiter, and the two minute cap loop (about :4687-4723) · tools/ts-ui/thornswood-select.js (window.thornswoodSelect, close at about :572) · tools/test-journal-key.js and tools/test-social-keys.js lift the arbiter and the key handler, keep them passing

## What is known

DJINN on dev, 24 September 4:18 PM: "Sitting on the character select window for too long causes you to lose your cursor, pressing F6 doesn't work, and you have to esc to quit". MEASURED FROM THE CODE: the character select page is not one of the arbiter's claims (chat, journal, party, skills, trade, wheel). The menu loop holds it up by calling sp.browser.setFocused(true) four times a second until a character is chosen. applyFocus meanwhile sees focus up with no claim behind it, treats it after 1.2 seconds as somebody's own F6, holds it for MANUAL_FOCUS_MS (two minutes), then says 'F6 focus has been up for 2 minutes with nothing using it, taking it back' and lowers it. So the two fight at the two minute mark, and Djinn's report matches: the cursor goes after sitting there a while. Nobody has read Djinn's thornswood-front.log for that session; if it can be found on this machine or on the site, read it, otherwise say what it would show. ALSO, found by the review of the J journal: the two minute cap on every claim closes the page only for skills (and wheel); a journal, party or trade claim is released with the window left drawn and no cursor, the same trap. WHAT TO BUILD: (1) The select page becomes a claim of the arbiter, 'select', raised while the menu phase has the choice up and lowered when the choice is made or the page is gone, so applyFocus wants focus for it instead of fighting it; keep the menu loop's own reassertion if it is still needed for the client hiding the browser, but it must no longer fight applyFocus. (2) 'select' is exempt from the two minute cap: sitting at the character select is not a stuck keyboard, it is the one thing to do there. (3) The cap closes the window that matches the claim it releases: skills, party, journal and trade each by its own window's close, the wheel as now, so no window is ever left drawn without its cursor. (4) F6 keeps working as it does now. IN HAND 24 September: a branch is being written and reviewed for this (patrick/select-keeps-its-cursor). Close this when it has merged and gone out. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #323. The entry blamed the wrong thing. The two-minute F6 cap never runs at the main menu. What really happens is in our fork of the client: after three minutes with no pick it logs in as the last character, and the world loads with the character choice still drawn. The update tick then drops focus and reloads the page, and the reload draws the choice again from the list still on disk. That leaves a full-screen choice over the world with no cursor, and Escape reaches the game. thornswood-front.js now makes the choice a named claim ('select'), held while the choice is up and let go at the pick, when ... STILL TO GO OUT: the dev Ship. Left: For Patrick, not done here: 1. Dev release. It ships in a dev release: .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "the character choice no longer sits over the world after the three minute fallback, and the two minute cap closes the window it takes". 2. To Do List. Correct the SEL entry's cause. The two-minute F6 cap never runs at the main menu. The real cause is the fork's three-minute fallback login (authService.ts:747) with the choice left drawn over the world. 3. New entry: F6 does nothing anywhere. The 22 Sep F6 hold in applyFocus (thornswood-front.js, the 'F6 IS A PERSON' block) never engages ...

## Steps

## Done when

A harness drives the real arbiter, applyFocus and the cap loop (lifted from thornswood-front.js) with a pretend clock and browser: with the select page up and nobody touching anything for ten minutes, focus stays up the whole time and nothing takes it back; choosing a character lowers the select claim; a journal, party or trade window up for over two minutes is closed by name when its claim is released. Never leave the person without a keyboard: every claim except select stays capped, and select must come down the moment the choice is made or the page goes, or the keyboard is stuck in the world. The game reports 34c5e of Skyrim.esm, so the server found the Skyrim.esm line, read "food", and the ale went to hunger. That matches Djinn's screenshot. With Gourmet's names now in front of the word lists, Flin, Mazte, Shein, Sujamma, Sadri's Sujamma, Argonian Bloodwine and Windhelm ... STILL TO GO OUT: the dev gamemode deploy. Whether a drug counts as a drink is a balance decision, and I did not make it. - The two ale paths behave differently. /drink ale (ate) adds thirst and costs rest. An ale actually drunk in the game (consumed) also costs hunger and gets worse with each one. For a session to pick up, same defect in another ...

issues.title: NPCs land on top of people, hit twice as hard as their weapon, and take the number printed on the sword
issues.body:
**Order:** 38 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

the fork, b375e5e3, skymp5-client\src\view\spawnProcess.ts and skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\formulas\DamageMultFormula · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1, a085e0d · NOT BUILT, NOT ON DEV

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by Patrick from playing it: "To many fucking NPCs spawning man all at once group together, on top of players, enimes hit way to hard and have to much health or dont die at all", and again "why is 5 chcikens psawing on top of me or 3 wolfs or a whole ass giant on top of me dude". THREE CAUSES, all measured in the fork. ONE, ON TOP OF PEOPLE. formView spawns every neighbour with player.placeAtMe(base, 1, true, true), so each one is born standing on the person, disabled, and SpawnProcess moves it away before enabling it. That move is correct. What undoes it is the last line: resurrect() resets an actor, and a reset returns an actor to its EDITOR LOCATION, which for a placeAtMe reference is where it was placed. So the sequence was move, enable, snap back onto whoever was standing there. It is not a race and the server was not sending a bad position: the position was applied and then discarded. The grouping is the same fault seen from outside, because everything lands on the same spot. Fixed by re-applying the position after the resurrect and after a non-actor has its motion type set. TWO, HIT TOO HARD. DamageMultFormula is always in the chain and had ONE multiplier, defaulting to 2, applied when an NPC hits a person. No server-settings.json this repo has ever written carried the key, so the server logged "Unable to get multiplier from config" at startup and doubled every blow landed on a person. Nobody chose that. THREE, TOO MUCH HEALTH. The other direction was never multiplied at all, and TES5DamageFormula under it reads the weapon's base damage, the target's armour and the power, block and sneak flags, and NOTHING about the person swinging: no skill, no perks, no attackDamageMult. So a giant keeps its full vanilla health and takes the number printed on the sword, over and over. The health is not wrong; the damage against it is. RULED OUT while measuring: the server does kill at zero health, MpActor::SetPercentages calls Kill, so the machinery is complete and it was only ever the numbers. FIXED as b375e5e3 in the fork, with playerMultiplier as a second key defaulting to 1 so an existing server is unchanged, and each key read on its own because the parser threw the whole default object away the moment multiplier was absent. Deploy-Gamemode writes both, a085e0d, as -HitsOnPeople 1 and -HitsOnNpcs 2. THE CLIENT HALF NEEDS A CLIENT BUILD and the server half needs a server build. DEV FIRST, both of them. THE FORK IS BUILT AND RECORDED, 23 September. Build-Server.ps1 recompiled and produced a byte for byte identical binary, which is correct rather than suspicious: the only change between b375e5e3 and c8832519 is one file, remoteServer.ts, and that is skymp5-client TypeScript, not the C++ server. The record now names the branch head. The client runtime was built at 05:58 today from that same commit and is on the dev feed. AND BOTH SERVERS ARE ALREADY RUNNING IT: C:\Thornswood-Server and C:\Thornswood-Server-Dev both hash to de74c582, the recorded binary, so there is nothing to send. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: All the code, builds and settings are in place. Fork: `git merge-base --is-ancestor b375e5e3 c8832519` is true, so the recorded commit contains the spawn and damage fix. skymp5-client/src/view/spawnProcess.ts keeps spawnPos and puts the position back after resurrect(). DamageMultFormula.cpp:40-41 reads playerMultiplier and :78 applies it. tools/client-build.json has forkCommit c8832519, recorded 2026-09-23T05:59Z. The installed Data/Platform/Plugins/skymp5-client.js has sha256 54e51f3f... in both C:\Thornswood\Game and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game, which matches the record, and the bundle contains 'spawnPos' 13 times. tools/server-build.json records c8832519, sha256 de74c582. tools/Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:98-99 and :627-629 write multiplier 1.0 and playerMultiplier 2.0. Entry 22 read both servers' settings on 23 Sep: both have those damage numbers, and both run de74c582. Steps 1 to 3 of this entry are done. The dev server spawns NPCs indoors only (spawnInExterior false), so wolves and giants spawn only on live, where spawnInExterior is true. NEXT STEP: No code or build work is left. Left for a person in the game: walk somewhere outdoors with animals, where live already spawns exterior NPCs, and see whether anything lands on top of anybody. Then hit a wolf and count the swings. If the numbers need turning, rerun Deploy-Gamemode -HitsOnPeople/-HitsOnNpcs and Publish-Server -Channel dev. That is a settings change and a server restart, not a rebuild. The entry's steps 1 to 3 can be ticked. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A playtest by a person in the game: does anything land on people outdoors, and how many swings does a wolf take. After that, Patrick tunes the two numbers if needed.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-client\src\view\spawnProcess.ts`: the note at the top says why the position is re-applied rather than the calls reordered
- `C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\formulas\DamageMultFormula.h`: the two multipliers and what each direction means
- `tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1, -HitsOnPeople and -HitsOnNpcs`: the numbers, and that the script never talks to the VPS

## Steps

- [ ] Record both builds, or the deploy and the release gates refuse them. (patrick)
- [ ] Write the settings locally with NPCs back on, then send the server to DEV. (patrick)

- [ ] Turn the two numbers until it feels right. They are settings, not code, so this costs a Publish-Server and no rebuild. (patrick)

## Commands

- Start in the repo. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo
  ```
- Stays on this machine. Writes the local dist settings: NPCs back on everywhere, and the two damage numbers. It has no ssh in it and talks to nothing. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 -Vortex -Npcs all
  ```
- LEAVES THIS MACHINE, to the DEV server on 7787. Patrick only. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Publish-Server.ps1 -Channel dev "NPCs stay where they are put, and a blow is worth what the settings say"
  ```

  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "NPCs stay where they are put"

## Done when

On dev, nothing lands on anybody, and a wolf dies in a sensible number of swings without two-shotting the person first.

## Traps

The client half and the server half are separate builds and each has its own record and its own gate. A client that is not the recorded build stops Ship; a server binary that is not the recorded one stops the deploy. Run both recorders after building. issues.title: Dev is laggy, and the first suspect is the thing that was turned back on tonight
issues.body:
**Order:** 42 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** measure it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

the dev server · npcSettings in server-settings.json · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 -Npcs

## What is known

REPORTED 21 SEPTEMBER by Patrick: "it's really laggy and I don't know why we need to do some performance enhcanments". NOT MEASURED YET, and this entry exists so it gets measured rather than guessed at. THE FIRST SUSPECT IS -Npcs all, which was set tonight at Patrick's own request after the NPC spawn work. Deploy-Gamemode's own comment says what that means: "npcEnabled true with an empty npcSettings means the server simulates EVERY npc in the world, interior and exterior ... that is one shared world, which is the thing SkyMP is for, and it is also every bandit and every chicken in Skyrim being kept alive by one process." It was on interior earlier in the evening and off before that, so the comparison is one flag and a redeploy. THE SECOND IS ALREADY ON THIS LIST further down: the unculled position broadcast, measured at 369 GB an evening at two hundred people. At two people that is not bandwidth, but the same absence of culling is CPU on the server for every neighbour of every actor, and with every NPC in Skyrim simulated the neighbour count is no longer small. HOW TO TELL THEM APART, and it is cheap: deploy dev with -Npcs interior, play the same spot, and say whether it is better. If it is, the number of simulated NPCs is the cost and the work is culling and budgeting them. If it is not, it is not the NPCs and the next thing to read is the server log for what the tick is spending its time on. NOTHING SHOULD BE OPTIMISED BEFORE THAT ANSWER. The two candidates want completely different work and guessing wrong costs a week. THE EXPERIMENT IS ALREADY SET UP, and nobody had noticed. Both servers' settings read from the box on 23 September. DEV is npcSettings default spawnInInterior true, spawnInExterior FALSE, which is -Npcs interior. LIVE is spawnInInterior true, spawnInExterior TRUE, which is -Npcs all and is every bandit and every chicken in Skyrim kept alive by one process. So dev went back to interior at some point after this entry was written and live is now the one carrying the heavy setting. THAT MAKES THE MEASUREMENT FREE: play dev, play live, same spot, same time of day, and say which is smoother. No deploy and no restart needed for it, and the dev session is one Patrick is about to do anyway for the fire. If dev is smoother it is the NPC count and the work is culling and budgeting; if they feel the same it is not the NPCs and the next thing to read is where the tick goes. WHILE THE SETTINGS WERE OPEN, two other things checked out: damageMultFormulaSettings is multiplier 1.0 and playerMultiplier 2.0 on BOTH servers, which is entry 18's server half live in both places, and all three equipment checks are off on both. AND THE INSTRUMENT IS BUILT, 23 September, pull request 150, because Patrick says the lag is on BOTH servers. That is the first suspect ruled out by his own report: dev simulates interior NPCs only and live simulates every NPC in Skyrim, so if both feel the same the number of simulated NPCs is not the cost. What both share is the front plugin, where nineteen handlers run on sp.on(update), which is every frame, and three of them did real work every frame until they were given a heartbeat, the door locks only today. So guard(), which every handler already goes through, now times all nineteen and writes one line every thirty seconds: updates a second, total plugin milliseconds, what share of a core that is, and the five costliest with their worst single call. Proved with a fake clock, not by hoping: a handler rigged to take 5ms a hundred times reports 500ms over 100 runs, worst 5ms. One dev session now says where the frame goes. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #239. WHAT CHANGED: I fixed the crash in fireSpotsHere in tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js. Its closing log line named `walked`, a variable that exists only inside refsInCell. It now names fireWalked, the fire probe's own counter, and a three-line comment says why. Every cell change threw a ReferenceError out of the place tick after the fires had been kept. That tick lost its /place report to the server, its fire distance and its burn check. The tick after it read the kept list and got through. I added tools/test-fire-walk.js. It runs the real code lifted from the plugin over a fake cell and a fake sp, calling it the same way the place tick does. MEASURED: C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log (last written 23 Sep 21:00) holds 80 lines of "place threw: ReferenceError: walked is not defined", from 20:08:29 to 20:59:48, and zero "fires: N of ours in this cell" lines, so the walk's log line never landed once. The live client log C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log was last written at 10:22, before #184, and has 0 such lines. The fix is thornswood-front.js:2443, which was :2440 before the comment went in. The bad name came in with 36f07ea (#184). The harness gives 19 passed, 0 failed on the branch. Against main's copy of the plugin (git show HEAD:... saved to the scratchpad and pointed at with FRONT=) it gives 13 passed, 6 failed, and the first failure reads "(it threw: walked is not defined)". That run also shows S1 "keeps the two lit fires" passing after the throw, which confirms fireHere was set before the throw. The file still has 5113 lines and 5113 CRs, so its CRLF endings are unchanged. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick: merge this, then ship it to dev with Ship.ps1 -Channel dev. The fix only reaches testers in a pack. Still open on entry 22 and deliberately not done here: (1) Spread the fire cell walk over several frames, or cap it per frame. 'place' worst single calls were 38 to 204 ms on cell changes. This changes when fire distances become known, and the temperature reads them, so it needs its own harness. (2) Cache busyMenuOpen/notOurs in the 'controls' handler, which is about 0.7 ms a frame with a 13 to 39 ms worst. (3) The measurement the entry exists for: Patrick has to say whether "laggy" means frame rate and stutter, or people and NPCs jumping about (network), and compare live (all NPCs) with dev (indoor NPCs only) in the same spot. The To Do List was not edited, as instructed. Entry 22 should record that the walked crash is fixed on this branch. The one-word crash fix is the part that could be done without Patrick; the frame side and the network side still need him to say which kind of lag he means.

issues.title: The game went down building an NPC's head, on a face from FishingInSkyrim.esp
issues.body:
**Order:** 46 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log · FishingInSkyrim.esp, NPC 0x30025905 "Rybek Kupiecski" · Data\meshes\actors\character\facegendata\facegeom\FishingInSkyrim.esp\00025905.nif

## What is known

REPORTED 22 SEPTEMBER by Patrick: "I just crashed after jumping". JUMPING IS NOT WHAT KILLED IT, and that matters because it is the kind of thing that sends somebody looking at the input plugin for an evening. The crash log is a FaceGen head crash: EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x168, which is a field offset off a null pointer, with BSFaceGenMorphDataHead, a BSFaceGenNiNodeSkinned and a BSTriShape named "BrowsMaleHumanoid05" all live in the registers. Four minutes into the session. The face belongs to NPC 0x30025905, "Rybek Kupiecski", from FishingInSkyrim.esp. Jumping is simply what he happened to be doing when that NPC came into range and the game went to build its head. NOT OUR CODE, and this is worth being exact about. Every frame on the stack is SkyrimSE.exe, KERNEL32, ntdll or KERNELBASE. No SKSE plugin, no Skyrim Platform, no SkyrimPlatform.dll, nothing from this repo. It is a load order and content fault. WHAT WAS CHECKED. The facegen mesh is NOT missing: 00025905.nif is there in the FishingInSkyrim.esp folder under facegeom. The crash log lists no other plugin overriding that NPC record; the "Modified by" chain it prints belongs to the parent CELL, which is Wilderness, through Skyrim.esm, Update.esm, The Great City of Solitude.esp and then FishingInSkyrim.esp. The brow textures are mismatched in a way worth following: diffuse is MaleBrow_5.dds and normal is MaleBrow1_n.dds, on a trishape called BrowsMaleHumanoid05. So the head parts the .nif was generated against and the head parts installed now may not be the same set, which is the usual shape of this crash. NOT THE SAME AS THE OTHER TWO. The 19 September crash log on this machine is a pathing crash, BSPathBuilder and PathingRequest, which is the entry below. The favourites menu one is its own. Three different crashes, three causes. WHAT IS LEFT is deciding what to do about it: regenerate that NPC's facegen, or find which head part mod is replacing the brows that face was built against, or leave it as a known issue in a closed playtest. Nobody else has reported it yet, and it is one NPC in one mod. THE CRASH LOG IS ON PATRICK'S OWN MACHINE, found 23 September: Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF reading 0x168, with R9 a BSTriShape "BrowsMaleHumanoid05", R15 a BSFaceGenMorphDataHead and the stack carrying BSFaceGenNiNodeSkinned. Four minutes into the session, working directory C:\Thornswood\Game. THREE HYPOTHESES RULED OUT by reading the plugins rather than guessing. ONE: nothing in the load order overrides the BrowsMaleHumanoid05 record. It is defined by Skyrim.esm and by nothing else; the only male brow anybody touches at all is BrowsMaleSnowElf, in Dawnguard. TWO: its mesh, Actors\Character\Character Assets\FaceParts\MaleBrows.nif, has no loose replacement in Data, so no mod is overwriting it as a file. THREE: the two faces FishingInSkyrim ships are its OWN NPCs, FISLillani and FishingVendorPolish, and neither carries an HNAM, so both keep the race's default head parts while carrying their own tint and morph data. That is the shape that crashes: morph data applied to parts the mod did not ship. WHAT IS LEFT is the Creation Kit end of it, which is regenerating the facegen for that plugin or dropping the two NPCs, and that is content work rather than anything this repo compiles. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log shows EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF, reading 0x168, 4:02 into the session. R9 is the BSTriShape 'BrowsMaleHumanoid05' and R15 is a BSFaceGenMorphDataHead. Lines 92-122 name 'Rybek Kupiecski' 0x30025905 from FishingInSkyrim.esp, with diffuse MaleBrow_5.dds and normal MaleBrow1_n.dds. The facegen mesh is present: Data/meshes/actors/character/facegendata/facegeom/fishinginskyrim.esp/00025905.nif, 279,993 bytes, dated 2021-03-27. The only other crash log on this machine is 19 Sep (the pathing one), and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Profile has none. Nothing in the repo refers to the NPC. There is one in-repo option. The server reads per-plugin npcSettings keys (fork ScampServer.cpp:327-337), so npcSettings['FishingInSkyrim.esp'] with both spawn flags false would stop the server spawning that plugin's NPCs. That also removes the fishing vendor. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build until Patrick chooses. The options: (a) regenerate FishingInSkyrim's facegen in the Creation Kit and ship it through the collection, which is a Nexus upload; (b) stop the server spawning FishingInSkyrim NPCs with a per-plugin npcSettings entry written by Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 (a dev gamemode deploy, which restarts the server, and it loses the vendor); (c) write it up as a known issue naming the mod and the NPC. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides between regenerating the facegen (Creation Kit plus a Nexus collection update), dropping FishingInSkyrim's NPCs, or leaving it as a known issue.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log`: the whole thing. POSSIBLE RELEVANT OBJECTS at the top names the head and the brows before you read a single stack frame

## Steps

- [ ] Look at whether anything in the collection replaces male brow head parts or their meshes. A head part mod that changes BrowsMaleHumanoid05 is the likeliest reason a face built against the vanilla one comes apart.
- [ ] If somebody hits it again, the same NPC or another face from the same mod in the log says it is the mod and not that one record.
- [ ] Then decide: regenerate the facegen for FishingInSkyrim.esp, drop the offending head part replacer, or write it up as a known issue. (patrick)

## Commands

- Read only, stays on this machine. Every crash this build has produced, oldest first. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-*.log | Sort-Object LastWriteTime
  ```
- Read only. The head, the brow trishape and the two mismatched brow textures. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59.log -Pattern 'FaceGen|Brows|Texture\[' | Select-Object -First 20
  ```
- Read only. Which plugins ship loose facegen at all, which is where a regenerated one would go. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\actors\character\facegendata\facegeom' -Directory
  ```

## Done when

Either that face is fixed and the NPC can be walked past, or it is written down as a known issue with the mod and the NPC named.

## Traps

DO NOT TAKE THE ACTION THE PERSON WAS DOING AS THE CAUSE. "Crashed after jumping" points at input, movement and the plugins that touch them, and the log says a face. Read POSSIBLE RELEVANT OBJECTS first, every time. And a facegen crash is not always a MISSING mesh: this one has its mesh, and the mismatch is between what the mesh was built against and what is installed now.

issues.title: Djinn's dev launcher says the mod order is wrong, and the servers say it is not
issues.body:
**Order:** 57 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** find out, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Djinn's machine · the Mods page in the launcher · the reference plugin list in a pack, profile\plugins.txt

## What is known

DJINN, 22 SEPTEMBER AT 10:18 PM: "Dev Launcher is not catching the correct mod order", with the dialog: "Your mod list does not match the one this build shipped with. Joining like this desyncs the whole server, so the launcher will not start the game until it is sorted. Press Fix on the Mods page, then try again." At 10:29 he sent the Mods page showing "1 problem with you connecting". WHAT WAS RULED OUT FROM HERE, so nobody spends the morning on it. The live and dev manifests were read over HTTP and compared row by row, filename, size and crc32: 57 plugins each and ZERO rows differing. So the two servers agree with each other and the dev server is not carrying a stale order, which is what the title of his report suggests and is the first thing anybody would check. AND A SECOND COMPARISON THAT LOOKS LIKE A FAULT AND IS NOT. The reference plugin list inside the newest pack has 94 entries and the server manifest has 57. That is the documented split, not a mismatch: Deploy-Gamemode leaves 42 light plugins out so the indices match the game exactly, and the five vanilla masters are implicit in a plugins.txt and listed in a manifest. Comparing those two lists directly is apples to oranges and will produce a confident wrong answer. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEEDED is the one line Djinn's own Mods page is already showing him. It says "1 problem", and the launcher names which plugin and what is wrong with it. That single line decides whether this is his collection revision, a plugin Vortex has not deployed, or something the dev feed sent him. Ask for it before touching anything. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The dialog Djinn saw is the non-absent branch at tools/app/Shell.cs:3758. Verify.Run (tools/app/Verify.cs:55-190) builds one sentence per problem, naming the plugin. The possible problems are: a plugin turned off, a plugin enabled that is not in this build, a plugin not flagged light, order against the server manifest, a stray Creation Club plugin, and bytes against the manifest. Since #142 (c226c78, 23 Sep 09:34) the scan writes those sentences into launcher.log, and session logs go up to the site (b75a62b, 22 Sep 12:01). Djinn's report was 22 Sep at 22:18, before #142, so any uploaded log from then carries only the count. The entry had already found that the live and dev manifests agree, 57 rows each with none different. Nothing on this machine can show Djinn's plugin list. NEXT STEP: No change to the feed or the launcher is justified yet. Get the one problem line from Djinn's Mods page, or have Patrick read Djinn's next dev launcher log on the site, which now names the plugin. Then fix whatever it names. Optional hardening: have the message box at Shell.cs:3758 quote the first blocking issue, so a screenshot of the dialog is enough. Shell.cs is on the shared-files list and needs a #dev line unless Patrick asks for it. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Evidence from Djinn's machine: the problem line on his Mods page and his collection revision, or Patrick reading his uploaded launcher log from the site. SOLVED ON THE LAUNCHER SIDE 24 September, waiting on Djinn to confirm. His Mods page finally gave the line this entry was blocked on: position 52 holds Hothtrooper44_Armor_Ecksstra.esp where the server has SkyHUD.esp, and Fix, a Vortex purge and a redeploy all failed to clear it. MEASURED: the Nexus archive of Immersive Armors, Script Free and Skypatched 1.3.0 ships that file light (171 bytes, flags 0x200), byte for byte the copy on Patrick's machine, which is where the server's order is built. So the server leaves it out as light and counts SkyHUD at 52; Djinn's copy is not flagged, so it takes an index of its own and pushes everything after it one place along. Fix only reorders, so it could never clear it. Pull request 252 put it on Checks.MustBeLight beside MCMHelper.esp, so the Mods page names it as not flagged light and Fix sets the flag on his own separated copy; out in dev 1.1.92.4. STILL OPEN: why Djinn's copy differs from the Nexus archive at all (an older or different Immersive Armors in his Vortex is the likely answer), and whether MustBeLight should be worked out from the server's order rather than kept by hand, since this is the second plugin to need it.

## Read first

- `tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1`: the 42 light plugins it leaves out so the indices match, which is why a pack's 94 and a manifest's 57 are not a mismatch

## Steps

- [ ] Ask Djinn for the one problem line off his Mods page, and for what Fix said when he pressed it. (patrick)
- [ ] Ask which collection revision his Vortex is on. The feed shipped against revision 5. (patrick)
- [ ] Only then look at the dev feed. The manifests already agree, so the burden is on evidence from his machine.

## Commands

- Start in the repo. (claude)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo
  ```
- Read only, over HTTP. The LIVE server's expected plugin list. (claude)
  ```powershell
  curl -s http://192.135.112.23:3000/api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json
  ```
- Read only, over HTTP. The DEV server's. These two were identical on 22 September. (claude)
