  ```powershell
  curl -s http://192.135.112.23:7788/api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json
  ```

## Done when

Djinn's dev launcher starts the game, or the one problem it names turns out to be something on the feed and that is fixed.

## Traps

DO NOT COMPARE A PACK'S plugins.txt AGAINST A SERVER MANIFEST AND CONCLUDE ANYTHING. 94 against 57 is the light plugin split and the vanilla masters, by design, and it reads exactly like a serious mismatch.

issues.title: The selector timed itself out to the name step, then came back with no cursor and had to be task-killed
issues.body:
**Order:** 64 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js, the chargen block and its timeout · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the F6 cursor · tools\ts-ui, the selector page

## What is known

DJINN, 22 SEPTEMBER AT 8:03 PM, in "Timed out", with a screenshot of the Begin your life in Thornswood panel: "Sitting in the selector window, it automatically timed me out to name choice without any input commands, then once I named the character it then brought back up the selector and is stuck there since the cursor icon F6 button does not show/initiate the cursor to choose anything and is now stuck on this window and have to task out exit." THREE FAULTS IN ONE SITTING AND THEY ARE PROBABLY NOT ONE BUG. First, the timeout fired while he was sitting there reading, and moved him on WITHOUT INPUT. That is the same timeout entry 34 is about, firing for somebody who is present rather than for somebody who has walked away, which is the opposite of what it is for. Second, naming the character brought the selector back up: the stage went backwards, so something re-entered a step that had already been passed. Third, and this is the one that made it unrecoverable, F6 would not give him a cursor, so the panel was on screen and unusable and the only way out was Task Manager. THE THIRD ONE IS THE WORST because it is the difference between a confusing minute and losing the session. The F6 cursor is the browser focus machinery in thornswood-front.js, which has a long history in this repo of being the thing that eats the keyboard, and a panel with no cursor is a panel that cannot be answered. AFTER 8 PM ON 22 SEPTEMBER, so this is against a recent build, not an old one. Worth checking whether it is reproducible by just sitting still on the selector, because that is a two minute test and it would settle the first of the three on its own. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: FAULT 1 IS IN THE LIVE LOG. logs/thornswood.log:134-138: profile 61415365 is a new profile, let in at 01:50:35Z (door.log:251). It went to appearance at 19:50:42. At 19:55:43 it logged 'appearance never arrived after 300s, going on to the choices anyway', then '-> choosing (no face after 300s), panel opened', and no 'home =' line ever followed. That fits Djinn's 8:03 PM report and the task-kill. The trigger is GIVEUP_MS = 300000 (gamemode.js:3578), which runs on the clock (:4646). beginChoosing (:3703) calls closeRaceMenu (:3709), but on the client setRaceMenuOpen(false) does nothing: fork remoteServer.ts:1064-1066 is '// TODO: Implement closeMenu'. So the race menu stays up and the K panel opens on top of it. The server cannot tell someone making a face from someone stuck, because the plugin only reports the race menu closing ('/face done', thornswood-front.js:1805-1813). FAULT 3 IS ONLY HALF FIXED. #124 (20069f6) says an F6 focus is held. A scratchpad harness lifted applyFocus (front.js:934) unchanged and drove it with a fake browser: outside the race menu, an F6 raise is put down on the first frame (60 frames, all unfocused); inside the race menu it is held. That first-frame put-down is also what stops Enter trapping people in the world, so the fix has to tell the two keys apart. FAULT 2, the selector coming back after naming, cannot be reproduced from code. It is most likely a consequence of the panel opening over a race menu that was never closed. NEXT STEP: gamemode.js plus thornswood-front.js: the plugin sends '/face open' when RaceSex Menu opens, plus a light activity beat from the input counter while it stays open. The '/face' branch in handle() (~gamemode.js:18200) records it through a new __thornswoodChargen.faceOpen. The give-up at :4646 waits while the race menu is reported open and input was seen recently, with a hard cap of about 30 minutes for the genuinely stuck. beginChoosing stops opening the panel over a race menu that is reported open. Extend tools/test-stuck-in-the-hall.js to cover a slow face (no give-up), an idle race menu (give-up after the cap) and a race menu that never opened (give-up at 300 s). In applyFocus, hold focus as manual when the last key the input watcher saw within about 0.5 s was F6 (DIK 0x40), and keep putting down a focus raised by Enter. Harness both. Ship to dev and deploy the dev gamemode. Left for Djinn or Patrick: sit in the race menu for more than 5 minutes on dev, and press F6 at a panel that has no claim. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A playtest on dev by Djinn or Patrick to confirm the race menu, name prompt, panel and F6 behaviour in the real game. Everything before that can be built and harnessed now. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #324. The server no longer times somebody out of the race menu while they are still in it. The plugin now sends /racemenu when the race menu opens and once a minute while it stays open. The gamemode records it (faceOpen). The five minute give up then waits while the last report is under 150 seconds old, for at most 30 minutes. A client that never reports still gets the old five minutes, and a reconnect clears the old reports. F6 now works: it gives a cursor at a panel with no claim, and F6 or Escape gives the keyboard back. It reads F6 and Escape with Input.isKeyPressed, the same way skymp5-client ... STILL TO GO OUT: the dev Ship; the dev gamemode deploy. Left: For Patrick: run Ship -Channel dev and Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 in the same sitting, because the plugin and the gamemode must both change. Then Patrick or Djinn checks it in play on dev, reading C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log and the dev server's chargen lines. 1) Make a new character and sit in the race menu for more than 6 minutes, touching nothing. The menu must stay up and no panel may appear. The server log should say "the plugin says the race menu is up", then "no face after ...s, but the race menu is still up, so the give up waits". There must be no "appearance ...

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js, the chargen timeout`: entry 34 is the same timeout seen from the other side, and the two should be read together
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the focus and cursor handling`: F6 not giving a cursor is the part that turned this from confusing into unrecoverable

## Steps

- [ ] Sit on the selector and touch nothing. If it moves on by itself, the timeout is firing for somebody present and that is the first fault reproduced. (patrick)
- [ ] Then name a character and watch whether the selector comes back. That is the second. (patrick)
- [ ] If a panel is ever up with no cursor, press F6 and then read the plugin log for what the focus machinery said. That log is the only witness to the third. (patrick)
- [ ] Ask Djinn whether the timeout was the six minute one or something shorter, because the two come from different places.
- [ ] Send it out: the dev Ship. (patrick)
- [ ] Send it out: the dev gamemode deploy. (patrick)

## Commands

- Start in the repo. (claude)
  ```powershell
  cd C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo
  ```
- Read only, TALKS TO THE VPS. What the server thought was happening to that session, stage by stage. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Chargen-Log.ps1
  ```
- Read only, stays on this machine. The focus machinery and the F6 cursor, which is the half the server cannot see. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log' -Tail 80
  ```

## Done when

Sitting still on the selector does not move anybody on, naming a character does not bring the selector back, and a panel that is up can always be answered.

## Traps

Do not treat this as entry 34 all over again. That one is about a rescue that did not fire for somebody standing still; this is a timeout firing for somebody who is sitting there reading, plus a stage going backwards, plus a cursor that never appeared. Fixing the timeout alone leaves somebody able to reach a window they cannot close.

issues.title: Nothing is code signed: SmartScreen warns forever, and one GitHub login is all that stands between a stranger and every installed machine
issues.body:
**Order:** 69 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Packaging · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Old number:** 14

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:222-330; tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs:79-90 · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Updater.cs:369-381, 405-418, 815-875

## What is known

Start the Trusted Signing identity validation today, because it takes days and nothing else about signing can begin until it clears. Then sign the installer and the launcher, and check the signer in SelfUpdate before the swap. The existing host pinning and checksum stay as a second layer UPDATE 17 September: Microsoft cleared the installer as a false positive, submission 20a8542e-6f21-415d-91b1-e15663cf45a3, and removed the detection. That clearance is for the binary that was submitted, so every new build is a new file and can be flagged again. It lowers the urgency for today's download and changes nothing about the underlying cause. EVERYTHING BUT THE CERTIFICATE IS DONE, 18 September. Three commits: 1143fcd adds tools/Sign-Artifact.ps1, one implementation driven by a gitignored tools/signing.json, wired into the launcher build so it signs the exe and the setup stub together or leaves both alone. de231da signs the installer after its payload is attached, which is the right order and one its own loader already expects, because Bootstrap.cs scans backwards for its magic precisely because a certificate lands after the trailer. f87a0bb adds the signer check to SelfUpdate, in front of the copy rather than after it, since once a file sits at exe.new the swap happens on the next start whatever the check says. PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the same call was compiled with the same Framework csc at langversion 5 and pointed at real files. It accepts a matching signer, refuses a different one and refuses an unsigned file. That test also turned up something worth knowing: the call reads embedded signatures only, so notepad.exe reports unsigned while Windows calls it Valid, because system binaries are catalog signed. WHAT IS LEFT is the certificate itself. Start the Azure Trusted Signing identity validation, which is a manual review with a photo ID and takes days, then write tools/signing.json and fill in Updater.ExpectedSigner in the same release that first ships a signed exe. CORRECTED 18 September after reading the current Microsoft documentation, because two things I had said were wrong. The service is called Artifact Signing now, not Trusted Signing. And validation does NOT take days for an individual: the 1 to 20 business days figure is organisation validation. An individual does a Verified ID check on a phone through AU10TIX and the portal status reaches Completed in minutes. This can be finished today. TWO THINGS THAT WILL STOP IT COLD. Individual developers must be located in the United States or Canada. And the Azure billing account on the subscription must have an Account Type of Individual, with a legal name and sold-to address matching the government ID, because the form is filled in from the billing account and is read only. Fix the billing account first if it does not match. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the certificates last three days, so the timestamp is what keeps a signature valid and is not optional. Sign-Artifact.ps1 now defaults to the service's own timestamp authority, commit 93a1e75. The endpoint in metadata.json must name the same region the account was created in, or signing fails with a bare 403. ACCOUNT TRAP, 18 September. Azure kept landing on an organisation directory called CCCS, because that sign-in is a work or school account. That is not a directory to switch out of: everything created under it lives in that organisation's tenant and its billing account is Organization type, so individual validation cannot run there. Being blocked is the kind outcome. A Public Trust certificate carries the validated identity, so signing under that account would put an organisation's legal name on every Thornswood binary, for a personal project, without their permission. Use the personal Microsoft account in a private window instead. AZURE FOR STUDENTS DOES NOT HELP and is worth saying out loud because it is offered on the way in. Verifying academic status uses the school account, so it lands back in the same tenant, and its subscription is credit based rather than an Individual billing account. Pay-as-you-go on the personal account is what creates the Individual billing account this needs. THE COST, since it is a running one: Basic is 9.99 US dollars a month for 5,000 signatures, against two or three files per release. Premium at 99.99 is not needed. A traditional certificate is a few hundred a year plus a hardware token, so this is the cheap route. CHECKED AGAINST AZURE, 18 September, and the Azure half is right. Signed in as the personal outlook.com account, subscription Enabled, ThornswoodSigning created in westus2 in resource group Thornswood-Signing. signtool 10.0.28000.0, the .NET 8.0.31 runtime and Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll are all installed, so the client tools step was done by hand rather than by winget and counts. tools/signing.json is correct, points at files that exist, and is properly gitignored and untracked. TWO THINGS WERE WRONG IN C:/tools/metadata.json AND ARE NOW FIXED. Its Endpoint read https://westus2.codesigning.azure.net/ which is the region NAME, not the endpoint tag. Azure reports the account's own accountUri as https://wus2.codesigning.azure.net and that is now what the file says; the old one is kept beside it as metadata.json.before-fix. That mistake is exactly the bare 403 the documentation warns about and it never mentions regions, so it would have been a long evening. Do not type the endpoint from the table, ask the account for its own accountUri. Its CertificateProfileName was still the placeholder YOUR_EXACT_PROFILE_NAME, which is not a mistake so much as getting ahead: there are no certificate profiles on the account at all yet, because the identity validation has not been done. SO WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT is the identity validation in the portal, then the profile, then the signer role, then filling in that one remaining field. Everything before and after that is in place. TICKS CORRECTED 18 September, which is what you asked me to check. Azure reports no certificate profiles on ThornswoodSigning at all. A profile cannot be created without a completed identity validation, so its absence is proof that the chain from the validation onwards is unfinished, and the steps from there down have been unticked. The resource provider does read Registered and the account does exist in westus2, so everything up to that point is genuinely done. The one thing I cannot see from here is the validation's own status, because identity validation is portal only and has no CLI or management API surface. Open the account, Identity validations under Objects, and read what the status says. In Progress means it is still working, Action Required means the phone half is waiting for you, Completed means only the profile is missing and that is one command. ENDPOINT MEASURED 18 September, and it corrects something I said. I described a wrong region as giving a bare 403. It does not: westus2.codesigning.azure.net does not resolve at all, so signing would have failed on DNS before it reached anything. The correct host, wus2.codesigning.azure.net, resolves to 48.192.88.101 and answers 403 to an unauthenticated browser. That 403 is the endpoint working. It is a signing API behind an application gateway, not a web page, so refusing a browser with no token is exactly right and is not a sign of a problem. WRONG FORM, seen 18 September. A browser tab read New organization validation. That is the default and it is not the one an individual wants: it asks for a legal business entity, a website on a domain that entity owns, and a business identifier. The Individual form is behind a dropdown on the Identity validations pane that opens on Organization, so it is genuinely easy to miss. Change the dropdown to Individual first, then New Identity, then Public. Everything else on the account was confirmed correct from a portal screenshot: ThornswoodSigning, West US 2, Basic, Account URI https://wus2.codesigning.azure.net/ matching metadata.json, and the directory is the personal one rather than CCCS. TERMS GATE, 18 September. The Identity validations pane carries an amber banner: the artifact signing terms of use have been updated and want accepting. Do that before starting the validation rather than after. Confirmed from the same screenshot: the dropdown now reads Individuals, the list says No identity validations yet, and Private is correctly greyed out because private trust is for organisations only. Public is the one to pick. VALIDATION CREATED 18 September: id 78b47be2-ed3f-4877-b0a2-e4a462668983, Public, United States, status In Progress. The profile command in this entry now carries that id so it can be pasted when the status reaches Completed. ONE THING TO DECIDE BEFORE IT SHIPS, and it cannot be undone afterwards: an individual Public Trust certificate carries the legal name from the government ID, and that name is visible to anyone who inspects a signed binary. The validation is in the legal name rather than the handle this project uses everywhere else. There is no alias option for individual certificates. Worth being comfortable with that now rather than after the first signed release. SIGNING IS TURNED OFF FOR NOW, 18 September, so that it stops blocking releases while the certificate is still being set up. tools/signing.json has "enabled": false and the old file is kept beside it as signing.json.before-disable. Take that line out when the profile exists. THE 403 IS EXPLAINED AND IT IS NOT THE ENDPOINT. signtool answered 403 on both files during the 1.1.48 build. The endpoint is correct: wus2.codesigning.azure.net resolves and answers. The refusal is because CertificateProfileName in C:/tools/metadata.json still reads FILL THIS IN AFTER THE PROFILE EXISTS, and there is no profile to sign with because the identity validation is still In Progress. Nothing is wrong. It is the middle of setting this up. SO THE MIDDLE OF SETTING IT UP NO LONGER BREAKS THE BUILD, commit bd7dabf. Sign-Artifact.ps1 skips, with a line saying which reason, when signing.json is absent, when it says "enabled": false, or when the certificate profile is still a placeholder. -Required overrides all three, because a real release has to be signed and that switch exists to find out. Measured against the real config on this machine: the placeholder case exits 0 with a reason, the same case with -Required exits 1, and a machine with no signing.json still skips the way it always did, which is what keeps Djinn's builds working. THE WARNING IS OFF THE SITE, 20 September, commit 1b447fc, asked for by Patrick. home.html carried a block under the download button saying Windows might call the installer a virus, naming Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml, explaining that the ml suffix means a machine guessed from the file's shape rather than recognising anything, and telling people to check it on VirusTotal rather than take our word for it. Gone, comment and all. WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THIS ENTRY: nothing on the site says anything about a detection now, so anybody who does meet a Defender block meets it with no explanation anywhere. That is a deliberate choice and it is defensible, because Microsoft cleared the installer as a false positive on 17 September, submission 20a8542e, and removed the detection, so the box may well have been describing something that no longer happens. It is worth checking against a current build rather than assumed: the clearance covers the binary that was submitted and every new build is a new file that can be flagged again. If it starts happening again the choice is to put something back or to finish the certificate, and this entry is the certificate. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Everything in the repo is done: Sign-Artifact.ps1, signing after the payload is attached, and CheckSigner at tools/app/Updater.cs:922-939, which returns early while ExpectedSigner at :898 is "". Local state read without printing any values: tools/signing.json has the keys dlib, enabled, metadata, method and timestampUrl, with enabled false, and is gitignored (.gitignore:46). C:/tools/metadata.json still has a placeholder CertificateProfileName. That is consistent with the entry: identity validation 78b47be2 was In Progress on 18 Sep and no certificate profile exists. Azure was not queried. NEXT STEP: Nothing in the repo until the certificate exists. Then, in order: Patrick completes the Verified ID check in the portal and sees Completed; creates the ThornswoodRelease profile; assigns himself the Certificate Profile Signer role; fills CertificateProfileName; removes "enabled": false; builds and reads Get-AuthenticodeSignature on both exes. Only then does a Claude put a Subject fragment into Updater.ExpectedSigner, in the same main release as the first signed exe. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's outside account: the Azure Artifact Signing identity validation, a phone Verified ID check, then the profile and role. He also has to accept that his legal name will be on the certificate. 25 SEPTEMBER, read by Patrick: C:\tools\metadata.json holds CodeSigningAccountName ThornswoodSigning, the endpoint https://wus2.codesigning.azure.net, and CertificateProfileName still reading "FILL THIS IN AFTER THE PROFILE EXISTS", so the certificate profile was never created, which is the step this entry already waits on. The file holds no key or password and can live in the repository; the rest of C:\tools is the signing client package (Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll, from nuget.exe), a metadata.json.before-fix backup and a test.exe from 12 August. Moving them is part of the folder consolidation proposal for #dev. AUDIT OF 25 SEPTEMBER, what one GitHub login can do: the launcher downloads and runs any pack version.json lists with a matching hash, the hash comes from the same file, and the host check (Updater.cs:389-411) admits any github.com release, not only Thornswood-Releases. Worse, each feed check saves updateRepo, serverAddress, siteUrl, voiceUrl and collectionUrl from the feed into config.json (Shell.cs:4548-4585), so one bad feed commit moves every launcher somewhere else for good. CreateFromSignedFile (Updater.cs:912) reads a subject and verifies nothing; WinVerifyTrust does. WHAT TO DO, in order: protect Thornswood-Releases (ruleset on main and dev, check collaborators); sign version.json with a key compiled into the launcher and refuse unsigned moves of those five fields; tie the host check to the Releases repo; finish signing, set ExpectedSigner last. ALSO: Publish-Update.ps1:1029-1040 says a voice token and the SkyMP sign-in went out in old packs and the installer: check whether those release assets are still downloadable and delete them. About 35 deploy scripts use StrictHostKeyChecking=no against the VPS: pin its host key in a tracked known_hosts. READ 25 September: Thornswood-Releases has three collaborators, EvilPatrick06 (admin), WiccanDjinn and Ture-Neko (Ataxayk), both write, so any of the three logins can change the feed every launcher reads. No script force-pushes the releases repo, so a ruleset refusing force pushes and deletion of main and dev costs nothing. The voice token that went out in pack 20260918-2340 was short lived and has expired (entry on the nine packs), so that asset is not worth breaking the pack chain to delete. DONE 25 September: a ruleset on Thornswood-Releases (id 23980877, active, no bypass) refuses force pushes and deletion of main and dev. DECIDED BY PATRICK, 25 September: WiccanDjinn and Ture-Neko keep write on the releases repo for now, since a dev Ship needs it. Left: feed signing, tying the host check to the releases repo, code signing.

## Read first

- `tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs:75-95`: the reputation argument stated in the file's own words: a new binary every release is a new hash every release
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:365-430`: the AllowedHosts array and the download that refuses an update with no checksum, the layer that already exists
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:815-873`: SelfUpdate, the swap with no verification at all, and the File.Copy at :821 the signer check goes in front of
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:218-300`: the compile section that ends with csc and no signing step

## Steps

- [x] Post the problem, the approach and what it touches in #dev before any edit, because Updater.cs is on CLAUDE.md's list of files both machines touch. (patrick)
- [x] Add a signing step at the end of tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 that does nothing when no certificate is configured, so Djinn's machine still builds. Done 18 Sep: tools\Sign-Artifact.ps1 is the one implementation, driven by a gitignored tools\signing.json. (claude)
- [x] Sign the installer AFTER its payload is attached, not before. Bootstrap.cs:648-660 already expects this: it scans backwards for STSFX001 precisely because the certificate lands after the trailer. Done 18 Sep. (claude)
- [x] In tools\app\Updater.cs SelfUpdate, before the File.Copy at :821, read the downloaded file's signer with X509Certificate.CreateFromSignedFile inside a try and throw a plain sentence when the subject does not match the constant, keeping the host pinning and the checksum as the second layer. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 817 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [x] Compile the launcher with the .NET Framework csc, the same gate the pull request build runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- [x] Prove the signer check without owning a certificate, by compiling the same call with the same csc and pointing it at real files. Done 18 Sep, all three branches. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe' | Format-List Status, StatusMessage
  ```
- [x] Parse-check the two scripts you changed, because a syntax error stops Ship at the build step and turns the pull request build red. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $e } else { 'parses' }
  ```
- [x] Sign in with the right account before anything else, and it is not your school one. Azure kept landing on the CCCS directory on 18 September because that sign-in belongs to that organisation. This is not a setting to toggle: a work or school account creates everything inside that organisation's tenant, and its billing account is Organization type, so individual validation cannot run there at all. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#prerequisites
- [x] Understand what signing under the school account would actually do, because being blocked is the kinder outcome. A Public Trust certificate carries the identity that was validated. Validated as CCCS, every Thornswood binary would be signed in that organisation's legal name, for a personal project, and you would need their permission to do it. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#create-an-identity-validation-request
- [x] Sign in as the personal Microsoft account instead, in a private or incognito window. The portal caches the work account hard and switching directory inside a signed-in session puts you straight back. The outlook.com address that submitted the Defender false positive on 17 September is a personal Microsoft account and is the one to use. (patrick)
  https://portal.azure.com/
- [x] Do not take Azure for Students, even though it is offered and looks cheaper. Verifying academic status uses the school account, so it puts you back in the CCCS tenant, which is the problem you are trying to leave. Its subscription is credit based rather than an Individual billing account, and individual identity validation reads its details from an Individual billing account and nowhere else. The credit cannot be spent on a thing you are not eligible to create. (patrick)
  https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/
- [x] Create a pay-as-you-go subscription on the personal account. That is what produces a billing account with an Account Type of Individual. It asks for a card and does not charge for anything you do not use, so the only cost here is the signing service itself. (patrick)
  https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/purchase-options/pay-as-you-go/
- [x] Know the price before you start, because it is a running cost rather than a one off and it belongs in the same conversation as the Patreon. Basic is 9.99 US dollars a month and covers 5,000 signatures, which is far more than this project will use; a release signs two or three files. Premium is 99.99 and is not needed. For comparison a traditional certificate is a few hundred a year and needs a hardware token, so this is the cheap option, not the expensive one. (patrick)
  https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/trusted-signing/
- [x] Confirm you are in the right place before spending any more time. Cost Management and Billing, then Billing account, then Properties. Account Type must read Individual. If it reads anything else you are still in an organisation tenant and the validation form will not let you fix it later. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/commerce/manage-billing-accounts
- [x] Check the two things that disqualify you before spending any time. Individual developers must be located in the United States or Canada; the geographic limit applies to Public Trust certificates, which is the kind that stops SmartScreen warning. If you are outside those two countries, stop here and raise it in #dev, because the rest of this entry does not apply. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart
- [x] Check the billing account, which is the step people lose days to. For an individual, the validation form is populated from the Azure billing account on the subscription and every field is read only. The account must have an Account Type of Individual, and its legal name and sold-to address must match your government ID exactly. If they do not match you cannot correct it on the form; you correct the billing account and start over. Check it first. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  az account show --query "{subscription:name, id:id, tenant:tenantId}" -o table
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/commerce/manage-billing-accounts
- [x] Register the resource provider. It is still named Microsoft.CodeSigning even though the service has been renamed twice, so do not go looking for one called ArtifactSigning. Wait for the state to read Registered before the next step; creating an account against an unregistered provider fails with an unhelpful error. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  az provider register --namespace Microsoft.CodeSigning; az provider show --namespace Microsoft.CodeSigning --query registrationState -o tsv
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#register-the-artifact-signing-resource-provider
- [x] Create the signing account, and write down the region. The service runs in a fixed list of regions and the endpoint you put in metadata.json later has to name the same one. West US 2 maps to https://wus2.codesigning.azure.net, and the region table on that page has the rest. Basic is the right SKU to start on. The account name must be 3 to 24 alphanumeric characters, globally unique, and must not begin with the word one. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  az extension add --name artifact-signing; az group create --name Thornswood-Signing --location westus2; az artifact-signing create -n ThornswoodSigning -l westus2 -g Thornswood-Signing --sku Basic
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#azure-regions-that-support-artifact-signing
- [x] Assign yourself the Artifact Signing Identity Verifier role on that account. Without it the New identity button in the portal is greyed out and nothing on screen tells you why. This is the single most common place to get stuck. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/tutorial-assign-roles
- [x] Accept the terms of use before starting, because the pane carries an amber banner saying they have been updated and an unaccepted version can refuse the validation partway through. Seen on 18 September: Review and accept the latest terms of use, at the top of the Identity validations pane. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/faq
- [x] Start the validation, and watch the dropdown, because the form defaults to Organization and the Individual one is hidden behind it. Open Identity validations in the left nav under Objects, not the big Identity validation button on the overview. The pane opens on Organization: change that dropdown to Individual FIRST, then New Identity, then Public. If the form is headed New organization validation you are on the wrong one and it will ask for a business name, a website and a business identifier that you do not have. This part cannot be done from the CLI at all. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#create-an-identity-validation-request
- [x] Know what the certificate will say about you before it is issued, because this is the one part that cannot be taken back. An individual Public Trust certificate carries the legal name from your government ID, and it is visible to anyone who inspects a signed binary. The validation created on 18 September is in the legal name rather than the handle used everywhere else in this project. That is how individual code signing works and there is no alias option, but decide you are comfortable with it now rather than after the first signed release goes out. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#create-an-identity-validation-request
- [ ] Complete the Verified ID check on a phone. The status goes to Action Required, you open the link, and a partner called AU10TIX takes you through email and phone verification then a QR code you scan with your phone camera. You photograph a government ID, add the credential to Microsoft Authenticator, scan a second QR code back on the desktop and share it. You need Microsoft Authenticator installed. This takes minutes, not days: the one to twenty business days figure in the documentation is organisation validation, not this. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#important-information-for-public-identity-validation-for-individual-developers
- [ ] Wait for the portal status to reach Completed. It takes a couple of minutes to update after the phone half succeeds. If it reads Failed you cannot edit the request, you create a new one, which is another reason to have checked the billing account first. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/faq
- [ ] Create a Public Trust certificate profile, but only once the validation reads Completed. The identity validation id is 78b47be2-ed3f-4877-b0a2-e4a462668983, created 18 September. Leave Program Type as None. The profile name is 5 to 100 characters and unique within the account; ThornswoodRelease is what metadata.json is waiting for. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  az artifact-signing certificate-profile create -g Thornswood-Signing --account-name ThornswoodSigning -n ThornswoodRelease --profile-type PublicTrust --identity-validation-id 78b47be2-ed3f-4877-b0a2-e4a462668983
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart#create-a-certificate-profile
- [ ] Assign yourself the Artifact Signing Certificate Profile Signer role. This is a different role from the verifier one: that role created the identity, this one is what actually permits signing. Having one does not give you the other. (patrick)
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/tutorial-assign-roles
- [x] Install the client tools on the shipping machine. One command brings all four pieces: a new enough signtool, the .NET 8 runtime, the Visual C++ redistributable and the signing library. Do not hand-assemble these. The signtool in the 20348 SDK is specifically not supported by the library. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  winget install -e --id Microsoft.Azure.ArtifactSigningClientTools
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/how-to-signing-integrations#artifact-signing-client-tools-installer
- [ ] Write the metadata.json the library reads. Do NOT type the endpoint from the region table: ask Azure for the account's own accountUri and paste that. The region is called westus2 but the endpoint host is wus2, and westus2.codesigning.azure.net does not exist as a hostname at all, measured on 18 September. The correct host answers 403 to a browser, which is right: it is a signing API behind a gateway, not a web page, and an unauthenticated visit is supposed to be refused. CertificateProfileName cannot be filled in until the profile exists. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  az resource show --resource-group Thornswood-Signing --name ThornswoodSigning --resource-type 'Microsoft.CodeSigning/codeSigningAccounts' --query properties.accountUri -o tsv
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/how-to-signing-integrations#create-a-json-file
- [x] Write tools\signing.json, which is what makes this repo's build sign anything. It is gitignored, so it stays on this machine and Djinn's builds carry on unsigned. Point dlib at Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll from the installer and metadata at the file from the previous step. Leave timestampUrl out; the script already defaults to the right authority. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'C:\Program Files' -Recurse -Filter 'Azure.CodeSigning.Dlib.dll' -EA SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/how-to-signing-integrations#use-signtool-to-sign-a-file
- [ ] Build, and read the result rather than trusting the exit code. Both the launcher and the setup stub must report Valid and Authenticode. If either says NotSigned the build did not fail, it just skipped, which is the whole point of the no-op design and also the way to fool yourself. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause; Get-AuthenticodeSignature C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe, C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\setup-stub.exe | Format-Table Status, SignatureType, Path -AutoSize
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/get-authenticodesignature
- [ ] Copy a distinctive fragment of the Subject from that output into Updater.ExpectedSigner. Use a fragment, not the whole line: certificate authorities reorder and add fields between renewals and an exact match would refuse every update the day the certificate renews. This is the last thing to change and it ships in the same release as the first signed exe, never earlier, or every launcher in the world stops updating. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern 'ExpectedSigner' -Context 0,3
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.x509certificate.createfromsignedfile
- [ ] Ship it as one release. Signing changes every file hash, so the first signed release invalidates every checksum published for the one before it. The launcher, the installer and the server go together or people on the old version cannot update to the new one. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Ship.ps1 "Signed release: Windows stops warning about the installer"
  ```
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/faq

## Commands

- shows the signing step reporting that it is not signing, on a machine with no certificate (claude)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Sign-Artifact.ps1 -Path .\tools\app.ico
  ```
- the difference that matters: one is Authenticode and readable by the check, the other is Catalog and is not (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-AuthenticodeSignature (Get-Command pwsh).Source, 'C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe' | Format-Table Status, SignatureType, Path -AutoSize
  ```
- Compiles the launcher into C:\Thornswood-DevBuild with the .NET Framework csc, which is the compile gate. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- Shows what a Valid signature looks like, so the new check can be tested against a known-good file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe' | Format-List Status, StatusMessage
  ```
- Reports NotSigned for the exe Build-Launcher just produced, and must report Valid with the expected subject afterwards. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe' | Format-List Status, StatusMessage
  ```
- Runs the same parse check the GitHub build workflow runs over every script. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $e } else { 'parses' }
  ```

## Done when

Get-AuthenticodeSignature on the built Thornswood.exe reports Valid with the expected subject rather than NotSigned, the installer reports the same after its payload is attached, and Updater.ExpectedSigner names that certificate. Everything except the certificate itself is in place as of 18 September: the build signs when signing.json exists and says plainly that it is not signing when it does not.

## Traps

CATALOG SIGNATURES ARE INVISIBLE TO THIS CHECK, found by testing on 18 September. X509Certificate.CreateFromSignedFile reads embedded Authenticode only. Most Windows system binaries are catalog signed, so notepad.exe and curl.exe both come back as unsigned from this call while Get-AuthenticodeSignature calls them Valid. That is harmless here, because signtool writes an embedded signature and that is what we will ship, but it makes notepad.exe a useless thing to test against. Use pwsh.exe, node.exe or gh.exe, which are all embedded signed. ExpectedSigner is empty on purpose and must stay empty until the release that first ships a signed exe, or every update stops working for everybody. Match on a fragment of the Subject rather than the whole line, because certificate authorities reorder fields between renewals. Updater.cs needs a line in #dev before anybody edits it. The launcher is C# 5 only, and CreateFromSignedFile throws on an unsigned file rather than returning null, so the throw is what unsigned looks like. Signing changes the file hash, so the first signed release invalidates every checksum published for the previous one and must go out as one complete release, launcher and installer together. Signing the small binaries while the 527 MB payload still has no hash check at all only moves the problem.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/quickstart the portal steps, the region table and the individual validation flow
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/how-to-signing-integrations the client tools installer, metadata.json and the signtool arguments
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/tutorial-assign-roles the two roles: Identity Verifier to create it, Certificate Profile Signer to use it
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation why reputation per file hash is the problem signing solves
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.x509certificate.createfromsignedfile the call the launcher uses, and that it throws on an unsigned file

issues.title: The progression and economy rulebook: classes, professions, sub-professions, ranks and a fifteen skill attribute tree
issues.body:
**Order:** 76 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Design · **Effort:** work it out, large · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Nowhere yet · the nearest thing in code is the flat sixteen in tools\gamemode.js CHARGEN, and lore\ has none of it

## What is known

GIVEN BY PATRICK ON 20 SEPTEMBER, in full, and it is the spec the other three entries below depend on. It is recorded here verbatim in substance because it arrived in chat and chat is gone when the window closes. Nothing in it is built yet. 

THE LAW OF EXCLUSIVITY. You are locked to one Class, one Profession and one Sub-Profession. Nobody can do everything. Lacking a skill means trading, roleplaying or finding a Master to teach you. 

CLASSES, THE VERBS, 100% EXCLUSIVE, ONE EACH, no perks and no cross-class teaching. Hunter is the only class that can loot an animal body. Fisher is the only one that can catch fish. Gatherer is the only one that can harvest flora and materials out of the world. Miner is the only one that can mine ore veins. Farmer is the only one that can plant and harvest crops. 

PROFESSIONS. One Profession and one Sub-Profession, which is the half you specialise in. Within your own Profession you automatically know NOVICE work of your sister sub-profession: a Platewright knows novice Edgewright work. You cannot progress past novice in it unless a Master Edgewright teaches you. Outside your Profession you can do nothing by default. To learn novice skills of another Profession you must be formally apprenticed to a Master of that specific Sub-Profession, you can never progress past novice in a secondary Profession, and you may only do this TWICE, excluding your sister sub-profession. 

THE MAGE EXCEPTION. Mages pick two schools and two starting spells, both in one school for a deep start or split for a wide one, or save a spell point. You must use a spell of the level below to level up. Ranking up unlocks higher-tier spells and one more spell point at the same time. At Master a Mage picks a third school and two more spell points. At the College each semester you can study for two more spell points. Outside the College each semester you may choose a school if you have not already got one from a master or an earlier semester, and study for one spell point and novice spells only. A NON-MAGE CANNOT USE MAGIC AT ALL. To learn a spell they need the spellbook AND a Master Mage willing to apprentice them, and they can only ever learn two novice spells, from one school, which must match the college's school. 

RANKS, earned by doing the work and roleplaying, never by sleeping or grinding offline. Novice is the basics: simple items, iron, leather, minor potions. Advanced is the everyday work: steel, elven, standard potions. Expert is high demand craftsmanship: glass, ebony, high-tier potions. Master is the peak, and unlocks the Master Perk and the right to take Apprentices. 

THE EIGHT PROFESSIONS, their halves and their Master Perks. WARRIOR: Bulwark (tanks, shields, heavy armour) or Berserker (damage, two-handed, dual wield). Warlord: teach novice combat to non-warriors, and master-tier maneuvers. MAGE: sub-professions are the chosen schools. Archmage: a third school, and authority to apprentice non-mages. ALCHEMIST: Blightbrewer (poisons and harm) or Physicker (medicine and restoration). Master Chemist: two potions per batch. COOK: Hearthcook (dinners, meats, stews) or Confectioner (desserts, breads, sweets). Grand Chef: two food per batch. SMITH: Platewright (armour) or Edgewright (weapons). Mastercraft: temper to Legendary, past normal limits. ENCHANTER: Bladebinder (weapons) or Wardweaver (armour and apparel). Twin Souls: two enchantments on one item. TAILOR: Liverywright (robes, uniforms, faction dress) or Haberdasher (common and fine clothing). Master Weaver: clothing gives hidden armour or weather protection without weight. WOODWORKER: Charburner (firewood, coke, campfires) or Woodwright (bows, arrows, instruments). Master Carver: campfires and kilns give maximum warmth. 

THE ATTRIBUTE SKILL TREE. Fifteen sub-skills across Health, Magicka and Stamina, bought with skill points; maxing one grants its Master Perk. HEALTH. Vitality, max health, Cheat Death: once a day a fatal blow leaves you at 1 HP. Fortitude, regen, Troll's Blood: regeneration is not stunted in combat. Might, melee damage, Devastating Blow: power attacks often stagger or knock down. Resilience, armour rating, Unshakeable: immune to stagger while blocking. Toughness, resistances, Purified Blood: immune to all disease, 75% poison resistance. MAGICKA. Capacity, max magicka, Archmage's Vessel: a burst of regeneration below 10%, on a cooldown. Clarity, regen, Leyline Attunement: magicka regenerates at full speed while casting or channelling. Potency, spell effect, Overcharge: 15% chance of double damage or double duration. Ward, magic resist, Spellbreaker: 25% chance to absorb a hostile spell and refill magicka instead. Efficiency, cost, Font of Magic: once a day, all spells cost nothing for 15 seconds. STAMINA. Endurance, max stamina, Tireless: sprinting and power attacks drain 50% less. Vigor, regen, Second Wind: full stamina the instant it empties, five minute cooldown. Agility, speed, Windwalker: 10% faster and no fall damage. Burden, carry weight, Pack Mule: no speed penalty up to 50 lbs over. Precision, critical and ranged, Lethal Aim: ranged attacks ignore 50% of physical armour. 

WHAT THE CODE HAS TODAY, AND IT DOES NOT MATCH. gamemode.js CHARGEN holds ONE FLAT LIST of 16 so-called classes with a starter kit each: warrior, hunter, mage, smith, miner, woodworker, alchemist, bard, cook, enchanter, farmer, fisher, merchant, priest, scholar, thief. There is no Class/Profession split, no sub-professions, no ranks, no skill tree and no perks anywhere. FIVE OF THEM HAVE NO HOME IN THE NEW RULEBOOK: bard, merchant, priest, scholar and thief. TWO IN THE RULEBOOK DO NOT EXIST: gatherer, the class that harvests flora, and tailor with its two halves. The launcher sends class, half and gathering keys already, gamemode.js:1786 onward, so the shape is half anticipated, but the tables behind it are the old flat sixteen. Deciding what happens to those five, and to every character already carrying one, is the first thing this needs and it is Patrick's call. WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE ENFORCED, measured on 20 September against the server source at C:/Thornswood-Dev/skymp, whose HEAD is what runs (git diff against the recorded binary commit is empty). The server offers eleven gamemode hooks and the gamemode subscribes to four. onCraft, onTakeItem, onPutItem, onDropItem and onEatItem are live on the VPS today with no subscriber. A handler returning false blocks; undefined allows. onActivate is refuse-before on the server: ActivateEvent fires at MpObjectReference.cpp 484-486 and ProcessActivateNormal at 490 runs only if nobody blocked. GATHERER AND MINER: gamemode only, in onActivate, and the gamemode already does this for salt and charcoal and shrines. FLOR and TREE are refused after the local fact, though: the client does not block those kinds, so the pick plays and the ingredient sits in the local pack until the next server inventory write, then vanishes, which testers will report as a bug unless the client is told. Any new base answered in onActivate must also go in publishServerBases (1912-1945) or the front re-activates it and it fires twice. HUNTER CANNOT BE ENFORCED WITH WHAT EXISTS. ProcessActivateNormal (1419-1560) has no branch for a dead actor at all, and the shipped client blocks dead actors (12424-12426). Read from source: corpse looting appears not to work on this build for anybody. Gating it means MpObjectReference.cpp growing a corpse branch, which is engine work and a server rebuild. FISHER: unknown. Only Fishing in Skyrim's kit items are in the repo; if the spots are spell or script driven there is no hook, since there is no cast hook anywhere. FARMER: nothing exists, no mod, no station, no record, no design; that is a #dev decision before any hook is chosen. CRAFTING BY RANK AND THE SISTER HALF: enforceable in onCraft, after the local craft, once a recipe-to-half table exists; nothing maps COBJ records to halves anywhere today, and that table is the work. MAGE SCHOOLS CANNOT BE LOCKED: no cast hook, and spell lists live client side. TREE PERKS THAT CHANGE STATS need a new server binding or a client plugin: the server exposes only percentages, and PapyrusActor::SetActorValue warns it executes locally and does not affect server calculations. AND THE BOOK PATH IS DEAD CODE THAT STILL SHIPS: beginClass has no caller, chooseClass and chooseDestination are reachable only through chargenReadBook, whose guards need stages nothing sets, yet chargenReadBook still runs first on every mp.onReadBook and swallows a writ read. The comment at 1449-1458 says outright there are no books any more. Also: state.half and state.gathering are written at 798-799 and read nowhere; the comment promising crafting and gathering checks describes checks that do not exist. And tools/docs-app/data/todo.md 76-79 already carries an entry 13, 'The professions themselves'; this entry extends it rather than sitting beside it. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Most of this entry is done. The rulebook is on the site: tools/docs-app/data/site/classes.md, 405 lines, covering the professions table with Tailor (Liverywright/Haberdasher), the classes table with Gatherer, the Mage rules, ranks, Master perks and the skill tree. gamemode.js:11080-11104 defines CLASSES, including gatherer, and PROFESSIONS, including tailor. `node tools/test-rulebook.js` passes 26 of 26. Built since the entry was written: 077268f (gatherer), 8367a87 (hunter and fisher own a verb), a2ba2ee (the profession gates crafting), d1418f5 (rank comes from work), 5d1f3f0/d2e0c24 (the dead books are removed; grep finds no chargenReadBook, beginClass or chooseDestination), and 0eadfbb (#141, the rulebook cannot drift). NOT DONE: gamemode.js:11066-11073 says the fate of bard, merchant, priest, scholar and thief 'is a decision for the list' and that the code does not make it. migrate() (:17028-17060) leaves the old key on the actor and asks the person again. gamemode.js:4322 still gives old bards their instrument ability. No other entry tracks the five, apart from a passing mention in 332. NEXT STEP: Cut the entry down to its one open item. Patrick decides what bard, merchant, priest, scholar and thief become: mapped onto a new class or profession, retired, or kept as roleplay only. Then a small change to migrate() and to the bard ability at gamemode.js:4322, with a harness case for each old key, deployed with the dev gamemode. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's design decision on the five trades the rulebook has no place for (bard, merchant, priest, scholar, thief).

## Done when

The rulebook is written down somewhere a person can read it, in lore\ or on the site, the five trades with no home in it have a decided fate, and gatherer and tailor exist. Nothing below this entry can be built until that is true.

## Traps

Do not start building the K menu or removing kits from the old flat list until the mapping is decided. Sixteen trades go in and thirteen come out, five of them have nowhere to go, and characters already exist carrying them.

issues.title: What the new collection revision should carry: revision 5 carries the order, the current plugin, the ini defaults and the client runtime, and this is what is left
issues.body:
**Order:** 82 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free · **Old number:** 46

## Where it lives

Nexus collection ombo2a revision 5 · Thornswood Content 1.1 (Nexus 192001, file 809365) · Thornswood Client Runtime (Nexus 192762, file 809366) · collection.json in the Vortex store · measured 22 September against revisions 2, 4 and 5

## What is known

ASKED FOR BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER: while the revision is being cut anyway, what else should go in, what settings make setup easier, is our own mod current, and what would free space. Audited against the revision 2 manifest actually installed here. ONE. THE COLLECTION PINS NO LOAD ORDER AT ALL, and this is the biggest thing on the list for a new person. collection.json has pluginRules.plugins = 0 and pluginRules.groups = 0, with 22 modRules and nothing else. So a fresh install lands on whatever LOOT produces. The server compares BY POSITION, so LOOT being sensible is not the same as LOOT being right, and the person is refused at the door having done everything asked of them. Vortex supports publishing the order with the collection and it costs minutes. This is the existing entry about the collection carrying no plugin order, and it should be done in this revision or the revision is half a fix. TWO. OUR OWN MOD IS STALE IN THE COLLECTION AND THE TWO COPIES ARE DIFFERENT FILES. The Vortex store holds Thornswood Content 1.0 at 158,754 bytes dated 15 September. The repo and the game folder both hold 141,234 bytes dated 21 September, and those two match each other by sha256. So the plugin the server was built against is not the plugin the collection hands out. Our own plugin, at index 22 in the server list, and the copies disagree by seventeen kilobytes. That needs uploading as part of the revision. THREE. THE FIVE BROKEN MODS, each already documented as broken in known.md: TavernGames.esp with its two BSAs, Respawn - Death Overhaul.esp, SunHelmSurvival.esp, SunHelmDiseases.esp and Embers XD - Patch - SunHelm Survival.esp. And a decision on Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation.esp, which is Immersive Armors 8.1 standard, the script version our own documentation calls broken, where a script free version exists. FOUR. THE SETTINGS THE LAUNCHER HAS TO REPAIR AFTER EVERY INSTALL could ship correct instead. Enforce.cs rewrites SkyrimSoulsRE.ini (bFavoritesMenu true, bTweenMenu false) and OpenAnimationReplacer.ini (bShowWelcomeBanner false, bEnableAnimationQueueProgressBar false) on this machine. Those are collection defaults being corrected by a launcher, which is the wrong end. Shipping them right in the revision means one less thing that can go wrong on a machine the launcher has not reached yet, and Enforce stays as the belt. collectionConfig already has recommendNewProfile true, which is correct and should stay. FIVE. SPACE, AND PATRICK'S OWN IDEA: put what ships in the installer into the collection instead. MEASURED: the installer zip is 511.1 MB. Data\Platform\Distribution alone is 364.5 MB across 70 files, which is the SkyMP client runtime, and it changes only when the fork is rebuilt. Moving that into the collection would take the installer to roughly 150 MB and hand the download to Vortex, which already does resume and mirrors. Data\Platform\UI is another 31.1 MB. WHAT MUST NOT MOVE: anything that changes every release. The five game plugins are 1.6 MB and change constantly; a collection revision per release is absurd and would make every release a Nexus upload. THE CATCH, and it is not small: Sync-Client.ps1 and Ship both refuse a release whose client is not the recorded build, so if Vortex provides those files the check has to compare against what Vortex deployed rather than what the build tree holds. And the client is modified GPLv3, so putting it on Nexus wants the source offer sorted, which the public fork now makes possible. Worth doing, not worth doing carelessly. SIX. SMALL ONES. collection.json has tools = 0, so the collection points at no tools; it could name the launcher. installInstructions exists and should be re-read while the revision is open, since it is the first thing a new person is shown. MEASURED PROPERLY ON 22 SEPTEMBER, and point FIVE above was written off a guess. This is what the machine says, and the shape of the answer is different. THE ARCHITECTURE, DECIDED BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER: the collection is the baseline and an update pack is only the delta since the last revision. Whatever has gone stable is folded into the collection when a revision is cut, comes out of the installer and out of the packs, and anything added afterwards lives in the packs until the next revision folds it back in as well. THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND NEEDS NO CODE AT ALL. Package-Thornswood.ps1 and Publish-Update.ps1 both leave out every file the collection provides, read from the launcher's own record at Profile\OwnGame\files.txt through Get-ShipOwnGameCollection in Ship-Rules.ps1. Package-Thornswood says so in a comment: the installer shrinks as the collection fills in and can never drop a file nobody can get back. So a file moved into the collection falls out of the installer and out of the packs by itself the next time either is built. Nothing to write, only a revision to publish. WHAT THE UPDATE PACKS ACTUALLY CARRY: ten packs, NINE DISTINCT PATHS, ever. profile\plugins.txt and profile\loadorder.txt in all ten; thornswood-front.js in seven; MpClientPlugin.dll in four; skymp5-client.js, thornswood-select.js, thornswood-skills.js and SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll in two each. Nothing else has ever gone out in a pack. The delta model is therefore already almost true and nobody had measured it. WHAT THE INSTALLER ACTUALLY CARRIES: 871 files, 945.3 MB out of the game folder, once Bethesda's files, the other launchers' folders and everything Vortex provides are taken off. Three things, and nothing else is worth a sentence. Data\Platform 245 files 392.6 MB. Data\textures 97 files 368.9 MB. Data\meshes 468 files 178.5 MB. Everything else together is 5.2 MB. The collection provides 29,444 files and 11.4 GB, and NOT ONE of them is under Data\Platform, Data\textures or Data\meshes. THE CLIENT RUNTIME SPLITS 68 TO 2, and it can move. Data\Platform\Distribution is 70 files and 364.7 MB. Two of them are recorded in tools\client-build.json: SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll at 14.9 MB and SkyrimPlatformCEF.exe.hidden at 0.4 MB. The other 68, 349.2 MB, are unmodified upstream CEF and Node redistributables: libcef.dll 183.0 MB, libnode.dll 104.0 MB, icudtl.dat 10.0 MB, resources.pak 7.2 MB, libGLESv2.dll 7.1 MB, d3dcompiler_47.dll 4.7 MB and fifty odd smaller ones. They are not in client-build.json, so moving them does not touch what Sync-Client.ps1 and Ship check, and they have never shipped in a pack. THE TRAP: the two recorded files must NOT go in the Nexus mod, or Vortex would deploy its own copies and Sync-Client would spend every run putting ours back over them. THE 547 MB NOBODY KNEW WAS THERE, and this is the bigger finding. Data\textures and Data\meshes hold 565 files and 547.4 MB that VORTEX HAS NEVER HEARD OF. They are loose files sitting in the Steam copy's Data folder, put there by hand outside Vortex, and the installer redistributes every one of them today. The folders and their sizes: textures\LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary 30 files 155.0 MB, textures\weapons 30 files 81.2 MB, textures\LostArk 26 files 64.7 MB, textures\leifcrops 9 files 57.3 MB, meshes\armor 194 files 54.6 MB, meshes\LostArk 19 files 43.3 MB, meshes\MCE 18 files 29.8 MB, meshes\actors 128 files 17.8 MB, meshes\LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary 25 files 11.7 MB, textures\interface 1 file 8.0 MB, meshes\0CCE 9 files 3.2 MB, meshes\clothes 28 files 2.9 MB. Vortex has 154 mod folders and not one of them matches any of those names. There is also Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa, 2.8 MB at the Data root, with no plugin in the list that loads it. NONE of this can go into a collection until somebody says where each folder came from. Whatever turns out to be somebody else's is the same problem as the entry about the installer redistributing forty named mods, except worse, because these are not even in the mod list to be named. Whatever turns out to be ours belongs in the Thornswood Content mod on Nexus, which is in the collection, and then it leaves the installer by itself like everything else. MUSIC AND VIDEO STAY IN THE INSTALLER, decided by Patrick on 22 September. thornswood-theme.mp3 and thornswood-menu.mp4 are ours and change when he changes them. WHERE THIS LANDS: the installer is 511 MB today. Moving the client runtime alone takes it to about 160 MB. Sorting the loose assets out as well takes it to about 45 MB. ONE LAUNCHER CHANGE WORTH DOING SEPARATELY, not part of the revision: OwnGame.MustCopy copies everything under Data\Platform\ rather than hard linking it, because another launcher rewrites files in place there. The CEF and Node redistributables are not rewritten by anything, so 349 MB is a second copy on the disk for no reason. Narrowing that rule to the folders that are actually rewritten gives the disk back. It is a Keep and OwnGame change, so it is its own commit and its own entry, not something to slip into a Vortex sitting. DONE IN REVISION 5, 22 SEPTEMBER, point by point. ONE, THE ORDER: 51 plugin rules chaining the 52 full plugins from Water for ENB.esm to Playable Rieklings.esp, written as LOOT after rules so Vortex publishes them with the collection. Light plugins are left to LOOT because the server only counts full plugins by position. TWO, OUR MOD: Thornswood Content 1.1 carries Thornswood-Content.esp at 141,234 bytes, sha256 3b3ecb3b, the same file as the repo and the game folder, and Vortex's copy now matches both. The 1.0 file is still up on the mod page, so revisions 2 to 4 still install. THREE, THE BROKEN MODS: Tavern Games, Respawn - Death Overhaul, SunHelm Survival with SunHelmDiseases.esp, and the Embers XD SunHelm patch (a FOMOD option) are out. Immersive Armors is now the script free and Skypatched version (Nexus 168741) over the original's assets, which adds AZ_IADistribution.esp, light flagged, and makes Hothtrooper44_Armor_Ecksstra.esp light. Patrick also added Playable Rieklings (5513) with RaceCompatibility (2853); RaceCompatibility.esm carries the master flag, which is why the release in entry 46 needs -NewOrder and a wipe. The script free plugin has 845 fewer tempering recipes, so the recipe table is rebuilt in that release. FOUR, THE INI DEFAULTS: Thornswood Content 1.1 also carries SKSE\Plugins\SkyrimSoulsRE.ini (bFavoritesMenu true, bTweenMenu false) and OpenAnimationReplacer.ini (bShowWelcomeBanner false, bEnableAnimationQueueProgressBar false), so a fresh install starts right and Enforce stays as the belt. FIVE, THE CLIENT RUNTIME: the 68 files are their own Nexus mod, Thornswood Client Runtime, with a README and the licence texts for CEF, Chromium, ANGLE, ICU, Node and SkyrimPlatform, and it is in revision 5. SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll and SkyrimPlatformCEF.exe.hidden are not in it, so Sync-Client and Ship check what they always checked. SIX: installInstructions were rewritten for revision 5 and say the collection carries the order. tools is still 0.
CORRECTIONS TO WHAT THIS ENTRY SAID. (a) Not all 68 runtime files are CEF and Node. d3dcompiler_47.dll is Microsoft's Direct3D shader compiler, which Chromium ships beside itself, and ___systemPolyfill.js is SkyrimPlatform's own script under GPLv3. The README on Nexus names both. (b) The collection does provide textures and meshes: files.txt has 2,594 files and 4,387 MB under Data\textures and 5,240 files and 1,382 MB under Data\meshes from Vortex. What was true is that nothing under Data\Platform came from Vortex, and that the 565 loose files the installer ships are the ones Vortex does not provide. (c) About 160 MB after the runtime moves was 511 MB zipped minus 349 MB unzipped. The runtime zips to about 150 MB, so expect roughly 350 MB after the runtime alone, and small only once the loose files are gone as well. (d) The copies of our plugin: the Vortex store held 158,754 bytes (sha256 71cedd37), the repo and the game folder 141,234 bytes (3b3ecb3b). Since revision 5 every copy on this machine is 3b3ecb3b.
THE 547 MB, TRACED FOLDER BY FOLDER. The full list is in entry 142, because it is an installer question. In short, none of it is a Nexus mod the collection could carry, and none of it belongs in Thornswood Content except our own 8 MB of backdrop: two other servers' drops (Lost Ark armour ports, the rpcustom and saarthal weapons, leifcrops), BodySlide builds for mods no longer installed, Nemesis and FNIS output, and Bethesda's MarketplaceTextures.bsa, which belongs on the vanilla list.
LEFT HERE, after the release in entry 46: (1) tools is still 0, so the collection names no tools. (2) OwnGame.MustCopy still copies all of Data\Platform, so the 349 MB runtime is on the disk twice; narrow it to the folders that are rewritten in place, as its own Keep and OwnGame change. (3) Archive the 1.0 file of Thornswood Content on Nexus once nobody is on revision 4. (4) The loose files and MarketplaceTextures.bsa, entry 142. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Measured on this machine. Installed collection: collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z\collection.json reads plugins 51, groups 0, modRules 17, tools 0, mods 103. Among the mods are Thornswood Content 1.1.0, Thornswood Client Runtime 1.0.0 and Start On Save 2.8.0. C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\files.txt (22 Sep 17:00) records the 68 Data\Platform\Distribution files as origin V and kind C: they come from Vortex now and are still copied, 349.2 MB. 566 loose files under Data\textures and Data\meshes, 547.4 MB, are still origin O. Under Distribution it now carries only SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll and SkyrimPlatformCEF.exe.hidden (15.4 MB), so moving the runtime out worked. It still carries 700 textures and meshes entries, 551.1 MB, which is entry 142. Code: OwnGame.cs:775-783 MustCopy returns true for anything under Data\Platform\. The CopyTypes list at OwnGame.cs:752-756 also contains .dll and .exe. Narrowing the folder prefix alone would therefore still copy libcef.dll (183 MB) and libnode.dll (104 MB). OwnGame.cs:172 has Rules = 3. NEXT STEP: The launcher half can be prepared now and must not merge until #dev agrees to it. In tools\app\OwnGame.cs, MustCopy gets an exception: a file under Data\Platform\Distribution whose origin is Vortex (deployed.Contains(rel)) and that is not one of the files recorded in tools\client-build.json is hard linked, even though it is a .dll or .exe. MustCopy only takes rel today, so the deployed set and the recorded names have to be passed in or held in a static. Everything else under Data\Platform keeps being copied. Bump Rules to 4, with a line in the history comment, so every folder made under 3 refreshes once. Prove it with a compile, plus a small harness that runs MustCopy over files.txt: the 68 should come out linked, the 2 recorded files copied, and nothing else under Data\Platform should change. The other three items left are not code: tools = 0 in the collection, archiving Thornswood Content 1.0 on Nexus, and the loose files (entry 142). WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: (1) A line in #dev and agreement between Patrick and Djinn before the MustCopy change, because it narrows the settled rule that the client folders are copied. (2) Patrick in Vortex/Nexus: set the collection's tools (it is still 0) in the next revision, and archive the Thornswood Content 1.0 file once nobody is on revision 4. The 'plugin-nexus' deploy tag here means these collection and mod-page actions, not an esp upload. (3) The 547 MB of loose files is entry 142 and waits on him saying where each folder came from.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Enforce.cs:130-150`: the ini settings the launcher repairs after every install; these are the collection defaults that could ship correct
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:30-60`: each of the five mods and why it is broken here, in the words already written for customers
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1`: what belongs in a release rather than in the collection, before moving anything between them

## Commands

- Read only. What the installed collection pins. Read 0, 0, 22, 0 on revision 2 and 51, 0, 17, 0 on revision 5. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $j = Get-Content "$env:APPDATA\Vortex\skyrimse\mods\collection_ombo2a_*\collection.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json; "plugins {0}  groups {1}  modRules {2}  tools {3}" -f @($j.pluginRules.plugins).Count, @($j.pluginRules.groups).Count, @($j.modRules).Count, @($j.tools).Count
  ```

  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Vortex\skyrimse\mods" -Directory | Where-Object Name -match "Thornswood Content" | ForEach-Object { Get-ChildItem $_.FullName -Recurse -Filter *.esp } | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime
  ```
- Read only. Splits the game folder by where each file came from. V is the collection, O is everything else. Read 29,444 files 11.4 GB from Vortex and 1,045 files not, on 22 September, before Maintenance had seen revision 5. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $rows = Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\files.txt' | ForEach-Object { $f=$_ -split '\|',5; if($f.Count -eq 5){[pscustomobject]@{Src=$f[1];Len=[long]$f[2];Rel=$f[4]}} }; $rows | Group-Object Src | ForEach-Object { '{0}  {1,6} files  {2,9:n1} MB' -f $_.Name, $_.Count, (($_.Group | Measure-Object Len -Sum).Sum/1MB) }
  ```
- Read only. The six recorded client files. These are the ones that must never come from Vortex. The list is an OBJECT keyed by path, not an array, which is the shape to expect. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $rec = @((Get-Content .\tools\client-build.json -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).files.PSObject.Properties.Name); $rec
  ```
- Read only. The big stable files that can move into the collection. libcef.dll and libnode.dll are 287 MB of the 349 MB on their own. (claude)

  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Distribution' -Recurse -File | Sort-Object Length -Descending | Select-Object -First 8 Name, @{n='MB';e={'{0:n1}' -f ($_.Length/1MB)}}
  ```

## Done when

Revision 5 did the first half: the order, the current plugin, none of the five broken mods, the ini defaults and the 68 runtime files. Done when the four things under LEFT are done and the next installer is built without the runtime and without the loose files.

## Traps

Cut it from revision 4, never from the 2 installed here, or the new revision silently reverts what 3 and 4 added. The plugin order and the mod removals must go in the SAME revision: publishing an order that still names removed mods is worse than publishing none. Moving the client runtime into the collection changes what Sync-Client and Ship check against, so it is its own change and not a thing to slip into this revision quietly. AND THE TWO FROM THE 22 SEPTEMBER MEASUREMENT. SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll and SkyrimPlatformCEF.exe.hidden are in tools\client-build.json and must stay out of any Nexus upload, or Vortex deploys its own copies and Sync-Client fights it on every run. And the 547 MB under Data\textures and Data\meshes is not in Vortex at all, so it cannot simply be added to the collection: each folder has to be traced to a mod first, and some of it may not be redistributable at all. FROM 22 SEPTEMBER: publishing revision 5 did not by itself shrink anything. The installer only drops what files.txt marks as from Vortex, and files.txt only changes when Maintenance runs, which the release in entry 46 has to unblock first.

The Azure CLI is installed. tools/Sign-Artifact.ps1 already covers enabled:false, a placeholder profile and -Required. Nothing in the repo is missing. What is unfinished is on the Azure side, and Patrick said so himself: 'the code signing stuff isnt finnished thats why its switched off'. NEXT STEP: No repo change.
