issues.title: Start On Save can come out now that nothing depends on it
issues.body:
**Order:** 91 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Data\SKSE\Plugins\po3_StartOnSave.dll and .ini · tools\app\Chars.cs WriteStartIni · tools\app\Checks.cs StartOnSaveInstalled · tools\Add-Characters.ps1 · tools\Run-Everything.ps1 · Nexus collection ombo2a, Start On Save 2.8.0 (Nexus 50054) since revision 3

## What is known

ASKED BY PATRICK ON 22 SEPTEMBER: if we no longer use it, get rid of it. Checked before deleting, and at that moment we did still use it, so it was left alone and this is what is left. WHAT IT DOES TODAY: nothing wanted. The launcher rewrites po3_StartOnSave.ini on every single Play to tell the mod to load nothing, and getting that right took real work. bStartNewGame false is not enough: with sSaveFile blank the mod loads the newest save in the folder whenever there is one. The trick is sCharacterName = Thornswood-Nobody, a name no save carries, so nothing ever qualifies. That was fixing thirty second crashes on every launch, with po3_StartOnSave.dll in the frame. ITS ONLY REMAINING VALUE IS ONE BOOLEAN, bDisableMissingContentWarning. Everything else about it is a hazard held off by an ini written after reading somebody else's Hooks.cpp, which is a thing that can change under us without warning. WHAT BLOCKED REMOVAL IS NOW GONE. Shell.CollectionProblem used StartOnSaveInstalled as the staleness probe for the whole collection, so removing the file made every install read as stale. That probe is a revision number now (pull request 96), so nothing decides anything from this file any more. WHAT REMOVING IT TOUCHES: the mod in Vortex, Checks.StartOnSaveInstalled and its readiness row, Chars.WriteStartIni and the ini path, Add-Characters.ps1, Run-Everything.ps1, and two documentation pages that name it. And a decision about bDisableMissingContentWarning, which goes with it. One complete release. CORRECTED 22 SEPTEMBER. The trap below said Start On Save is not in the collection and that removing it is not a Vortex change. It is in the collection: revision 3 added it, and revision 5 still carries Start On Save 2.8.0 (Nexus 50054). Entry 48's line that it never was is true of revision 2 only. So taking it out is both the launcher and script changes listed above and a collection revision that drops the mod. It was left in revision 5 as it was, because the decision about bDisableMissingContentWarning is still open and this entry's own trap says not to pull the file alone. It carries no plugin, so dropping it from the collection moves nothing in the load order and needs no wipe. Add-Characters.ps1 installing it by hand is now a second copy of what the collection provides. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Every reference the entry lists is still there. Checks.cs:23 StartOnSaveInstalled, with the 'Auto load' readiness row at Checks.cs:660-663, which still says 'walks past the main menu', no longer true. Chars.cs:68 is the ini path, and WriteStartIni at Chars.cs:~895-925 writes sCharacterName = Thornswood-Nobody and bDisableMissingContentWarning = true. Add-Characters.ps1 installs the mod by hand (lines 51-100). Run-Everything.ps1:43 wants SKSE\Plugins\po3_StartOnSave.dll. help.md:120 and known.md:49 name it. The installed revision 5 collection.json still lists Start On Save 2.8.0. files.txt has po3_StartOnSave.dll and .ini as C|V, meaning Vortex deploys them into the game folder. Nothing still uses the mod as a staleness probe: test-collection-revision.js:135 checks that. One finding bears on the open decision. In the fork, remoteServer.ts:782-785 builds loadOrder from Game.getModCount/getModName, the running game's own full plugin list, and passes it to sp.loadGame (loadGameService.ts:20). So the save SkyMP loads never names a plugin the game lacks, and the missing-content warning that the one remaining boolean suppresses has nothing to fire on in SkyMP's own load. That comes from reading the code. Nobody has observed it in the game. NEXT STEP: Stage it so the thirty-second crash cannot come back. Launcher first, on a branch. Remove the 'Auto load' readiness row and StartOnSaveInstalled from Checks.cs. Keep Chars.WriteStartIni, but run it only when Data\SKSE\Plugins\po3_StartOnSave.dll is in the game folder, so a machine still on revision 5 keeps the load-nothing ini. Drop the Character slots step from Run-Everything.ps1 and retire Add-Characters.ps1. Update help.md:120 and known.md:49, and the comments in thornswood-front.js:535/1190/1215. Prove it with a compile and a PowerShell parse check. Then Patrick cuts a collection revision without Start On Save; it carries no plugin, so no load order change and no wipe. Once nobody is on revision 5, delete WriteStartIni and StartIni. Readiness is checked in Checks.cs, one of the six shared files: it needs a line in #dev, which Patrick waives when he is the one asking. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: (1) Patrick decides what happens to bDisableMissingContentWarning. The fork reading above argues it earns nothing on SkyMP's load path, but that needs his decision and ideally one playtest start without it. (2) Patrick cuts a Nexus collection revision without Start On Save 2.8.0. The 'plugin-nexus' tag here means that collection revision, not an esp. (3) A line in #dev for Checks.cs unless Patrick is the one asking.

## Done when

No po3_StartOnSave file in a build, nothing in the launcher names it, the readiness row is gone rather than red, and a fresh install shows no card about it, and the collection no longer carries it.

## Traps

Do not remove the file alone: the readiness row goes red on every launcher and Add-Characters.ps1 puts it straight back into the next build. Decide what happens to bDisableMissingContentWarning first, because that is the one thing the mod still earns. It IS in the collection, since revision 3, so removing it also takes a collection revision. It carries no plugin, so that revision moves nothing in the load order.

issues.title: A gatherer gathers herbs, not dinner, and a farmer has no way to get milk
issues.body:
**Order:** 116 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools\Build-HarvestTable.ps1: the produce type decides whose a plant is · tools\gamemode.js: the branch order and the living-actor fall through · dev only

## What is known

PATRICK, 21 September: 'The farmer grows the crops? Those crops should be used to make food, why is a gatherer giving them all the food ingredients when they gather herbs and things.' Then: 'give milk and butter to farmers and make mammoth cheese bowls able to be picked up by literally anybody.' HE IS RIGHT AND THE SPLIT IS IN THE RECORDS. Of the 131 rows in the gatherer's plant table, 106 produce an INGR, which is an alchemy reagent, and those are herbs and are his. 24 produce an ALCH, which is food, and not one of them should be the gatherer's. Thirteen are grown crops and belong to the farmer: the apples, carrot, tomato, ash yam, leek, potato, cabbage and gourd. Seven are hanging game and belong to the hunter: pheasant, rabbit and the skewered skeever. Two are props, the butter churn and the mammoth cheese bowl. Two are Soul Husk, a real plant you pick in the Soul Cairn. WHY THE CROP PASS MISSED THEM: it took TREE records whose produce is food, and every one of these is a FLOR variant of the same plant. A cabbage is a cabbage whichever record type Bethesda used. WHAT IT COST: the gatherer supplies the Cook 165 inputs, among them Butter 46, Leek 12, Potato 8, Cabbage 6, Carrot 6, Gourd 4, Tomato 4, Ash Yam 4 and both apples. The farmer supplies the Cook nothing at all. THE BUTTER CHURN IS THE FARMER'S and that is easy, because BYOHButterChurn is a FLOR somebody presses E on, so there is a verb to gate. THE MAMMOTH CHEESE BOWL GOES TO NOBODY, which needs no code: a base in none of the tables falls through to the engine, which hands the produce to whoever pressed it. MILK IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS SOMETHING BUILT. BYOHFoodMilk exists in HearthFires and Gourmet reprices it, and ten cooking recipes across both Cook halves want it. Nothing in the world hands it out. A cow is in the hunter's table as a CARCASS giving Cow Hide and Raw Beef at novice, which is a dead cow. THE ANSWER THAT NEEDS NO NEW RECORD: loot() already reads isDead and falls through for a living actor, so a farmer pressing E on a LIVING cow can be given milk on a cooldown, and the machinery for telling a living cow from a dead one is already written and already tested. That is a farmer milking a cow, which is what the word means. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Step 1 is DONE on main in 077268f. tools/harvests.json now holds 109 plant rows, and every one produces an INGR except the two Soul Husk rows (named in FOOD_STAYS_THE_GATHERERS, Build-HarvestTable.ps1:582) and Canticle Bark. crops has 15 rows including the apples, carrot, tomato, ash yam, leek, potato, cabbage and gourd. game has the 7 hanging-game rows. MammothCheese01 and BYOHButterChurn are in the unranked list as FOOD_PROP_BY_EDITOR_ID (Build-HarvestTable.ps1:563). The comment there says the churn becoming a farm station is still for #dev, but Patrick's own words in the entry ('give milk and butter to farmers') already settle it. Steps 2 and 3 are NOT built. There is no churn or milk code in gamemode.js (grep for Churn, BYOHFoodMilk and milk finds only recipe rows). A churn press matches no branch in onActivate (gamemode.js:6771-6990), so the engine hands Butter to anybody who presses it. recipes.json shows 46 rows wanting Butter with suppliedBy null for all of them, and 10 wanting Jug of Milk with no producer. loot() does fall through for a living actor at gamemode.js:6649 (`if (!dead) return null;`). But the fork's activationService.ts only sends an activation when Skyrim's own activate event fires, and nobody has measured whether pressing E on a living cow fires one: vanilla cows show no activation prompt as far as is known. Cow and goat rows in hunts.json are all dead-body rows (Cow Hide + Raw Beef, Goat Hide + Goat Meat, novice). NEXT STEP: Churn (can be done now): in tools/gamemode.js add isChurn and churn(actorId, refrId, baseDesc), following game() (gamemode.js ~5975): classGate(actorId,'farm'), a cooldown with stampCooldown, addItem of BYOHFoodMilk's sibling Butter (353c:HearthFires.esm), creditWork(actorId,'farm'). Put the branch before isPlant at :6953 and return false so the engine's free handover stops. Add @{ Fn = 'churn'; Who = 'farmer' ... } to STATION_VERBS in tools/Build-RecipeTable.ps1:816 so Butter gets a producer. Rewrite the FOOD_PROP comment in tools/Build-HarvestTable.ps1:544-563 so the churn is the farmer's and only the mammoth cheese goes to nobody. Rebuild recipes.json and the RECIPES_BY_ID block, run Check-Balance.ps1 -NoPause, and add a harness (tools/test-churn.js) covering: a farmer gets butter, a non-farmer is refused, the cooldown holds. Milk: add a branch beside loot() for a living cow base (a small set out of hunts.json) that gives Jug of Milk (3534:HearthFires.esm) to a farmer on a cooldown and returns null for everybody else, so the fall-through is kept. Add a log line so a dev press proves whether the activation reaches the server at all. If it does not, the answer changes, for example /milk near a cow, and that is a new decision. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick: step 4, whether a goat gives milk too and whether milking has a rank. Somebody on dev: press E on a living cow with the new log line in place, and report whether the server sees the press at all. The milk half cannot be finished until that is known. 24 SEPTEMBER: THE CHURN IS BUILT on patrick/todo-94-churn (c54b275) and not merged. A farmer at a HearthFires butter churn (BYOHButterChurn bc0:HearthFires.esm) gets one Butter on the plants' ten minute wait, everybody else is refused, and the churn is put back after every answer; Build-RecipeTable.ps1 names churn() so the next recipes.json build puts all 46 Butter inputs on a farmer. test-churn.js 56 pass. MILK IS NOT BUILT, which is why its review is not clean. One press on dev decides whether it can be: stand at a living cow outdoors, press E, open the console with ~ and look for 'Sent activation for caster='. If it shows, milk is built beside loot(); if not, milk needs another way in. Patrick also decides whether a goat gives milk and whether milking has a rank. recipes.json still needs rebuilding on a machine whose Game\Data has the current Thornswood-Content.esp. 25 SEPTEMBER: patrick/todo-94-churn (c54b275, with a6866be) existed only on Patrick's disk. Pushed to GitHub, not merged, so the churn survives the worktree cleanup. No pull request yet.

## Steps

- [ ] A plant whose produce is a reagent is the gatherer's and a plant whose produce is food is not. The crops go to the farmer, the hanging game to the hunter, the mammoth cheese to nobody. (claude)
- [ ] The butter churn becomes the farmer's, because it is a record with a verb behind it. (claude)
- [ ] A farmer pressing E on a living cow gets milk. loot() already tells a living actor from a dead one and falls through, so the branch goes beside it. (claude)
- [ ] Say whether a goat should give milk too, and whether milking should have a rank. (patrick)

## Done when

On dev: a gatherer pressing a cabbage is refused, a farmer picking one is not, a hunter gets the hanging pheasant, anybody at all can take the mammoth cheese, and a farmer can milk a living cow while a dead one still gives a hunter hide and beef.

## Traps

A living cow must still be nothing to everybody else. The hunter branch falls through for a living actor today and that fall through is what keeps every other press in the game working, so the farmer branch has to be as careful with it.

issues.title: Property offices, rent, the drop box and the boards: built and on dev, waiting on a test
issues.body:
**Order:** 118 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** test it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js: roleFromDoor is the office machinery, the farm claim block is the shape a property claim takes · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js: isLocked, lockChanged and the lock call · a new table pass for door to key · the site's Records section for the office log

## What is known

DESIGNED WITH PATRICK ON 21 SEPTEMBER, IN CONVERSATION, AND NOT YET BUILT. Every line below is either a decision he made or a limit measured in the engine, and the measured ones are marked so nobody spends a day arguing with them. THE OFFICES. A JARL is an office held by a character. An admin gives an account the Jarl role, out of character, as world setup, and that is the ONLY out of character grant in the whole chain: nothing in the world can create the first office, so somebody has to place it. After that admins never grant anything again. A JARL gives the Steward role. A STEWARD grants and revokes city property, sets and waives rent, and can see which of the city's houses have somebody living in them who is not paying. A steward is NOT an admin and carries no admin powers: Patrick, 21 September, 'admins only overlook the RP and not get involved on their admin characters'. The machinery already exists: roleFromDoor(name, profileId) in tools\gamemode.js takes any role name, the site reads Discord roles and hands them over, and Admin, Dev and Allowed already go through it. Jarl and Steward are a role in Discord and a name in that function. THE ONE THING STILL OPEN ABOUT THE OFFICES: a Discord role sits on the ACCOUNT, so it follows somebody onto every character they play, which is the exact thing Patrick objected to for admins. Two ways out. Leave it on the account and rely on discipline, which costs nothing. Or the role grants eligibility and one named character on that account holds the office, which is one field beside class and profession and means somebody can hold an office and still have an ordinary second character with no authority. The second was recommended and not yet chosen. An office also needs a lapse, or a jarl who stops logging in stalls every property in the hold. PROPERTY. A claim on a door and, where there is one, the ground around it. A HOUSE AND ITS FARM ARE ONE PROPERTY: claim either and you hold both, release either and you release both, which also settles somebody claiming the field behind your house. CLAIMED BY STANDING AT THE DOOR WITH IT OPEN, and that is not a compromise, it falls out of a measured limit: a locked door is never announced to the server at all, so every door press the server can answer is one that was already open to you. You bought it, you were let in, or you picked the lock, and the server cannot tell those apart and does not need to. IT LAPSES if you never open the door, thirty days for a home against fourteen for a farm, because a farm left unworked is going to seed and a house left shut is just a house; rented property should be shorter because missing rent is a decision rather than an absence. It is also released deliberately. TRANSFERRED BY AN ACT AT THE DOOR between two people both present, never by an item, so nobody loses a house to a pickpocket. RENTED FROM THE CITY is the same claim with a due date and a payer; the server owns everybody's pack so it can take the rent, and missing enough of them lapses it. SQUATTING falls out for free: the server knows a property is the city's and knows who is standing in it, so it flags the state and does nothing, and a steward deals with it as a person. The server never evicts on anybody's behalf except by the lapse. BELONGINGS ARE NEVER TOUCHED: the next holder inherits whatever is in the containers, because the alternative is a server that deletes people's possessions on a timer. SHARING is an owner and residents: residents use the house and lock it, only the owner adds or removes a name, or one bad housemate gives your house away while you are out. KEYS ARE REAL ITEMS AND THAT IS MEASURED. Skyrim has 334 KEYM records and 108 of them name a specific house, farm or manor, so Bethesda already made a key per property. Giving one away, pickpocketing one, looting one out of a chest and losing one all work for free because they are ordinary items. Keys are cut by a smith from a mold. A KEY IS FOREVER: nothing in the engine can change which key a door wants, so eviction ends your CLAIM and does not take back a key you already hold. An evicted tenant who kept their key can still walk in at night and the city's only answer is to deal with them like a person, which is the squatter roleplay Patrick asked for, running itself out of the constraint. NO KEY CONFERS OWNERSHIP: a master key that made you the owner would mean looting the right key out of a chest takes a house, which is worse while somebody is asleep than the mold problem it was meant to solve. THE MOLD IS NOT AN ITEM, and this is measured rather than chosen: there is no mold, blank or template record anywhere in the load order, and an inventory entry carries a base id and a count with nowhere to write which door it belongs to. So the mold is something the server remembers about a person: you have molded this door, and a smith can cut you keys for it. TO MOLD A DOOR YOU MUST BE AT IT AND EITHER OWN IT OR HOLD A KEY TO IT. That is the rule that protects somebody while they are offline, and it needs no online check at all, which is better than the rule Patrick first described because it does not break when he is asleep. A locksmith copying a key somebody hands them is realistic; a thief who steals your key can have it copied, which is the interesting story rather than a hole; what nobody can do is conjure a mold from a door they have never had access to. LOCKS. A DOOR IS LOCKED ONLY IF SOMEBODY LOCKED IT. The server owns whether a door is locked and the plugin applies it locally: lock(abLock, abAsOwner) is confirmed present in the platform's generated API at skyrimPlatform.ts:1854, and tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js already reads isLocked and handles the lockChanged event and hands a reference back to the server when a lock opens. Once applied it is a real Skyrim lock, so a key opens it, a lockpick picks it and the mini game appears. THE SERVER NEVER REFUSES A DOOR, which is what keeps lockpicking working, and Patrick asked for that by name. THE FOUR MEASURED LIMITS, so nobody re-derives them. The server cannot see a locked door at all: our own client patch in activationService.ts does not announce a locked reference on purpose, so the lockpicking mini game works. The server does not know which key opens which door: libespm parses XOWN and does not parse XLOC, so a door to key table needs a NEW pass over placed references rather than base records, and that is the one real piece of work this design still needs before any of it can be built. No mold record exists. Locks cannot be changed. STILL OPEN AND WORTH ASKING: whether the office is an account role or a named character, the exact lapse lengths, whether somebody may hold more than one property, and whether the deed should be stealable after all despite the warning above. SETTLED WITH PATRICK, 21 SEPTEMBER, AND THIS REPLACES EVERY OPEN QUESTION ABOVE. THE OFFICES ARE CHARACTER SPECIFIC, NOT ACCOUNT WIDE. The Discord role makes an account eligible and one named character on it holds the office, stored beside class and profession, so somebody can be a jarl on one character and an ordinary farmer with no authority on another. The office shows on the K panel so people know who to ask. An admin places the first jarl, once, out of character, because nothing in the world can create the first office; after that admins never grant anything and only watch. A jarl grants stewardship and assigns the City Court, which sits UNDER the jarl. Roles are per hold and named that way, so 'Whiterun City Court' is a role, there is no role per position, and people inventing their own titles for roleplay is encouraged because the server matches the names it knows and ignores the rest. EVERY BUILDING IN THE GAME IS CLAIMABLE. Shops, temples, halls, palaces, all of it, so people can lock doors and own shops. CLAIMING COSTS NOTHING, and that holds even for a building the city owns but is not renting out: somebody can claim it for zero gold and it becomes the city's problem to solve, which is the point. YOU MAY HOLD MORE THAN ONE and disputes are the court's problem. A HOME AND ITS FARM ARE ONE CLAIM. THE LAPSE IS TWO WEEKS, one number for everything: home, farm and rented. CLAIMING HANDS YOU THE DEED THERE AND THEN, which is why it has to happen at the door. A STOLEN KEY GETS YOU IN. A STOLEN DEED GIVES OWNERSHIP. So handing somebody a key is safe and stealing a title is a deliberate burglary of a specific object, and there is nowhere safe to keep one: in your pocket a pickpocket takes it, in your house a burglar does. AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES 'EVERY BUILDING' AFFORDABLE: Inventory::ExtraData in the fork carries an optional name per entry, so ONE deed record covers every property in the game. A single Deed book becomes 'Deed to Breezehome' or 'Deed to the Farmhouse at Rorikstead' per instance, it reads that way in the pack, it is stolen as that, and the server reads the name to know which property. One record rather than a thousand. The server keeps its own record of every deed it issued, so a deed somebody renamed by hand is not a deed. THE BOARDS go outside each keep, one place per hold, our own records at our own locations and not the Keizaal board. Placeholder coordinates first, moved once Patrick gives exact ones. Twenty gold to post a notice, which is read only; thirty for a job, which goes on the taker's list. The fee routes into the drop box, which is the hold's money and only the City Court may draw from it. The same box takes rent, Merchant's Guild ledgers and Free Skyrim Trading Company payment and pickup. FSTC is the Free Skyrim Trading Company and will eventually replace the EEC. THE DROP BOX WORKS TODAY AND IS MEASURED: mp.onPutItem(containerRefrId, actorId, baseId, count) exists and PutItemEvent::OnFireSuccess is what removes the items, so returning false refuses the put and the gold stays in the hand. The server knows who paid, what, and how much, and can refuse anything that should not be in there. RENT is either handed to a steward in person, which is two characters trading and needs nothing built, or put in the box. SQUATTING falls out for free: the server knows a building is the city's and who is standing in it, so it flags the state and does nothing. The server never evicts except by the lapse. THE FIRST WORKING PIECE IS ON MAIN, 21 SEPTEMBER. THE DOOR TABLE EXISTS, which this entry said nothing could be built without. tools/Build-DoorTable.py walks every placed reference in all 101 plugins, inflating the compressed records every other scanner here skips, and measured: 362 door records, 5,658 placed door references, 2,798 of them leading somewhere, 385 of those locked with 335 of the locks wanting a named key, 331 carrying an owner Bethesda already set, and 852 interior cells reached through a door, which is the number of claimable buildings this world actually holds. 425 of those have more than one way in, and that is the number that decides the shape of a claim: nearly half of everything claimable has a back door, so a claim covers a BUILDING and a lock has to follow the claim rather than the door somebody happened to stand at. Proudspire Manor has four doors and BYOHHouse2Hjaalmarch has fourteen. Zero doors name a partner the pass never saw and zero compressed records failed to inflate, which is the check that the walk reached everything. BUILDINGS HAVE THEIR REAL NAMES: a cell stores FULL as a string id into a .STRINGS table inside a BSA, so tools/bsa.py reads the archives, and 851 of the 852 buildings now carry the name people use. The one that does not is a mod utility cell. THE CLAIM IS BUILT, on main as 1100de7: open a door, say /claim, and the building is yours and the deed is in your pack named for it. One deed record for all 852 buildings, because Inventory::Entry carries a per-instance name. More than one property allowed, lapse counted from the last time you went IN rather than from the day you claimed, and the lapse reads TUNING.farming.claimLapseDays so property and farming can never drift to two different fortnights. propertytest.js is 32 checks. WHAT IS LEFT, and it is most of the system: locks and keys and the smith's key mold, the jarl and steward offices, the City Court, rent, the drop box, the notice boards, and the deed being stealable. AND ONE THING THE BUILD TURNED UP: a home and its farm are ONE claim in the design and TWO in the code, because farming keys ground and property keys buildings. /claim already decides between them by whether the engine just said you opened a door, which works, but joining the two records is its own piece of work and nobody should assume it is done. LOCKS AND KEYS ARE BUILT, 21 SEPTEMBER, ON MAIN AS 1a0bdb5. THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE SHAPE, and it is not what anybody would guess: the client does not tell the server about a press on a LOCKED reference at all. The Thornswood patch in activationService.ts returns before it sends, on purpose, so Skyrim keeps the reference and runs its own lockpicking game, which is exactly what was asked for. So a lock cannot be something the server does when somebody presses a door. The door has to already be locked on their machine. SO IT IS TWO HALVES: the server writes to each person which doors they should find shut and an updateOwner script on their client calls lock() on each, and onActivate refuses a locked door anyway, because a press that reached the server proves the client script did not run. The honest client gets a lock it can pick; the changed one gets a door that does not open. A KEY IS ITS NAME, with no register of keys at all, because a key can be handed over, pickpocketed or taken out of a chest and every one of those is the item moving with nobody telling the server. Key and mold are MISC and not KEYM on purpose: a vanilla key is weightless, is not dropped and is not what a pickpocket takes, and every one of those is the opposite of what this needs. THE MOLD BALANCE: cut at the door, by a smith, with whoever holds the place standing there, which is what stops one being cut while somebody is offline and is not a rule anybody has to remember. And the mold goes to the HOLDER, not the smith, because a smith who kept it could cut himself a key to that house for ever after. propertytest.js is 61 checks. NOT VERIFIED IN A RUNNING GAME: the client half is a script this repo cannot run, the same as every other client plugin here. WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS ENTRY: the deed being stealable so that carrying it moves ownership, the jarl and steward offices and the City Court, rent and the drop box, the notice boards, and joining a home and its farm into the one claim the design says they are. THE FARM AND THE HOUSE ARE ONE RECORD NOW, 21 September, which Patrick asked for in as many words: "I was meaning the farm and property being one property in the code and not just the claim". The property claim carries the ground its door stands on, read when the door is OPENED rather than when /claim is said, because by then the person is in the hallway. claimCovering in the farming block asks the property block before it looks at its own claims, so ground outside a front door belongs to the house and claiming the house claimed it: no second /claim, no second record. What is left in the farming block is ground with no building on it, which is what a farm claim was always for. Both halves read TUNING.farming.claimRadius so there is one size of farm and not two. A door that stands indoors records no ground, which is right: there is no farm outside an inn's landing. ALSO DONE: the Property page on K, which appears the moment somebody holds a place or carries a key, and /help now names /deed, /lock, /unlock, /mold and /key, none of which a tester could have discovered before. BUILT ON 21 SEPTEMBER AND ON DEV, six commits, 0a6eed0 through f84506f, all on dev and none on live. THE DEED IS THE TITLE, which this entry asked for and which /claim had been promising since it was written while nothing in the code did it: holderOf read the register only, so a stolen deed was a piece of paper. Carrying it to the door is the act now, which is safe to hang on a door because a locked one is never announced to the server, so every press that arrives is a door already open to whoever pressed it. The lock and the ground survive the transfer and the old holder is not notified, because that would turn a theft into an alarm system. THE OFFICES: an admin places the first Jarl out of character and never grants anything again; a jarl names stewards with /steward and a profile id, kept beside the claims rather than in Discord; a steward is not an admin and their one power is /evict, which ends a claim and nothing else, touching no belongings and taking back no key, so an evicted tenant who kept theirs can still walk in at night. THE DROP BOX is real because mp.onPutItem is real: returning false refuses the put and the gold stays in the hand. Only coin goes in, and every other chest in Skyrim is untouched. A steward designates it by standing at it, which beat a placeholder coordinate. RENT is counted and never seized: gold into the box pays down what the payer owes first, and the ordinary lapse does the rest. THE BOARDS are places rather than records: the nine arrival points out of the chargen table, one inn per hold, which are positions the server already stands people up on, so they are not guesses, and /board here moves one. A new record with nine placed references would have needed the plugin rebuilt and packed to every client, and a corrupt plugin takes the server down for everybody. THE TAKER'S LIST: /take, /jobs and /dropjob, with no /done and no payment, because whether a job was finished is between two people and a server that judged it would be refereeing roleplay. STILL NOT BUILT from this entry: the Merchant's Guild and FSTC ledgers, and moving a board to a keep once somebody decides where. Harnesses: test-deed-title 15, test-offices 26, test-coffers 38. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The property system is on main and every harness passes, run here: test-offices 26, test-coffers 38, test-boards 20, test-deed-title 15, test-locks 16, test-key-chain 35, test-cut-key 18, all 0 failed. Since the entry was written, keys and molds moved on in a59b699 (#198), bb687a7 (#199) and 29beece (#200). Step 2 (board placement) is done: c1597be (#107) put the nine boards outside on Djinn's coordinates, and 36f4432 (#149) corrected Solitude's. Step 3 is stale as written: the entry's own text records the decision (SETTLED 21 September, character-specific offices), but the code still carries the old wording at gamemode.js:13988-13993 ('STILL OPEN ... not built'), and stewards are keyed by profileId (account), not by character. A new finding: the Jarl role is not wired at all. isJarl reads globalThis.__thornswoodIsJarl at gamemode.js:14016, and that is never defined anywhere. Only __thornswoodIsDev, IsAdmin and IsAllowed are defined (:10583-10601). The site's door answer carries profiles, devProfiles and adminProfiles only (tools/docs-app/server.js:2439). So today only an admin can act as a jarl, and a Discord Jarl role does nothing. test-offices.js:195 only checks that the name is read, which is why it passes. Also still unbuilt: the Merchant's Guild and FSTC ledgers. NEXT STEP: 1) tools/docs-app/server.js ~2439-2475: add jarlProfiles from a Discord role named in the site config, next to devProfiles and adminProfiles. 2) tools/gamemode.js door loader (~10530-10601): read doc.jarlProfiles into jarlIds and define __thornswoodIsJarl. 3) Make the office character-specific as settled: keep the Discord role as eligibility and store the held office on one named character (an actor property next to class and profession). isJarl and isSteward then check the pressing actor's character, not only the profile. Show the office on the K panel. Replace the STILL OPEN comment at :13988. 4) Extend test-offices.js so a Jarl-role profile with no admin can name a steward, a second character on the same account cannot, and the harness would fail if __thornswoodIsJarl were never defined. Then Patrick runs the dev test in step 1. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick: the in-game dev test of the whole chain (step 1). A Jarl role has to exist in the Discord server, which is Discord production. The Merchant's Guild and FSTC ledgers have no design yet.

## Read first

- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js`: the lockChanged handler and the comment saying a locked reference is never announced to the server
- `tools\gamemode.js`: roleFromDoor for the offices, and the farm claim block for the shape a property claim takes

## Steps

- [ ] Test it on dev. As an admin you are already a jarl, so /steward your own profile id, then /box, /rent, /notice, /job, /take all work. (patrick)
- [ ] Decide where each hold's board belongs and put it there with /board here. (patrick)
- [ ] The account versus character question for the offices is still open and is the one design decision left in this entry. (patrick)

## Done when

On dev: a jarl names a steward, anybody can claim any open door for nothing and is handed the deed, the owner can lock it, a smith molds it only for the owner or a keyholder, a thief who lifts a key can get in but not take the house, a thief who lifts the deed takes the house, an evicted tenant who kept a key can still get in, and the board outside the keep takes twenty gold for a notice and thirty for a job into the hold's box.

## Traps

Every rule here sits on the mold or the claim and never on the door, because the server cannot see a locked door. Any design that starts with the server refusing entry breaks lockpicking, which Patrick asked for by name.

issues.title: The ladders have to line up across classes and professions, or one of them is dead weight
issues.body:
**Order:** 125 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** measure it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\ores.json, harvests.json, hunts.json, recipes.json: the five ladders that have to agree · tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1, the reverse index and the ranking · tools\Check-Balance.ps1, the chain report · dev only

## What is known

PATRICK, 21 September: 'we also need to make sure the different tiers match across so like farmer matches with tiers of cook for their recipes, miner and smith, woodworker and miner and so on, so there isn't an imbalance'. He is right and it is checkable rather than a matter of taste. THE SHAPE OF THE CHECK: every recipe has inputs, and every input is something a class produces at some rank. A novice Hearthcook recipe whose inputs include a crop only an expert Farmer may grow is an imbalance, and so is an expert Platewright recipe whose inputs a novice Miner can bring in all day. So: for each recipe, take the highest producer rank among its inputs and compare it to the rank the recipe itself sits at. Report every half where the two disagree by more than one rung. WHAT IS MISSING BEFORE IT CAN RUN: tools\recipes.json records how MANY inputs a recipe has and not WHICH. The CNTO subrecords are already parsed by the build script, so carrying the form ids through is a small change to a script that already reads them. WHAT CAN BE SAID ALREADY, from the rank spreads as they stand: plants 57 novice, 61 advanced, 24 expert, 5 master. Ore veins 88, 310, 159, 24. Animals 156, 150, 47, 8. Crops 5, 4, 2, 0. The crop ladder is the thin one, which is a consequence of there being only eleven farmable records in the whole game, and it is the one most likely to hold a cook back. THE CHECK EXISTS, tools\Check-Balance.ps1, commit 94f8955, and it found three walls on its first run. Cook/Confectioner has nothing at advanced, so becoming an Advanced Confectioner opens no recipe at all. Enchanter/Bladebinder has nothing at advanced and nothing at expert: 160 of its 161 recipes are novice and the last is master. Those are numbers to argue about rather than defects to fix quietly, so they are reported and nothing was moved. The producing ladders are all sound: ore 88/310/159/24, plants 46/61/24/5, animals 157/150/47/8, water 11/2/1/1, crops 5/4/2/0. The crop ladder is the thin one and that is a consequence of there being eleven farmable records in the whole game. WHAT IT STILL CANNOT DO is follow one recipe to the class that makes its inputs, because recipes.json records how many inputs a recipe has and not which. THE CHAIN IS READABLE, 21 September, and it turned the whole rule over. The three empty rungs were not a threshold problem: they were the wrong measure. Measured on the table this repo built: Cook/Confectioner has 28 recipes and TWO distinct output prices in the whole half, 18 at 6 gold and 10 at 14. Enchanter/Bladebinder has 161 and two, 160 at 5 gold and one at 1250. Woodworker/Charburner has four and one price, 2 gold. Four rungs cannot be cut out of two numbers. SO A RECIPE IS RANKED BY WHAT ITS INPUTS COST A PRODUCER, the dearest thing it asks for, which is also the answer to the question this entry opens with: a Cook's rungs are the Farmer's rungs because they are the same numbers off the same table. tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1 keeps the CNTO form ids now, every owned row carries inputItems with the class that produces each one and the rank it is produced at, and inputRank is the dearest of them. THE REVERSE INDEX: 137 distinct items, gatherer 63, hunter 50, miner 18, fisher 6, each recorded at the LOWEST rank any class gets it, because if a novice miner can find iron anywhere then iron costs novice. WHAT IT PLACES: the owned recipes ask for 176 distinct items and 71 have a producer. 531 of the 3437 owned rows have at least one input with a producer behind it. RANK SPREADS, before by price and after by input cost, every owned row: Confectioner 18/0/10/0 to 12/16/0/0. Hearthcook 31/52/28/1 to 71/22/14/5. Bladebinder 160/0/0/1 to 41/56/40/24. Platewright 511/733/473/298 to 492/744/474/305. Edgewright 185/242/179/104 to 181/241/175/113. Haberdasher 47/73/48/19 to 54/100/29/4. Liverywright 37/39/9/11 to 37/48/9/2. Woodwright 34/45/27/18 to 33/42/26/23. Charburner 4/0/0/0 unchanged. No half now has an empty rung with work above it, counting every owned row and counting only the rows the server is asked about, and the build refuses to write the table if one has. ONE HALF NEEDED A SECOND RULE AND IT IS NAMED: the Bladebinder. Every one of its 161 rows but one sells for 5 gold, and 160 of them want a Heart Stone, which ores.json ranks as master work for a miner, so input cost put the WHOLE half on master and left three rungs empty. It is ranked by total input count for that half alone, the SECOND_RULE_KEY knob, and the cost of that is printed every run: 97 of its rows now sit more than one rung below what their inputs cost. That is a decision for Patrick rather than a defect: either the Bladebinder's rank stops meaning cost, or the half has one usable rung. CHECK-BALANCE SAYS, 21 September: 342 rows in step with what their inputs cost, 138 not, 1248 asking for nothing any class produces; per half the average gap is 0 rungs everywhere except the Bladebinder at 1.72. All seven harnesses pass unchanged, 828 checks, and crafttest's pinned ranks all held, so nothing had to be loosened. WHAT IS LEFT, AND IT IS THE BIG ONE: one more hop. The three commonest inputs in the whole table are Leather Strips, wanted by 924 recipes, Steel Ingot by 888 and Leather by 665, and none of the three comes out of the ground. They come out of a smelter or a tanning rack, which is itself a recipe, one of the 1679 nobody owns. That is why the Smith is still 1875 of 2015 rows ranked by price, and it is exactly the miner-and-smith pair Patrick named. Following the chain through the unowned stock recipes needs a fixpoint, because an ingot recipe can want another ingot, and it was left out deliberately rather than guessed at. ALSO WORTH DECIDING: Tomato ranks as gatherer novice rather than farmer advanced, because it grows wild as well as on a farm and the index takes the lowest. Every crop that also grows wild does the same, so the Farmer's ladder is bypassed wherever it overlaps the Gatherer's. That is the PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST knob working as written, and it may not be what farming wants. UNCOMMITTED ON THIS MACHINE: tools/Build-RecipeTable.ps1, tools/Check-Balance.ps1, tools/gamemode.js and tools/recipes.json are modified on main and not committed. gamemode.js changed only inside the generated RECIPES_BY_ID block. Nothing client side changed, so no client update is needed for the dev launcher: Sync-Client.ps1 -Check against C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game reports all six recorded files in place, build 1c53c0aa. FIXED, 21 September morning, commit 091eb6a. THE CAUSE OF THE THREE EMPTY RUNGS WAS NOT A THRESHOLD. The Confectioner's 28 recipes have TWO distinct output values in the whole half, 6 gold and 14. The Bladebinder's 161 have two, 5 and 1250. The Charburner's four have one. No ranking by what the output sells for can make four rungs out of two numbers, and nothing anybody could have tuned would have changed that. SO A RECIPE IS RANKED BY WHAT ITS INPUTS COST A PRODUCER, which is the same question from the other end and is exactly what matching the tiers means. The CNTO subrecords were already being read to count them, so the form ids were in the script's hands and were being thrown away. Every empty rung is gone, and Check-Balance has a chain report where its 'cannot answer yet' section used to be. ONE HALF NEEDED A SECOND RULE AND THE RUN SAYS SO: 160 of the Bladebinder's 161 staves want a Heart Stone, which is master mining, so the input rule put the whole half on master and made it worse than the price rule did. That half alone ranks by how long the shopping list is, and the 97 rows still more than a rung from their inputs are reported every run, by name, as something to decide. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Every Claude step is done. Input ids: 091eb6a. The one-hop fixpoint through the stock recipes: 077268f, with HopFixpoint at Build-RecipeTable.ps1:3766 and FOLLOW_THE_HOP at :930. The 'UNCOMMITTED ON THIS MACHINE' paragraph is stale: git status shows only 'Claude outputs/' untracked. Ran .\tools\Check-Balance.ps1 here. The exit 1 came only from Read-Host at :708 in a non-interactive shell (pass -NoPause), and the report itself ends green: every ladder has a bottom rung. Measured now: 1489 rows in step with their inputs, 361 not, 34 asking for nothing any class produces. Counted from tools/recipes.json, 177 rows sit more than one rung from their input cost, not the 97 that doneWhen says. 97 are Bladebinder rows ranked below their cost (the SECOND_RULE_KEY decision). 80 are ranked above their cost: Platewright 27, Haberdasher 17, Liverywright 14, Edgewright 10, Hearthcook 4, Confectioner 5, Charburner 2, Woodwright 1. These are mostly rows whose dearest input has no producer (Dragon Bone 139 entries, Linen Wrap 106, Dwarven Metal Ingot 104, Dragon Scales 97), for example Dragonplate ranked master against a novice Leather Strips. Check-Balance also reports that the gatherer-to-Tailor pairing does not hold (2%) and that the Alchemist owns no recipe. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build until the decisions are made. The entry's doneWhen should be corrected to 177 rows: 97 Bladebinder below cost and 80 above cost, most of them because an input such as Dragon Bone or Dwarven Metal Ingot has no producer. Once Patrick decides, apply the decisions as knob changes in tools/Build-RecipeTable.ps1 (SECOND_RULE_KEY, PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST, UNPLACED_INPUT_RULE), rebuild, run Check-Balance.ps1 -NoPause and the harnesses, and deploy the gamemode to dev. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides: (1) the Bladebinder rule (97 rows ranked below cost, or one usable rung); (2) whether a crop that also grows wild costs the Farmer's rank or the Gatherer's (PRODUCER_RANK_IS_LOWEST); (3) what an input nobody produces costs (Dragon Bone, Linen Wrap, Dwarven Metal Ingot, Dragon Scales), which drives the 80 rows ranked above cost; (4) whether gatherer-to-Tailor and gatherer-to-Alchemist should hold.

## Steps

- [x] Carry the CNTO input form ids through into tools\recipes.json. Done 21 September: every owned row has inputItems with the item, the count, the class that produces it and the rank. (claude)
- [x] Build the reverse index, item to the lowest rank any class gets it at, out of ores.json, harvests.json's three maps and hunts.json. Done: 137 items. (claude)
- [x] Rank every recipe by the dearest of its inputs, falling back to the output price where nothing it asks for is produced. Done, and it closed all three empty rungs. (claude)
- [x] Report the chain in tools\Check-Balance.ps1: per half, how far its recipes sit from what their inputs cost, and every row more than one rung out. Done. (claude)
- [ ] Read the Bladebinder decision and settle it. 97 of its rows are ranked below what they cost because the second rule had to fill three empty rungs. Either that stands, or the half keeps one usable rung, or somebody decides what a Bladebinder is meant to gather. (patrick)
- [ ] Decide whether a crop that also grows wild should cost the Farmer's rank or the Gatherer's. Tomato is gatherer novice today, not farmer advanced, and every overlapping crop is the same. (patrick)
- [ ] Follow the stock recipes one hop: a smelter turns ore into an ingot and a tanning rack turns a pelt into leather, and those are the inputs 924, 888 and 665 recipes ask for. Needs a fixpoint because an ingot recipe can want another ingot. This is what puts the Smith's ladder against the Miner's. (claude)
- [ ] Ship it. The four changed files go out together: the launcher pack carries nothing here, but gamemode.js does, and the table is inside it. (patrick)

## Commands

- reads every COBJ in the load order, builds the reverse index, ranks by input cost and writes tools\recipes.json and the RECIPES_BY_ID block in tools\gamemode.js. Read only against the game folder and it proves that with a fingerprint before and after (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-RecipeTable.ps1
  ```
- the five ladders, the rungs, and the chain from a recipe to what its inputs cost. Exit 1 only for an empty rung with work above it (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Balance.ps1
  ```
- answers whether the dev launcher needs a client update. On 21 September: all six recorded files in place, build 1c53c0aa, so it does not (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Sync-Client.ps1 -Check -Game 'C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game'
  ```

## Done when

Check-Balance.ps1 runs green, no half has an empty rung with work above it, and every recipe whose inputs sit more than one rung from its own rank is one somebody looked at and kept. 97 remain, all Bladebinder, all waiting on a decision.

## Traps

A crop ladder with eleven records in it cannot be stretched as far as an ore ladder with 581. Matching the ladders may mean changing what a rank asks for rather than which rung a thing sits on. The reverse index takes the LOWEST rank an item is produced at, so a crop that also grows wild costs the Gatherer's rank and never the Farmer's. And a half can pass the ranking and still fail Check-Balance, because the ranking counts every owned row while Check-Balance counts only the rows the server is asked about; the build checks both subsets now for that reason.

issues.title: The other servers are gone from everything we control, on the branch, and the last of it is on the disk and in Djinn's hands
issues.body:
**Order:** 131 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

Your PC · branch patrick/progression, commit c301f91 · the Steam copy's Data and DaedricData · Djinn's machine

## What is known

DECIDED BY PATRICK ON 20 SEPTEMBER: Thornswood does not support, detect or work around any other server's install, and their names appear nowhere in our stuff. Done on the branch in one commit with the client switch, because OwnGame.cs and Ship-Rules.ps1 each carry both halves and they revert together. WHAT WENT: New-GameFolder.ps1, Why-Keizaal.ps1, Clean-OtherServers.ps1, Restore-KzlContent.ps1, Patch-Client.ps1 and a 155 KB content JSON that nothing read. OwnGame.OtherServerHere and ReplacedByOthers, with their callers; the nine named rules in OwnGame.Foreign and Test-ShipOtherServer, replaced by what belongs; the startup offer to make the own folder is now made whenever it is possible rather than only when another server's files were found; two dead plugin names in Links.cs and two dead script names in Clean-Downloads; the three probe file names in Checks.ForeignNames, now an empty list Fix still walks; DaedricData from the installer's root skip list. A wording pass took the names out of every comment and prose line, two of them user facing in Help.cs and ui.xaml, and two shipped release notes in version.json now say 'the earlier server's', which is the one place history was reworded and it is said here so nobody wonders. CLAUDE.md's settled design, SECOND-DEVELOPER's two sections, HANDOFF and the site runbook are rewritten. Left deliberately: WORKING-NOTES.md and AUDIT-2026-09-17.md, which are dated records of what was true, and the provenance notes in thornswood-src, reworded to 'the earlier plugin'. A repo-wide search for any of the names across every text file we control returns nothing. THE DISK: the Steam copy held DaedricData, 158 MB of that launcher's bookkeeping whose own README says Skyrim never loads from it, and four loose Keizaal paths under Data, meshes/Keizaal, meshes/kzlcustommeshs, Scripts/KzlChop.pex, textures/Keizaal, none of them in Thornswood's folder, none referenced by our esp, none deployed by Vortex. NOT REMOVED FROM HERE: a Claude's shell refuses to delete anything under Program Files, so these five are Patrick's to remove, and the lines are in the reply of 20 September and below. Recorded before they go: that launcher's 'vanilla-backup' held 269 files and was not vanilla at all but mod files it overwrote, of which 15 still differed from the live Steam copy, every one of them a SkyMP runtime file or a body mesh, meaning that launcher's overlay was still in place in the Steam copy. The clean remedy for the Steam copy afterwards is Vortex's own purge and redeploy, which rewrites Data from staging. The lines, from any PowerShell: $S = 'C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Skyrim Special Edition'; foreach ($r in 'DaedricData','Data/meshes/Keizaal','Data/meshes/kzlcustommeshs','Data/Scripts/KzlChop.pex','Data/textures/Keizaal') { Remove-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $S $r) -Recurse -Force -Confirm:$false }. DJINN: Keep.cs, Hold.cs and OwnGame.cs changed and CLAUDE.md says those need a line in #dev. Patrick waived it for his own machine; Djinn's machine plays by the same launcher, so the line still goes in #dev before this is merged to main: the launcher no longer parks another server's plugins by name, it parks anything in Plugins that is not thornswood-*.js or the recorded bundle, and it no longer leaves another server's files out of the own folder by name, it leaves out whatever does not belong. FOUND 22 SEPTEMBER, WHAT IS STILL ON THE DISK, and Patrick asked for it to be gone. A Claude will not delete these, so they are Patrick's. (1) THE LOOSE FILES the two other launchers dropped into the Steam copy's Data, traced in entry 142: LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary and LostArk under both textures and meshes, weapons\rpcustom and weapons\saarthal under both, and leifcrops under both. Ten whole folders, not one file in them from Vortex, and the same ten are in C:\Thornswood\Game\Data. The command is step 2 of entry 46, together with the two orphaned body builds, and it has to run before Maintenance. (2) THE LAUNCHER: Daedric Online's is installed at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\skyrim-rp-launcher, keeps its data in %APPDATA%\skyrim-rp-launcher and its updater in %LOCALAPPDATA%\daedric-launcher-updater. Uninstall it from Windows Settings, Apps first, then remove whichever of the three folders is left. (3) VORTEX: one profile is left and the other servers' mods are uninstalled, but their archives are still on the Downloads page: Daedric-Online, Keizaal-Online and KzlOnlineContent (140 MB). About 120 archives in all have nothing installed from them, around 11 GB by a name match, so treat the count as close rather than exact. In Vortex, Downloads, sort by Status, select the ones not installed, Remove, and tick Delete Archive. Keep the three collection_ombo2a archives until nobody is on revision 4, then remove 2 and 4. Also a second copy in the Downloads folder: Playable Riekling SSE 1.3.2-5513-1-3-2 (1).7z. (4) LOOT: Vortex's userlist.yaml still has an empty entry for kzlonlinemods.esp. It does nothing, and it goes through LOOT's own metadata editor, not by hand. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Repo side done: c301f91 is an ancestor of main (git merge-base --is-ancestor). A git grep for keizaal|kzl|daedric online|daedricdata|skyrim-rp-launcher now matches only: AUDIT-2026-09-17.md and WORKING-NOTES.md (kept on purpose), Rename-ContentRecords.ps1 (its rule has to match Kzl), Audit-Leftovers.ps1:46 and Clean-Leftovers.ps1:47 (the path of that launcher's data, which they must name to find it), and two history comments, tools/app/Enforce.cs:89 and tools/Build-RecipeTable.ps1:1752. Disk, measured here: DaedricData and the Keizaal folders under the Steam Data are gone, KzlChop.pex is gone, and the three skyrim-rp-launcher folders are gone. STILL PRESENT: all ten loose folders (meshes and textures for 'LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary', LostArk, weapons\rpcustom, weapons\saarthal and leifcrops) in the Steam copy's Data, in C:\Thornswood\Game\Data and in C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data. fsutil shows they are the same files as hard links with three names, created 17 September before the branch. Vortex downloads\skyrimse still holds Daedric-Online, Keizaal-Online and the KzlOnlineContent rar. %APPDATA%\Vortex\skyrimse\userlist.yaml:3 still names kzlonlinemods.esp. NEXT STEP: Repo: optionally reword the two history comments (Enforce.cs:89, Build-RecipeTable.ps1:1752). Correct doneWhen: the search can never be empty, because the rename tool and the leftover scripts have to name what they look for. Everything else is Patrick's. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick, by hand: remove the ten folders from the Steam copy's Data (a Claude shell refuses Program Files) and from C:\Thornswood\Game\Data and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data. In Vortex, remove the uninstalled archives (Daedric-Online, Keizaal-Online, KzlOnlineContent and the rest), then purge and redeploy. Remove the kzlonlinemods.esp entry through LOOT's metadata editor. Post the #dev line to Djinn about Keep, Hold and OwnGame parking by what belongs.

## Done when

A search for the names across every text file we control returns nothing, the launcher compiles, the Ship-Rules harness passes, the branch is merged to main after a dev test, and Djinn has read the #dev line. On this machine, the Steam copy has been purged and redeployed in Vortex.

## Traps

Do not rename the 33 records inside Thornswood-Content.esp or KzlChop.pex as part of this; that is a plugin edit and it is the entry below. And never touch the bare word daedric: it is a vanilla material that names thousands of ordinary files.

issues.title: Thornswood-Content.esp carries 33 records and one script named for the server the content was salvaged from
issues.body:
**Order:** 132 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Content · **Effort:** work it out, medium · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

The esp in the collection · tools\thornswood-src\patch_esp.py rewrites its records · Data\Scripts\KzlChop.pex is attached by name and was never in Thornswood's folder

## What is known

The last place the name lives is inside the plugin. Restore-KzlContent's header, before it was deleted, recorded it: the chopping block, the charcoal kilns and their markers, the salt mine furniture, the beehive, and the alchemy and mining manuals are 33 records whose editor ids begin Kzl, and the chopping block's script is KzlChop.pex. The gamemode refers to all of them by form id, not by editor id, so renaming the editor ids is cosmetic to the server and safe. Renaming the script is not: the esp attaches it by name in a VMAD record, so it means a recompiled script under the new name and the attachment rewritten, then a test that the chopping block still works. NOTE what was measured on 20 September: KzlChop.pex was in the Steam copy's Data and never in C:/Thornswood/Game, so the block's script has not been shipping with the block at all, which is consistent with entry 216 and may be why nobody noticed. Either the script goes in with the rename or the block is scripted server side. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The editor id rename is done in b8e57da by tools/Rename-ContentRecords.ps1. Scanning tools/Thornswood-Content.esp here (the repo copy, C:\Thornswood\Game\Data and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data all hash 14b19436...), exactly one 'Kzl' string is left in the file, and it is not an editor id. It is the script name in the VMAD of FURN 0x05DF7B34 ThornswoodExecutionerChoppingBlock ('Execution Block', Furniture\HeadChoppingBlock.nif). Its one property, animIdle, points at Skyrim.esm IDLE 0x0F95BE IdleExecutionerChop_Player. The block is placed once, REFR 0x05DFCC75 in cell 0x37EE9 SolitudeOrigin. So it is an executioner's block in Solitude, not a wood chopping block. The wood blocks are the three vanilla bases answered server side in CHOPPING_BLOCKS (gamemode.js:3140) and are untouched by the plugin, as Patrick decided on 21 September. So 'chopping wood at the block works on dev' in doneWhen is wrong. KzlChop.pex is in neither game folder nor the Steam copy, so the attached script has never run for anybody on Thornswood. Stale trap: tools\thornswood-src\patch_esp.py no longer exists (removed in 5d1f3f0). The plugin is now edited by tools/Add-ContentRecords.py (used in bb687a7, #199). NEXT STEP: After Patrick decides what the Execution Block is for: (a) a plain prop: extend Add-ContentRecords.py or Rename-ContentRecords.ps1 to drop the VMAD subrecord from 0x05DF7B34, re-reading the result and comparing every other record byte for byte, like Rename-ContentRecords already does; (b) keep the executioner idle: have the front plugin play IdleExecutionerChop_Player on activating that base, the way the axe animation is already played client side, and drop the VMAD as in (a); (c) keep a Papyrus script: this needs a compiled .pex under a Thornswood name, which needs the Creation Kit's compiler and the script source, and the .pex then has to ship in a pack. Bundle the plugin change into the Nexus upload that #199's plugin change is already waiting for (29beece says the plugin has not reached everybody). WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides whether the Solitude Execution Block is a plain prop, plays the executioner idle, or is removed. Then he uploads the rebuilt Thornswood-Content.esp to the Nexus collection. doneWhen needs rewriting, because this block was never a wood chopping block.

## Done when

No editor id in Thornswood-Content.esp begins Kzl, the chopping block's script has a Thornswood name and ships in the game folder, and chopping wood at the block works on the dev server.

## Traps

patch_esp.py is the tool that rewrites this esp and it is the thing to extend, not a hand edit in xEdit that the next build overwrites.

issues.title: Nothing backs up the world, and the only two backups are from the same sixteen minutes
issues.body:
**Order:** 138 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 12

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · C:\Thornswood-Server\world, not in the backup · Your PC · Downloads\Thornswood-Backups, two files from 15 September · tools\Backup-Server.ps1:132-139, 245-248

## What is known

The 15 September zip was opened during the audit: 195 KB, 47 entries, nothing under the world folder. A nightly task on the box taking world, data and the three config files, encrypted, pushed off the box, seven daily and four weekly kept, and one restore rehearsed on a throwaway box so the runbook is known to work. Characters are the only thing here people would grieve THE WORLD IS NOW BACKED UP, commit 2761d47 on main, but nothing has run yet. Backup-Server.ps1 takes world and private as well as data, which fixes the manual backup on its own. Measured on the box: world is 1,423 files and 2.07 MB, newest change 03:42 on 18 September, so there was never a size reason to skip it. private, created yesterday by entry 4's fix, was missing from the backup for the same reason. There is no backup scheduled task on the VPS at all. FOUR NEW SCRIPTS. vps-nightly-backup.ps1 runs on the box at 03:15 and takes world, private, data, server-settings.json, gamemode.js, the site's data, the bot and site configs and the voice register, keeping seven daily and four weekly where a weekly is a run that landed on a Sunday. Install-Backup.ps1 puts it there, makes the passphrase on the box and copies it down here. Fetch-Backups.ps1 brings them off the box and opens the newest, because copying bytes proves nothing and the failure worth catching is a backup that reads fine and holds no characters, which is exactly what the 15 September pair were. Restore-Backup.ps1 checks, decrypts and unpacks. RESTORING.md is the runbook. ENCRYPTED: AES-256-CBC, PBKDF2-SHA256 at 200,000 iterations, random salt and IV per backup, HMAC-SHA256 over salt, IV and ciphertext checked before anything is decrypted, separate keys for encrypting and signing. The passphrase is never printed, logged or committed, and both its names are gitignored. MEASURED against 40 characters: backup, encrypt, decrypt, unpack, all 40 back with contents intact. A wrong passphrase and a single flipped ciphertext byte are both refused before decryption. Retention over 30 nights kept exactly 7 daily and 4 weekly and left two hand-placed files alone. WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the part that matters: run Install-Backup.ps1, run Fetch-Backups.ps1, and rehearse one restore. RESTORING.md says Last rehearsed: never and should keep saying it until somebody has done it. Until then this is a careful guess rather than a backup. THE FIRST REAL BACKUP EXISTS, 18 September. Install-Backup.ps1 registered the task, next run 03:15 on 19 September, and -RunNow took one: 1,514 files, world 1,423 files, private 3, data 62, the site's data 21, zipped to 13.3 MB and encrypted. The passphrase was made on the box and copied to Documents on Patrick's machine. A BUG THE FIRST RUN FOUND, fixed in commit dd03dd3. It asked for C:/Thornswood-Bot/config.json and reported it missing. The bot's config is called bot.env.json, 703 bytes, and it holds the Discord token, so the one file that cannot be rebuilt from the repo was the one file not being taken. Found by looking at the box rather than guessing twice. Two more things were added while there, both needed by a restore onto a fresh machine and neither present before: C:/Thornswood-Voice/secret.txt, without which the character register is switched off until somebody rotates it, and C:/Thornswood-Caddy/Caddyfile, which RESTORING.md step 1 needs. token-key.txt is deliberately left out because it makes itself on first run. THE FIXED SCRIPT IS NOT ON THE BOX YET. Install-Backup.ps1 has to run again to send it, or tonight's backup will miss the same three files. STILL LEFT AFTER THAT: run Fetch-Backups.ps1 to get a copy off the box, and rehearse one restore. RESTORING.md says Last rehearsed: never. THE FIXED SCRIPT IS ON THE BOX, 18 September. Install-Backup.ps1 re-sent it and confirmed the passphrase was left alone rather than replaced. C:/Thornswood-Backup/vps-nightly-backup.ps1 now asks for bot.env.json and takes the Caddyfile, so tonight's 03:15 run gets the Discord token, the voice secret and the TLS config that the first run missed. Task next due 03:15 on 19 September. STILL LEFT: Fetch-Backups.ps1 to get a copy off the box, and one rehearsed restore. RESTORING.md still says Last rehearsed: never, and until that changes none of this is known to work. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The scripts are on main: 2761d47, dd03dd3 and 57d7a7c (#157, 23 September, which drops secret.txt and owners.json from vps-nightly-backup.ps1). tools/RESTORING.md:116 still reads '**Last rehearsed: never.**' No encrypted nightly backup has ever been fetched to this machine: C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Backups, the default -To of Fetch-Backups.ps1:25, holds only the two 195 KB zips from 15 September and the 26 MB Backup-Server zip from 18 September 01:16. The key file is in Documents. Nothing shows whether Install-Backup.ps1 was run again after 57d7a7c. If it was not, the box still runs the older script, which reports secret.txt and owners.json as missing (vps-nightly-backup.ps1:80 notes a missing file and carries on), so this is untidy rather than broken. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change in the repo. Patrick runs Install-Backup.ps1 again if 57d7a7c has not reached the box, then Fetch-Backups.ps1 to bring the newest encrypted copy off the VPS and open it. Then the restore rehearsal: Restore-Backup.ps1 on the fetched file, and Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 -Zip <it> -Root C:\Thornswood-Restore-Test -NoTask. Check that the load order resolves and a character from the backup is present, then write the date and the exact commands into RESTORING.md in place of 'never'. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Production: Fetch-Backups.ps1 and Install-Backup.ps1 both reach the VPS over ssh, which is refused from a Claude session here, so Patrick runs them and the restore rehearsal.

## Read first

- `tools\Backup-Server.ps1:100-150`: the Grab list, which takes server-settings.json, gamemode.js and the whole data folder and never the world folder
- `tools\Backup-Server.ps1:230-250`: the script's own warning that the zip holds the bot token, the Discord client secret and the register secret
- `tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:70-95 and 128-138`: the world folder is set aside and restored on install, and the load order refusal that tells you a restore rehearsal actually worked
- `tools\vps-dev-instance.ps1:27-47`: the clearest statement in the repo of which folders hold state and which do not

## Steps

- [x] Add the world folder to the Grab list in tools\Backup-Server.ps1 beside the data grab at :136, guarded by a Test-Path so a missing folder does not stop the run. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Backup-Server.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 132 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [x] Parse-check the script the way the pull request build does. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Backup-Server.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $e } else { 'parses' }
  ```
- [x] Take one backup and keep it somewhere that is not a shared drive and not the repo. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Backup-Server.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- [x] List the new zip and confirm it carries entries under game/world and is much larger than the 195 KB the 15 September copies were. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $zip = (Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Backups\*.zip' | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName; py -c "import zipfile,sys;z=zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]);n=z.namelist();print(len(n));print([x for x in n if x.startswith('game/world')][:5])" $zip
  ```
- [x] Register a daily scheduled task on the VPS that runs the same collection locally, encrypts the result and pushes it off the box to storage that is not the VPS, keeping seven daily and four weekly. (patrick)
- [ ] Rehearse one restore onto a throwaway box and write down exactly what you typed, because an untested runbook is not a backup. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  $zip = (Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Backups\*.zip' | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName; pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 -Zip $zip -Root C:\Thornswood-Restore-Test -NoTask
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the newest copy can be fetched from a machine that is not the VPS, which is the only thing that makes it off-box. (patrick)

## Commands

- Runs the same parse check the GitHub build workflow runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Backup-Server.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $e } else { 'parses' }
  ```
- Pulls a backup off the VPS with the world folder now included. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Backup-Server.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- Takes the newest backup zip, counts its entries and proves the world folder is in it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $zip = (Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Backups\*.zip' | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName; py -c "import zipfile,sys;z=zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]);n=z.namelist();print(len(n));print([x for x in n if x.startswith('game/world')][:5])" $zip
  ```
- Restores the newest backup onto a throwaway root without registering a scheduled task. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  $zip = (Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Backups\*.zip' | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1).FullName; pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 -Zip $zip -Root C:\Thornswood-Restore-Test -NoTask
  ```

## Done when

A fresh zip lists entries under game/world and is far larger than 195 KB, a throwaway server started from it resolves its load order (Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:128-138 refuses and names the missing plugins otherwise) with a character from the backup present, and the newest copy can be fetched from a machine that is not the VPS.

## Traps

The zip holds the bot token, the Discord client secret and the register secret, which is why the script's own warning at :245-247 exists: encrypt it, keep it off shared drives and out of the repo, and never put a path and a password in the same message. The world folder is live while the server runs, so a copy taken without stopping may be torn; take it from a stopped window or accept that and prove the restore. Do not add a twenty-third copy of the StrictHostKeyChecking=no pattern here. Everything in this script reaches the VPS, so a person runs it.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask how the nightly task on the VPS is registered
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/new-scheduledtasksettingsset the settings object, including the execution time limit a long backup needs
- https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/ the restic documentation index, for an encrypted deduplicating backup tool with its own retention, if you would rather not write the loop
- https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/030_preparing_a_new_repo.html setting up the off-box destination, which is the half that makes this a real backup
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.archive/expand-archive unpacking a backup zip for the restore rehearsal

issues.title: A mismatched session carries on behind a red caption, and the launcher never compares positions at all
issues.body:
**Order:** 143 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Old number:** 40

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · skymp5-client loadOrderVerificationService.ts:33-41, 60-75 (a caption, no disconnect); tools\app\Verify.cs:84-131, 240-283 (name check only) · VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:2493-2508

## What is known

Refuse the session and say why in one sentence. Have the front plugin send its sixty names with size and CRC on first update and the gamemode refuse. On the launcher side, derive the client's full list and compare by position; it already holds the manifest, the headers and the list. Raised in priority on 17 September: a tester's screenshot of the mining bug shows this caption on screen, which means he was playing a mismatched session and every custom object on his machine could resolve to something else. So this does not only break sessions, it poisons the bug queue, and nothing on screen tells the person to stop and press Fix. Until it refuses, treat any report from a session showing that caption as unusable DONE ON THE BRANCH patrick/progression, commit c301f91, and it was bigger than this entry knew. The runtime Thornswood's folder runs is not only another server's bundle. Measured against the fork's build output and against the pre-overlay backup that launcher keeps in the Steam copy: MpClientPlugin.dll, SkyrimPlatform.dll, SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll, the CEF host, the bundle and TESModPlatform.pex are each a third version in Thornswood's folder that matches neither the fork nor the backup, that launcher's builds of all of them, and none of the six is in Vortex's deployment manifest, so none ever came from the collection. OwnGame copied them from the Steam copy on every rebuild and Patch-Client patched the bundle by text. So Thornswood has been shipping another server's native SkyMP client, not just its JavaScript, which bears on entry 25 directly. WHAT SHIPS NOW: the six files the fork builds that differ from upstream, 18.2 MB, and nothing else, because the other 85 files the build produces are byte for byte what is already there. tools/New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1 records them by hash against the fork commit into tools/client-build.json and refuses a bundle with no THORNSWOOD PATCH block or any marker from another lineage; tools/Sync-Client.ps1 copies them from the fork's dist into the game folder and refuses any file that is not the recorded one, with -Check reporting without copying; Go.ps1 runs it beside the overlays and the plugins; Ship runs the check and refuses a release whose client is not the recorded build; OwnGame.Foreign never takes those six paths from the Steam copy, with their own reason in WhyLeft; the launcher's Client row tests for THORNSWOOD PATCH and still accepts the old prefix so an install mid transition is not blocked; Ship-Rules treats a recorded path as ours by hash. Patch-Client.ps1 is deleted: all four of its blocks are in the fork's source since 94cfd550, one of them having never been needed. Binaries are not in git; the record is, which is the same pattern as server-build.json. THE LAST UPSTREAM-LINEAGE FILES are Data/Platform/UI/build.js and index.html, the SkyMP front that our overlays inject into. The fork does not build skymp5-front, and swapping build.js blind would break the chat and the names above heads, so it stays for now and is named here so nobody thinks it was missed. NOT DEPLOYED. Sync-Client has run as -Check only: all six differ, nothing copied, because copying changes what the next Ship packs and that belongs in the dev sequence, in this order: Sync-Client, Ship -Channel dev, play on dev. 28 assertions on the rewritten Ship-Rules function, the launcher compiles with no new warnings. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Half of the title is stale. The launcher DOES compare positions against the server's own manifest (tools/app/Verify.cs:139-157, using LoadOrder.GameOrder and FirstMismatch) and compares size and crc32 per plugin (:303-345), and both are blocking issues. The manifest is published with mods, filtered to plugins, at gamemode.js ~10940-10965. The session refusal does not exist, even though steps 3 and 4 are marked done. The fork's skymp5-client/src/services/services/loadOrderVerificationService.ts still only paints 'LOAD ORDER ERROR' (the catch block after the positional loop) and never disconnects. The front plugin only writes thornswood-loadorder.txt to disk (thornswood-front.js:4999-5039) and sends nothing to the server. That file reaches the site through the log collector (Discord.cs:508). gamemode.js has no comparison against a client list: its only mp.kick calls are at :10697 and :19346, for other reasons. There is no unit check. The trap about Patch-Client.ps1 is stale too: that script is deleted, and the client is built from the fork and recorded in tools/client-build.json. NEXT STEP: Two routes; pick one in #dev first. (A) In the fork, loadOrderVerificationService.ts: on a mismatch, unless ignoreLoadOrderMismatch is set, show one sentence and end the session instead of leaving a caption. Rebuild the client, run New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1 and Sync-Client.ps1, and add a test that feeds an altered list. (B) Server side: the front plugin computes a digest of getModName plus sp.getFileInfo size and crc32 on the first update and sends it over the chat relay (page, then the voice service on 7778, then the gamemode). The gamemode compares it with a digest of its published manifest and calls mp.kick with one sentence on a difference.
