The comparison is a pure function, so a tools/test-load-order-refusal.js harness can feed it an altered list and assert a refusal. B avoids a client rebuild but touches three components. Either way, run node --check tools/gamemode.js. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn choose the route in #dev (a fork client change or a server-side refusal). They also decide whether an in-session kick is still wanted now that the launcher refuses Play on the same mismatch. A person on dev confirms nobody with a correct install is refused.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:2490-2560`: the whole manifest block: the comment is the best account anywhere of why the client-side check was doing nothing, and the code below it is the fix
- `tools\app\Verify.cs:84-133 and 220-283`: the positional pass and the size and CRC pass that already exist, so you do not rebuild them
- `HANDOFF.md:20-27`: the confirmation that the byte check is live, which dates the rest of this row
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js:866`: tellServer, where a refusal message would be sent from

## Steps

- [x] Read the correction before you write anything: Verify.cs already compares positions at :122-133 and bytes at :240-283, and the red caption is the signature of a failed manifest lookup rather than proof of a mismatched session. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Verify.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 118 -First 18 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [x] Confirm on the live server that /api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json now answers with a non-empty mods array; if it does, the caption people have been ignoring should already be gone and this row changes shape. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  curl.exe -s http://<host>:3000/api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json | Select-Object -First 5
  ```
- [x] Have the front plugin send its plugin names with size and CRC on first update, and compare them server side against the manifest tools\gamemode.js already generates at :2520-2560. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2516 -First 47 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [x] Refuse the session with one named sentence on a mismatch instead of letting it continue, and show it through tellServer at thornswood-front.js:866 once the note channel lands. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 862 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [x] Leave the .esp, .esm and .esl filter on the republish alone: gamemode.js:2515-2519 records that one bsa entry shifts every position after it and turns a healthy install into a red load order error. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2511 -First 11 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Write a unit check that feeds a deliberately altered plugin list into the comparison and asserts a refusal rather than a caption. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --test .\tools\
  ```
- [ ] Syntax check the gamemode before any deploy. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- Shows the first lines of the server's published manifest, so you can see whether the mods array is empty. curl.exe and Select-Object, because PowerShell 7 has neither a curl alias nor head. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  curl.exe -s http://<host>:3000/api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json | Select-Object -First 5
  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the refusal is added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Runs the node test runner over whatever test file you put the comparison check in. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --test .\tools\
  ```
- Prints both lists in full over ssh, read only, so the manifest can be compared by eye. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Manifest.ps1 -Full
  ```

## Done when

curl against /api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json returns a mods array with filename, size and crc32 for every plugin rather than an empty list or a 404, and a unit check that feeds an altered plugin list into the comparison asserts a refusal rather than a caption.

## Traps

This row's premise is stale, so anyone acting on it as written will spend the day reimplementing Verify.cs. The manifest is compared positionally against Game.getModName, which is plugins only, so do not remove the extension filter from the republish. Verify.cs's positional check only runs when the counts are equal and no other issue was found, so a missing plugin masks a reorder, and that is the better target. skymp5-client.js is not built here, so a change inside loadOrderVerificationService means a block in Patch-Client.ps1, not an edit to a source file you will not find.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp the client whose load order verification service paints the caption
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status/404 the status the client was getting from gateway.skymp.net, which is why the list came back empty
- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:Mod_File_Format why light plugins get no index, which is what makes positional comparison delicate
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#-check the parse gate for the gamemode change

issues.title: The rule that keeps other servers' files out decides this one is ours because we patched it
issues.body:
**Order:** 150 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Leftovers · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 216

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\New-GameFolder.ps1:205-206 classifies the bundle as Thornswood's if the file contains the text thornswood, and the only five occurrences in it come from Patch-Client's own blocks · tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:150 returns not-foreign for skymp5-client.js outright, with the assumption written out at :103-104

## What is known

A test that passes because of something we did to the file is not a test. Identify the bundle by a recorded hash of the upstream build it came from, not by grepping for our own name. This is the same blind spot as Djinn's Steam copy showing a Thornswood menu, and it is why entry 16 went unnoticed for weeks MEASURED AND THE CIRCULARITY IS CONFIRMED, 20 September. The shipped bundle contains exactly five case-insensitive thornswood strings and all five are comments Patch-Client.ps1 wrote: two on the locked door and chest handling, the _thornswoodLock catch, the launcher picking the character, and the Expert not Legendary difficulty pin. Nothing else in the file is ours. Meanwhile it carries 21 daedric markers. So New-GameFolder.ps1 calling it Thornswood's because it contains the text thornswood is true only because we wrote that text into somebody else's build. THE HASH TO PIN, now that both sides exist: Daedric's patched bundle as shipped is sha256 7c756d052d2e94258ff026f222cae7ab67ee20eebd6b8f7b8b7fda611a7f456d, and a bundle built from our own fork today is 9ecaae46b885808a42a8c2abc544c8fb. Recording the one we actually intend to ship and refusing anything else is the fix, and it wants doing in the same change as entry 20 rather than pinning a hash for a bundle we are about to stop shipping. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Both files the entry names changed. tools/New-GameFolder.ps1 no longer exists: it was deleted in c301f91 'Our own SkyMP client, and the other servers gone from everything we control'. tools/Ship-Rules.ps1:157-176 no longer greps for our name. It loads the six paths from tools/client-build.json, and Test-ShipOtherServer returns not-foreign for them first thing. Identity by hash is enforced where it matters: Ship.ps1:510-519 calls Sync-Client.ps1 -Check and dies unless every recorded file matches its recorded sha256, and Publish-Update.ps1:905-930 checks again. I proved the done-when in the scratchpad. The six recorded files were copied into a fake game folder and Sync-Client.ps1 -Check -Game <scratch> returned exit 0 ('every recorded file is already in the game folder'). After one byte of skymp5-client.js was flipped, it returned exit 2 ('differs 1,417,521 b Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js'), which is the code Ship.ps1:513 turns into Die. git status afterwards shows the repo unchanged. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: I agree with part of the claim. tools/New-GameFolder.ps1 was deleted in c301f91, and nothing that runs still identifies the bundle by our name. Checks.ClientPatched (tools/app/Checks.cs:527-552) still holds the "THORNSWOOD PATCH"/"Thornswood:" text search, but nothing calls it; that is dead code to delete. I reran the reviewer's proof in the scratchpad. I copied the six recorded files from C:\Thornswood\Game, and `Sync-Client.ps1 -Check -Game <scratch>` exited 0. After flipping one byte of skymp5-client.js it exited 2 ("differs"). Ship.ps1:510-519 turns exit 2 into Die. The launcher's ClientRuntime.Wrong/Heal (tools/app/ClientRuntime.cs:153-184, 237, 365, 384) also compares against the recorded sha256. It has been in launcher releases since a4acb90 (#108). Some of the done-when is still not true, and some of the reviewer's evidence is wrong: 1. Ship-Rules.ps1 still does not check by hash. The entry's step was to change the ownership rule there to ask whether the file's hash matches a recorded build. Test-ShipOtherServer (tools/Ship-Rules.ps1:176-178) returns not-foreign on the path alone (`if ($ShipClientFiles.Contains($rel)) { return $false }`) and never reads the file. A one-byte-altered bundle, or another launcher's bundle at that path, is still classified as ours. The outright return the entry complained about is still there. It now comes from a path list instead of being hard-coded. 2. The installer path has no hash check at all. Package-Thornswood.ps1:360-366 ships any file at the six recorded paths "ours by record" by path. Its only guard (:389-404) is that all six are present, and it never calls Sync-Client or compares a sha256. Worse, :113-119 builds out of the Steam copy when run with -Vortex or when C:\Thornswood\Game has no SkyrimSE.exe. In that case another launcher's skymp5-client.js and DLLs would go into the installer without a word. That is exactly what this entry and CLAUDE.md say must not happen. 3. The reviewer said "Publish-Update.ps1:905-930 checks again". It does not. Those lines only check that the six files exist (`$missingClient`). The zip is then built from whatever bytes are in the game folder and named with the recorded forkCommit, with no hash compare (:917-944). Run through Ship it is covered by Ship's Sync-Client gate. Run on its own, it publishes a client-runtime zip named for the recorded fork commit without checking its bytes. What is left: make Package-Thornswood refuse unless `Sync-Client -Check` passes (or check the six sha256s against client-build.json). Put the same hash check in Publish-Update's client-runtime block. Delete the dead Checks.ClientPatched. Publish-Update is on the do-not-edit-without-a-#dev-line list. A branch exists, patrick/todo-128-client-by-hash, not merged: These carry over from the author's report and are not needed for this entry's done-when. They are not on the To Do List yet. 1. When Publish-Update.ps1 is run on its own, its client-runtime zip block (around :927-941) copies the six files without hashing them. Ship covers this through the Sync-Client -Check gate. 2. The older "client runtime is incomplete" refusal in Package-Thornswood.ps1 uses throw, which stops Ship itself. It should be Die, like the new refusal above it. 3. test-ship-lists.ps1 -Before c32b820 has 2 failures that were there before this change too, because MarketplaceTextures.bsa became leave-alone after c32b820. 4. After merge the launcher changed (Checks.cs, ClientRuntime.cs), so it goes out through Ship -Channel dev. Say in #dev when it lands: a pack or installer built over a client that is not the recorded build now leaves that file out or stops, where before it shipped it silently. Push, pull request and merge are not done: this run was barred from them. NEXT STEP: Close it. It was superseded by the fork client build, client-build.json, Sync-Client.ps1 and the Ship gate. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: Checked on origin/main at c13ada9. Part of this is done. tools\New-GameFolder.ps1 is gone. Ship.ps1:542-560 runs Sync-Client.ps1 -Check and stops unless every recorded file matches its sha256, and the first reader showed that a copy with one byte changed fails that check (exit 2). The done-when is about the ownership test itself, though, and that test still does not look at the file's contents. Test-ShipOtherServer in tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:184-186 says "not foreign" as soon as the path is in client-build.json (`if ($ShipClientFiles.Contains($rel)) { return $false }`). It never hashes the file. The comment at :164-170 says these files are "ours by recorded hash", which is not what the code does. So a bundle with one byte changed, or another launcher's bundle at the same path, is still treated as ours. The entry's own step asked for Ship-Rules to be changed to a hash check, and that has not happened. The installer has the same gap. Package-Thornswood.ps1:229-257 keeps the six client files by path whatever else would leave them out. It never calls Sync-Client and never runs Get-FileHash on them. At :120 it builds from the Steam copy when run with -Vortex or when C:\Thornswood\Game has no SkyrimSE.exe. In that case another launcher's skymp5-client.js and DLLs would go into the installer without a word. Publish-Update.ps1:915-952 only checks that the six files exist ($missingClient). It zips whatever bytes are in the folder and labels the zip with the recorded forkCommit, with no hash compare, so run on its own it is not protected. The Ship route turns an altered copy away. The ownership rule this entry names still passes it, and so does the installer. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: Checks.ClientPatched in tools\app\Checks.cs (about lines 527-552) still searches for the text "THORNSWOOD PATCH", and nothing calls it. That dead code should be deleted, either as part of this entry or as its own line on the To Do List. The comment at Ship-Rules.ps1:164-170 says "ours by recorded hash". It should be corrected in the same change that makes the rule really check the hash. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #306. I merged origin/main (5a9ba5c) into patrick/todo-128-client-by-hash. The merge commit is 4e72a03, and a fix commit on top of it is 70cface. There was one text conflict, in Test-ShipOtherServer in tools/Ship-Rules.ps1. Main (#300, entry 127) had added the retired dresser rule on the line above the comment this branch reworded. I kept both: main's dresser rule as it was, then this branch's comment ("The bundle was decided by its hash above"). The merge also broke something that git did not flag as a conflict. Main's new Check-Secrets.ps1 (entry 236) asks Test-ShipMachine about every path inside ... STILL TO GO OUT: the dev Ship. Left: 1. Push the branch and update PR 306. I did not do this; the brief rules it out. 2. After merge, the launcher has changed (Checks.cs, ClientRuntime.cs), so it goes out through Ship -Channel dev. Say in #dev when it lands. 3. From the earlier author's notes, still open and not in this change: - Publish-Update.ps1:927-941 packs the client-runtime zip without hashing the files when Publish-Update is run on its own. Its entries have no game/ prefix, so Check-Secrets does not judge them either. - The older "incomplete" refusal in Package-Thornswood.ps1 uses throw where it should use Die. - The ...

## Read first

- `tools\New-GameFolder.ps1:196-208`: the ownership test, where :206 returns true if the file merely contains the text thornswood: the bug in one statement
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:99-152`: the foreign-file rules, the outright return at :150, and the assumption spelled out in the comment at :103-104
- `tools\Patch-Client.ps1:97-249`: the four Marker strings that are the only reason the ownership test passes at all

## Steps

- [ ] Put a line in #dev first: Ship-Rules.ps1 decides what never leaves a machine in a release, so a mistake here either leaks another server's files into a pack or excludes our own. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm the five thornswood hits in the shipped bundle are all ours: four Patch-Client Marker strings and the thornswoodLock identifier inside the locked-refs patch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js' -Pattern 'thornswood' -AllMatches | Measure-Object
  ```
- [ ] Record the SHA-256 of the bundle currently shipping in a file beside tools\Patch-Client.ps1 so it is reviewable, with a comment saying its provenance is unconfirmed and is entry 16's job. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js' -Algorithm SHA256
  ```
- [ ] Change tools\New-GameFolder.ps1:205-206 to ask whether the file's hash matches a recorded build rather than whether it contains our name. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\New-GameFolder.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 201 -First 8 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Change tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:150 the same way and update the comment at :103-104 in the same commit, because a wrong comment outlives a wrong line. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship-Rules.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 146 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Prove it offline: copy the bundle to the scratchpad, change one byte, confirm the ownership test now returns foreign or unrecognised, and confirm the unmodified bundle is still accepted. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Copy-Item 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js' "$env:TEMP\thornswood-check\bundle-altered.js" -Force
  ```
- [ ] Parse-check both scripts the way the pull request build does, and do not run Publish-Update.ps1 or any Deploy script to test this. (claude)
  ```powershell
  foreach ($f in '.\tools\New-GameFolder.ps1', '.\tools\Ship-Rules.ps1') { $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path $f), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $f; $e } else { "$f parses" } }
  ```
- [ ] Send it out: the dev Ship. (patrick)

## Commands

- Sums every occurrence of our name in the bundle rather than the lines holding one; it reads 5 today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $p = 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js'; (Select-String -Path $p -Pattern 'thornswood' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches.Count } | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
  ```
- Produces the recorded hash that replaces identity-by-grep. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js' -Algorithm SHA256
  ```
- Makes the scratch copy that gets one byte changed for the refusal test. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Copy-Item 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js' "$env:TEMP\thornswood-check\bundle-altered.js" -Force
  ```
- Runs the pull request build's parse check over both edited scripts. (claude)
  ```powershell
  foreach ($f in '.\tools\New-GameFolder.ps1', '.\tools\Ship-Rules.ps1') { $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path $f), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $f; $e } else { "$f parses" } }
  ```

## Done when

A one-byte-altered copy of the bundle is classified as foreign or unrecognised while the unmodified bundle is still accepted, and both scripts parse.

## Traps

Ship-Rules.ps1 decides what never leaves a machine, so a mistake here either leaks another server's files into a pack or excludes our own, and Publish-Update.ps1 next door is on the do-not-edit-without-#dev list. Getting the pin wrong in the strict direction stops Ship at the build step, which is the correct failure but will surprise whoever ships next, so say in #dev when it lands. This is one fix and entry 16's rebuild is another: do not combine them in one pull request.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/get-filehash the cmdlet that replaces the grep, with the algorithm names it accepts
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.sha256 what SHA-256 gives you over a name match, in one page
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.management.automation.language.parser.parsefile the parser the build check uses over every script in tools
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/about-workflows what a GitHub Actions workflow is and what triggers it, so you know what red on the pull request build would mean here

issues.title: You load in naked, get dressed twice, and one unknown item in your pack makes the server strip you for the rest of the session
issues.body:
**Order:** 151 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Old number:** 217

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · the shipped bundle: applyEquipment does removeAllItems, unequipAll, removeAllItems before dressing you, called at wait(1) and wait(1.3) and again later · VPS · game server · ActionListener.cpp:306-316 rejects the whole equipment update if the client's pack holds any id the server does not have, then orders an unequip of every newly worn item · confirmed in logs\server.log:72 · the word equipment appears zero times in gamemode.js

## What is known

FIXED AND LIVE, 21 September 05:18 UTC. The server was built out of the fork at 2943c910, which is the commit that stops one unknown worn item taking everything else off with it. tools\Build-Server.ps1 was written for it, the binary came out 5,573,632 bytes at sha256 10865561b4f039081c8e1c8152f09722ebe737b93379e737843ea4c6dfa0ba3a, and the build script confirmed it differed from the one that was there, which is what says the change is actually in it. It was put on the DEV server first and proved there before it went anywhere else. Then Publish-Server took it live at 23:18 local with nobody online, the last session having ended an hour earlier. The live log now reads: armour slot conflict check is off, equipped spell must be server granted: no, an unknown worn item refuses the whole update: no, it is dropped and the rest is kept. The hash on the box matches the recorded one exactly. STILL TO CONFIRM WITH A PERSON: log out wearing armour and a weapon, log back in, and see that they are still on. Nothing in the log can prove that half. MEASURED PROPERLY, LATER THE SAME NIGHT, AND IT CORRECTS THE PARAGRAPH BELOW. Patrick: 'that's a lie because this was a chac5gerther made after we removed the kits also when I went to my inventory none of it actually went in it'. He was right on both counts and the earlier reading here was inference, not measurement. Get-Logs was run and the live server.log read. WHAT THE LOG ACTUALLY SAYS: 24 refused equipment updates across two days, and every single one of them is the SAME item and the SAME reason, 'inventory does not contain item 13790', on every character within seconds of spawning. 0x13790 was read out of Skyrim.esm rather than looked up: it is IronWarAxe. Skyrim Unbound is in the load order and hands out starting gear inside the client's own game, which the server never sees happen, so the first equipment update a new character sends names an item the server has no record of, and upstream throws the WHOLE update away for it and breaks out of the loop. WHY THAT EMPTIES THE PACK, which is the part that was missing: the server's equipment record then stays empty for the whole session, and on spawn the client's applyEquipment in skymp5-client/src/sync/equipment.ts does removeAllItems, unequipAll, removeAllItems and then sets the pack to the worn set it was handed, which is nothing. remoteServer.ts calls that four times, at wait(1), wait(1.3), immediately and wait(0.3). So the pack is emptied and refilled and emptied again in a second and a half. That is 'it flashed all of the old starter stuff going into my inventory' AND 'none of it actually went in it' AND 'I came in with no clothes on', all one defect and not three. CORRECTION TO WHAT WAS WRITTEN HERE EARLIER TONIGHT: the two switchable checks are NOT the cause. The log prints 'armour slot conflict check is off' at every start, and the server only prints that when the setting is present, so equipmentSlotCheckEnabled was already set by hand on the VPS. Nothing in the repo set it, which is still worth fixing because a fresh install loses it, and that is commit bf12806. equipmentSpellCheckEnabled prints nothing and has genuinely never been set. Neither fired here. FIXED IN THE FORK, branch thornswood/engine-changes, commit 2943c910: the inventory check becomes a third setting, equipmentInventoryCheckEnabled, and with it off the unknown item is DROPPED from the update and everything else is kept. The item is still not granted; it simply no longer vetoes the rest. Two details that were nearly wrong and are written into that commit: the incoming Equipment had to become a copy rather than a const reference because SetEquipment stores that object itself, and the kept entries are copied whole rather than rebuilt from a base id and a count because an entry carries the worn flag and that flag IS the equipment update. tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 and tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 write the setting, commit c277644; an unknown key in server-settings.json is ignored, so that is safe to ship ahead of the build. NOT COMPILED. The build was refused on this machine, so the C++ is checked by reading only: Equipment is an aggregate of an Inventory and four optionals and copies by default, Inventory::entries is a public vector, and unordered_set is already included in ActionListener.cpp. IT HAS TO BE BUILT BEFORE IT DOES ANYTHING. ALSO STILL TRUE AND NOT FIXED: the shipped client bundle carries THORNSWOOD PATCH eleven times, so the upload filter this entry once said was missing HAS shipped. And applyEquipment replacing the whole pack with the worn set is upstream's design, not a bug we introduced; dropping the unknown item is what stops it biting, but a client that asked for the pack it already has rather than being handed a replacement would be the better answer one day. THE ORIGINAL TEXT: MEASURED AND HALF FIXED, 20 SEPTEMBER EVENING. PATRICK, having just rejoined an existing character: 'I came in with no clothes on even though I left the last time with equipment on', and then the rule he wants: 'there shouldnt need to be a script to equip me with cloths starting chacrthers should have the default boots and tunic and whatever they had on after the last time they left should stay equioped armour, clothes, weaopns, sheilds, spells, etc'. THE CAUSE IS NEITHER OF THE TWO THIS ENTRY NAMED. Measured tonight: the shipped client bundle at C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js carries THORNSWOOD PATCH eleven times, so the upload filter this entry says is missing HAS shipped, and that half is done. The real cause is that the server refuses an equipment update outright in two places and on a modded load order both fire constantly. equipmentSlotCheckEnabled is the gear strip: OnUpdateEquipment ORs together the biped slot flags of everything worn, refuses the whole update the moment two items share one bit, and sends an UnequipItem for every item involved, and vanilla Skyrim already uses slots 44 to 47 while every cloak, scarf and backpack mod reaches for the same free-looking ones. equipmentSpellCheckEnabled refuses any spell the server did not itself grant and sends a RemoveSpell back, which is every spell learned from a tome in the world. BOTH WERE MADE SWITCHABLE IN OUR OWN FORK AND BOTH STILL DEFAULT TO TRUE in WorldState.h:277-278, and nothing in this repository had ever written either setting, so the switches were built and never once thrown. FIXED, commit bf12806: Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 writes both as false into server-settings.json, and Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 sets them in place on the dev box the same way it already sets the voice port, and reads them back. WHY THE GAMEMODE CANNOT DO THIS JOB INSTEAD, which this entry asked for: EquipmentBinding.cpp has a Get and no Set, so the server can read what somebody is wearing and cannot write it. It does not need to. MpChangeForm carries an equipment field and MpChangeForms.cpp writes it to the world save, so what is worn already persists, on the one condition that the update was accepted. Those two settings are that condition. The starting clothes are already right: giveShift hands over the roughspun tunic and the footwraps with worn: true on both, which is exactly the default boots and tunic Patrick asked for, and they never stayed on for the same reason nothing else did. STILL TO PROVE, and it needs the dev server up: deploy, relog, and check the server log no longer carries 'rejected equipment update'. THE ORIGINAL TEXT, kept because it is the record of what was believed: Three links. The strip is SkyMP's design, and the shortcut that would avoid it is switched off for the customer actor by form id and needs a setting only Daedric's gamemode sets. Nothing dresses you back because the gamemode never stores equipment, so the server hands back an empty set. Then the client uploads its whole pack unfiltered, one unrecognised id poisons every update after it, and the server unequips you. Fix the upload filter first, which is the patch already written in your own source and missing from the shipped bundle, then make the gamemode own equipment. The armour test cannot catch any of it: it has no relog step and both re-apply loops sleep while the inventory is open THE TEST HAS ITS RELOG STEP NOW, commit af6f5ee, and it is deployed to the site. TEST 4 quits to the desktop, comes back, and looks before touching anything, and it asks which of the two failures it was: nothing worn, or nothing in the pack. TEST 5 got the same step, because a spell the server did not grant used to come straight back off your hand and only leaving and returning shows it.  HALF OF THIS IS DONE, 23 September. The dropped-item half: the fork keeps the equipment update and drops only what the server has no record of, and the dev log shows it working, "kept the equipment update and dropped 4 item(s) the server has no record of: 1397e, 13790, 1397d, 3b562", which are Skyrim Unbound’s starting gear handed out inside the client’s own game. The naked half is entry 27 and is done. WHAT IS LEFT is that those four items are invisible to everything server side for ever: they cannot be counted for warmth, worn back on after a relog, or traded. Either the client stops being handed them, or the server learns about them at spawn. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The equipment half is fixed and working. The live logs/server.log (pulled 23 Sep 11:21) reads 'an unknown worn item refuses the whole update: no, it is dropped and the rest is kept' on every start. Its last OnUpdateEquipment line (10:20:38) is 'kept the equipment update and dropped 4 item(s) the server has no record of: 1397e, 13790, 1397d, 3b562'. There is no 'rejected equipment update' line. Dressing is fixed too. 0e2488a (#185), b3ca7f7 (#186) and 437bfd6 (#187) are on main. logs/dev/thornswood.log shows 'login ff000003 put 2 worn thing(s) back on' on four logins and 'dress ff000003 wearing nothing with 2 worn thing(s) in the pack, put back on'. tools/test-new-character.js: 26 passed, 0 failed. What the entry says is left: the four ids are Iron Dagger (1397e), Iron War Axe (13790), Iron Arrow (1397d) and Long Bow (3b562), named from tools/recipes.json. I measured that all four are referenced inside C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Skyrim Unbound.esp (2, 2, 3 and 3 times), so they are Unbound's starting kit, handed out inside the client's own game. The b3ca7f7 commit body calls not granting items the server does not know deliberate, 'the line between dressing somebody and letting a client mint items'. NEXT STEP: Once Patrick picks, either route is a small gamemode change with a node harness. (a) The server learns the kit at a new character's first spawn: giveShift in tools/gamemode.js also grants 1397e, 13790, 1397d and 3b562 in Unbound's counts, so the server's pack matches the client's and the items can be traded and worn after a relog. (b) The client stops holding them: an edge-triggered updateOwner script, like the dressing one, removes those four from the new character's own inventory at first spawn, so client and server agree on an empty kit. (c) Unbound's start gear is switched off in the collection, which is a Nexus change. After either (a) or (b), test-new-character.js gets checks, and the dev log should stop printing 'dropped 4 item(s)'. The relog half of the done-when still needs a person: log out wearing armour and a weapon, log back in, and still be wearing them. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's decision: does a new character keep Skyrim Unbound's starting weapons, which the server would then grant, or lose them? Separately, a person has to do the relog test in the game.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-client\src\sync\equipment.ts:82-116`: the fix is already written here and its comment explains the whole failure: sumInventories makes a count negative, the server's count is unsigned, one negative number kills the message
- `C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-server\cpp\server_guest_lib\ActionListener.cpp:295-450`: the reject at :306-316, the slot-flag strip at :318-399 with its equipmentSlotCheckEnabled gate, and the unequip diff at :421-448, which is where the strip actually happens
- `tools\gamemode.js:304-318 and 369-394`: ensureProperties and the inventory reads, where making the gamemode own equipment starts; the word equipment appears nowhere in that file today
- `tools\docs-app\data\tests.md:45-56`: TEST 4 'Armour stays on', six steps and no relog, which is why a green test is not evidence

## Steps

- [ ] Log out of the live server wearing armour and a weapon, log back in, and see what is still on. The only part a log cannot answer. (patrick)
- [ ] Add a relog step to TEST 4 in tests.md. DONE, commit af6f5ee, deployed. (claude)

## Commands

- Counts the patch marker in the shipped bundle; it reads 0 today, which is the fact the entry rests on. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $p = 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js'; (Select-String -Path $p -Pattern 'THORNSWOOD PATCH' -CaseSensitive -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches.Count } | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
  ```
- Reports which blocks are not applied to the bundle in the game folder, and changes nothing. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check -Game 'C:\Thornswood\Game'
  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the equipment property is added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Copies the bundle to the scratchpad and parses the copy without running it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:TEMP\thornswood-check | Out-Null; Copy-Item 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js' "$env:TEMP\thornswood-check\skymp5-client.js" -Force; node --check "$env:TEMP\thornswood-check\skymp5-client.js"
  ```
- Returns nothing today and must return the new property afterwards. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'equipment'
  ```

## Done when

You log out wearing armour and a weapon, log back in, and you are still wearing them. The log carries no 'rejected equipment update' line. Nothing flashes into the pack and then vanishes.

## Traps

The gear-diff shortcut in the shipped bundle is opt-in and excluded for the person's own character by form id, so setting rpNetTuning.gearDiff would not help. TEST 4 as written cannot fail on this bug, and both re-apply schedulings sit behind a guard that skips while the inventory, favourites, magic, container or crafting menu is open, which is precisely when a tester is looking. server-settings.json on the VPS holds secrets and is named by location only. This is the widest blast radius in the slice: three pull requests and one coordinated release, not one change.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/tree/main/skymp5-server the server source that holds ActionListener.cpp and ScampServer.cpp
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/tree/main/skymp5-client the client source that holds sync/equipment.ts, the fix already written
- https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html unsigned integer reads, which is why one negative count kills the whole message
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#-check the parse gate for the gamemode and the patched bundle
- https://thornswood.net/known what the server owns, as a customer reads it, which is the list equipment should join

issues.title: The shipped female body is the fully nude mesh with genital shapes, and the build script puts it back every time it runs
issues.body:
**Order:** 157 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** World · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 221

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · Game\Data\meshes\actors\character\character assets\femalebody_0.nif and _1.nif hold three shapes, 3BA, 3BA_Anus and 3BA_Vagina, with zero matches for Bra or Panty · Your PC · tools\Add-Bodies.ps1:192-193 says every NeverNude and Underwear option is left out on purpose · the male body was rebuilt as the covered HIMBO build on 6 March

## What is known

Everything needed is already on disk: the NeverNude slider set is installed, it writes to the same two filenames, and the underwear textures come out of vanilla Skyrim's own archive. One BodySlide build, no download, no plugin, no movement in the load order, so it ships in a normal release rather than as an optional pack, because a pack is opt-in and anyone who skips it stays nude. Take the first-person meshes from the Underwear option in the same pass, and change Add-Bodies so the next run does not undo it MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The shipped meshes are unchanged. femalebody_0.nif and femalebody_1.nif in C:\Thornswood\Game\Data are 2,007,574 bytes, dated 21 Mar 2021. Both contain 3BA_Vagina and 3BA_Anus and neither contains Bra or Panty. The NeverNude slider set is on disk (SE 3BBB Amazing NeverNude.osp exists). The entry's route no longer fits settled design. Profile\OwnGame\files.txt records femalebody_1.nif and 1stpersonfemalebody_1.nif as 'L|V', hard links from Vortex, and fsutil reports 4 links on each. Writing a BodySlide build over them would change Vortex's own staging files, which CLAUDE.md forbids. Publish-Update.ps1:326-352 never packs Vortex-deployed files, so a rebuilt mesh in Game\Data would not ship either. tools/Add-Bodies.ps1 (Data = Root\Game\Data, line 44) is from before the own-game-folder design and pours archives straight over those links. It is still wired into tools/Run-Everything.ps1:57. NEXT STEP: This goes through the collection, not this repo. Patrick picks the covered body (for example the 3BA NeverNude or Underwear option, built or prebuilt), puts it in the Nexus collection, and the next collection revision carries it to everybody the way every other mesh arrives. Afterwards the entry's own shape check can be run read-only on the rebuilt game folder: the ASCII search of femalebody_1.nif for Bra, Panty, 3BA_Vagina and 3BA_Anus. A repo-side follow-up, only if agreed in #dev: retire or fence off Add-Bodies.ps1 and its Run-Everything.ps1 step, because running it now writes into Vortex-linked files. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides whether the requirement is covered (NeverNude keeps the shapes underneath) or removed. He makes the change in the Nexus collection, which is his account and a visual BodySlide build. Retiring Add-Bodies.ps1 needs a line in #dev.

## Read first

- `tools\Add-Bodies.ps1:189-230`: :192-193 is the decision being reversed, in the script's own words, and :220-223 shows how the covered HIMBO build was done for men
- `C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\CalienteTools\BodySlide\SliderSets\SE 3BBB Amazing NeverNude.osp`: it names the two sets to build and confirms they write femalebody with GenWeights, the same two filenames
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1`: to confirm meshes under Data ship normally and that nothing here is classified as another server's file

## Steps

- [ ] Read tools\Add-Bodies.ps1:189-230 so you can see the decision being reversed and the male precedent from 6 March in one place. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Add-Bodies.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 185 -First 48 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Ask in #dev whether the requirement is that the 3BA_Vagina and 3BA_Anus shapes are covered or gone, because the NeverNude set keeps them underneath the Bra and Panty; if they must be gone, this is the wrong slider set. (patrick)
- [ ] In BodySlide, select CBBE 3BBB Amazing NeverNude (or the UniBoob variant, pick one and stay with it), choose the preset the current body uses, tick Build Morphs so RaceMenu sliders keep working, and build. (patrick)
- [ ] Take the first-person meshes from the same Underwear option in the same pass. (patrick)
- [ ] Edit tools\Add-Bodies.ps1: rewrite the comment at :191-194 so the covered option reads as deliberate, and add the NeverNude folder to the CBBE PourArchive list at :195-205 so the next run does not put the nude build back. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Add-Bodies.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 187 -First 10 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Read the shape names out of the new mesh and confirm Bra and Panty are present while 3BA_Vagina and 3BA_Anus are still there, which is expected rather than a failed build. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $s = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\actors\character\character assets\femalebody_1.nif')); foreach ($n in 'Bra', 'Panty', '3BA_Vagina', '3BA_Anus') { '{0}: {1}' -f $n, $s.Contains($n) }
  ```
- [ ] Parse-check the script and ship it in a normal release rather than an optional pack, because a pack is opt-in and anyone who skips it stays nude. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Add-Bodies.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $e } else { 'parses' }
  ```

## Commands

- Reads the shape names straight out of the mesh, which is the build check without starting the game. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $s = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\actors\character\character assets\femalebody_1.nif')); foreach ($n in 'Bra', 'Panty', '3BA_Vagina', '3BA_Anus') { '{0}: {1}' -f $n, $s.Contains($n) }
  ```
- Confirms both weights were written and the timestamps moved. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Item 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\actors\character\character assets\femalebody_0.nif', 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\actors\character\character assets\femalebody_1.nif' | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime
  ```
- The parse check the pull request build runs over the edited script. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Add-Bodies.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { $e } else { 'parses' }
  ```

## Done when

The new femalebody_1.nif reports Bra and Panty present, both weights have new timestamps, and tools\Add-Bodies.ps1 lists the NeverNude folder so a rerun cannot put the nude build back.

## Traps

The biggest trap is that Add-Bodies.ps1 silently undoes this on its next run, so the mesh build and the script edit are one change and must not be split across releases. The NeverNude set covers the 3BA_Vagina and 3BA_Anus shapes rather than removing them, so somebody has to say which of the two the requirement is before the build. No plugin changes, so the load order does not move and this can ship in an ordinary release. The meshes under Data may be Vortex hard links, so writing over them touches the staging copy too, which is expected. Everyone gets identical meshes by design, so this is all-or-nothing across every machine.

## Links

- https://github.com/ousnius/BodySlide-and-Outfit-Studio the tool that builds the meshes and reads the slider set
- https://github.com/ousnius/BodySlide-and-Outfit-Studio/wiki the BodySlide and Outfit Studio documentation wiki, for what the build options do
- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:File_Format_Conventions why shape names are readable as plain ASCII inside the nif, which is what the check relies on

issues.title: The quick favourites menu crashes the game, and the first fix went into the wrong folder
issues.body:
**Order:** 160 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Djinn

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · Profile\MyGames\SKSE holds six crash logs from 18 and 19 September and they are the same crash down to the address · Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll v1.1.1 · tools\New-GameFolder.ps1, Test-KeptOut · CORRECTED 19 September: the fix went into New-GameFolder.ps1, which builds Keizaal's and Daedric's folders, not Thornswood's. Thornswood's is built by the launcher in tools\app\OwnGame.cs. The 21:51 crash log still has InventoryInjector.dll v1.1.1 loaded and the same fault.

## What is known

MEASURED FROM THE CRASH LOGS, 19 September. All six are EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION executing 0x0000656D6167, which is the four characters "game" being called as code. The return address at the top of the stack is InventoryInjector.dll+0x3AA85 and R13 holds that library's own Hooks::IconSetter::ProcessListFunc, with FavoritesMenu and MagicFavorites in the live objects beside them. Inventory Interface Information Injector calls through a freed pointer while it is building the favourites list. What frees it is this server: SkyMP rebuilds the character's inventory from the server's copy after an equip, and the Papyrus VM in every log has a TESModPlatform.Add queued at the moment of the fault, so items were being written underneath the menu as it was drawn. THE FIX on branch djinn/favourites-menu-crash is to stop shipping the library: it is the code that faults, it is not built here, 1.1.1 from 2023 is its last release, and nothing else in the build asks for it (the string InventoryInjector appears in no other SKSE plugin, moreHUD, moreHUD Inventory Edition, Crafting Categories and QuickLoot IE included). What goes with it is the icons its JSON files add to inventory rows, the I4 Icon Addon and nothing else. No plugin is enabled or disabled, so the load order does not move and the server manifest is untouched. A second, separate bug found in the same place is on branch djinn/favorites-menu-name: thornswood-front.js asked Ui.isMenuOpen for "Favorites Menu" and Skyrim's name is "FavoritesMenu", so for as long as somebody had Q open our own plugin believed no menu was open at all, and the magic menu was missing from that list outright. ALSO FOUND, not fixed: the bundle applies a server inventory update to a reference on the next frame at onUpdatePropertyMessage with no menu guard, while the periodic apply for your own character thirty lines away does wait for isBadMenuShown. That is the same crash class for containers and belongs with entry 20. WRONG FOLDER, corrected on branch djinn/i4-out-of-the-right-folder. 52af856 put the exclusion in New-GameFolder.ps1. That script builds Keizaal's and Daedric's folders, which its own header says; Thornswood's folder is built by the launcher, in OwnGame.cs. So nothing was removed: the crash log from 21:51 on 19 September, after 1.1.53, has InventoryInjector.dll v1.1.1 still loaded and the same fault at 0x656D6167 with FavoritesMenu and MagicFavorites on the stack, and the source path and "Running IconSetter.processList hook" visible in the stack strings. Worse, the change would have taken the library out of two other servers' folders, which are not ours to edit, so it is reverted byte for byte. The exclusion now sits in OwnGame.Skip beside the Creation Club one; a file already in the folder goes on the next refresh, because the sweep at the end removes anything in the record that the pass did not take and that came from Vortex. Compiled with the Framework csc, 48 files, exit 0. ONE DETAIL CORRECTED: I4IconAddon.esp IS a plugin and it is in the load order at FE:5. It stays loaded and inert once the library is gone, so the load order still does not move, but the earlier wording said no plugin was involved and that was wrong. AND THE FOLDER HAS TO BE REBUILT: shipping the launcher does not delete the file by itself. Settings, Maintenance, Thornswood's own Skyrim folder, Refresh. THE REPO HALF IS DONE AND WAS ALREADY DONE, measured 20 September; what is left is a person. The exclusion lives in tools/app/OwnGame.cs:627-628, skipping both Data/SKSE/Plugins/InventoryInjector.dll and anything under the InventoryInjector folder, put there by 5f88499 after the first attempt went into New-GameFolder.ps1, which builds Keizaal's and Daedric's folders rather than ours. On disk now: the dll is gone from C:/Thornswood/Game and the newest crash log anywhere is crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38, which predates the fix shipping. So two of the three conditions in the done-when are met. THE THIRD IS NOT MINE: a tester opens Q, equips a favourite, opens Q again, and the game does not close. Until somebody does that this stays open. WORTH RECORDING: a grep for InventoryInjector limited to ps1, json and md finds nothing and reads as though nothing enforces this. The enforcement is in C#. Search the whole tree. AND THE PAUSE ITSELF LEAKED, reported by Djinn 20 September: 'the Q favorite menu that was pausing the game in Thornswood is still lingering and causing that to happen while playing Keizaal'. That is a second fault in the same place and it has its own entry below; this entry is still the crash and the library. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The repo half is on main and has shipped. tools/app/OwnGame.cs:564 skips 'it crashes the quick favourites menu', and CrashesUs at :602-607 matches Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll and the InventoryInjector folder. The fix landed as c024f7a (#82). The favourites menu name fix is in: tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js:854 and :3886 use 'FavoritesMenu' and list 'MagicMenu'. Measured on disk: Test-Path C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll is False. The InventoryInjector folder is there but holds 0 files. Profile\MyGames\SKSE now holds only two crash logs. crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38 is the pathing one (entry 140). The new crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59 has no InventoryInjector in its module list and no FavoritesMenu. It is a different crash: a read of 0x168 with BSFaceGenMorphDataHead and BrowsMaleHumanoid05 on FishingInSkyrim.esp's NPC 'Rybek Kupiecski' 0x30025905. So there is no favourites crash since the fix. No plugin log (thornswood-front.log, thornswood-input.log) shows the favourites menu being opened, so nothing proves the Q test has been done. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change in the repo. When a person has opened Q, equipped a favourite and opened Q again without a crash, check that no new crash log appears in Profile\MyGames\SKSE, then close it. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A tester in the game on the current build: open Q, equip a favourite, open Q again, and confirm the game stays up. Separately, the new 22 Sep facegen crash needs its own To Do entry. It is neither this crash nor 140's.

## Read first

- `Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-19-16-14-35.log, the first forty lines`: the faulting address, the InventoryInjector frames, and FavoritesMenu and MagicFavorites in the relevant objects; the other five say the same
- `tools\New-GameFolder.ps1, Test-KeptOut`: what is left out of the build and why, with the date, so it can be put back when the reason goes
- `Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js, applyEquipment and isBadMenuShown`: the inventory being torn down and rebuilt after an equip, which is what leaves the menu holding freed entries
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, KEYBOARD_MENUS`: the menu name that was off by a space, which is the second bug on the same menu

## Steps

- [x] Read the six crash logs and see that they are one crash. Done 19 September. (claude)
- [x] Check that nothing else in the build needs the library before taking it out. Done 19 September: no other SKSE plugin names it. (claude)
- [x] Keep it out of the game folder, with the reason and the date written where the next person will find them. Done on branch djinn/favourites-menu-crash. (claude)
- [ ] Decide whether losing the I4 Icon Addon's inventory icons is acceptable. It is the only thing that goes with it. (patrick)
- [ ] Merge both branches and ship one complete release, then have a tester open Q, equip a favourite, and open Q again. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm the library is gone from the built folder after the release. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Test-Path 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll'
  ```

## Commands

- The six crash logs side by side, showing they are one crash and not six. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-*.log' -Pattern 'Unhandled exception|InventoryInjector|FavoritesMenu'
  ```
- False after a release built with the change is what done looks like. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Test-Path 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\InventoryInjector.dll'
  ```
- Parses the build script, which is what the pull request build check does. (claude)
  ```powershell
  powershell -NoProfile -Command "[void][ScriptBlock]::Create((Get-Content -Raw .\tools\New-GameFolder.ps1))"
  ```

## Done when

After a release built from the corrected branch AND a refresh of the game folder, Test-Path on InventoryInjector.dll in the built folder answers False, a tester opens Q, equips a favourite and opens Q again without the game closing, and no new crash log appears.

## Traps

The game folder is built from what Vortex deployed, so the library is still in the Steam copy and still in the collection; only Thornswood's own folder loses it. New-GameFolder removes a file it placed itself only while that file is unchanged, so a copy somebody edited by hand stays and keeps crashing. This is a change to what ships, so it goes out as one complete release, and it is worth a line in #dev because it takes a mod out of everybody's game. Do not chase this in our own plugins: nothing in tools\ts-plugins can reach the favourites list or the library that faults. Do not put a Patch-Client.ps1 block on the inventory apply for your own character either; that path already waits for the menu, and the write that lands under the menu is a Papyrus call queued a frame earlier, which no guard in the bundle can recall.

## Links

- https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/85702 Inventory Interface Information Injector, the library being taken out, last released 2023
- https://github.com/alandtse/CrashLogger the crash logger that wrote the six logs, and how to read its stack and register sections
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp the client that rebuilds the inventory after an equip, which is what leaves the menu holding freed entries

issues.title: A second crash, in the pathing thread, unrelated to the favourites one
issues.body:
**Order:** 162 · **Wave:** 2 This week · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** work it out, medium

## Where it lives

Patrick's machine · report thornswood-20260919-1947.zip, crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38.log · launcher 1.1.53, C:\Thornswood\Game, 49 seconds into the session

## What is known

Not the favourites crash and must not be filed with it. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION executing 0x0128EEC171E0, an address on the heap rather than the ASCII "game" the favourites one always lands on, and the live objects are the pathing system: BSPathBuilder, PathingRequest, PathingCell, PathingDoor, PathingLockData, BSPrecomputedNavmeshInfoSearch, on a worker thread under BSWin32TaskletManager. No script extender plugin appears in the probable frame; EngineFixes is on the stack twice but only from the stack scan. Crashed 49 seconds in, which is about when a fresh session finishes spawning everybody. Pathing crashes on a SkyMP server are usually about how many actors are in the cell at once, and ActorLimitFix is installed, so its setting and the server's spawn count are the first two things to read. One report is not a pattern: this needs a second occurrence before anybody spends a release on it. CANNOT BE CLOSED BY ANY AMOUNT OF WORK RIGHT NOW, and its own done-when says so: either a second pathing crash arrives and this entry names a cause measured from both, or a month of sessions passes without one and it is closed as a one-off. One report is not a pattern. Checked on 20 September: the newest crash log anywhere on this machine is still crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38, which is the favourites one from entry 31, so no second pathing crash has arrived and the clock is running. Nothing to do but wait and keep the reports. The two things to read WHEN a second one arrives are already named above: ActorLimitFix's setting and the server's spawn count. AND ITS LOG IS ON THIS MACHINE TOO: Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38.log, found 23 September. EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION trying to EXECUTE memory at 0x0128EEC171E0, which is a jump into data rather than a bad read, with BSPrecomputedNavmeshInfoSearch, PathingDoor, PathingCell, BSPathBuilder and PathingLockData on the stack. So the pathing thread was walking a door when it went, which matches what this entry says and now has a file behind it. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: There is still only one pathing crash. Profile\MyGames\SKSE holds crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38 (execute at 0x0128EEC171E0, with BSPrecomputedNavmeshInfoSearch, PathingDoor, PathingCell, BSPathBuilder, PathingLockData and PathingRequest at lines 18-26) and crash-2026-09-22-20-48-59. The second is not pathing: it reads 0x168 at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF, with BSFaceGenMorphDataHead, BSFaceGenNiNodeSkinned and BrowsMaleHumanoid05 on FishingInSkyrim.esp NPC 'Rybek Kupiecski' 0x30025905, 4 minutes in. This pass did step 2, reading the two numbers together. Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\ActorLimitFix.json asks for moverLimit 100,000,000 (default 128) and morphLimit 10,000,000 (default 10), with replaceStaticArray true. ActorLimitFix.log (23 Sep 10:19:48) shows morphLimit clamped to 512 and moverLimit left at 100,000,000. Server side, tools/Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:513 writes npcEnabled true, so the server simulates every NPC in one shared world. b3b46ba means the gamemode spawns nothing of its own. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change on one report. Record the two numbers above on the entry. The clock started 19 Sep: close it as a one-off around 19 Oct unless a second crash with pathing objects arrives, and if one does, compare the two. Add the 22 Sep facegen crash to the To Do List as a new entry. Its first things to read are ActorLimitFix's morphLimit, now 512 against a default of 10, since the fault is in face morph data, and whether FishingInSkyrim.esp NPCs show up in other crashes. That is a hypothesis, not a measurement. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A second pathing crash from any machine, or a month of sessions without one. Both are time and play, not work.

## Read first

- `crash-2026-09-19-19-46-38.log, the first thirty lines`: the fault address and the pathing objects, which is the whole of what is known
- `Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\ActorLimitFix.json`: the actor limit in force, which is the first number to check against how many the server spawns

## Steps

- [ ] Keep the next crash log rather than deleting it. Two of these with the same pathing objects is a bug; one is an event. (patrick)
- [ ] Read ActorLimitFix.json and the server's spawn count together, and say in the entry what both are. (claude)
- [ ] Do not change anything on one report. (claude)

## Commands

- Every crash log with its fault line, so the pathing ones can be told from the favourites ones at a glance. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\MyGames\SKSE\crash-*.log' | ForEach-Object { '{0}  {1}' -f $_.Name, (Select-String -Path $_ -Pattern 'Unhandled exception' | Select-Object -First 1).Line }
  ```

## Done when

Either a second pathing crash arrives and this entry names a cause measured from both, or a month of sessions passes without one and it is closed as a one-off.

## Traps

Do not fold this into the favourites entry: different fault address, different subsystem, different thread. Do not read the stack-scan frames as a call stack; only frame 0 is marked probable here and it is the bad address itself. EngineFixes appearing twice is the stack scan finding its return addresses on a deep stack, not evidence against it.

## Links

- https://github.com/alandtse/CrashLogger how to read the probable-versus-stack-scan distinction in these logs
- https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/32349 Actor Limit Fix, whose setting bounds how many actors the pathing system is asked about

issues.title: A third crash, on dev 1.1.94.1: an access violation at SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D (Blade Da Razor, 25 September)
issues.body:
**Order:** 163 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

the staff sessions page, Blade Da Razor's red session on 25 September · the crash-*.log in it · tools/docs-app/server.js:1374 (the alert) and lineAround (the line it quotes)

## What is known

REPORTED 25 SEPTEMBER by the site's trouble alert: "A session went wrong. Blade Da Razor, on the dev build, launcher 1.1.94.1. something threw and nothing caught it", quoting Crash Logger's first line: Unhandled exception "EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION" at 0x7FF6AC81799D SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D, cmp r9, r12. NOT THE SAME ADDRESS as either crash on file: the FaceGen head crash is at SkyrimSE.exe+01AF7EF (entry 44), and the pathing one jumped into heap memory (the entry above). Nothing in the repo or on this list names +0CF799D. ONE ODD THING, worth reading the log for: the alert copies Crash Logger's line as it is (server.js lineAround, trimmed only), and cmp r9, r12 compares two registers and touches no memory, so that instruction cannot be what read the bad address. Either the fault was the jump to that address, or the code there changed while another thread ran it (a plugin patching the game at runtime does that); the registers, the stack and the probable call stack in the log say which. NOT READ YET: the whole crash log is on the staff sessions page, which a session here cannot open. What to read in it: the probable call stack (only SkyrimSE.exe, or SkyrimPlatform.dll, the SkyMP client or another SKSE plugin on it), the objects Crash Logger names in the registers, and how far into the session it went. One report is not a pattern. READ 25 SEPTEMBER, the whole log Patrick pasted (CrashLoggerSSE 1.24, crash time 24 September 22:47:42 on Blade's clock, 23 minutes into the session, E:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game, SkyrimSE.exe 37,157,144 bytes, which is 1.6.1170). NONE OF OUR CODE IS ON IT. The crashing thread is one of the game's own job threads (BSJobs::JobThread on the stack), and every frame, probable and scanned, is SkyrimSE.exe, KERNEL32, ntdll or KERNELBASE: Address Library ids 69378+0x1ED, called from 69380+0x361, from 69344+0x8A, from 68445+0x3D, the thread's start. No SkyrimPlatform, no MpClientPlugin, no SKSE plugin. THE FAULT DOES NOT ADD UP AS A SOFTWARE ONE. Windows says the thread tried to EXECUTE memory at 0x7FF6FEDED89D, while the instruction it stopped on is at 0x7FF6AC81799D (SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D), a register compare that cannot fault. The execute address is 1.3 GB past the start of SkyrimSE.exe, whose furthest object in this log is 50 MB in, and it is inside no loaded module. A fault address that is not the instruction's own, on an instruction that cannot fault, in the game's own code with nothing else on the stack, is most often an unstable machine (an overclock, a memory profile such as XMP, or heat) rather than a bug. One log cannot prove that. THE QUEST IN R9 IS MOST LIKELY A BYSTANDER: Crash Logger names any register that happens to point at a game object, and R9 held AWAconquest (0x1A000FEF, Solitude Arena.esp, not running, stage 0) while being compared with a pointer into the job system's own globals (R12, SkyrimSE.exe+32580C8), which is not quest code. Memory was not short: 19.6 of 31.8 GB in use, the game at 6 GB private. The log also says Hyper-V, which is how Windows 11 with Memory Integrity looks to it and is not a cause by itself. WHAT SETTLES IT is a second report: the same SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D and 69378 again means a real fault in the game's job system with something feeding it; a different address each time on Blade's machine means the machine. BLADE'S ANSWER, 25 September, through Patrick: the PC is overclocked "for sure" and he thinks XMP is on, and he was in a small village in the Rift when it went. That fits the reading above: an unstable machine rather than anything in the game or ours. Left open for a second report, which is what would say otherwise.

## Steps

- [x] Open the sessions page, find Blade Da Razor's red session, and paste its whole crash log into a session here. (patrick)
- [x] Ask Blade what they were doing when it went: where, what they had just pressed, who was near. (patrick)
- [x] Read the log: the call stack, the registers and the modules. Done: only the game and Windows are on the stack. (claude)
- [x] Ask Blade: is the PC overclocked, or running a memory profile such as XMP, and do other games crash on it? Did it happen again? (patrick)
- [ ] On a second crash at SkyrimSE.exe+0CF799D from anybody, look up ids 69378, 69380 and 69344 in the Address Library and name the job it was running. (claude)

## Done when

A second crash at the same address names a cause in the game's job system, or Blade's machine is found unstable, or a month passes with no second report and it is closed as a one-off.

## Traps

Do not file it with entry 44 or the pathing crash on the strength of both being access violations: the address is different, and entry 44 already records three crashes that looked alike and had three causes.

## Links

- https://thornswood.net/sessions the sessions page, staff sign in
