issues.title: Identity on the game server is a number the client picks, so anyone can be anyone, including the admin
issues.body:
**Order:** 167 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Security · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 15

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · offlineMode set by tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:185 · tools\gamemode.js:2274-2296, 2362-2392, 3097-3108 (admin is a hardcoded id) · Everyone's PC · tools\app\AutoJoin.cs:247-260

## What is known

The server never takes identity from the client. Either SkyMP's non-offline flow, or a short-lived signed token from the site after Discord sign-in, verified before the actor is bound to a profile. Admin becomes a role on a verified identity rather than a number in the source. Every other control is keyed on this, so fixing it makes all of them real at once MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: In-world identity is still a claim. The fork's offline login (C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\skymp5-server\ts\systems\login.ts:233-237) emits spawnAllowed with gameData.profileId unchecked, and Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:469 writes offlineMode true. admins() still falls back to the hardcoded 816507994 (gamemode.js:19198-19205), and the comments at gamemode.js:18664-18672 and 19230-19238 still call the profile id a claim. Voice has real proof: /token (voice-server.js:727-760) mints an HMAC token after the site's /api/play/owns answers, and onJoin (:392-424) takes the id from the token. But AUTH defaults to 'log' (voice-server.js:520, Install-Voice.ps1:46), so unproven joins keep the id they claim. commands.push (:932-937) also drops the proven flag, so handle() (gamemode.js:18194) cannot tell the two apart. NEW HOLE, found reading the code: /api/play/join (server.js:2150-2157) adds any profileId to the caller's linked list without checking whether another Discord account holds it. /owns checks the caller's own list first (server.js:2531-2533). Every profile id is broadcast to every voice peer five times a second (voice-server.js:430-443). So any account with the play role can learn a victim's id, check it in, and get a PROVEN voice token for it. Commands and chat-log lines then carry the victim's id as proven. Profile ids are crypto-random (Chars.cs:273-280), so first-claim-wins cannot collide by accident. A branch exists, patrick/todo-142-join-owner-check, not merged: 1) The site change and the launcher change have to reach people together, and in a set order. thornswood.net is shared by the dev and live launchers. With the holder check live, any launcher without Chars.EnsureSpare files a relinked install's next New character under the old account. main's site did not do this: there, B's check-in shared the id. So the launcher carrying this fix must be live, or go out in the same sitting, before Deploy-Docs.ps1 publishes server.js. 2) The branch is 12 commits behind origin/main. It merges cleanly and the relevant tests pass merged, but it has not been merged. 3) Not pushed, no pull request opened. 4) Out of scope and unchanged, but part of entry 142's core problem: on a relinked install, B's menu still lists A's characters. They show without names, and B can pick one and be let in on A's standing, because identity is still a number the client picks. 5) The To Do List was not edited: entry 142 should record this rollout order, and that the launcher half is on this branch. NEXT STEP: Doable now, one branch each: (1) tools/docs-app/server.js /api/play/join: refuse, with 409 'somebody else', a profileId that another Discord id already holds in linked.json, using the same loop /owns uses at :2535-2542. Add tools/test-play-join.js, which lifts the block out of server.js the way test-bans.js does. Cases: an unclaimed id is recorded; an id you already hold is recorded; somebody else's id is refused and not written. (2) tools/voice/voice-server.js:932: queue proven: !!(me && me.proven) with each command. In tools/gamemode.js handle(), refuse the playtester-gated branches (/tp, /goto :18662; /give, /spawn ~:18770) when cmd.proven is false, with a named reason. Harness it by calling handle() with fabricated commands. (3) gamemode.js:19204: return [] instead of the hardcoded id, so admin comes only from thornswoodAdmins and the site's adminProfiles. node --check on all three files. Left for Patrick: read the UNPROVEN lines and then run Install-Voice.ps1 -Auth on (production). The game connection itself needs a signed token in the client's gameData, verified in login.ts:233 before spawnAllowed. That is a fork, client and engine change to how the client connects, so it needs a #dev line first. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn agree in #dev on the connection-level token (fork login.ts plus client gameData, an engine release). Patrick flips the production voice service to -Auth on after reading its UNPROVEN lines. A RELINKED INSTALL LOSES VOICE ON NEW CHARACTERS, found 24 September by the review of the check in fix (branch patrick/todo-142-join-owner-check). The launcher keeps its character list per install, not per Discord account. So when a second person links a different Discord account on the same install, the spare and the played characters all stay on the first account in linked.json, a new character made from the spare stays there too, and the voice service asks /owns, gets no, and answers 403 not your profile: that person has no proximity voice on a character they made. The game still starts. Patrick decides: the launcher mints a fresh spare when the linked Discord id changes (Chars.cs and Discord.cs, a launcher release), or staff move the character. And Shell.CheckIn still logs that it checked a character in when the site answers claimed false; Standing and Discord.Join do not read claimed yet. 24 SEPTEMBER: BUILT on patrick/todo-142-join-owner-check (5ef9b34) and held, not merged, for a decision. An account counts as having left only when Discord says it is not in the server, it is not in bans.json and it is not on Discord's own ban list; only then does a new account get the old one's ids. While the old account is still in the Discord, the new one has no voice on characters made under the old one, and the door lets those characters in only on the old account's standing. Patrick decides that trade, or asks for an admin action on the hub that moves an id between accounts. The site and launcher halves go out together (Deploy-Docs.ps1 and a dev Ship). 25 SEPTEMBER: patrick/todo-142-join-owner-check (5ef9b34, with fcf4b10) existed only on Patrick's disk. Pushed to GitHub, still held and not merged, waiting on the same decision.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:2910-2930`: the comment that already describes the whole attack in four sentences: the profile id this arrives under is a claim and not a fact
- `tools\app\AutoJoin.cs:230-300`: SetProfileId, which writes the profile number into a plain settings file on the person's own machine
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:404-430 and 1240-1300`: the Discord sign-in and the ticket reply, the only component in the system that already knows who somebody is and therefore where a token is minted
- `tools\gamemode.js:3097-3108`: admins(), which reads cfg.thornswoodAdmins first and falls back to a hardcoded id, so the number in the source is a fallback rather than the whole list

## Steps

- [ ] Start this in #dev: it is a large coordinated release across launcher, gamemode and site, and one of the two options changes how the client connects, which CLAUDE.md settles is not built here. (patrick)
- [ ] Read tools\gamemode.js:2910-2930 and tools\app\AutoJoin.cs:230-300 so you can see the identity is a number in a file the person owns. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2906 -First 27 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add a route to tools\docs-app\server.js beside the existing sign-in that, for a signed-in person, returns a short-lived token carrying profileId, an expiry and an HMAC over both, keyed on a secret the game server also holds. (claude)
- [ ] Verify that token in tools\gamemode.js before an actor is bound to a profile, in the same place the door sweep runs at :2358-2392, and refuse rather than kick. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2354 -First 41 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Change admins() at :3097 to read a role out of the verified identity instead of matching a number, keeping cfg.thornswoodAdmins as the transition. (claude)
- [ ] Pass the token through the same path AutoJoin already uses for the profile number, and do not keep the verified set in a module-level cache that survives a hot reload without being rebuilt. (claude)
- [ ] Write the mint and the verify as two small functions and unit test them in node: an expired token fails, a token whose profileId is edited fails, a valid one passes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --test .\tools\
  ```
- [ ] Syntax check the gamemode and the site. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- Runs the node test runner over the token mint and verify tests. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --test .\tools\
  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the token verification lands. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Parses the site after the mint route is added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\docs-app\server.js
  ```
- Compiles the launcher after AutoJoin carries the token. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- Brings the server log down so a refusal with a named reason can be read after the change is live. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Get-Logs.ps1 -Lines 4000 -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

The mint and verify unit tests pass on all three cases, node --check passes on the gamemode and the site, the launcher compiles, and in the world a client with a hand-edited profileId and no token is refused with a named reason in thornswood.log while /tp from that identity does not run.

## Traps

This is the entry every other control depends on: the door, moderator powers, moderation, the character register and voice identity are all keyed on the same number, so fixing it makes them real and leaving it makes them decoration. Say that when you hand it over. gamemode.js is hot reloaded with mp.clear() first, so do not cache the verified set across a reload. Turning offlineMode off instead would change how the client connects and needs a matching client change, which CLAUDE.md settles is not built here. This needs the problem, the approach and what it touches in #dev before any code.

## Links

- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519 the token shape this is reinventing, including the expiry claim and why signature verification comes before use
- https://nodejs.org/api/crypto.html#cryptocreatehmacalgorithm-key-options the HMAC the token is signed and verified with on both sides
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/oauth2 the sign-in the site already has, which is the only place identity is actually known
- https://nodejs.org/api/test.html the built-in test runner behind node --test, for the three token cases
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#-check the parse gate for both files

issues.title: The Discord ticket, a thirty day credential as good as identity, is sent in clear HTTP every time a character is made
issues.body:
**Order:** 169 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Security · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 17

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Creation.cs:670-684 · VPS · voice · the /choose route

## What is known

A choose route on the site over HTTPS that checks the ticket and relays to the voice service over loopback, which is already the shape of the owns route in the other direction. Take the ticket out of the choose body. The launcher protects it with DPAPI on disk and then puts it on the wire in the clear PART DONE 24 September, pull request #223. WHAT CHANGED: Voice.FetchToken in tools/app/Voice.cs now sends the Discord ticket only when the voice address it posts to starts with https:// (case-insensitive). For any other address it sends nothing, returns no join token, and writes to the log: "Voice: no join token, because the voice address is not https and the Discord ticket only goes over https. Voice may be refused." Before this, VoiceBase fell back to http://address:7778 whenever VoiceUrl was empty. That covers a new install until its first update check and the feed's deliberate rollback. In both cases FetchToken posted the ticket in the clear. A new harness, tools/test-voice-ticket.ps1, takes the real FetchToken and JsonEscape text out of Voice.cs, compiles it against stubs, and points it at a loopback socket that records every byte it receives. MEASURED: The change is 20 added lines in tools/app/Voice.cs, just after the url is built (line 561) and before the body is built. The check is at Voice.cs:577-581. Before the change: tools/test-voice-ticket.ps1 run against the old Voice.cs (git show HEAD saved to the scratchpad) gives 10 passed, 8 failed under both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. In the old code the ticket reached the raw http port and came back with a token, both with an http base and with no config (conf null). After the change: 18 passed, 0 failed under both pwsh and 5.1. Nothing connects to an http address, including one written in capitals and one with https later in the path. An https address is still asked for a token (the socket saw a TLS connection). The ticket never shows up in readable bytes. The "not linked to Discord" path is unchanged. Build-Launcher.ps1 into $env:TEMP\ts-build-144 exit 0 and produced Launcher\Thornswood.exe (3,215 KB). The PowerShell parser finds 0 errors in the new .ps1. I confirmed the triage findings in the code: VoiceBase's http fallback is at Config.cs:67-75, and the empty voiceUrl rollback is at Shell.cs:4374-4378. Roster.cs:94 and every Discord.cs ticket post go to Discord.Site, which is https://thornswood.net (Discord.cs:54). A failed fetch is retried by RenewToken five minutes later (tokenGot set to now-25 minutes, checked on the 2 s tick at Voice.cs:971). The voice service's default THORNSWOOD_VOICE_AUTH is log (voice-server.js:520), so on the fallback paths the join goes through unproven rather than being refused. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick, after merge: none of this has gone out yet. It goes out with the launcher on the next dev Ship (.\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "..."). No site, voice or gamemode deploy is needed. Still open on entry 144, not done here: (1) Close the raw voice ports. tools/Caddyfile:27-30 still lists "only then THORNSWOOD_VOICE_BIND=127.0.0.1 and the two ports close" as not done. Install-Voice.ps1:39 defaults -Bind to 0.0.0.0, and nothing in the repo records the dev service's bind. This is VPS work for Patrick. (2) The doneWhen playtest: a character made against the dev server still gets its trade and town. Creation now happens on the K panel in game, so this can only be confirmed by testing. (3) The entry's title and todo still describe Creation.cs and /choose, which are gone (3aa37ef, c87da23). Someone with list access should reword it around the /token fallback. I did not edit the To Do List. Side effect to know about: while VoiceUrl is empty, voice joins go through unproven. With THORNSWOOD_VOICE_AUTH=log that is allowed and logged. If it is ever set to on, voice is refused on the rollback path. That is the intended trade: no voice proof rather than the ticket in the clear.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Creation.cs:670-700`: the whole Send path: the plain http URL built at :679, the comment at :681-684 saying what the ticket proves, the ticket read at :686 and put in the body at :689
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:30-40 and :342-392`: the /choose route and the comment saying it cannot be locked to loopback because every launcher calls it from its own machine
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:1364-1381`: /api/owns, the same shape in the other direction, including the 503 on a failed lookup at :1378-1379; this is the route to copy
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:410`: ServicePointManager.SecurityProtocol = (SecurityProtocolType)3072, the TLS 1.2 line the new call has to repeat

## Steps

- [ ] Confirm what /choose the VPS is actually running before touching the caller, because entry 7 says the deployed voice service is not tools\voice\voice-server.js and changing a caller against unread code breaks character creation for everybody. (patrick)
- [ ] Open tools\app\Creation.cs at 670-700 and list everything in the body besides the ticket, which is profileId, trade, half, cls and town, so the new site route accepts exactly that set. (claude)

- [ ] Add an /api/choose route to tools\docs-app\server.js modelled line for line on /api/owns at :1364-1381: read the ticket the way readTicket already does, answer 503 when the lookup failed, and relay the choice to 127.0.0.1 on the voice port with no ticket in the relayed body. (claude)

(claude)

  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 406 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Prove no plain HTTP is left in the file and that all three components still build. (claude)

  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Creation.cs -Pattern 'http://'
  ```
- [ ] Hand the branch over for a pull request; the ticket value never appears in a log line, a commit or a test output. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Start the branch this fix lives on. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/choose-over-https
  ```
- Prints the whole Send path so the body's fields and the plain http URL are visible in one read. (claude)




## Done when

Select-String for 'http://' in tools\app\Creation.cs returns nothing, node --check passes on server.js and voice-server.js, Build-Launcher.ps1 produces Thornswood.exe, and a character made against the dev server still gets its trade and town while the request body carries no ticket string.

## Traps

Shipping this before entry 7 is resolved breaks character creation for everyone, because the /choose running on the VPS may not behave like the file in this repo. Creation.cs is C# 5 only, and the natural way to write a new URL is string interpolation, which will not compile. issues.title: A moderator has no powers in the game at all
issues.body:
**Order:** 170 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** RP fit · **Effort:** change it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 16

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:2862-3060 (the whole command set is /ooc, /where, /roll, /help and admin-only /tp) · VPS · bot · tools\discord\bot.py:676

## What is known

goto and bring, freeze, mute, kick, temporary ban, an observe mode, and a note written against a person's record. That is the baseline every roleplay server opens with. A moderator watching somebody break rule 9 at midnight currently has nothing to press but a Discord role the game never reads. Enforcing who may connect at all is entry 30; this row is the kit for somebody already in the world MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The command list (WORDS, gamemode.js:17579-17613) has /tp and /goto, both place teleports (:18662), plus /give and /spawn for playtesters, and /restart refused from chat (:18750-18770). There is no bring, freeze, kick, timed ban, observe or note command. A server-side mute was deliberately not built (gamemode.js:21886-21897). The gates are isAdmin, isDev and isPlaytester (:19198-19290), which read written lists plus the site's adminProfiles, devProfiles and profiles. No moderator tier exists anywhere: the door stores only profiles, devProfiles and adminProfiles (gamemode.js:10528-10566). Commands arrive under a claimed profile: voice AUTH defaults to 'log' (voice-server.js:520) and the queue drops proven (:932-937). Any play-role account can also claim someone else's profile number through /api/play/join (server.js:2157; see 142). NEXT STEP: Once decided: the site returns modProfiles for the agreed Discord role, the door writes it, and the gamemode gets isStaff. Carry proven through the command queue (142) and require it. Then one branch per command: /goto <person> and /bring <person> reusing the locationalData move in the /tp branch (~gamemode.js:18735); /freeze; /kick using mp.getUserByActor plus mp.kick as the door does; a timed ban written to the site's bans.json; notes kept where the site can show them under /sessions. Each action is mirrored to the staff channel from tools/discord/bot.py. Each command gets a harness that calls handle() as staff and as non-staff. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn settle in #dev which Discord role counts as staff, where a note against a person lives, and that this arrives as several branches. 142's proven identity has to land first.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:2863-3066`: handle(), the whole command surface, so a new command follows the same shape: it is dispatched from a queue, not from a chat packet
- `tools\gamemode.js:2916-2931`: /tp, which is the teleport half of goto and bring already written, plus the comment saying the profile id is a claim and not a fact and the isAdmin refusal at :2928-2931
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:495-523 and :410-419`: slash lines are queued on the voice socket and the gamemode polls the loopback-only GET /commands, so no moderator command works while voice is down
- `tools\gamemode.js:3097-3115`: admins() and isAdmin(), the only gate that exists today, which is a list of numbers
- `tools\discord\bot.py:676`: @tree.command(name='close'), the only staff command the bot has, and the place a mirrored record would be written from

## Steps

- [ ] Take this to #dev first and get it settled between Patrick and Djinn: what the staff role is, where a note written against a person lives, and the agreement that this arrives as several branches rather than one, because CLAUDE.md asks for one fix per pull request and a Claude does not settle a design question here. (patrick)
- [ ] Agree with Patrick that entry 15 lands first, because every command below is keyed on a profile id the client chose and gamemode.js:2917-2927 already says so in its own comment. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2913 -First 17 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Read handle() at tools\gamemode.js:2863-3066 and write down the four things every existing command does: resolve the profile, find the actor, do the work, answer through toProfile. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2859 -First 210 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add one command per branch beside the existing ones, each guarded by a role test rather than isAdmin's number list, starting with goto and bring since the teleport machinery at :2916-2970 already exists. (claude)
- [ ] Write a timed ban into allowed.json so the door at gamemode.js:2434-2438 picks it up, and remember it only bites when enforce is true, which is entry 5. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2430 -First 11 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Mirror every staff action into a Discord staff channel from tools\discord\bot.py so there is a record outside the game that a hot reload cannot lose. (claude)
- [ ] Parse both files and exercise each new branch with a Node harness that calls handle() with a fabricated command object, once as a non-staff profile and once as staff. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- One branch for the first command only; the rest get their own. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/moderator-goto-and-bring
  ```
- Parses the gamemode; a syntax error takes the live handlers down on hot reload. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Lists every place the old number-list gate is still used. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'isAdmin\('
  ```
- Compiles the bot after adding the staff-channel mirror. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -m py_compile tools\discord\bot.py
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/moderator-goto-and-bring
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

node --check passes on tools/gamemode.js, py_compile passes on tools/discord/bot.py, and a harness over handle() shows a non-staff profile getting "That one is not yours to run." while a staff profile reaches the action. In the world each command answers through toProfile and writes one line to thornswood.log.

## Traps

Every command here is keyed on profileId, which gamemode.js's own comment at :2917-2927 calls a claim and not a fact, so shipping this before entry 15 hands a stranger the moderator's kit by editing one number in a settings file. Commands arrive through the voice service, so the whole kit is unavailable whenever voice is down, and the deployed voice service is not the file in this repo. A ban in allowed.json only bites when enforce is true, which is entry 5.

## Links

- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/permissions how a staff role is actually checked, if the role test reads Discord rather than a local list
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits the budget for mirroring every staff action into a Discord channel
- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html the discord.py surface bot.py uses to write into a staff channel
- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html what a moderation record has to contain to be worth anything later
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/tree/main/skymp5-server the server this gamemode is loaded into, and its hot reload behaviour
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/gamemode.js handle() on main, for reading the command shape in a browser

issues.title: Nothing anybody says is written down, so every report is one person's word against another's
issues.body:
**Order:** 173 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Moderation · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 64

## Where it lives

VPS · voice · tools\voice\voice-server.js has seven log calls in total and none in the chat path · VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:3038 logs /ooc as heard by a count, with no text

## What is known

Keep text chat for a fixed window, thirty to ninety days is normal, and have a report pull the surrounding messages automatically so the moderator reads the actual exchange. This has to be in the privacy page from entry 33, and it is the thing that makes every other moderation control fair rather than arbitrary MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Most of it landed in 74155d1 and 6119b9e (#102). voice-server.js:145-190 appends one JSON line per message to chat/<day>.jsonl. That covers plain lines and slash commands, so /ooc text is kept too. It prunes whole days past THORNSWOOD_CHAT_DAYS, default 365. server.js:1111-1160 chatSlice shows a person's lines under their session on /sessions. node tools/test-chat-log.js: 23 passed; test-session-chat.js: 21 passed. Still open: (a) privacy.md:67-68 says 'Nothing ages them out yet', but voice-server.js:147,180-190 deletes days past 365, and Install-Voice.ps1:184 sets no THORNSWOOD_CHAT_DAYS. The page is wrong, and the entry asks for 30-90 days. (b) A session marked kept (/api/session-keep, server.js:~2690; pruneSessionLogs :966) is never pruned, but its chat lives in the voice folder and is deleted at the window anyway. (c) chatSlice filters to one profile (:1152), so a moderator sees one side of an exchange and not the room around it. (d) The comment at server.js:878-881 still says nothing records what anybody said. (e) Each line's proven flag can be forged through the /api/play/join hole described in 142. NEXT STEP: After Patrick picks the window: set it through Install-Voice.ps1:184 (THORNSWOOD_CHAT_DAYS) or the default at voice-server.js:147, and correct 'How long it is kept' in privacy.md to match. In server.js /api/session-keep, copy the session's chat slice into its session-log file, so a held session keeps its words past the window. If he wants it, add an 'everyone in this window' view beside the per-person chat on /sessions. Fix the stale comment at server.js:878-881. Extend test-session-chat.js for the kept copy and test-chat-log.js for the window. node --check both files. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick picks the retention window (365 today, 30-90 suggested) and says whether a moderator should see the other people's lines around a report. He decided the per-person layout on 22 September.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:486-535`: the chat branch and the comment above it explaining that chat rides the voice socket because adding a packet type to skymp5-client would mean recompiling it; the broadcast is the single line at :532
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:383-425`: the loopback-gated routes (/choices at :386, /claimed at :394, GET /commands at :410, POST /say at :420), which is the pattern a /chatlog route has to follow
- `tools\gamemode.js:2982-3040`: the /ooc handler, the only other place words are exchanged, which already counts hearers at :3038 without keeping the line
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:575-610`: where the other personal data already lives, because whatever window you pick has to be declared on the privacy page from entry 33

## Steps

- [ ] Pick the retention window with Patrick first, thirty to ninety days is normal, and get entry 33's privacy page written and shipped before a single line is written to disk, because this is personal data and the page is what makes keeping it legitimate. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm with Patrick what voice service the VPS is actually running, because entry 7 says it is not tools\voice\voice-server.js and a change here may never reach the running process. (patrick)
- [ ] Add a small appendLine(obj) helper to tools\voice\voice-server.js that JSON-stringifies one row per line to chat.log with fs.appendFile, and call it in the chat branch just before the broadcast at :532 with {at, profileId, name, text, cell}. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\voice\voice-server.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 528 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Roll the file the way entry 26 asks for the other services, chat.log to chat.log.1 keeping five, and make the roller enforce the window you picked rather than only a size. (claude)
- [ ] Add a loopback-only GET /chatlog?from=&to= beside the routes at :383-425, copying the isLoopback guard at :387 exactly, so staff can fetch a window without anybody reading the file by hand. (claude)
- [ ] Change tools\gamemode.js:3038 to log the text alongside the hearer count, so the second text path is not a blank either. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 3034 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Parse both files, then prove the write with two local sockets on a spare port: send one chat line and confirm chat.log gained exactly one JSON row holding the text and the profile id, then write past the size limit and confirm chat.log.1 appears and the sixth file is gone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/voice/voice-server.js
  ```

## Commands

- Start the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/chat-retained-for-reports
  ```
- Parses the voice service. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/voice/voice-server.js
  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the /ooc log line changes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Confirms the new /chatlog route carries the same guard as every other loopback route. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\voice\voice-server.js -Pattern 'isLoopback\(req\)'
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/chat-retained-for-reports
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

node --check passes on tools/voice/voice-server.js and tools/gamemode.js, a locally started service on a spare port with two connected sockets writes exactly one JSON line to chat.log for one chat line, that line carries the text and the profile id, and forcing the size limit produces chat.log.1 while the sixth file is gone.

## Traps

This cannot land before entry 33's privacy page says the log exists, how long it is kept and how to ask for deletion. The deployed voice service is not this file, so the change may not reach the running process at all. Everything a moderator would act on also depends on identity being real, which is entry 15: a log keyed on a profile number the client chose proves nothing. Do not put a disk write in the 200ms position tick; only the chat branch touches the disk.

## Links

- https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fsappendfilepath-data-options-callback fs.appendFile, the non-blocking write the chat branch should use
- https://nodejs.org/api/net.html the socket layer the two-socket local test drives
- https://gdpr-info.eu/art-5-gdpr/ storage limitation and data minimisation, which decide the window and the fields
- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html what to record per line and what never to record
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/voice/voice-server.js the chat branch and the loopback routes on main

issues.title: There is no way to ask anyone for help from inside the game, and no way to report a person from anywhere
issues.body:
**Order:** 177 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 46

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:2860-3066 (the full command handler) · VPS · site · tools\docs-app\server.js:1017-1038 (the report form takes idea or bug only) · VPS · bot · tools\discord\bot.py:284

## What is known

Every roleplay server ships a way to page an online moderator and a way to unstick a wedged character. A report sits one click from the thing being reported, attaches the surrounding messages, and tells the reporter it was received. Today the only route is opening a Discord ticket, which means leaving the game MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Neither command exists. The WORDS list (gamemode.js:17579-17614) and PLAYER_WORDS (17620-17647) have no /report or /stuck. The dispatch list (grep "if (word === '") shows /ooc at 18900, /roll at 18985 and /help at 19076, with no report or stuck branch. The site's /api/report (server.js:1818-1840) still stores kind as `o.kind === 'idea' ? 'idea' : 'bug'` at :1827. The inbox it writes to is shown to admins only (server.js:2583), and there is already a keyed /api/ticket route at :1843. The bot's ticket kinds include ('report','Report somebody') and ('help','I need help') at bot.py:394-395, so the entry's own correction still holds: a Discord route exists, and the in-game and site routes are what is missing. arrive() at gamemode.js:261 only builds a temple destination record; resolveArrival (~:284) is the thing /stuck would actually call. The bot's fallback that posts into the public panel channel is still live (bot.py:669-690), and that is entry 154, which has to land first. The gamemode already calls the site with the door key (gamemode.js:10773, /api/allowed), so a keyed report route is plumbing that already exists. NEXT STEP: After 154 lands. (1) tools/docs-app/server.js: add a keyed POST route, e.g. /api/report/game, checked with sameSecret against cfg.botKey the way /api/allowed does. It writes an INBOX row with kind 'report', from 'in game', the reporter's profileId and name, the target text, cell, position and time. Widen :1827 to accept 'report' as well. (2) tools/gamemode.js: add '/report' and '/stuck' to WORDS, PLAYER_WORDS and the /help text. The /report branch posts to that route using the door.json key and answers through toProfile ('Your report reached staff'); the answer says plainly that the profile id is the client's claim. /stuck is built to whatever Patrick decides: resolveArrival on the current position, a cooldown, refused while dead or in a fight. (3) New tools/test-report-stuck.js that extracts the handle() branches the way test-discord-members.js extracts functions, and asserts both branches reply through toProfile. (4) node --check on both files. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides: (a) what /stuck does: nearest consecrated ground via resolveArrival, a short nudge, or the home inn; the cooldown; and whether it is refused while dead, in combat or inside a claim, since it is an escape hatch. (b) Where staff are paged: the admin-only site inbox only, the staff #reports channel (Build-Discord.py:255) through the bot, and/or an in-game line to online admins from adminProfiles. Entry 154 has to land first. After that, a person on the dev server has to type both commands once.

## Read first

issues.title: The door's allow list stops refreshing somewhere past a hundred linked accounts, and one rate-limited lookup throws the whole list away
issues.body:
**Order:** 181 · **Wave:** 3 Identity and safety · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 57

## Where it lives

VPS · site · tools\docs-app\server.js:1316-1329 (a sequential await loop), :522-551 (no 429 handling) · VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:2434-2437, 2462 (a ten second timeout)

## What is known

Keep the membership in memory from the bot's gateway events rather than re-deriving it one account at a time on every refresh. The bot already has the members intent. Honour Discord's documented rate limit headers, and treat a partial failure as partial rather than discarding everything PART DONE 24 September, pull request #226. WHAT CHANGED: /api/allowed now sends a new field, failedProfiles: the profile numbers of every linked account whose Discord lookup failed. lookupFailed and lookupFailedWhy are unchanged. When the site names who failed and at least one profile came back, the gamemode door's refresh() writes the fresh answer for everybody else and gives each failed profile the standing it had in the old allowed.json: the same place in profiles, devProfiles and adminProfiles, and the same people row. So a failed lookup can no longer let anybody in or turn anybody away. The early return is still there. The door keeps its whole list when the site reached Discord for nobody, when the site is older than this change and does not name who failed, or when failedProfiles is empty. enforce is never touched. MEASURED: tools/test-allowed-failed.js takes the real /api/allowed route out of tools/docs-app/server.js and the real refresh() out of tools/gamemode.js. It runs the two together against made-up Discord answers and a made-up disk: five linked accounts, one of them rate limited, with a ban and a new tester arriving in the same refresh. On this branch: 39 passed, 0 failed. Against main's server.js and gamemode.js (HEAD c32b820, passed in through the SITE and GAMEMODE env vars): 21 passed, 18 failed, because the door writes nothing and the ban and the new tester both wait. I also ran both mixed pairs. With the new site and an old door the result is 25/14: the old door still sees lookupFailed true and keeps its whole list, which is what it did before, and it does not throw. With an old site and the new door the result is 21/18: there is no failedProfiles field, so the new door keeps its whole list, and the check 'a new door reading an old site keeps the whole list' passes. In both mixed runs every failure is the partial-write behaviour, which needs both halves deployed. The server.js changes are at the out object and the failed branch of the /api/allowed route (about lines 2440-2471). The gamemode.js changes are keepWhatFailed() (about 10743-10797), the early-return condition (about 10852) and the merge before the write (about 10889-10905). WHAT IS LEFT: These parts of entry 156 are not in this commit and are for Claude or Patrick. (1) discordGet (server.js, around line 649) still reads neither Retry-After nor x-ratelimit-reset-after. The triage plan is a module-level quiet-until time, set once per refresh and not a sleep for each account. (2) If the bulk /members?limit=1000 call is refused (Server Members intent off, a 403), memberOf falls back to one lookup per account. That brings back the burst and the risk of hitting the gamemode's 10 s timeout at around 100 accounts; the 100ms-per-call timing proof in doneWhen was not done here. (3) Keeping membership in the bot's gateway cache needs Patrick and Djinn to agree in #dev on which key the bot would POST with (entry 2's key rotation). (4) Patrick should read the live door and site logs from after #101 to see whether 'rate limited by Discord' still appears. Deploy order once merged: either half can go first, because both mixed pairs keep the old behaviour. Partial writes only start when both the site (Deploy-Docs.ps1) and the gamemode (Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1, then the live pair) are out.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\server.js:1292-1331`: /api/allowed and the block comment above it, which states the intended failure behaviour in the author's own words; the sequential await loop is :1317-1329 and the per-account skip is :1324
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:522-551`: discordGet: it does recognise 429 and resolves {ok:false, status:429, why:'rate limited by Discord'} at :546, but it never reads Retry-After, never retries and never backs off
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:428-435 and :556-566`: standingCached's 60 second cache, always cold at a 300 second refresh, and roleNames' 300 second global cache, which only the first account in a run pays for
- `tools\gamemode.js:2400-2472`: the consumer: the early return on doc.lookupFailed at :2434-2438 with the comment saying keeping the old list is the safe failure, the 10 second timeout at :2462 and the 300000 ms interval at :2469-2471
- `tools\discord\bot.py:102`: the bot already runs with members=True, which is what makes the gateway cache possible

## Steps

- [ ] Take the shared secret question to #dev first: a route the bot POSTs to needs a key, the bot key already lives in the site config on the VPS and in door.json, and entry 2 is about rotating it, so coordinate rather than minting a second one. (patrick)
- [ ] Do the back-off once per refresh, not inside discordGet: /api/allowed calls standingCached once per linked account in a sequential loop, so a sleep inside discordGet multiplies by the number of accounts and blows the gamemode's 10 second timeout at gamemode.js:2462 rather than fixing it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2458 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add a shared cooldown at the top of /api/allowed that reads res.headers['retry-after'] or res.headers['x-ratelimit-reset-after'] from the first 429 and stops the run rather than grinding through the rest. (claude)
- [ ] Change out.lookupFailed at server.js:1315 and :1324 from a single boolean into a count plus the list of ids that failed, and return both, keeping the old boolean field so an old gamemode still works. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\server.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 1311 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] In tools\gamemode.js:2434-2438 accept the answer when the failures are a small fraction, say under ten percent, and merge rather than replace, refusing the write only when the site says it could reach Discord for nobody. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 2430 -First 11 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Stop re-deriving membership per account: have tools\discord\bot.py keep a dict of member id to role names updated from on_member_update, on_member_join and on_member_remove and POST it to a new site route, then have /api/allowed read that cache instead of looping, which turns N Discord calls into zero. (claude)
- [ ] Parse both files and prove the partial case without Discord: stub discordGet to return {ok:false,status:429} for one id out of five and success for the rest, call the /api/allowed handler, and assert the response still lists the four good profiles and that a copy of the gamemode's refresh() logic writes them. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/docs-app/server.js
  ```
- [ ] Time the loop with a stub that sleeps 100ms per call and confirm a hundred accounts crossed the 10 second timeout before the fix and does not after. (claude)

## Commands

- Start the branch; the three changes here are three branches. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/allow-list-survives-a-rate-limit
  ```
- Parses the site. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/docs-app/server.js
  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the merge logic changes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Compiles the bot after the gateway cache is added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -m py_compile tools\discord\bot.py
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/allow-list-survives-a-rate-limit
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```
- Puts the gamemode half on the VPS, which is a different path from the site half. Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1
  ```

## Done when

node --check passes on tools/docs-app/server.js and tools/gamemode.js, a stub returning 429 for one id in five still yields a response listing the four good profiles, a copy of the gamemode's refresh() logic writes them rather than returning early, and a 100ms-per-call stub over a hundred accounts finishes inside the 10 second timeout.

## Traps

Do not simply drop the gamemode's early return at :2434-2438. Its comment records why it exists: a short list written while Discord was unreachable turns away everybody missing from it, and with entry 5's enforce flag true that is a mass lockout, not a logged warning. The site and the gamemode deploy through two different paths and can be live at different times, so make the new field additive. The hundred-account figure is arithmetic, not a measurement: the live list is about 20 profiles today.

## Links

- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits the Retry-After and x-ratelimit-reset-after headers the back-off has to read
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Retry-After the header's exact format, which is seconds or a date
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/gateway the gateway the bot is already connected to, which is where membership can come from for free
- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/intents.html the members intent bot.py:102 already requests, which makes the cache possible
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/gateway-events the member add, update and remove events that keep the cache honest
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/docs-app/server.js the /api/allowed route and discordGet on main

issues.title: The whole of character creation is narrated to a log file on the VPS and to nothing the person can see
issues.body:
**Order:** 183 · **Wave:** 4 Arriving in the world · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 43

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js makes 72 log() calls and exactly two that can put words on a screen (1806-1807, both for hitting a rock). Silent: :899 sendToHall, :951 beginAppearance, :770-773 applyLauncherChoice, :1231-1240 the kit arriving

## What is known

Narrate every state change: creating your character, welcome to Whiterun, your starting kit has been added to your pack. The first ten minutes are currently a stone room with nobody in it, a race menu, silence, an unexplained teleport, and items appearing one at a time with no note saying why. This is the single biggest difference between how the project reads from the inside and how it reads to a stranger PART DONE 24 September, pull request #292. WHAT CHANGED: When the person picks their home town and arriveAt moves them to the inn, the server now sends them one chat line: "Welcome to <town>. You start at the inn." Before this, all the server did was write "home = whiterun" to its own log. The line goes through say(), next to that log line, not in place of it. notify() is not used. A new harness, tools/test-arrival-line.js, pulls the real arriveAt and the real town table out of gamemode.js and runs them. Nothing else in creation was changed: the hall, the race menu and the shift being handed over still say nothing, because Patrick decides which of those get a line. MEASURED: The code has moved on since the entry was written. applyLauncherChoice, beginClass, chooseClass, chooseDestination and the kit block no longer exist; Patrick removed the kits on 20 Sep (gamemode.js comment over PASSAGES, around line 3658). Creation now runs sendToHall, then beginAppearance, then beginChoosing/giveShift, then arriveAt at gamemode.js:3809. The entry's port trap is fixed: say() at gamemode.js:238 posts to voicePort() at :175, which reads thornswoodVoicePort from server-settings.json, and Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1:664 writes that setting on the dev server. arriveAt has one caller, chargen.arrive in the /pick town handler at gamemode.js:17887, so the line goes out once per creation. Nothing was said before this: the /pick town branch at :17746-17757 and the arrive branch at :17886-17894 only write state and clog. The new line is at gamemode.js:3850, with its comment at :3831-3849. The harness tools/test-arrival-line.js gives 25 passed, 0 failed on this change and 18 passed, 7 failed when pointed with GM at the file from before it (git show HEAD~1:tools/gamemode.js). It checks: exactly one line; sent to that actor; sent through say; names the town and the inn; correct for all nine towns; the log line and the move are still there; nothing is said for an unknown town, someone already done, someone still making their face, or someone with no record; the line has no "player", no em dash, is under 80 characters and is a single line. tools/docs-app/data/site/join.md:86 already tells people "the last one sends you to your inn", so the line matches the public page. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick, a decision: which other creation steps, if any, get a line. The candidates are entering the hall (sendToHall), the race menu opening (beginAppearance) and the shift being handed over (giveShift). The panel-choice step (beginChoosing) only speaks when the panel fails to open, and he called the old line there "chat spam" on 21 Sep. The rest of the entry cannot close until he decides. For whoever tests on dev after Patrick runs .\tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1: nobody has checked whether the arrival line can still be read after the load screen into the inn. say() sends it at the same moment the teleport starts, so it lands in the chat during the load. A creation run on dev should confirm the line is in the chat window once the inn appears. If it has scrolled away or faded, the next step is to delay it a few seconds. The entry's doneWhen ("roughly a dozen" say calls, one per state change) was written against the old flow and the old list, and needs rewording to fit today's four-step flow once Patrick decides.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:117-160`: notify, whose own comment at :117-121 says it may well do nothing when the call does not start in a game event, and say at :140-160 which posts to the voice service's /say on 127.0.0.1:7778 and actually works
- `tools\gamemode.js:1173-1229`: the arriving and kit state machine, the largest silent stretch: the "put N missing items into the kit" log at :1205-1208 and "kit confirmed" at :1222
- `tools\gamemode.js:893-903 and :950-951 and :771-774`: sendToHall which returns silently, beginAppearance which only logs, and applyLauncherChoice which only logs
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js:132-146`: the client's say and note, the other end of the same problem, and entry 44's dependency

## Steps

- [ ] Land entry 44 first if any of these lines should reach the client's corner-of-screen channel rather than the chat window, because note() has no callers until then. (patrick)
- [ ] Know before you test that say() hardcodes port 7778 at gamemode.js:148 and entry 1 is that the dev gamemode ships that file unchanged, so every message you add is delivered by the live voice service even while you are testing on dev. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 144 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add a say() beside each existing log(), never instead of it, because the log lines are the debugging record and must stay. (claude)
- [ ] Work the list in order: sendToHall at :893-903 "You are in the creation hall.", beginAppearance at :950-951 "Choose how you look.", beginClass at :954-959 "Choose a trade.", chooseClass at :962-971, chooseDestination at :973-998, applyLauncherChoice at :771-774 "Creating your character...", the arrival teleport "Welcome to <town>.", and the kit block at :1205-1222 "Your starting kit is in your pack." (claude)
- [ ] Use say(actorId, text), which takes the actor and resolves the profile at :141-142, and never notify, whose own comment says it will not fire from here. (claude)
- [ ] Do not restructure the chargen state machine while adding messages: it has an arrival window, face-change detection and reconnect handling with comments recording specific bugs at :1176-1183 and :1232-1245, and this is narration only. (claude)
- [ ] Parse the file and count the rise: say occurrences should go from two, which today are the definition at :140 and the single real call at :1807, to roughly a dozen. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] On the dev server only, tail the voice service's log for POSTs to /say during a creation run, since the voice service is what actually delivers the line. (patrick)

## Commands

- Start the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/narrate-character-creation
  ```
- Parses the gamemode; a syntax error takes the live handlers down on hot reload. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Lists every say occurrence; today there are two, the definition at :140 and one real call at :1807. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '\bsay\(' | Select-Object LineNumber, Line
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/narrate-character-creation
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```
- Puts the gamemode on the dev server so the lines can be watched. Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1
  ```

## Done when

node --check passes on tools/gamemode.js and the say occurrence count has risen from two, the definition at :140 and the one call at :1807, to roughly a dozen, with one line at each state change named in the list. On dev, the voice service's log shows a POST to /say for each of them during a creation run.

## Traps

say() hardcodes port 7778, which is the live voice service, so messages added here are delivered live even when you think you are testing dev; that is entry 1 and it has to be known before testing. Do not use notify for any of these, its own comment says it will not fire from here. gamemode.js is deployed by Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 and Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1, both of which talk to the VPS and are the person's to run.

## Links

- https://papyrus.bellcube.dev/skyrimse/script/debug/function/notification/ what the client-side note channel actually draws, if any of these lines go there instead
- https://nodejs.org/api/http.html the loopback POST say() makes to the voice service, which is why it works and notify does not
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/tree/main/skymp5-server the server that hot reloads gamemode.js, which is why the parse check comes before the deploy
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html node --check, the parse gate
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/gamemode.js notify, say and the chargen state machine on main

issues.title: Four of the nine starting towns use hand-written arrival points, and the shipped config says one of them puts you in a wall
issues.body:
**Order:** 186 · **Wave:** 4 Arriving in the world · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 51

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:617 (the towns table) · Everyone's PC · tools\emotes\Thornswood.ini, the Tools section

## What is known

Walk each of the nine before launch. Your own config already says it: Morthal and Dawnstar are two units apart, which is two different inns in two different holds sharing one position, so at least one of them puts a person in a wall. The first thing somebody sees is the one nobody checked PART DONE 24 September, pull request #262. WHAT CHANGED: I merged origin/main (8ed8c5b) into patrick/todo-161-arrival-points with no conflicts. Main had not done any of this work, so the branch still carries all of it. - **Three arrival points fixed.** Solitude, Falkreath and Dawnstar in the CHARGEN table in tools/gamemode.js now use the spot where the game places anybody who walks in through that inn's front door, facing into the room. - **Old points.** Each was the inn's front door moved 110 units along the door's own heading. Solitude ended up in the wall line, 128 units above the floor. Falkreath and Dawnstar ended up 110 units behind the door, outside the room. - **Markarth unchanged.** Its point is on the floor about 386 units into the room, and nothing in the records says it is wrong. - **Stale comments corrected.** The "Morthal and Dawnstar are two units apart" claim is gone from Thornswood.ini, both copies of thornswood-mark.js and Mark-Spot.ps1. - **New harness.** tools/test-arrivals.js checks every arrival against its inn's front door. The earlier reviewer's one major problem is real: the entry's doneWhen is not met as worded. The same reviewer confirmed the code is correct and said changing the doneWhen is Patrick's call. So no code can clear it, and the entry stays partial. My only fix commit (77e64f8) rewraps one over-long comment line in the header of both thornswood-mark.js copies. I did not edit the To Do List. MEASURED: - **Merge.** `git merge --no-edit origin/main` made merge commit 3e2d0f7 with no conflicts. After it, the branch differs from main in 6 files: gamemode.js (a comment above CHARGEN plus 3 rows of CHARGEN), test-arrivals.js (new), Thornswood.ini, both thornswood-mark.js copies and Mark-Spot.ps1. - **CHARGEN is safe to edit by hand.** It sits outside every ==== generated block. The only nearby marker, at line 3272, is the chopping-blocks note. - **Entry's data check, as worded, on the merged branch.** Five rows pass: whiterun, riften, windhelm, morthal and winterhold. Four fail, all on the quarter-turn rule: solitude rot 0, markarth 180, falkreath 0, dawnstar 0. No two positions are within 100 units of each other any more. - **Stale claim.** `git grep "two units apart"` finds it only in the new explanatory comments and in test-arrivals.js. It is no longer in the ini or either mark.js. - **Parse checks.** `node --check` passes on gamemode.js, test-arrivals.js and both thornswood-mark.js copies. The PowerShell parser finds 0 errors in Mark-Spot.ps1. - **Launcher build.** `Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root %TEMP%\ts-build-161 -NoPause` exits 0 and builds Launcher\Thornswood.exe. I built it because the ini is embedded in the exe. - **Full sweep: 82 harnesses.** - 58 tools/test-*.js, all pass, including test-arrivals 69/0, test-boards 20/0 and test-source-bytes 2/0. - 7 tools/voice/test-*.js, all pass. - 17 tools/test-*.ps1 under pwsh, all pass. - test-ice.js failed twice inside the sweep, once with a TypeError and once with ECONNRESET. Both times another process, gone before it could be identified, was listening on its fixed port 7903 (most likely another worktree's sweep running at the same time). With the port free it passed 15/0. WHAT IS LEFT: - **Patrick: the doneWhen.** Replace it with "node tools/test-arrivals.js passes". Its quarter-turn rule rejects the game's own door landing points, which face exactly 0 degrees. Its 100-unit rule compares coordinates from different interior cells, which says nothing about walls. Or Patrick keeps it as worded, and the walk below has to produce non-round facings. - **Patrick or Djinn: the walk.** Walk the four inns in game and press F8. - Markarth has not been checked against geometry. It faces 180, back toward the entrance. - Solitude, Falkreath and Dawnstar now arrive just inside the doorway. A better spot can be marked and pasted from Mark-Spot.ps1, and test-arrivals.js will accept it if it is on the room side of the door and on the ground floor. - **Landing it.** Open the pull request and merge it. Then run Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 for the table, and a dev Ship for thornswood-mark.js and the ini, which is embedded in the launcher. - **Open questions.** - The dead copy tools/emotes/thornswood-mark.js is not installed by Install-Emotes.ps1. Deleting it is a separate call. - test-boards.js still uses the old coordinates in its pretend CHARGEN table. It passes, and it is labelled a fixture, so I left it alone.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:616`: the generated CHARGEN constant, one long line holding all nine towns with their cell, description, position and rotation
- `tools\gamemode.js:623-626`: the comment saying the table is generated from the same source the plugin and the message box records came from, which is what the trap below is about
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-mark.js:1-20`: the measuring tool's header, which is also one of the two stale comments this row has to correct
- `tools\emotes\Thornswood.ini:95-101`: MarkKey = 66 (F8) and the other stale comment claiming Morthal and Dawnstar are two units apart
- `tools\Mark-Spot.ps1`: what turns Data\Platform\thornswood-spots.txt into the line the table wants, so a generated line is pasted rather than coordinates hand-typed again

## Steps

- [ ] Run the data check now, before any walking: parse the CHARGEN towns table at gamemode.js:616 and assert no two arrival positions are within a hundred units of each other and no rot[2] is exactly 0.0, 90.0, 180.0 or 270.0. Four rows fail today, which are Solitude at rot 90.0, Markarth at 180.0, Falkreath at 180.0 and Dawnstar at 180.0; the five measured ones pass. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 612 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Correct the two stale comments in this branch, because they will send the next person after a bug 1.1.41 already fixed: Thornswood.ini:97-101 and thornswood-mark.js:4-8 both still say Morthal and Dawnstar are two units apart, and Morthal now sits at 1970.6, -160.2 while only Dawnstar is still at 1824.3, -683.7. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\emotes\Thornswood.ini -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 93 -First 9 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the table is edited directly and not regenerated: tools\thornswood-src exists but build.py writes to /mnt/user-data/outputs/thornswood/gamemode.js, a sandbox path that does not exist on this machine, so never regenerate gamemode.js from it. (claude)
- [ ] Walk the four: Solitude's Winking Skeever, Markarth's Silver-Blood Inn, Falkreath's Dead Man's Drink and Dawnstar's Windpeak Inn. Stand where somebody should arrive, face the way they should face, press F8. This is Patrick or Djinn's; a Claude never starts the game. (patrick)
- [ ] Turn the marks into table lines and paste the four results into the CHARGEN constant at gamemode.js:616. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Mark-Spot.ps1
  ```
- [ ] Re-run the data check and confirm all nine rows now pass, then parse the file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- Start the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/nine-arrival-points
  ```
- Prints all nine arrival points so the round hand-written rotations are visible at a glance. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import re,io,json;s=io.open('tools/gamemode.js',encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')[615];d=json.loads(re.search(r'=\s*(\{.*\});?\s*$',s).group(1));[print(k,v['arrival']['cell'],v['arrival']['pos'],v['arrival']['rot']) for k,v in d['towns'].items()]"
  ```
- Reads Data\Platform\thornswood-spots.txt and prints the lines the CHARGEN table wants. Read only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Mark-Spot.ps1
  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the four lines are pasted. (claude)
  ```powershell

  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/nine-arrival-points
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```
- Puts the corrected table on the server. Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell

  ```

## Done when

The data check over the CHARGEN towns table passes for all nine rows, meaning no two positions within a hundred units and no rotation that is exactly a quarter turn, node --check passes on tools/gamemode.js, and neither tools\emotes\Thornswood.ini nor tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-mark.js still claims Morthal and Dawnstar are two units apart.

## Traps

You cannot do the measuring part yourself; CLAUDE.md forbids a Claude starting the launcher or the game, so the walk is Patrick or Djinn's and what you can do is the data check, the comment corrections and the paste. The stale comments are the real trap: anybody reading them today goes looking for a collision 1.1.41 already fixed. thornswood-mark.js is the tool that does the measuring and is also the file another entry wants gated behind a developer flag, so gate it in a way that still lets a developer machine measure or these four never get walked.
