issues.title: The launcher Help page is the old project's help page with edits: a dead address, a password box that does not exist, and an explanation of parties
issues.body:
**Order:** 189 · **Wave:** 4 Arriving in the world · **Category:** RP fit · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 73

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Help.cs:17-27, 87, 129-133, 143, 146, 155-159, 199

## What is known

Rebuild it from help.md and known.md, which are current, plus a chat and commands section and a character section. Delete every entry that starts from the old engine. It currently tells people to type 192.135.119.166:25565 into a screen that does not exist, and explains a password error the software cannot raise MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: tools/app/Help.cs, 214 lines, one HelpItem array rendered by Shell.cs:2683-2712. Sections come from the data and nothing is hard coded, so the array can be replaced whole. Still there, as the entry says: :26-27 (the Skyrim Together save item), :87 ("how Together carries sound"), :155-156 ("The address has to be 192.135.119.166:25565"), :158-159 ("The password you entered is incorrect"). Wrong since the entry was written: :129-130 "There is no party system", while /party exists (gamemode.js:18355-18413, #133, #139). :149 "There is no text chat box", while thornswood-front.js:1050-1056 and :4196-4258 run a chat box (#185). :143 "configurable in the SunHelm MCM", while the needs are now the gamemode's own (8fe8119, 20069f6) and known.md lists SunHelm as not working. :71-126 are sixteen per-trade starting kits and "50 to 150 gold", but gamemode.js:13618 says "The sixteen starter kits went on 20 September", :16201 says forty gold once, classes.md:10-11 says nothing is handed out but clothes, and Help.cs:18 itself says "carrying nothing". help.md is NOT a safe source: help.md:43-53 and known.md's "Around Play" table still say the launcher asks for profession, half, class and town. That is contradicted by 3aa37ef, classes.md:5-11 and Help.cs:18-24 (the K panel in the hall). That is a public-site defect of its own and needs its own entry. A branch exists, patrick/todo-164-launcher-help, not merged: - **Patrick, after the merge:** a dev Ship, because the text lives inside the launcher exe. `.\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "The Help page is rebuilt: the old address, the password and the kits are gone, and it now covers your character, chat and commands"`. Then somebody should open Help in the dev launcher and read it, since nobody has seen the page rendered yet. - **Entry 163:** the ui.xaml half (FirstRunCard, "name it after yourself" and "Save once") is still open. Its Help.cs half (name rule and the save line) is done here. If 163 lands first, keep this Help.cs when resolving the conflict. - **Other entries this touches:** it clears the Help.cs parts of entries 133 (SunHelm), 193 (password), 237 ("single player"), 297 (Help.cs:36-37 wheel wording), 306 (Bard item) and 336 (party item). Their other parts are still open: - 297: Keys.cs:477 still says "Twelve gestures, and a second ring". - 336: gamemode.js:18413 and thornswood-party.js:312 still say "press the party key". - 133: Pages.cs:291 and known.md still mention SunHelm. - **New findings for the To Do List** (I did not edit it): 1. Key clash on a fresh install: the ini template sets WheelKey = 34 (G), and FriendKey defaults to 34 (G) at thornswood-front.js:299 and Keys.cs:519. So G while looking at somebody both opens the wheel and asks them to be friends. The comment at front.js:308 still says the wheel is on B. 2. Keys.cs:493-495 puts an "Open the creation menu" row (MenuKey, M) on the Controls page, and no plugin reads that key any more. 3. The emote stop key only works while the wheel is shut (!open, thornswood-emotes.js stopKey handler), but its comment and the Keys.cs row text say it works either way. 4. The whisper/normal/yell key B is not on the Controls page. 5. Site pages are out of date: - help.md:43-52 and known.md's "Around Play" table still say the launcher asks for profession, half, class and town. - help.md and join.md say Thornswood "does not make a second copy of the game", but StartPlay now requires the own game folder (Shell.cs:4023, OwnGameRequired). - classes.md says nothing is handed out but clothes, while the gamemode hands out 40 gold once. - **Not done, on purpose:** the entry's optional step of embedding help.md in the launcher for Help.cs to parse at runtime. help.md is itself out of date, and embedding it would change Build-Launcher.ps1. That is a design decision for Patrick. NEXT STEP: Branch off main. Rewrite the Items array in tools/app/Help.cs from sources that are current. Keep Joining 1-2b (Help.cs:14-24, 20 Sep, with entry 163's name fix). Keep the Emotes, The mods and Tips items that are still true. Delete :26-27, the sixteen kit items :71-126 and the gold line at :75-78, :129-133, :143, :149, :151-152 (help.md says there is no saving) and :155-159. Add a Character section drawn from classes.md: profession, half, class, what each gates, and K. Add a Chat and commands section drawn from gamemode.js: the WORDS and PLAYER_WORDS lists at :17579-17641, /ooc at :18900, and /party, /friend and /trade at :18355+. Also cover the chat box. State only what the code shows, and drop anything that cannot be checked. Do not put any server address in its place. Keep C# 5 verbatim literals. Check: Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause, then Select-String -Path tools\app\Help.cs -Pattern 'Together|192.135.119.166|password you entered|no party system|no text chat box|SunHelm MCM|50 to 150 gold' returns nothing. Record help.md and known.md's launcher-chargen wording as a separate site entry. 24 SEPTEMBER: built and reviewed on patrick/todo-164-launcher-help, pull request #334 open, not merged yet. I merged origin/main (5a9ba5c) into patrick/todo-164-launcher-help. The only conflict was the needs item in tools/app/Help.cs. Entry 133 (#307) had rewritten that item on main as "You will get hungry, thirsty and cold", and tools/test-sunhelm-gone.js checks its text against the gamemode. This branch had its own version, titled "Food, water, rest and warmth". I kept one item: main's title, comment and text, plus the branch's last sentence on /eat, /drink and /rest. That sentence uses the same ...

## Read first

- `tools\app\Help.cs, all 214 lines`: the page is one array of HelpItem, so you have to see which items are current and which are inherited before you can rebuild it
- `tools\app\Help.cs:155-159`: the two items that describe a screen the launcher no longer has: "The address has to be 192.135.119.166:25565 in full" and "The password you entered is incorrect"
- `tools\docs-app\data\help.md and tools\docs-app\data\known.md`: the current, accurate source the rebuild comes from; note they are in data, not data\site, and server.js:163-173 serves them at /help and /known
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\join.md`: so the launcher's joining section matches the one story the site tells

## Steps

- [ ] Do not patch item by item. Rebuild the HelpItem array from tools\docs-app\data\help.md and known.md, one item per heading, keeping the HelpItem(category, title, body) shape. (claude)
- [ ] Delete every item that starts from the old engine: the save item at :26-27, the Together sentence at :87, the parties and quests items at :129-133, and the address and password items at :155-159. (claude)
- [ ] Ignore three of the row's eight citations, because they do not support the claim: :143 is the SunHelm needs display, :146 is what dying costs and :199 is the mods-list tip, none of which is old-project text. (claude)
- [ ] Add the two sections that do not exist anywhere yet: a chat and commands section covering what /ooc does and its range and what the console does per entry 47, and a character section covering the name rule from entry 51 and what the launcher choices do per entry 55. (claude)
- [ ] Do not paste the current server address in as a replacement for the dead one: entries 28 and 60 both want the address to come from the feed so raising or moving the server does not need a reinstall. (claude)
- [ ] If you want the page to stop drifting, have Build-Launcher.ps1 embed help.md as a resource that Help.cs parses at runtime, which is the same trick the site uses and makes the next rewrite a markdown edit. (claude)
- [ ] Compile and prove the leftovers are gone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Start the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/rebuild-the-help-page
  ```
- Compiles the launcher with the rebuilt array, which is the CI check. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- Must return nothing when the rebuild is done. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Help.cs -Pattern 'Skyrim Together|192.135.119.166|password you entered'
  ```
- The current source the new items are written from. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Content tools\docs-app\data\help.md
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/rebuild-the-help-page
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

Build-Launcher.ps1 produces Thornswood.exe and Select-String for 'Skyrim Together|192.135.119.166|password you entered' across tools\app\Help.cs returns nothing.

## Traps

C# 5 only: the HelpItem array is verbatim string literals, so no string interpolation and no expression bodied members if you add helpers. The dead address is a Skyrim Together address, and copying the current one in its place is the wrong fix; the address belongs in the feed. Entry 51 edits :14-15 and :26-27 of this same file, and entries 47 and 54 both change what this page should say, so read those three rows before writing the new text. This ships as a launcher release, so launcher, game files and server go together.

## Links

- https://thornswood.net/help the current, accurate public help page the rebuild is written from
- https://thornswood.net/known the known issues page, the other source for the rebuilt items
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/ the C# reference, for keeping verbatim literals and helpers inside C# 5
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/docs-app/data/help.md help.md on main, the markdown that becomes the new items
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/app/Help.cs the whole HelpItem array on main, so the inherited items are visible in one read

issues.title: Two of the three choices the launcher makes you agonise over do nothing in the game
issues.body:
**Order:** 192 · **Wave:** 4 Arriving in the world · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 50

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:760-761 (written), :772-773 (the only other reference, a log line) · VPS · site · data\site\classes.md:22-44 describes them as systems

## What is known

Either make them do something or say on the page that they are planned. A published systems page describes the system that runs. Somebody who spent ten minutes choosing between them and then finds no difference concludes the rest is the same MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Both choices now drive systems that run. The launcher's old state.half and state.gathering are migrated into the progression state (gamemode.js:16316-16324 and :17032-17054: the gathering maps to P.pickClass, and trade plus half map to P.pickProfession), and new characters choose in the K panel (3aa37ef). The half gates what can be made: canWork at gamemode.js:12403-12410, the bench gate at :9376-9404 and gateHalf at :17118-17123 (a2ba2ee, 21 Sep: "A profession decides what you can make"). The class gates the verbs: canDo at :12413-12416, and gate() at :17103-17109 with refusals such as "Only a miner can work a seam" at :17091-17097. classGate is called for mine (:1933, :2882), harvest (:5824), fish (:5876), loot (:5983, :6654) and farm (:13259, :13407, :13506) (8367a87, 077268f). classes.md (last changed 077268f, 21 Sep) describes this running system at :36-60 ("Your half decides what you are able to make, and the server holds you to it"). applyLauncherChoice and the line numbers the entry cites no longer exist. node --check tools/gamemode.js passes. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: Most of the reviewer's case holds. c87da23 (20 Sep, on main) removed applyLauncherChoice, and the launcher no longer offers these choices: grepping tools/app/*.cs and tools/ui.xaml for half or gathering finds nothing. The class gate is real: classGate at gamemode.js:1330 is called for mine, harvest, fish, loot and farm, and it refuses anybody with no class (:17104). The half gate is real too: mp.onCraft at :9822 calls craftAnswer at :9453, and the fork's CraftService.cpp fires onCraft at recorded build c8832519. node --check passes. All of these commits come before launcher 1.1.90. Three parts of doneWhen or the entry's own requirement still fail. (1) The entry says "A published systems page describes the system that runs", and classes.md does not. The half only binds somebody who has chosen a profession. benchGate returns null when there is no profession (gamemode.js:9399: `if (!s.prof) { return null; }`). craftAnswer lets the craft through before any half or rank check (:9532), so somebody with no profession can make Master-rank work at any bench. That state lasts for good. The K panel has a "choose later" for class and profession (ts-ui/thornswood-skills.js:25-29, :1740-1742), and the server ends creation on the town alone (gamemode.js:17516: "The home is the one pick that ends creation. Class and profession may still be unset"). So never picking the half is strictly better for making things, and the half choice only takes options away. classes.md:22 says "What nobody gets is all of it", and :52 says "Your half decides what you are able to make, and the server holds you to it". Neither mentions this. classes.md:7-9 and join.md:86 say "Take them in any order. The third one sends you to your inn", which is not what the code does. Entry 86 records the no-profession allowance as deliberate. No page says so, and no open entry covers it. (2) The literal code test in doneWhen fails. state.half occurs once in gamemode.js, in a comment at :16317, not more than three times. The half is now read as s.half, so this test is out of date rather than failed, but it is not met as written. (3) Deployment is second-hand. "The rendered page says so" and live status come only from To Do records (entries 85, 52, 160, 146). Nothing here measured them, because the VPS was not contacted. Deploy-Docs.ps1 notes that site pages can be edited on the site, so the live /classes page may not match the repo. The fix is to correct classes.md:7-9, :22 and :52, and join.md:86, to say that class and profession can be left for later and what that means at a bench. The alternative is to close the no-profession path in benchGate and craftAnswer. Either needs Patrick's decision. NEXT STEP: Close the entry. Nothing to build, and no page correction is needed: classes.md already describes what the server enforces. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: Read on origin/main at c13ada9. Most of the work is done. The launcher choice was replaced by class and profession picks in the K panel, the class gates the verbs, and the half gates the benches. node --check passes on tools/gamemode.js. Two parts of doneWhen are still not met. (1) The code test as written fails: state.half appears once in gamemode.js, in a comment at :16684. The count has fallen from three instead of rising above it, because the code now reads s.half. That part of the test is out of date more than failed. (2) The real gap is the entry's own requirement that the published page describes the system that runs, and it does not. benchGate returns null for anybody with no profession (gamemode.js:9468 `if (!s.prof) { return null; }`), and craftAnswer (:9522) makes the same allowance. The comment there calls it a first-evening allowance, but nothing ever makes the choice: creation ends on the home pick alone, and class and profession "may still be unset" (:17883-17885). So somebody who never picks a profession can make anything at any bench for good, and choosing a half only takes options away. classes.md:52-55 says "Your half decides what you are able to make, and the server holds you to it". classes.md:22 says "What nobody gets is all of it". classes.md:8-9 says "Take them in any order. The third one sends you to your inn", but the home pick ends creation whether or not the other two are made. None of this is on the page. Fixing it means either correcting classes.md (and join.md:86, per the triage) or closing the no-profession path in benchGate and craftAnswer. That is Patrick's decision. The live /classes page was not measured. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: Entry 86 records the no-profession allowance at the bench as deliberate. It should either say that the allowance never ends, because creation finishes on the home pick alone, or be the place where that path gets closed. Right now no open entry covers the public pages being wrong about it.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:736-775`: applyLauncherChoice and the comment block at :747-759, which is the specification for what half and gathering were meant to do: half decides what they can make, gathering owns a verb nobody else has
- `tools\gamemode.js:760-761 and :771-774`: the two writes, state.half and state.gathering, and the only other occurrence of either name in the whole file, which is a log line; nothing reads them back
- `tools\gamemode.js:1780-1812`: the craft and harvest handler, where a half check would have to go; it is the one place in the file that already produces a message a person sees, at :1805-1808
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md:22-44 and :123-135`: what the public has been told, which is the other half of the row

## Steps

- [ ] Take the decision to #dev first, because CLAUDE.md is explicit that a design question like this goes there as a few lines, the problem, the approach and what it touches, and is agreed between Patrick and Djinn before code. A Claude does not settle which way this goes. (patrick)
- [ ] If the page is corrected: edit tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md so the half and the gathering specialisation are described as planned rather than as running systems, and say when they are expected. That is markdown and a site deploy, with no game change. (claude)
- [ ] If the systems are built: hook into the craft and harvest branch at gamemode.js:1780-1804 where baseDesc is already matched against STATIONS, SHRINES and HARVESTS, read state.half through the same getChargen the file uses elsewhere, and allow or refuse the recipe. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 1776 -First 31 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Return the refusal through the existing message path at :1805-1808 rather than adding a new one, and do the gathering verb the same shape against HARVESTS. (claude)
- [ ] Pass anything you add to state through setChargen, because gamemode.js:1300-1314 records that a field written to the local copy is gone three seconds later. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 1296 -First 21 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Change the public page and the server in the same release either way, or the row just moves from one file to the other. (claude)
- [ ] Parse the gamemode and count the reads: state.half should appear more than the current three occurrences, which are the write at :760 and twice inside the log line at :772, with at least one new one a read rather than a write. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- Start the branch, after #dev has picked build or correct. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/half-and-gathering-decision
  ```
- Parses the gamemode if the systems are built. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Counts occurrences of state.half; it is 3 today, the write at :760 and twice inside the log line at :772, and none is a read. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'state\.half' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches.Count } | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
  ```
- Shows how the public page describes the two systems today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md -Pattern 'half|gathering'
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/half-and-gathering-decision
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```
- Puts a corrected classes page on the VPS. Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Done when

For the page fix, classes.md describes the half and the gathering specialisation as planned and the rendered page says so. For the code fix, node --check passes on tools/gamemode.js and the state.half occurrence count has risen above the current three, with at least one of the new ones a read rather than a write.

## Traps

A Claude does not settle which way this goes; it is a #dev decision between Patrick and Djinn. The state object is read back off the actor at the top of every tick, so anything you add must go through setChargen or it vanishes. The public page and the server have to change together: build the system and update classes.md in the same release, or correct the page and say when the system is expected. Anything in gamemode.js ships with the launcher and the game files as one complete release.

## Links

issues.title: The installer payload is publicly downloadable and redistributes about forty named third-party mods, including Bethesda's own assets
issues.body:
**Order:** 193 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Legal · **Effort:** change it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 8

## Where it lives

VPS · site · the payload answers 200 anonymously at 527 MB · tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:133-199 and the exclusion list that misses the Bethesda files · Your PC · Profile\OwnGame\files.txt

## What is known

The collection model is the right one and is already in place: people install the mods themselves from Nexus, under the mod authors' own terms. The payload undercuts it by shipping the same files. Take the third-party content out of the payload so it carries only what is yours, and put the download behind the same door as the rest TWO RELEASES BEHIND AS OF 1.1.70: Ship said so on 21 September. Thornswood-Setup.zip was built 20 September at 19:06 and the site is offering Thornswood-Setup-20260920-1902. Anybody installing from it sits through every release since on first launch. Nobody who already has the game is affected. Package-Thornswood.ps1 rebuilds it and takes about twenty minutes. AND IT IS WORSE THAN FORTY NAMED MODS, measured 22 September. Data\textures and Data\meshes in the game folder hold 565 files and 547.4 MB that Vortex has never deployed and does not know about: loose files dropped into the Steam copy's Data folder by hand. Vortex has 154 mod folders and none of them matches any of these names. So these are not on the list of forty, they are not on any list, and the installer hands them to everybody: LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary, LostArk, leifcrops, MCE, 0CCE, and the loose contents of textures\weapons, textures\interface, meshes\armor, meshes\actors and meshes\clothes. Also Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa, 2.8 MB at the Data root, loaded by no plugin in the list. The entry about what the new collection revision should carry has the full folder by folder breakdown with sizes. Whichever of these are somebody else's have to come out or be traced to a mod page and put in the collection; whichever are ours belong in the Thornswood Content mod, and then they leave the installer by themselves, because the packager already drops anything the collection provides. TRACED 22 SEPTEMBER, FOLDER BY FOLDER: the 565 loose files and 547 MB under Data\textures and Data\meshes that Vortex does not provide, read from Profile\OwnGame\files.txt, the file dates, and every archive in Vortex's downloads. CANNOT STAY, NOT OURS AND NOT A NEXUS MOD: textures and meshes\LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary (155.0 and 11.7 MB) and textures and meshes\LostArk (64.7 and 43.3 MB), Lost Ark armour ports with HIMBO BodySlide builds, dropped 14 September 20:43 to 20:51, minutes before that day's Daedric Online collection downloads, in no archive and loaded by no plugin. textures\weapons\rpcustom (78.0 MB: apocalypse, balmung, dibella, hircine, zireael) and textures\weapons\saarthal (3.2 MB) with their meshes, dated 14 September 20:56 and referenced by nothing. textures\leifcrops (57.3 MB) and meshes\leifcrops, maple and tomato, dated 12 September 19:40, seven minutes before the Keizaal collection download, not in KzlOnlineContent and referenced by nothing, so most likely that launcher's. ORPHANED BUILDS FOR MODS NO LONGER INSTALLED: meshes\MCE (29.8 MB, Mage Clothing Expansion and its 3BA patch) and meshes\0CCE (3.2 MB, Common Clothing Expansion and its 3BA patch). meshes\armor holds 54.6 MB of BodySlide output built on this machine: Common Clothes travel clothes (150 files, 43.5 MB), dragon priests matching Dragon Priests Retexture SE (24 files), and Immersive Armors' bosmer armour from one of the 13 slider sets still installed (18 files). meshes\clothes (2.9 MB) and the small dlc01, dlc02, creationclub, _byoh, surarmorcustommeshes, surwhiterunmeshes and pulcharmsolis folders are more of the same. BodySlide output is built for one person's body choice and has no place in anybody else's installer, whichever mod it is for. meshes\actors (17.8 MB) is Nemesis output from 11 September, which the build treats as ours and which wants regenerating, plus 17 FNIS Behavior SE first person files from a mod the collection does not carry, plus BodySlide body, beard and draugr builds. Three small strays: Armor_Replacer (Sentinel's resources), furniture\noble (Assorted Mesh Fixes) and architecture\riften (B. Noble Skyrim), none of them installed. OURS, 8 MB: textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds and meshes\interface\logo, made by Build-Backdrop and Go.ps1. They stay in the installer with the music and the video. MARKETPLACETEXTURES.BSA is Bethesda's, 2.8 MB, stamped the same as _ResourcePack.bsa, and missing from Package-Thornswood's list of Bethesda files, so it ships. NOT YET GONE THROUGH: the other not-from-Vortex files in Data\Scripts (rp_trapcactusscript, ski_*.pex, wbptlight*, dlc1vcmoondial*), Data\Interface (the RaceMenu swfs and map.swf), music\special\mus_maintheme.xwm, MCM\Settings, SKSE\Plugins\TrueHUD\RP_Bosses.ini, and the hashed UI assets and the Fonts, Images and Modules folders under Data\Platform. THE ORDER THIS PUTS ON THE RELEASE: the twelve whole folders come out of the Steam copy before Maintenance and before the next Package-Thornswood, and that step is in entry 46. What stays here is the rule side: keeping BodySlide output and other people's leftovers out of the installer by the Vortex record rather than by hand. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #227. WHAT CHANGED: Steps 1 and 2 of the triage plan are done. Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa is Bethesda's, and it is now left out of packs and the installer through a new $ShipBethesdaLeftAlone list in tools\Ship-Rules.ps1. Test-ShipMachine asks that list, so the file is never shipped and never listed as removed. It deliberately does not go in a vanilla list, because a vanilla rule would have put it in the next pack's delete.txt. Package-Thornswood.ps1 now prints a report after its filter loop. The report names, one folder at a time with sizes, the loose textures and meshes the installer is about to carry that are neither the collection's nor ours. Ours is the three menu backdrop files Go.ps1 writes. The report does not stop anything. MEASURED: MarketplaceTextures.bsa is 2,938,167 bytes. Its header lists 121 files in 5 folders, all under interface\marketplace (buttons for pc and xbox, and stars). It is dated 2026-09-10 11:08:10, five seconds after _ResourcePack.bsa (11:08:05). files.txt has it as L|O at line 561 (linked from the Steam copy, not Vortex), and _DowngraderBackups holds a 3,224,203 byte copy. Both pack baselines, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json and published-dev.json (943 keys each), list Data\MarketplaceTextures.bsa, and that is why it cannot be a vanilla rule: Publish-Update.ps1:587-592 lists as removed anything that is not in the scan unless Test-Machine claims it. Run over the non-V lines of C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\files.txt, the new report names 24 folders, 563 files, 539.4 MB. The largest: textures\LoA Reborn Paladin Legendary 155.0 MB, textures\weapons 81.2, textures\LostArk 64.7, textures\leifcrops 57.3, meshes\armor 54.6 (194 files), meshes\LostArk 43.3, meshes\MCE 29.8, meshes\actors 17.8 (128 files), meshes\LoA 11.7, meshes\0CCE 3.2. The 22 Sep total of 547.4 MB included our 8 MB backdrop, which is now excluded. The pack baselines list the same folders (meshes\armor 194, actors 128, LoA 30+25, LostArk 26+19, MCE 18, leifcrops 9+2), so packs have carried them too. The lifted report block ran cleanly under Set-StrictMode Latest in PowerShell 5.1 and 7, for 0, 1 and 24 folders. Against HEAD's scripts, test-ship-rules.ps1 fails 4 checks and then crashes on the missing Get-ShipLooseArt. With the change it passes 33 of 33. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick, from the entry and the triage, none of it done here: (1) Delete the stray loose folders from the Steam copy and run Maintenance (the entry that owns that step). The report will then shrink to nothing. Warning: the pack baselines list those same 565-odd files, so the first pack after they are deleted lists them all as removed and hits Publish-Update's MaxRemovals guard. It needs -AcceptRemovals, and that is only right if taking them off every tester is what he wants. (2) Decide whether BodySlide output and the Nemesis output in meshes\actors (plus Data\meshes\animationdatasinglefile.txt and animationsetdatasinglefile.txt) ship at all. After that decision, the report can become a refusal with an allowlist in Ship-Rules and an -AcceptLoose switch. The refusal is left out on purpose because it would block every installer build today. (3) Decide how the download gets a door when the installer cannot sign in (server.js says /api/payload must stay public). A short-lived signed URL is one way, and the patrick/todo-189-download-is-the-door branch may cover it. (4) Rebuild with Package-Thornswood.ps1 and republish the installer. That goes to the live site. For the merger: entry 169 (patrick/todo-169-exclusion-lists) is folding the vanilla lists into Ship-Rules. $ShipBethesdaLeftAlone should stay a never-removed list, or be folded into 169's never-removed category. It must not go in its vanilla list. Not gone through, from the entry: Data\Scripts, Data\Interface, music, MCM, SKSE, and the Platform assets outside textures and meshes.

## Read first

- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:317-327`: the filter loop that decides what the installer carries: it calls Test-Vanilla, Test-Runtime, Test-ShipMachine, Test-Optional and Test-FromCollection, and never once calls Test-ShipOtherServer
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:119-162`: Test-ShipOtherServer, which already excludes Data\(Meshes|Textures)\(Keizaal|kzlcustommeshs) at :133-135 and Data\NirnLabUIPlatform at :141, so the rules exist and the installer simply never asks them
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:130-215`: the whole decision about what ships in order: Bethesda files at :133-138, foreign frameworks at :155, root files at :163, root dirs at :180, Test-Vanilla at :188 and the dot-source of Ship-Rules at :215
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:258-306`: the Vortex record branch and the Die at :273, which guards only the own-game-folder path at :271 while the Steam and Vortex branch at :281 carries on and prints "no Vortex record found, so this installer carries every mod file." at :302-305

## Steps

- [ ] Fix the actual defect first, which is one line: tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1's filter loop never calls Test-ShipOtherServer, so Ship-Rules.ps1:133-135 already excludes the Keizaal and kzlcustommeshs folders from packs and has never once been applied to the installer. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship-Rules.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 129 -First 9 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add `if (Test-ShipOtherServer $rel) { $skipBytes += $f.Length; continue }` to the loop in Package-Thornswood.ps1 immediately after the Test-ShipMachine line at :321, so the installer and the packs ask the same questions. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 317 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Re-measure a fresh build rather than quoting September's numbers, so the finding is about today: open the built zip and count the top folder of every entry. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import zipfile,collections;z=zipfile.ZipFile(r'C:\\Thornswood\\_dist\\Thornswood-Setup.zip');print(collections.Counter(i.filename.split('/')[2] if i.filename.count('/')>2 else i.filename for i in z.infolist()).most_common(40))"
  ```
- [ ] Check the seventeen entries outside payload/ as well, because that is where the load orders live: the zip carries profile\Plugins.txt and profile\loadorder.txt plus three other servers' load-order backups. (claude)
- [ ] For the remaining third-party loose assets, move each one into the Nexus collection and let Test-FromCollection drop it, rather than adding mod names to a deny list, because the file's own comment at :258-262 says the Vortex record and not a guess at which folders count as mods is what decides. (patrick)
- [ ] Put the download behind the same Discord door the rest of the site uses, whose access lists are at tools\docs-app\server.js:60-74. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\server.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 56 -First 21 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Parse the script the way CI does, then have Patrick rebuild and re-measure. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e.Count
  ```
- [ ] Add MarketplaceTextures.bsa to the Bethesda files Package-Thornswood leaves out by name. It is a base game archive, 2.8 MB, and it ships today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern 'ResourcePack|MarketplaceTextures'
  ```
- [ ] Decide what the installer does with BodySlide output under meshes, which no rule knows about: it is per person and should never ship, even for a mod the collection carries. (patrick)

## Commands

- Start the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/installer-asks-the-other-server-rule
  ```
- Parses the script the same way the GitHub build check does; prints 0 when it is clean. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e.Count
  ```
- Returns nothing today, which is the whole defect, and must hit once after the fix. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern 'Test-ShipOtherServer'
  ```
- Shows the rules that already exist and have never been applied to the installer. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship-Rules.ps1 -Pattern 'Keizaal|kzlcustommeshs'
  ```
- Counts what the built payload actually carries, by folder. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import zipfile,collections;z=zipfile.ZipFile(r'C:\\Thornswood\\_dist\\Thornswood-Setup.zip');print(collections.Counter(i.filename.split('/')[2] if i.filename.count('/')>2 else i.filename for i in z.infolist()).most_common(40))"
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/installer-asks-the-other-server-rule
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```
- Rebuilds the installer so the measurement can be repeated. Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1
  ```

## Done when

Select-String for 'Test-ShipOtherServer' in tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1 hits once inside the filter loop, both scripts parse, and after a rebuild the zip count shows no folder named Keizaal or kzlcustommeshs and fewer mod-asset folders under payload/Data/meshes and payload/Data/textures than before. An anonymous request to the download route no longer returns 200 with the zip.

## Traps

Do not add a deny list of mod names to Package-Thornswood: its own comment at :258-262 says the Vortex record, not a guess at which folders count as mods, is what decides, and a hand list will drift. The Die that refuses to ship an empty collection record guards only the own-game-folder branch at :271; the Steam and Vortex branch at :281 prints a warning and carries on, and CLAUDE.md says the Steam shape is what ships today. Data\Platform is skyrim-platform, which is GPLv3 and is entry 58, so those go out together or the notices file is wrong twice.

## Links

- https://help.nexusmods.com/article/18-do-i-need-permission-to-use-a-mod-in-my-video-or-mod-pack Nexus Mods' terms, where an uploader sets what others may do with their files, which is what the payload is redistributing
- https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.en.html GPLv3, which covers the 392 MB of Data/Platform inside the payload
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/select-string the grep that proves the missing rule call before and after
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_scripts dot-sourcing, which is how Package-Thornswood gets Ship-Rules' functions in the first place
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/Ship-Rules.ps1 Test-ShipOtherServer on main, the rule the installer never asks
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/Package-Thornswood.ps1 the filter loop on main, the four lines the fix lands in

issues.title: There is no licence on this project and no third-party notices file anywhere
issues.body:
**Order:** 196 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Legal · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 87

## Where it lives

Your PC · no LICENSE, COPYING, NOTICE or THIRD-PARTY file exists in either repository, checked by name and by content

## What is known

Private source with no licence is normal for a product and is fine. What is missing is the other half: a notices file listing what is shipped that is not yours and under what terms, and terms on the site where the public looks. That file is also where the GPL source offer from entry 58 lives MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Searching the repo to depth 3 for LICENSE, COPYING, NOTICE or THIRD-PARTY finds only tools/Add-NoticeBoards.ps1; there is no notices file. What the launcher exe carries: Build-Launcher.ps1:125-126 and :254-258 embed Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Core.dll, Microsoft.Web.WebView2.Wpf.dll and WebView2Loader.dll from tools/lib/webview2, which is the only thing in tools/lib. The other /resource: entries at :243-291 are the project's own (ui.xaml, logo, header art and video, icon, voice-host.html, Thornswood.ini, client-build.json). The 23 Sep payload also carries the six SkyMP runtime files (GPL/AGPL, fork c8832519), 9 .ttf fonts under Data/Platform/UI and the spritefonts under Data/Platform/Fonts, and third-party mod files, which are entry 168. The site half is partly done: terms.md came in 9706317 on 23 Sep, and :74-81 "What Thornswood is built on" names SkyMP and Skyrim Platform in general terms, with no licences. A branch exists, patrick/todo-171-third-party-notices, not merged: For Patrick: (1) Choosing a licence for Thornswood's own code. I deliberately left it alone, as instructed. (2) Putting the credits page live with .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site. (3) Entry 170 still has to put the source directions and the GPL/AGPL texts into the installer's READ ME FIRST.txt and next to the files on the release pages. Nothing hands the licence texts over together with the files yet. Entry 170 also edits credits.md, so its branch will clash with this one. (4) New findings for the To Do List (I could not edit it): - a. 37 files and 16.2 MB of another menu's pictures, fonts and music under Data\Platform\UI, plus 4 sprite fonts and 2 images, ship in packs and the installer with no licence we can trace. The rule that lets them through is the flat-file rule for UI at Ship-Rules.ps1:221-225. This could be folded into entry 168. - b. The skymp5-front build.js has no recorded commit, so the source offer does not cover it exactly. It needs rebuilding from the fork and recording, the way the six client files are. - c. The Futura PT and DIN Pro fonts that upstream ships in skymp5-front point at their foundries' own licences. Patrick has to decide what to do about them. - d. The vcpkg licence texts (build\vcpkg_installed\x64-windows-sp\share\<port>\copyright) do not travel with the client runtime. - e. The theme track's artist and terms are not written down anywhere. (5) The entry asked for the collection mods to be listed by author. I did not do that, because Thornswood does not ship them. THIRD-PARTY.md points to the launcher's list (Links.cs) and the credits page instead. NEXT STEP: Branch off main. Write THIRD-PARTY.md at the repo root with one row per third-party component Thornswood itself ships, each with an SPDX id and a link. SkyMP client runtime: MpClientPlugin.dll, SkyrimPlatform.dll, SkyrimPlatformImpl.dll, SkyrimPlatformCEF.exe, skymp5-client.js and TESModPlatform.pex, GPL-3.0 (read the fork's LICENSE files for the exact version), with the source directions from entry 170. The server under AGPL-3.0. The three WebView2 files under Microsoft's WebView2 SDK licence, whose distributable-code terms allow redistribution. Chromium Embedded Framework inside skyrim-platform (BSD-3-Clause) if its binaries ship. Each font under Data/Platform/UI and Data/Platform/Fonts, identified from the font's own name and licence tables; if one cannot be identified, say so in the file rather than guess. Cross-check mechanically: every /resource: in Build-Launcher.ps1, every file in tools/lib, and every file a pack or installer ships that the collection does not provide is either ours or listed. Add a plain-words paragraph to credits.md or terms.md linking it. Do not list the loose mod assets in the payload as if they were licensed: that is entry 168. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #333. The reviewer's major finding was real, and it was not already fixed on the branch. THIRD-PARTY.md said the CEF and Node runtime under Data\Platform\Distribution was "Not shipped by Thornswood". Thornswood publishes those files itself as a Nexus mod, Thornswood Client Runtime (mod 192762, file 809366, version 1.0.0, a required mod in collection revision 5). The fix, commit 5f85034: (1) New section "Thornswood Client Runtime, Thornswood's mod on Nexus Mods". It covers the mod id, the file, the collection's size and md5, and 68 files totalling 366,157,850 bytes. It has a table of each part with ... STILL TO GO OUT: Deploy-Docs.ps1 (the live site; see the entry for which switches). Left: 1. Push the branch and open, then merge, its pull request. After the merge, run .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site so the public credits page gets the new paragraphs. 2. Two things only Patrick can do on Nexus, both in the next upload of the Client Runtime mod: - The README.txt names the fork branch but no commit, and ___systemPolyfill.js is no longer on that branch. Either name 43eedb56 for it, or leave the file out, since nothing in the shipped client loads it. - Consider shipping ICU 71's own licence text in place of the newer V3 text, and a licence for d3dcompiler_47.dll. 3. origin/main is 2 ...

## Read first

- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:110-132 and :244`: where three Microsoft WebView2 redistributable files are compiled into the shipped exe, which is one of the things a notices file has to cover
- `tools\Patch-Client.ps1:1-45`: the record that the shipped client bundle is a GPLv3 SkyMP build patched here, which is where entry 58's source offer lives
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\credits.md`: the public page that already names what the project stands on, and the natural companion to the notices file

## Steps

- [ ] Confirm the absence for yourself rather than taking it on trust: there is no LICENSE, COPYING, NOTICE or THIRD-PARTY at the root of either repository, checked by name and by listing. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path . -Force -File | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'LICENSE|COPYING|NOTICE|THIRD-PARTY' }
  ```
- [ ] Leave the source unlicensed, which is normal for a product, and add only the other half: a notices file and public terms. (claude)
- [ ] Write THIRD-PARTY.md at the repo root listing, each with its licence and a link: skymp5-client and skyrim-platform as GPLv3, skymp5-server as AGPLv3, the three Microsoft WebView2 files embedded by Build-Launcher.ps1, and the Nexus collection mods by author. (claude)
- [ ] Put the GPL written offer from entry 58 in the same file, because those two entries ship together or the offer has no home. (claude)
- [ ] Put the same list in plainer words on a site page beside credits.md, because that is where the public looks. (claude)
- [ ] Cross-check mechanically rather than by memory: every /resource: in Build-Launcher.ps1 and every file under tools\lib must be either yours or listed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Pattern '/resource:'
  ```
- [ ] Send it out: Deploy-Docs.ps1 (the live site; see the entry for which switches). (patrick)

## Commands

- Start the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/third-party-notices
  ```
- Returns nothing today and must return THIRD-PARTY.md afterwards. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path . -Force -File | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'LICENSE|COPYING|NOTICE|THIRD-PARTY' }
  ```
- Lists every file compiled into the shipped exe, each of which must appear in the notices. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Pattern '/resource:'
  ```
- Lists the shipped libraries, the other set the notices file has to cover. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem tools\lib -Recurse -File | Select-Object Name, Length
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/third-party-notices
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```
- Puts the public notices page on the VPS. Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Done when

THIRD-PARTY.md exists at the repo root, every binary the installer or the launcher ships that was not written here appears in it, and every /resource: hit in Build-Launcher.ps1 and every file under tools\lib is either the project's own or listed by name and licence.

## Traps

The notices file is where entry 58's source offer lives, so those two ship together or the offer has no home. The installer payload also carries third-party mod assets, which is a redistribution problem a notices file does not solve and must not be used to paper over; that is entry 56. The secrets rule still applies: if a config example ends up quoted, name the location and never the value.

## Links

- https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.en.html AGPLv3, the licence covering skymp5-server

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/concepts/distribution what Microsoft requires when you redistribute the WebView2 files Build-Launcher.ps1 embeds
- https://help.nexusmods.com/article/18-do-i-need-permission-to-use-a-mod-in-my-video-or-mod-pack Nexus Mods' terms, the ones the collection mods sit under, for the by-author section

issues.title: The installer is a snapshot of your game folder with your home folder path baked into the script, and it is stale by design
issues.body:
**Order:** 200 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Old number:** 33

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:490-513 (the hard-coded path); tools\Ship.ps1:453-499

## What is known

A bootstrap that fetches the current manifest and syncs. Until then remove the hard-coded home path and make Ship refuse when the installer is behind. It was five releases behind at 1.1.47, and anyone installing from it sits through all of them on first launch MEASURED AGAIN 22 SEPTEMBER, in the 1.1.78 Ship's own output: "Thornswood-Setup.zip is 9 releases behind, built 20 Sep 19:06. Anyone installing from it sits through all of those on first launch. Nobody who already has the game is affected." The public feed still offers Thornswood-Setup-20260920-1902.exe. Ship says this every time and nothing acts on it, which is the shape this entry is about. Package-Thornswood.ps1 rebuilds it and takes about twenty minutes. REBUILT 22 SEPTEMBER. Package-Thornswood ran and published Thornswood-Setup-20260922-1141, and the old 20260920-1902 pair was removed from the site. The feed offers the new one. It went 9 releases behind before anybody acted on the line Ship prints every time, which is the shape of this entry rather than an aside: it is one release behind again already. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #228. WHAT CHANGED: tools/Package-Thornswood.ps1 now has a -ReleaseDir parameter. It sits last in the param list so no positional argument shifts. Left empty, it resolves to the Thornswood-Releases folder beside the repo, the same place Ship, Publish-Update and Check-ShipReady already look. The hard-coded 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Releases' path is gone, and so is the fallback to the repo's own stale version.json. The lookup now runs before the game is closed or anything is staged. A missing version.json stops the packager with a named reason: the folder it looked in, the git clone command, and -ReleaseDir. It no longer builds an installer with a stale applied.txt or none at all. Ship.ps1 is not changed, because its own lookup falls back to the repo root and passing that value through would bring the fallback back. MEASURED: Derived path on this machine: C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Releases\version.json. It exists and is a git clone; the lifted block ran against the real tools folder and returned it without stopping. The live feed lists 227 packs: 164 on the private repo (api.github.com/repos/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/releases) and 63 on the public host. The repo-root version.json (last written 20 Sep 23:19) lists 164 packs and is missing 63 of the live ones. So on any machine without the home-folder path, the old fallback seeded an installer that fetched those 63 packs again, and with no file at all all 227 were pending. The old lines were tools/Package-Thornswood.ps1:567 (the literal) and :568 (the fallback). The new lookup block is at tools/Package-Thornswood.ps1:139-159, before Close-Launcher, Head 'Packaging' and Stop-Game; the applied.txt section now uses the $vLive it found (:597). The new harness tools/test-package-release-dir.ps1 gives 25 passed, 0 failed under both pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1. Against main's copy of the packager it gives 2 passed, 4 failed (no -ReleaseDir, the C:\Users literal at line 567, stray Join-Path onto version.json at 567 and 568, no markers). WHAT IS LEFT: Patrick decides the second half of the entry: whether a main Ship refuses while the installer is behind. The choices are to refuse before the publish unless -Package is given, to make -Package the default on main (it runs after the publish and does not block), or to keep the yellow warning. Every main release puts the installer one release behind by construction, and since 23 Sep a main Ship is only for a security fix or an untestable game, so a hard refusal would put a twenty-minute rebuild in front of an urgent fix. That is why this branch does not touch the gate. Also for Patrick, on his machine: the next Package-Thornswood run (his to run, about twenty minutes) should print '227 packs marked as already in this build' or the current count; that end-to-end check was not done here. The bootstrap that syncs to the current manifest is entries 87 and 88, not this branch. Not in scope and still carrying the same home-folder default for -ReleaseDir: tools/Publish-News.ps1:34, tools/Publish-Discord.ps1:68 and tools/Publish-Pack.ps1:30. They are worth their own entry or a note on this one.

## Read first

- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:488-495`: the applied.txt seeding; :491 is the hard coded $vLive = Join-Path 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Releases' 'version.json' and :492 is the fallback that silently lands on the repo's own version.json
- `tools\Ship.ps1:445-500`: the behind count and Show-Installer, including the comment explaining why the count was moved above the early return; it prints yellow and never refuses
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1`: Package-Thornswood dot-sources it, so what the installer may carry is decided there rather than in the packaging script

## Steps

- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/installer-path-and-behind-gate origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Replace the literal at Package-Thornswood.ps1:491 with a path derived from $here, which the script already sets at :450, or take a -ReleasesDir parameter defaulting to it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 487 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Repoint or drop the fallback at :492: it resolves to the repo root's own version.json, which is the 15 September copy with 164 packs and zero stamps newer than the zip, so a broken primary path currently reports behind 0 instead of failing. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path version.json -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 488 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] In Ship.ps1, beside the existing Head 'The installer' block at :454-478 where $behind and $haveZip are already in scope, turn the yellow warning into a Die on the main channel when $behind is greater than zero, and leave -Channel dev alone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 450 -First 31 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the derived path resolves to the live Releases feed and not to the repo copy. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Test-Path (Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools')) 'Thornswood-Releases\version.json')
  ```
- [ ] Parse both scripts with the same gate the build check uses, then push and open the pull request. (claude)
- [ ] Leave the bootstrap that fetches the current manifest and syncs out of this branch; that is entry 87 and entry 88 and it is a larger change. (claude)

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the derived path and the Ship gate. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/installer-path-and-behind-gate origin/main
  ```
- Proves the derived expression lands on the live Releases feed. Expect True. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Test-Path (Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent 'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools')) 'Thornswood-Releases\version.json')
  ```
- Shows when the shipped installer was built and how big it is, which is what the behind count is measured against. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Item C:\Thornswood\_dist\Thornswood-Setup.zip | Select-Object LastWriteTime, Length
  ```
- Runs the build check's parse gate on the packaging script. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1).Path,[ref]$null,[ref]$e); $e
  ```
- Exercises the new refusal without publishing anything. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Ship.ps1 -DryRun -NoPause -Notes "behind gate dry run"
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub for the build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/installer-path-and-behind-gate
  ```

## Done when

The derived expression returns True against the live Releases folder, a missing primary path no longer falls back to the repository's own version.json, both scripts parse clean, and a main Ship stops with a named reason while the installer is behind while a dev Ship still runs.

## Traps

Package-Thornswood.ps1 builds the installer, takes about twenty minutes and is Patrick's to run, not yours. It also writes applied.txt from the live version.json: break that path and a fresh install stops being seeded, so every one of the 192 packs becomes a pending update on first launch and 164 of them 404 because that repository is private. The fallback hides a broken primary path silently, so test the primary explicitly rather than trusting that packaging succeeded. Nothing here may be mixed with the own game folder branch shape; what ships today is the Steam copy with Vortex.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/split-path Split-Path -Parent, which is how the derived path walks up from the tools folder
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/join-path Join-Path, for building the Releases path without a hard coded home folder
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases/blob/main/version.json the published feed the behind count compares the installer against
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases/releases the release assets a stale installer has to replay on first launch

issues.title: The virus warning is honest, too long, and in the wrong place
issues.body:
**Order:** 201 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Website · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 81

## Where it lives

VPS · site · public\home.html:836-861, a block that opens the download page by telling people Windows may call the file a virus

## What is known

Signing is the real fix and it is entry 2. Until then: one sentence above the button, the SHA-256 beside the size and date, and a link to the VirusTotal report for that hash rather than instructions for running one. The honesty is right; the length and the position are where a stranger closes the tab UPDATE 17 September: Microsoft removed the detection on the submitted installer, so the warning block is now describing something that is not currently happening. Cut it to one sentence and the hash now rather than leaving a wall of text about a virus alert a visitor will not see. Keep a short honest line, because an unsigned installer will be flagged again. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #229. WHAT CHANGED: The Downloads page now shows the installer's SHA-256 under its size and date, with a "VirusTotal report" link for that hash, in both download layouts. The hash comes from Publish-Installer.ps1. It now runs Get-FileHash on the exe it publishes and writes the result as sha256 on the exe's files.json entry, for the one-file build and for the pair. When it finishes it also prints the VirusTotal address for that build. server.js listFiles passes the hash on to /api/public in lower case, and only when it is exactly 64 hex characters. An installer published before this change has no hash, so the page shows nothing extra rather than a broken link. Patrick's 20 Sep removal of the warning block (2fa5dbe) was left as it is. MEASURED: New harness tools/test-download-hash.js runs 38 checks and all pass. On the code before this change, 18 of its checks failed (15 passed, 18 failed out of 33; the PowerShell section never ran because the hash line did not exist). What it runs: - Publish-Installer.ps1's own hash line and files.json block in PowerShell against a temp file, compared with node's SHA-256. Proved under pwsh 7 and under Windows PowerShell 5.1. - server.js listFiles against a temp folder with an uppercase hash, a malformed hash and a file with no entry. - The whole /downloads branch of the page script with fetch stubbed. It checks all three layouts (one-file build, stub with hidden payload, stub with visible payload), then a missing hash, a site with no sha256 field, and a malformed hash, which is never put in the page. What the diff touches: tools/Publish-Installer.ps1 (hash line near :108, sha256 on the two exe entries near :161 and :173, VirusTotal line at the end), tools/docs-app/server.js listFiles (:444-451) and tools/docs-app/public/home.html (sum() near :878, used at :936 and :947). The "Wacatac" count in home.html is 0, so the doneWhen condition on the detection name holds. Parse checks: Publish-Installer.ps1 has 0 parse errors in pwsh and in PowerShell 5.1. server.js, the harness and both inline scripts in home.html pass node --check. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick: 1. Decide whether the page gets one short honest sentence about a possible Defender warning. The entry's 17 Sep update asked for one. His own 20 Sep removal (2fa5dbe) took the whole block out, and this branch does not put any of it back. The doneWhen condition "one sentence plus a collapsed details element" is overtaken by that removal and should be reworded on the To Do List. 2. The VirusTotal link only shows a report once someone has uploaded that exact build to VirusTotal. Until then it lands on VirusTotal's not-found page. Publish-Installer now prints the address at the end so this is one click to check. Doing it automatically needs a VirusTotal API key, which is an outside account and his decision. 3. The hash only appears on the live page after the next Package-Thornswood / Publish-Installer run and a Deploy-Docs of server.js and home.html. Until then files.json has no sha256 and the page shows exactly what it shows today. For the merger: entry 173 (patrick/todo-173-installer-integrity) edits the same $meta block in Publish-Installer to hash the zip. This branch only touches the exe entries and puts its hash line right after $exeItem. It should merge cleanly, but check that block when both land. Entry 2 (signing) is still the real fix.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:790-870`: the downloads step builder, including the comment at :797-799 recording why the button sits under the step that tells you to take it; do not undo a considered decision
- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:839-852`: the warning itself, guarded by if (exe), twelve lines of prose naming Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml and explaining the ml suffix
- `tools\Publish-Installer.ps1:115-136`: where files.json is written, which is where the SHA-256 this page needs has to come from, and that is entry 61

## Steps

- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/download-warning-shorter origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Cut :839-852 down to one sentence above the button, along the lines of: Windows may warn about this file because it is not signed yet, the SHA-256 is below and you can check it on VirusTotal. (claude)
- [ ] Keep the rest of the current text inside a collapsed details element rather than deleting it, because the reasoning is good and the honesty is the part the row praises. (claude)
- [ ] Print the SHA-256 beside the size and date, taking it from the payload data the page already receives, which means entry 61 has to land first. (claude)
- [ ] Link the VirusTotal report for that hash instead of telling people to upload 527 MB themselves, and never tell anybody to switch off Defender. (claude)
- [ ] Keep the closing line saying that not clicking past a malware warning is a reasonable thing to do. (claude)
- [ ] Confirm the detection name now appears once at most and only inside the collapsed text, then open home.html locally to check it renders. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\public\home.html -Pattern 'Wacatac').Count
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the download page copy. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/download-warning-shorter origin/main
  ```
- Counts how many times the detection name appears. Expect 1 at most, inside the collapsed text. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\public\home.html -Pattern 'Wacatac').Count
  ```
- Shows whether the hash is on the page yet. It returns nothing today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\public\home.html -Pattern 'sha256|checksum|SHA-256'
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub for the build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/download-warning-shorter
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

The downloads step renders as one sentence plus a collapsed details element, the SHA-256 shows beside the size and date, a VirusTotal report link for that hash is there instead of upload instructions, and the detection name appears at most once and only inside the collapsed text.

## Traps

Signing is the actual fix and it is its own entry, which says to start the signing service's identity validation now because it takes days; anything here is interim and should read that way. The hash cannot be published until something computes it, which is entry 61, so this has a hard dependency. Do not shorten the warning into something dismissive. Entries 62 and 71 edit the same builder function, so sequence them.

## Links

- https://www.virustotal.com/ where a published hash is looked up, so people read a report rather than uploading half a gigabyte
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/malware-naming how Microsoft names a detection, the type, platform, family, variant and suffix parts of a name like Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/artifact-signing/ Microsoft's managed end to end signing service, now called Artifact Signing, which is the real fix for an unsigned installer
- https://thornswood.net/downloads the page as a stranger meets it today, warning and all

issues.title: No screenshots or footage anywhere on the site
issues.body:
**Order:** 202 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Trust · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 80

## Where it lives

VPS · site · public\home.html:104-109, 338-352, 501-509 (the gallery band hides itself when gallery.json is empty)

## What is known

Twenty to thirty in-game shots at the next session, six chosen, resized, uploaded, gallery.json written, and the band unhides itself. Nobody joins a world they cannot see, and the machinery is already there waiting for the file MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The page side is ready. home.html:1104-1116 unhides #gallerySection when /api/public returns a gallery, and the /gallery page at home.html:828-843 draws the same list. Both read s.url and s.by, with by used as the alt text. server.js:1770 reads data\gallery.json. server.js:1906-1925 serves /shot/<name> from uploads\ only when the name is listed in gallery.json (lowercase comparison), with a one-day cache. tools/docs-app/data has no gallery.json. Two corrections to the entry. First, each item is {name, url:'/shot/<name>', by}, and the pictures belong in the site's uploads folder, which /api/upload fills (server.js:2062-2098, needs a signed-in member, prefixes names with yyyyMMdd-HHmm-), not in data. Second, Deploy-Docs sends data\*.json only when the file is missing on the VPS (Deploy-Docs.ps1:181-190), so the first gallery.json goes up with any run and later edits need -Docs gallery.json. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build. When the pictures exist: upload them through the site, write gallery.json with name set to each upload's stored filename, url set to '/shot/' plus that name, and by set to a caption that works as alt text. Check it with node, then run Deploy-Docs. Correct the entry's steps with the field shape and folder above. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Needs a person in the game: twenty to thirty screenshots at a session, six chosen, and every tester who can be seen agreeing to be published. Patrick.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:1005-1025`: the script that reads the gallery array and unhides the band at :1013; this fixes the exact shape every entry must have
- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:501-509`: the hidden gallerySection and the empty gallery div, the machinery already waiting for the file
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:969 and 1109-1113`: where gallery.json is read into the page data and where a picture request is refused unless it is listed in that file
- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:104-109`: the hero comment, which sets the bar: a fake picture would be worse than none

## Steps

- [ ] Read home.html:1005-1025 and write down the exact field names an entry needs before anybody takes a photograph. (claude)

  ```powershell
  Get-Content tools\docs-app\public\home.html | Select-Object -Skip 1004 -First 21
  ```
- [ ] Take twenty to thirty shots at the next session and pick six that show people rather than scenery. (patrick)
- [ ] Ask every tester whose character or name is visible before publishing their picture, because the people in the shots are testers and nothing states yet what is public. (patrick)
- [ ] Resize the long edge to about 1600 pixels and save as WebP or well compressed JPEG under about 250 KB each. (patrick)
- [ ] Write gallery.json listing the six in the field shape from step one, and check it parses as an array of the right length. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node -e "const g=require(process.env.TEMP+'/gallery.json'); console.log(Array.isArray(g), g.length)"
  ```
- [ ] Put the pictures and gallery.json into the site's data pictures folder on the VPS and deploy, after which the band unhides itself. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```
- [ ] Pick the best of the six as the 1200x630 share image entry 78 needs, under 300 KB. (patrick)

## Commands

- Prints lines 1005 to 1025, the gallery reader, so the JSON matches the field names the page expects. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Content tools\docs-app\public\home.html | Select-Object -Skip 1004 -First 21
  ```

gallery.json parses as an array of six entries whose field names match home.html:1005-1025, every image is under about 250 KB, and after the deploy the gallery band on the home page has lost its hidden attribute and all six pictures load.

Every picture has people in it and those people are testers, so ask before publishing anybody's character or name. The pictures go into the site's data folder on the VPS and are deployed by Deploy-Docs.ps1, which is Patrick's script to run.
