issues.title: The main menu draws the backdrop twice, and the picture it draws is 8.5 times too small, has no mipmaps, and is built to a plane shape the mesh disagrees with
issues.body:
**Order:** 203 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Trust · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** new

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo.nif and logo01ae.nif are byte identical, md5 5c3cf588, both named CivilWarMap01, both pointing at the same texture · Game\Data\textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds, 4096x4096 DXT1, 8,388,736 bytes, one mip level · source art tools\art\thornswood-art-1536.png at 1536 x 1024 · tools\Build-Backdrop.py defaults to the Steam copy, not C:\Thornswood\Game · brief tools\art\ART-PROMPT.md, measured spec tools\art\BACKDROP-SPEC.md

## What is known

Two defects, and the cheap one ships first. PART ONE, THE DOUBLE, CONFIRMED by Patrick on 17 September. Both logo meshes are byte identical copies of one replacer plane named CivilWarMap01, and both reference MAINMENUWALLPAPER.dds. Skyrim carries both names because the Anniversary Edition menu draws a second plate under the first, so whoever made this replacer overwrote both and the menu now draws the backdrop twice. The fix is one float: in logo01ae.nif the root BSFadeNode scale sits at offset 0x163 and reads 0.8; set it to 0.0 and the mesh collapses to a point and draws nothing. Four bytes, same file length, still parses, all five blocks intact, verified on a copy. Do not simply delete logo01ae.nif, because the game then falls back to the vanilla Anniversary Edition plate inside Skyrim - Meshes1.bsa and you get a Bethesda logo over the backdrop instead. Note also that neither mesh is in this repo and neither is in any of the 157 Vortex staging folders; they were dropped into the Steam Data folder by hand, six copies exist on disk, and nothing restores them if they go. Bring both into the repo in the same change. PART TWO, THE PICTURE. Ask the artist for 4466 x 3016 PNG, 8 bit RGB, sRGB, no alpha. The floor below which the build enlarges is 4450 x 3005. What is in the repo is 1536 x 1024, which is 2.897 times too narrow, 2.935 times too short and 8.5 times too few pixels. THE PLANE IS NOT 3:2: parsed from the mesh, the drawn aspect is 1.4807558229, so even a perfect 3:2 source is 1.283 percent wrong before anything is resampled. The nearest clean ratio is 77:52. The safe rectangle on a 4466 x 3016 source is left 107, top 622, right 4359, bottom 2394 for everything up to 21:9, and top 910, bottom 2106 if 32:9 counts. The brief's middle 80 percent of the width was needlessly tight; the true figure is 95.2381 percent. The texture should be BC7_UNORM with 13 mip levels at 22,369,796 bytes, picture in rows 0 to 3004 with the last row repeated rather than black, because black padding bleeds up into the picture at every mip level. DXT1 with a full chain is 11,184,952 bytes and is the cheap option. Exact header values are in BACKDROP-SPEC.md. STILL OPEN: the 105 percent of screen width figure that every safe-zone number scales from appears once in the repo, in a docstring, recorded as eyeballed. One dev build with a ruler in the picture settles it. Also open: whether to re-fit the mesh to a true 3:2 rather than matching the script to the mesh, which is a Patrick and Djinn call in #dev. IN FLIGHT 17 September: pull request 64 carries the measured spec and the corrected artist brief. It is open, green, and blocked only on the review. It is the correction half only. The artwork itself, the mesh fix for the double, and the Build-Backdrop.py changes are all still to do. MERGED 19 September: pull request 67 (d3f855e) adds tools/art/thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png, the overlook with the wordmark, measured at 1535 x 1024. That is one pixel narrower than the 1536 x 1024 this entry measures as 8.5 times too few pixels against the 4466 x 3016 the spec asks for, so the resolution half is still open. The pull request changed no mesh and not Build-Backdrop.py, so the double draw and the build changes are still open too. THE BANNER IS ON THE SITE, 20 September, commits f90ce3e then c60c5d0, and that is one of the three places asked for. The hero was ridge.svg, a generated ridgeline, and is now the ANIMATED banner: the same tools/launcher-header.mp4 the launcher plays in its title band, 1.0 MB, 24 seconds, H.264 with no audio, served as banner.mp4. The first attempt used the still PNG and that was the wrong asset, corrected within the hour. muted and playsinline because autoplay is only allowed without sound and iOS opens it fullscreen otherwise; the still is the poster, so it is both the first paint and what anybody who asked for less motion sees instead. Deploy-Docs lists the public folder rather than keeping names, so both files go out unnamed. NEITHER IN-GAME SLOT CAN PLAY IT, which is worth saying before somebody sees it and thinks it failed. Skyrim's main menu is a DDS texture, Data\textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds, and its loading screens are NIF meshes with their own textures. Both take a frame, never the animation. AND THE GAME SIDE IS MAPPED, NOT BUILT. The backdrop is built from tools/art/thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png by tools/Build-Backdrop.py, and commit d3f855e added the source picture and nothing else, so the built texture only ever existed on the machine that built it. That is exactly why Djinn is the only person who has seen it. Three things stand in the way: Build-Backdrop.py needs Pillow, which is not installed on Patrick's machine; Go.ps1 copies ts-ui and ts-plugins into the game folder and has no path for art at all; and the folder is rebuilt by OwnGame from what Vortex deployed with a sweep at the end, so a file of ours has to be shown to survive that sweep before any of this is worth building. WHY ONLY DJINN SAW IT, AND WHY THE SITE COPY LOOKED WRONG. 20 September. The banner did go on the front page, and then Patrick reported it as the old picture and not moving. Both were true and both were mine. FIRST, the site served banner.mp4 as text/plain: the TYPES map in tools/docs-app/server.js had no .mp4 and no .jpg, so both fell through to the default, and with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on every answer a browser is not allowed to guess past that. The file arrived whole, status 200, correct bytes, and was refused. Nothing errored anywhere, which is what made it look like the wrong file had been published. SECOND, with the video refused the poster was the entire hero, and the poster was built from tools/art/thornswood-banner-1672.png, which is different art in a different shape: 1672x941 against the video's 1536x300. So the front page showed older art, and showed it still. One screen, two causes. Fixed in 5c0b36a (the types, plus byte ranges, because Safari and iOS ask for a range before playing a video and give up when the answer ignores the header) and f98bfb4 (the poster is now tools/launcher-header.jpg, the video's own first frame, byte for byte what the launcher embeds). CORRECTING THIS ENTRY: the line above saying the first attempt used the still PNG and was corrected within the hour is only half right. The VIDEO was right from c60c5d0 and still is, same md5 as tools/launcher-header.mp4. It was the POSTER that stayed wrong until f98bfb4. The range handling was checked by lifting the branch out of server.js and driving it with a fake request, 18 assertions, including that bytes=-100 is the last hundred and not the first. NOT DEPLOYED YET: both commits sit on main on Patrick's machine. server.js changed, so this needs the full Deploy-Docs.ps1 with no switch, not the -Site form. Until that runs the live site is still serving the video as text. COVERED AT THE MENU, 20 September, commit 7515bcf: the character choice page now draws the site's banner behind its panel, the still at once and the loop over it if the browser decodes H.264 (unknown; the page says which in the front log as 'painting: ...'). So while the choice is up the doubled, soft menu backdrop is not visible. The meshes and the texture are untouched and this entry stands for the game's own menu before and after the page. DONE BAR THE RENDER, 20 September, commit f1372b0, at Patrick's word. Measured first: every game folder on this machine (Thornswood, DevBuild, the Steam copy) had both meshes at md5 5c3cf588 with root scale 0.8 and the texture at md5 dbb15e20, 4096x4096 DXT1, one mip level. PART ONE: both meshes are in the repo under tools/art/menu; logo01ae.nif has the four bytes at 0x163 set to 0.0, so the second plate draws nothing. PART TWO: Build-Backdrop.py rewritten to the spec (77:52, 3005 rows, last row repeated, thirteen DXT1 mips, writes into the repo) and run on thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png, the new painting: 11,184,952 bytes, 13 levels. It is a 2.7x enlargement and will read soft; the artist's 4466 x 3016 render is the only thing that makes it sharp and is the one item still open here. Go.ps1 copies the three files into every game folder it runs on (removing the destination first, since in an own folder they are hard links into the Steam copy) and Ship carries them. tools/Check-Backdrop.ps1 -Game <folder> is the read only check and prints green once the pack is in. ART-PROMPT.md already says 77:52 and not 3:2, checked. ON DEV, 20 September 15:35: pack 20260920-1535-dev carries logo01ae.nif collapsed and the 13 mip texture, and Check-Backdrop on the dev build folder reads green. LEFT: see it in the game, then the artist's 4466x3016 render for a sharp texture. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Commit f1372b0 landed both halves. tools/art/menu holds logo.nif, logo01ae.nif and Mainmenuwallpaper.dds, and Go.ps1:145-160 copies them into the game folder. I ran tools\Check-Backdrop.ps1 -Game C:\Thornswood\Game (read only). It printed: logo01ae.nif md5 09565b43, root scale 0.000, collapsed; Mainmenuwallpaper.dds 4096x4096, 13 mip levels, DXT1, 11,184,952 bytes; each '= the repo copy'; and 'one plate, mipped texture, all as the repo has them.' The source art is still thornswood-mainmenu-1535.png at 1535x1024, against the 4466x3016 the spec asks for. Correction to the traps: Pillow 11.3.0 is installed under 'python', though not under 'py'. texconv is still absent. NEXT STEP: Nothing left to do in code. When the artist's 4466x3016 PNG arrives: check its size and mode, run python tools\Build-Backdrop.py on it, check the result with Check-Backdrop, then dev Ship. Update the trap line about Pillow. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick has to look at the main menu in the game and confirm one plate; that is the only open check of the double-draw fix. The 105 percent screen-width figure needs a dev build with a ruler in the picture, looked at in the game. A sharp texture needs the artist's 4466x3016 render, which is outside work.

## Read first

- `tools\art\BACKDROP-SPEC.md`: the full measured spec, every number with its proof and the exact DDS header values
- `C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif`: the duplicate plane, root scale float at offset 0x163
- `tools\Build-Backdrop.py`: the build, and the docstring whose 3:2 claim the mesh refutes
- `tools\art\ART-PROMPT.md`: the artist brief, corrected 17 September

## Steps

- [ ] Confirm the two logo meshes are still byte identical, which is why the backdrop draws twice. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo.nif, C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif -Algorithm MD5
  ```
- [ ] Set the root node scale in logo01ae.nif to zero so that copy of the plane draws nothing. Four bytes at offset 0x163, file length unchanged. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import struct; p=r'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif'; b=bytearray(open(p,'rb').read()); struct.pack_into('<f', b, 0x163, 0.0); open(p,'wb').write(bytes(b))"
  ```
- [ ] Check the edit landed and nothing else moved. The scale must read 0.0 and the file must still be 10562 bytes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import struct,os; p=r'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif'; b=open(p,'rb').read(); print(os.path.getsize(p), struct.unpack_from('<f',b,0x163)[0])"
  ```
- [ ] Do not delete logo01ae.nif instead. The game falls back to the vanilla Anniversary Edition plate in Skyrim - Meshes1.bsa and you get a Bethesda logo over the backdrop. (claude)
- [ ] Copy both logo meshes into the repo so they are tracked, because neither is in git and neither is in any Vortex staging folder. (claude)
  ```powershell
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force tools\art\meshes; Copy-Item C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\*.nif tools\art\meshes\
  ```
- [ ] Ship the mesh fix on its own, before any new artwork, because it is four bytes and it is confirmed. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "The main menu draws the backdrop once"
  ```
- [ ] Settle in #dev whether to match the script to the mesh or re-fit the mesh to a true 3:2. Everything below assumes the first. (patrick)
- [ ] Commission the picture at exactly 4466 by 3016, PNG, 8 bit RGB, sRGB, no alpha, painted at that size rather than upscaled. (patrick)
- [ ] Check the delivered file before it goes near the build. Width, height and mode must match the brief exactly. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "from PIL import Image; im=Image.open(r'tools\art\new.png'); print(im.size, im.mode, im.width/im.height)"
  ```
- [ ] Keep the emblem, the wordmark and anything readable inside left 107, top 622, right 4359, bottom 2394. Use top 910 and bottom 2106 instead if 32:9 screens count. (claude)
- [ ] Change Build-Backdrop.py as section D of the spec sets out: the measured aspect, one resample instead of two, edge repeat instead of black padding, a real mip chain, and an output path inside the repo. (claude)
- [ ] Build the texture and confirm the header reports 13 mip levels and the right linear size. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py tools\Build-Backdrop.py tools\art\new.png tools\art\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds
  ```
- [ ] Ship it on dev and look at the menu at 1920 and at 3440 before it goes to main. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "New main menu backdrop"
  ```

## Commands

- shows both logo meshes are the same file, which is why the backdrop draws twice (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo.nif, C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif -Algorithm MD5
  ```
- zeroes the root scale so the duplicate plane draws nothing (patrick)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import struct; p=r'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif'; b=bytearray(open(p,'rb').read()); struct.pack_into('<f', b, 0x163, 0.0); open(p,'wb').write(bytes(b))"
  ```
- lists every game folder that shares the mesh, so you know what one edit touches (claude)
  ```powershell
  fsutil hardlink list C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\meshes\interface\logo\logo01ae.nif
  ```
- shows why a write to the Steam copy currently reaches the game by luck (claude)
  ```powershell
  fsutil hardlink list C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\textures\interface\objects\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds
  ```
- builds the texture from a delivered picture (claude)
  ```powershell
  py tools\Build-Backdrop.py tools\art\new.png tools\art\Mainmenuwallpaper.dds
  ```
- puts the mesh fix on the dev feed so the menu can be looked at (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "The main menu draws the backdrop once"
  ```

## Done when

One backdrop loads, not two: done. The texture header reports 13 mip levels: done. Both logo meshes are tracked in the repo: done. Build-Backdrop.py writes into the repo: done. STILL OPEN: the picture sharp at 3440 wide, which needs the artist's 4466 x 3016 render fed to Build-Backdrop.py, and Patrick seeing one plate in the dev build.

## Traps

The mesh edit touches four game folders at once, because all copies are hard links to one file. Do not delete logo01ae.nif as a shortcut; the vanilla plate replaces it. Do not test the doubling by disabling a plugin, because that moves the load order and produces entry 12. The 105 percent of screen width figure that every safe zone number scales from is unverified and appears once, in a docstring, recorded as eyeballed. Build-Backdrop.py cannot run on this machine today: Pillow is not installed under any of the three Python installs, and texconv is not present either.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3ddds/dds-header the DDS_HEADER fields that have to change
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dxgiformat/ne-dxgiformat-dxgi_format DXGI_FORMAT 98 is BC7_UNORM
- https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/wiki/Texconv texconv, which is what writes BC7 with a mip chain
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d11/bc7-format why BC7 endpoints stop the sky banding BC1 causes
- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:File_Format_Conventions how Skyrim resolves a loose file against the one in a BSA
- https://pillow.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/Image.html the resize and crop calls the script uses

issues.title: The icon set is one file and it is the old one, across the launcher, the site and every share link
issues.body:
**Order:** 204 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Trust · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** new

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app.ico is the only icon in the repo, embedded by tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, and tools\app\Register.cs:96 points the Installed apps row at the exe so it inherits that same icon · VPS · site · tools\docs-app\public\favicon.ico (237 KB) and tools\docs-app\public\presence.png (1.4 MB)

## What is known

In progress. Deliver it once as a set rather than one file: a multi-size .ico for the launcher and the Installed apps row, a 15 KB multi-size favicon plus an SVG for the site, and a 1200x630 share image under 300 KB. Doing it as a set closes the icon half of entry 80 at the same time. The launcher icon also shows in the Start menu and the taskbar, so it wants the small sizes drawn deliberately rather than downscaled. PART LANDED 19 September: pull request 68 (a7c65e0) replaces the artwork in tools/app.ico and tools/docs-app/public/favicon.ico and adds a 192 pixel icon-192.png linked from both site pages. Measured on main: the two .ico files are still byte identical at 255,344 bytes, seven frames of which 16 to 128 are uncompressed bitmaps and the 128 alone is 67,624 bytes, so the favicon is still far over 15 KB. There is no SVG, and the share image is still the relative /presence.png at 1,450,149 bytes. What is left: a small favicon, the SVG and the share image. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The site half is done. Commit 2e7bda8 (#161) made tools/docs-app/public/favicon.ico 10,723 bytes, three PNG frames at 16, 32 and 48. It also added og.png at 1200x630 and 174,497 bytes, which the header check confirms, and home.html:42-45 now uses it as an absolute og:image and twitter:image. Measured tools/app.ico: 255,344 bytes, 7 frames. The 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 128 frames are uncompressed bitmaps (the 128 alone is 67,624 bytes) and only the 256 is PNG. The two .ico files are no longer identical: app.ico md5 7CD05EBB, favicon.ico md5 F99D6984. The only SVG in the repo is ridge.svg, and tools/art holds no vector source for the emblem. The launcher reads its icon through ExtractAssociatedIcon (Shell.cs:1009), which handles PNG frames. Pillow 11.3.0 is available under 'python'. NEXT STEP: Can be done now, optional and small: rewrite tools/app.ico with every frame PNG-compressed and each existing frame's pixels kept, using Pillow's ICO reader and writer. Print the frame table to prove all seven sizes are there as PNG, then compile with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root to a temp folder. Update the entry to say the favicon and share image are done. Left for Patrick: the SVG needs a vector drawing of the emblem, and the small frames at 16 to 48 drawn by hand are art. Once those exist, replace app.ico, dev Ship, and run Fix-Icons.ps1 on his machine. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick has to agree or commission the vector emblem for the SVG and the hand-drawn small frames. Both are art.

## Read first

- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:143-145, 234, 242, 299, 342-347`: every place app.ico is used: found next to the script or in -Src, passed as /win32icon, embedded as a resource, stamped on the setup stub, and copied out as icon-<hash>.ico
- `tools\app\Register.cs:96`: DisplayIcon is set to the exe, so the Installed apps row inherits whatever icon the exe carries; there is no second file to update
- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:19-20`: the two icon link tags, favicon.ico and logo.png, which is what a browser tab reads
- `tools\app.ico`: 237,344 bytes, seven frames at 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256; only the 256 is PNG compressed and the 128 alone costs 67,624 bytes as an uncompressed bitmap. favicon.ico is byte identical to it

## Steps

- [ ] Agree the artwork once with Patrick before anybody exports, because the same drawing lands on the launcher, the Start menu, the taskbar, the Installed apps row, the browser tab and every share link. (patrick)
- [ ] Draw the small sizes deliberately at 16, 24, 32 and 48 rather than downscaling the 256, because those are the frames the taskbar and the Installed apps row actually read. (patrick)
- [ ] Export one multi size .ico with every frame PNG compressed, and check what came out before shipping it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $b=[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('tools\app.ico'); $n=[BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b,4); "frames $n"; 0..($n-1) | ForEach-Object { $o=6+$_*16; [pscustomobject]@{ W=$(if($b[$o] -eq 0){256}else{$b[$o]}); H=$(if($b[$o+1] -eq 0){256}else{$b[$o+1]}); Bytes=[BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b,$o+8) } }
  ```
- [ ] Replace tools\app.ico with the new file and rebuild; Build-Launcher.ps1:143 picks it up with no code change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] Put a 15 KB multi size copy at tools\docs-app\public\favicon.ico and add an SVG icon beside it, keeping both link tags at home.html:19-20. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\public\home.html -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 15 -First 8 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Produce a 1200x630 share image under 300 KB to replace presence.png, which is 1,450,149 bytes today, and hand it to entry 78 which makes the og:image absolute. (patrick)
- [ ] After the new exe is installed, clear the shortcut icon cache, because Windows keeps drawing the old picture and a pinned taskbar item keeps its own copy. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Fix-Icons.ps1
  ```

## Commands

- Shows the four icon and share assets and their sizes as they stand. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Item tools\app.ico, tools\docs-app\public\favicon.ico, tools\docs-app\public\presence.png, tools\docs-app\public\logo.png | Select-Object Name, Length
  ```
- Lists every frame inside the .ico with its pixel size and byte cost, which is how you see the wasted 128 x 128 bitmap. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $b=[IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('tools\app.ico'); $n=[BitConverter]::ToUInt16($b,4); "frames $n"; 0..($n-1) | ForEach-Object { $o=6+$_*16; [pscustomobject]@{ W=$(if($b[$o] -eq 0){256}else{$b[$o]}); H=$(if($b[$o+1] -eq 0){256}else{$b[$o+1]}); Bytes=[BitConverter]::ToUInt32($b,$o+8) } }
  ```
- Rebuilds the launcher and the setup stub with the new icon embedded. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- Prints what the shortcuts point at, clears the Windows icon caches and restarts Explorer. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Fix-Icons.ps1
  ```
- Sends the new favicon, SVG and share image to the site. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Done when

tools\app.ico is one file with the small sizes drawn rather than downscaled and every frame PNG compressed, favicon.ico is under about 15 KB, an SVG icon sits beside it, the share image is 1200x630 and under 300 KB, and a rebuilt Thornswood.exe shows the new icon in the taskbar once the icon cache is cleared.

## Traps

tools\app.ico and tools\docs-app\public\favicon.ico are byte identical today, so replacing one and not the other leaves the launcher and the site disagreeing. Build-Launcher.ps1:143 prefers the app.ico next to itself over the one in -Src, so a stale copy in tools wins silently. Windows keeps drawing the cached icon long after the exe changed and a pinned taskbar item keeps its own copy, which is what Fix-Icons.ps1 exists for. Do not ship an .ico without the 16 and 32 frames.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/menurc/about-icons how Windows picks an image out of an icon resource, the closest size first, which is why the small frames have to be in the file
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/link the link element and rel="icon", including the sizes and type attributes both tags use
- https://ogp.me/ the Open Graph properties a share card is built from, including og:image, which the 1200x630 picture fills
- https://thornswood.net the tab icon and the share card as they look right now

issues.title: Discord onboarding is written out field by field and has never been switched on
issues.body:
**Order:** 205 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 191

## Where it lives

VPS · site · data\todo.md section 8 has every field: nine default channels, the hold question that hands out Member and ten citizen roles, and a second optional question

## What is known

Nothing to run, it is server settings, and the copy is already written. It is also the cleanest place to put the rules acceptance and the age question from entries 69 and 69, so doing it closes three rows at once MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: In tools/docs-app/data/board.json, section s24n rows r25n to r34n are all done=false. r25n still says 'These are nine, six writable' while its own list has five writable channels, so the typo is still there. Build-Discord.py:110-146 builds the nine 'Citizen of <hold>' roles and Member. All fourteen channels the rows name (welcome, rules, start-here, news, general, media, character-introductions, tales, rp-appreciation, test-these, lore, applications, game-rules, faq) are in Build-Discord.py. Nothing in tools/discord or tools/*.ps1 touches Discord onboarding (grep). NEXT STEP: Patrick in Discord: Server Settings, Onboarding, following r25n to r34n, then Preview. Fix the r25n typo from the site hub. board.json is edited live, and the repo copy only goes up with Deploy-Docs -Boards, which overwrites the live board, so a repo edit is the wrong route. If Patrick would rather script it, Discord's API has a Modify Guild Onboarding endpoint that Build-Discord.py could write, but running it changes the live guild. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Discord server settings, which only Patrick can change. He and Djinn also need to decide whether the rules acceptance and age statement go into onboarding too (entry 181), so onboarding is switched on once.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json, todo board, section s24n, rows r25n to r34n`: the whole script to follow; the copy is already written field by field and every row is still done=false
- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json, row r25n`: the nine default channels; its middle cell says six writable while its own list says five, and five is the number Discord requires
- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json, section s5, row s5r0`: the shorter Onboarding card, so the same work is not started twice from two cards

## Steps

- [ ] Agree with Patrick and Djinn that the rules acceptance from entry 69 and the age statement from entry 70 go in here, because switching onboarding on twice is the thing to avoid. (patrick)
- [ ] Print the nine rows so the wording in front of you is the wording in the file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8'; python -c "import json,io; d=json.load(io.open('tools/docs-app/data/board.json',encoding='utf-8')); [print(r['id'], r['cells']) for s in d['todo']['sections'] if s['id']=='s24n' for r in s['rows']]"
  ```
- [ ] Create the nine Citizen roles in Discord before building the question, because an option cannot grant a role that does not exist yet. (patrick)
- [ ] In Server Settings, Onboarding, add the nine default channels from r25n: welcome, rules, start-here and news read only, general, media, character-introductions, tales and rp-appreciation writable. (patrick)
- [ ] Add question one from r26n as pick one with members must answer, then the ten options from r27n, each granting Member plus its own Citizen role except Not decided yet, which grants Member only. (patrick)
- [ ] Add question two from r28n as pick several and optional, granting channels only and no roles. (patrick)
- [ ] Paste the Server Guide text from rows r31n to r33n as written, then fix r25n in board.json, which says six writable while listing five. (claude)
- [ ] Walk Preview at the top right of Server Settings, Onboarding, per r34n, and check each option shows the role you meant. (patrick)

## Commands

- Prints all nine onboarding rows with their exact copy, which is the script to follow. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8'; python -c "import json,io; d=json.load(io.open('tools/docs-app/data/board.json',encoding='utf-8')); [print(r['id'], r['cells']) for s in d['todo']['sections'] if s['id']=='s24n' for r in s['rows']]"
  ```
- Shows row r25n's two cells so the six writable typo can be checked before and after the fix. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:PYTHONIOENCODING='utf-8'; python -c "import json,io; d=json.load(io.open('tools/docs-app/data/board.json',encoding='utf-8')); print([r['cells'] for s in d['todo']['sections'] if s['id']=='s24n' for r in s['rows'] if r['id']=='r25n'])"
  ```
- Reports what the Discord server currently has against what the builder expects. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Check
  ```

## Done when

Preview at Server Settings, Onboarding walks end to end and every option shows the role you meant, and in board.json row r25n no longer says six writable while its own list says five.

## Traps

Five writable channels is the exact Discord minimum, not a comfortable margin, and read only channels do not count toward it, which r29n already anticipates with its note that a refusal will be the channel count. The Citizen role names have to exist and match exactly before the question is built. This is server settings, so a Claude cannot do it and there is nothing to ship; the only repo change is the one line typo fix. board.json is edited from the hub as well as the repo and last save wins, so make that fix once.

Entry is an explicit act: a rules question, a rules-acceptance role through Discord onboarding, or a first-launch acceptance recorded against the Discord id. Today the one line that must change on launch day is sitting in a comment, and a stranger can join for the invite embed, press Play, and have agreed to nothing MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Still entirely closed-playtest. server.js:158-173 has the comment 'add Member to this list and that is the entire change', and access.play has no Member. server.js:194 merges cfg.access from the VPS config, and standing() sets out.play at :1362. bot.py:382-396 keeps KINDS with 'playtest' first, :430-431 sets AGE_Q and AGE_KINDS=('playtest',), and the PANEL at :842-854 says 'Apply to playtest is the one everybody starts with'. Bootstrap.cs:471-475 is the only acceptance anywhere, and it is the age checkbox. A grep for a rules acceptance across tools/app, tools/setup, server.js, bot.py and gamemode.js finds none. The word 'playtest' appears in bot.py 7 times, content.py 3, Build-Discord.py 2, home.html 4 and server.js 7, plus join.md, privacy.md, terms.md and classes.md. No flag exists yet. NEXT STEP: After the #dev line: on a branch, have server.js read cfg.open (default false). When true, add Member to cfg.access.play at load and expose open on /api/public. The bot already calls SITE (bot.py:61) and can read the flag from /api/public, or from its own environment if that is what they agree. It then drops playtest from KINDS and AGE_KINDS and switches PANEL to an open variant. The notice bar and hero in home.html and the wording in join.md follow the same flag. Harnesses: tools/test-open-flag.js lifts standing() and checks that Member alone plays with the flag on and does not with it off; tools/discord/test-open.py checks KINDS and PANEL both ways. Then node --check and py_compile. Left for Patrick: agree the flag name and its source with Djinn in #dev (entry 72 is the site half of the same switch); choose the rules-acceptance mechanism, which depends on Discord onboarding from entry 180; and flip the flag in the site's config.json on the VPS on launch day. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Needs a #dev agreement between Patrick and Djinn on the flag name and source. Patrick decides how rules acceptance is recorded (onboarding role or first-launch acceptance), and that depends on entry 180's Discord settings. The launch-day flip is a production config change on the VPS.

## Read first

## Steps

- [ ] Compile both sides and unit check standing() with the flag on and off, then try it on dev and say in #dev that you have taken the dev feed. (claude)

## Commands

This is the launch day switch, so it goes on dev first, and there is one dev feed where the last dev Ship wins. issues.title: What the eighteen-plus gate actually achieves, and what adult content obliges
issues.body:
**Order:** 207 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Legal · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 153

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs:471-475 and 524-529 (a checkbox that enables the Install button) · VPS · bot · tools\discord\bot.py:320-352 · site · data\site\rules.md:11-30

## What is known

A checkbox is a record, not a gate, and that is fine as long as it is treated as one. Use the platform's own age controls where they exist, put the statement on the door rather than implying it, and say in the terms page what the server is. Entry 40 is the one automated check and it currently goes quiet in the case it exists for MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The statement is on rules.md:10-25 and terms.md:12 and :21-23. The terms page landed in 9706317 (#167). Neither page says that the installer box and the Discord answer are kept as a record, not as verification. Terms also does not say what the server contains; only rules.md:15-17 does. The landing page and the downloads builder have no age line at all: grep 'eighteen|adult' in home.html finds only the /terms blurb at :725, and the downloads lede at :897-906 names Skyrim, Vortex and the closed playtest but not age. The Discord WELCOME text at content.py:10-48 has no age line either. The 'goes quiet' half (the entry 40 reference) is fixed by 1db2c05 (#166). I extracted said_yes from bot.py (now at :430-470, not :314-355) and ran it in a scratch harness. Answers read as no: "I'm 16", '16', 'my brother is 30, im 16', 'born in 2009' and 'no'. Answers read as yes: '27', 'im 34' and 'yeah im 19'. Bootstrap.cs:471-475 (checkbox) and :524-535 (the gate, and the else branch that enables Install when the control is missing) are unchanged and correct. grep 'verif' across the site markdown, content.py and help.md finds no claim that age is verified. tools\discord\README.md says nothing about age restricted channels. NEXT STEP: rules.md, after :13: one plain paragraph saying the installer box and the Discord answer are kept as a record of what somebody said, not a check. terms.md, 'Who can be here': say what the server contains (sexual content between adult characters, violence, language) and add the same record sentence. home.html: one short 'Eighteen and over' line in the notice bar (:391-397) or under the hero pitch (:452), plus a sentence in the downloads lede at :897 before the installer step. The lede is inside a JS string, so no em dashes and keep the quoting intact. content.py WELCOME: an 'Eighteen and over' line near the top, pointing at the rules. README.md: a short section on which channels are age restricted and why, written once Patrick has said which. Leave said_yes and the Bootstrap else branch alone. Check: grep 'eighteen' across data\site\*.md and home.html; python -c import content; open home.html from a scratch copy of the site to see the lede render. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick marks the channels that carry adult content as age restricted in Discord's server settings, or says that none do (rules.md:37-38 says nothing graphic goes in public channels). He also re-posts #welcome with .\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Posts, which asks for the bot token at the keyboard and rewrites the read-only channels.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\site\rules.md:10-26`: the eighteen and over section as people actually read it, including the sentence that applying, being in the Discord or connecting is a statement of age; this is the text everything else has to match
- `tools\discord\bot.py:314-355`: AGE_Q, AGE_KINDS, the _NO and _YES tuples and said_yes(), whose comment at :316-319 already states the honest position that it is a record and not a gate
- `tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs:465-535`: the checkbox at :471-475, the button gate at :524-529 and the else branch at :531-535 that enables Install anyway when the control cannot be found

## Steps

- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/age-statement-on-the-door origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Extend the existing wording at rules.md:12-13 with a plain paragraph saying what the server is and that the checkbox and the Discord answer are kept as a record of a statement somebody made, not as verification, rather than duplicating it elsewhere. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\data\site\rules.md -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 8 -First 8 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Put the adult server line where a stranger meets it before downloading or applying, which means the site's home page and the Discord join card, not only inside the installer at Bootstrap.cs:475. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 471 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Mark the Discord channels that carry adult content as age restricted in Discord's own settings, which is a person's action, and write it into tools\discord\README.md so it is not lost. (patrick)
- [ ] Leave said_yes() as generous as it is and do not tighten the else branch at Bootstrap.cs:531-535 into a hard failure, which would produce an installer nobody can start. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\setup\Bootstrap.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 527 -First 11 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Check the statement now appears on the terms page as well as rules.md and before the download on the home page. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\data\site\*.md -Pattern 'eighteen|18 or over'
  ```
- [ ] Compile anything you touched, then push and open the pull request. (claude)

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the age statement wording. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/age-statement-on-the-door origin/main
  ```
- Shows which public pages carry the statement. Today it is rules.md only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\data\site\*.md -Pattern 'eighteen|18 or over'
  ```
- Shows whether the line appears before the download on the home page. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\public\home.html -Pattern 'eighteen|18 or over|adult'
  ```
- Checks the bot still compiles if you touched said_yes or AGE_Q. (claude)
  ```powershell
  python -m py_compile tools\discord\bot.py
  ```
- Compiles Bootstrap.cs if you touched the installer's XAML or its checkbox code. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

The statement appears on the terms page as well as rules.md and on the home page before the download, the Discord channels carrying adult content are marked age restricted and that is written into the bot's README, the bot still compiles and the installer still builds, and nothing anywhere claims the server verifies age.

## Traps

Bootstrap.cs is C# 5 under the .NET Framework 4 csc, and its XAML at :465-475 lives inside a verbatim string with doubled quotes, so every quotation mark in the markup is two; get that wrong and the build fails. The else branch at :531-535 deliberately enables Install when the checkbox control is missing, so do not tighten it without thinking about an installer nobody can start. Site page text is people facing, so no em dashes and never the word this project does not use. Do not write anything claiming the server verifies age; it does not, and saying so would be worse than saying nothing.

## Links

- https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel the channel object and its nsfw field, described there as whether the channel is age restricted
- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html discord.py's reference, for reading how the bot's modal answers are recorded
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.controls.checkbox the WPF CheckBox and its Checked and Unchecked events, which is exactly what gates the Install button
- https://thornswood.net/rules the eighteen and over statement as people read it today

issues.title: The rules disagree with themselves on the one rule people get banned over
issues.body:
**Order:** 208 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** RP fit · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 60

## Where it lives

Discord · tools\discord\content.py:163-174, 190-192 (ask before you draw) · VPS · site · data\site\rules.md:102-110 (fights start freely, ambush them on the road) · Your PC · lore\game-rules.md:22-31

## What is known

Make rules.md the source, turn the lore copy into a pointer, generate the Discord copy from it, and fix the escalation order to match who can actually do what. Two people in the same fight can each be following the posted rules today MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The three copies still disagree. rules.md:102-110 says '## 3. Fights start freely' and 'does not need asking first'. content.py:172-174 says '**4. Ask before you draw on someone.**' and 'Fighting another character takes one line out of character first'. lore\game-rules.md:46 says '## 4. Fights between people are agreed first'. git log -S shows all three wordings arrived in the 16 Sep import (5b1ee05) and none has changed since. No commit, HANDOFF or rules text records a choice; grep across *.md finds only WORKING-NOTES.md:1025-1037 restating the contradiction. The rule numbers differ between copies, so 'rule 4' means different things in different places. The enforcement section at rules.md:280-287 names Moderator then Gamemaster. The gamemode has no staff kick, ban or jail command (its /mute at :18439-18512 is one person muting another), and tools\discord\README.md:129 says a Gamemaster can time out but not ban. So the escalation names roles and powers that exist only in Discord. NEXT STEP: Once the rule is chosen: make rules.md the source. Replace lore\game-rules.md's body with a pointer to /rules. In content.py, replace only GAME_RULES with a pathlib loader that reads the '# In the World' part of rules.md, splits on '## ' and rewrites relative links to https://thornswood.net. Leave RULES (the seven Discord conduct rules) alone. Word the enforcement section as a Discord timeout or removal, which is what exists. Check: python -c 'import content; print(len(content.RULES), len(content.GAME_RULES))', and the two greps give one file and none. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn choose 'fights start freely' or 'ask before you draw' in #dev. Loading GAME_RULES from rules.md before then would settle it for them in rules.md's favour. Afterwards Patrick re-posts with .\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Posts (asks for the bot token).

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\site\rules.md:102-110`: "3. Fights start freely. What they cost does not" and "Combat against another character does not need asking first", the public copy and the one proposed as the source
- `tools\discord\content.py:149-212`: GAME_RULES, ten roleplay rules, whose rule 4 at :172-174 says "Ask before you draw on someone" and "Fighting another character takes one line out of character first", the opposite of the site
- `tools\discord\content.py:50-82`: RULES, a different document: seven Discord conduct rules including the only written no slurs and no sexual content involving minors lines. Sourcing this from rules.md would delete them
- `lore\game-rules.md:46`: "4. Fights between people are agreed first", the third copy, which agrees with Discord and contradicts the site
- `tools\discord\Build-Discord.py:135-215`: the PLAN table, where the rules channel is mode='read' and post=C.RULES, which is the mechanism that would read from markdown instead

## Steps

- [ ] Patrick and Djinn pick one of fights start freely or ask before you draw in #dev before any code; this is settled design and a Claude does not settle it for them. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/one-copy-of-the-rules origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Make rules.md the only copy of the roleplay rules and replace lore\game-rules.md's body with a pointer to /rules. (claude)
- [ ] Replace only GAME_RULES in content.py with a module level loader that reads rules.md at import time, stripping the front matter and splitting on '## ' so each rule is its own message under Discord's 2000 character limit. (claude)
- [ ] Leave RULES alone: it is the seven conduct rules and none of them are in rules.md. (claude)
- [ ] Correct the escalation order in rules.md's enforcement section so it names powers that exist, which today is a Discord role and nothing inside the game. (claude)
- [ ] Check content.py still imports and that only one wording survives across tools and lore. (claude)
  ```powershell
  python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/discord'); import content; print(len(content.RULES), len(content.GAME_RULES))"
  ```
- [ ] Patrick re-posts the channel text, which rewrites a read only channel people have already read. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Posts
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the rules contradiction. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/one-copy-of-the-rules origin/main
  ```
- Finds every copy of the site's version of the fight rule. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path tools,lore -Recurse -File -Include *.md,*.py | Select-String -Pattern 'does not need asking first'
  ```
- Finds every copy of the Discord and lore version, which says the opposite. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path tools,lore -Recurse -File -Include *.md,*.py | Select-String -Pattern 'Ask before you draw'
  ```
- Checks content.py still imports and both documents are still there after the loader change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'tools/discord'); import content; print(len(content.RULES), len(content.GAME_RULES))"
  ```
- Re-posts the channel text from content.py into the read only channels. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Posts
  ```

## Done when

One of the two searches returns exactly one file and the other returns nothing, content.py still imports with both RULES and GAME_RULES present, lore\game-rules.md points at /rules instead of carrying its own copy, and the enforcement section names powers that exist.

## Traps

Which way this goes is a design decision between Patrick and Djinn, not a Claude's to settle. Rule numbering changes break every existing link and every moderator's habit of citing rule 4, and rule 4 already means two things: rules.md has nine rules and folds one away, while GAME_RULES and lore\game-rules.md have ten. Build-Discord.py posts into mode='read' channels, so re-running the builder rewrites live channel content. content.py is also entry 73, so decide whether the two changes go out together or the second one will conflict.

## Links

- https://thornswood.net/rules the public copy, the one the row proposes making the single source
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/message the message object and its content field, which is what each split rule is posted into
- https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html pathlib, for the module level read that lets content.py load the markdown at import time

issues.title: The public copy still describes a closed playtest in nine places, and rule 4 contradicts the download page
issues.body:
**Order:** 209 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Website · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 75

## Where it lives

VPS · site · public\home.html:328-335, 347, 379-384, 795-884; data\site\join.md:26; rules.md:44

## What is known

One join story in one place, and an open flag beside the server's own that swaps the notice bar, the hero button and the download copy together, so opening the doors is one change rather than a hunt through nine strings and two markdown files. Entry 69 is the same switch on the Discord side; they should be the same flag MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: There is no open flag: grep in server.js finds none. The entry's line numbers are stale, because home.html is now 1126 lines. The closed-playtest strings are at home.html:393-395 (notice bar and 'Apply →'), :454 (hero 'Apply to playtest', pointing at /downloads), :493 (card 02, 'application while we are playtesting'), :635 (closing 'Apply in the Discord'), :903 (downloads lede, 'We are in closed playtesting'), :936-938 ('Apply first, then four steps') and :990-994. They are also at join.md:26 and terms.md:94 ('It is in closed playtest'), and content.py WELCOME, START and FAQ carry the Discord copies, which are entry 181. rules.md:44, 'Do not share the installer outside the Discord', contradicts home.html:990, 'The installer is open to anybody. The world is not'. The downloads data object is built at server.js:1760-1775. Its collection address arrives by version.json collectionUrl, then Publish-News.ps1's payload, then news.json, then feed.collection. That route survives the Deploy-Docs -Password config wipe and is a file the bot on the same box could also read. NEXT STEP: Add `open` beside collectionUrl in version.json. Carry it in the Publish-News payload, then expose it in the server.js public data object as a strict boolean that defaults to false when missing. In home.html, gate the notice bar, the hero button text and href, card 02, the downloads lede, the step heading and first step, and the closing paragraph on d.open. With the flag false, the page is byte-for-byte today's copy. For join.md and terms.md, either the page swaps in a short generated paragraph when open, or the closed sentences move into a marked block the server drops when open. Check: node --check server.js. Then run a scratch copy of tools\docs-app on its own port with the flag false and with it true, fetch /, /downloads and /join, and grep 'closed playtest|Apply to playtest' in each. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick agrees one flag and where it lives with entry 181, the Discord side. He writes or approves the open-state copy, because what the hero says when the doors open is a public promise. He also decides the installer sharing policy, so that rules.md:44 and home.html:990 say the same thing.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:780-905`: the downloads page builder, where most of the closed playtest strings live inside a JavaScript template rather than static markup
- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:329-335 and :347`: the notice bar, "Closed playtest. Thornswood is not open to everybody yet", and the hero button, "Apply to playtest"
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:960-1000`: where the page's data object is assembled beside gallery and collection, which is where an open flag arrives

issues.title: The repository's own docs still describe the Skyrim Together product
issues.body:
**Order:** 218 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Leftovers · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Old number:** 86

## Where it lives

Your PC · README.md, all 97 lines (co-op, a party menu on F2, a password in Discord, send it to Gavin); SETUP.md, all 66 lines, describing a repo, a token and a build script that do not exist; tools\Message to friends.txt; config.example.json

## What is known

A short Thornswood README saying what the repo is and linking SECOND-DEVELOPER.md and the site; delete the superseded files rather than leaving them beside the current ones. The Drive link inside it is entry 10 and should go first. It also breaks the repo's own no-em-dash rule in four places PART DONE 24 September, pull request #265. WHAT CHANGED: I fixed the reviewer's major. This time `git rm SETUP.md` went through, where it had been refused twice before. New commit 9ca78d0, "SETUP.md is gone, and nothing lists it any more", does four things: - Deletes SETUP.md, the 66-line walkthrough of the old product: the skyrim-together repo, the personal access token, C:\SkyrimTogether\config.json and a build script that does not exist. - Takes SETUP.md out of CLAUDE.md:248 ("Where things are"). I edited CLAUDE.md only because the entry names that line, and it would be false once the file is gone. - Replaces SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:354. It now says README.md is what the repo is and where to start, a customer's install is tools\docs-app\data\site\join.md, and a developer's machine is the "Setting up a machine" section of the same file. - Adds three checks to tools/test-repo-docs.js: SETUP.md is not tracked, CLAUDE.md does not name it, and SECOND-DEVELOPER.md does not name it. The header comment now says why. The earlier commits on the branch already covered the rest of the entry: README.md rewritten, tools/READ ME FIRST.txt rewritten rather than removed, and config.example.json matching the defaults in Config.cs with an empty UpdateToken. tools/Message to friends.txt was already off main. The whole branch against origin/main is now 7 files: CLAUDE.md, README.md, SECOND-DEVELOPER.md, SETUP.md (deleted), config.example.json, tools/READ ME FIRST.txt and tools/test-repo-docs.js. The worktree is detached at 9ca78d0. MEASURED: The entry's done-when searches: - grep 'Skyrim Together' README.md: nothing. - Em dash search over README.md, CLAUDE.md, SECOND-DEVELOPER.md and tools/READ ME FIRST.txt: nothing. - git grep drive.google.com: one hit, WORKING-NOTES.md:1449, which quotes the search command itself and is not a link. The test matches drive.google.com after a scheme for that reason. - SETUP.md is not on disk and not in git ls-files. node tools/test-repo-docs.js: 49 passed, 0 failed (the three new checks included). test-source-bytes.js: 2 passed. Full sweep: every tools/test-*.js, every tools/voice/test-*.js and every tools/test-*.ps1 under pwsh exited 0, except tools/test-command-ack.js. That test failed on the first sweep and on 2 of the 5 reruns after it, then passed 49/49 on the rest. It binds the fixed port 7911, and netstat showed that port in TIME_WAIT from other connections, which fits other worktree sessions running the same sweep at the same time. This branch does not touch it or anything it reads. No .ps1, .py or tools/app file changed, so there was nothing to parse and no launcher build to run. The Discord tests were skipped because the bot did not change. WHAT IS LEFT: One part of the entry's done-when is still open: a green build check on a pull request. No pull request exists yet, and pushing and opening one were outside this run's limits. Patrick (or a session he runs) pushes patrick/todo-193-docs-product-name and opens the pull request. Once it is merged, nothing needs deploying, because documentation reaches people on the push.

## Read first

- `README.md, all 97 lines`: titled # Skyrim Together at :1, the five person co-op line at :3, the Google Drive link at :8, the password line at :60-61, the F2 party line at :63 and a person's name at :92; seven em dashes at :8, :16, :45, :63, :77, :80 and :86
- `SETUP.md, all 66 lines`: describes creating a repository at :16, a read only token at :19-29 and a build script at :52 that does not exist; CLAUDE.md:97 and SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:319 both still list this file
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:451-454`: it copies tools\READ ME FIRST.txt into the customer installer and prints a warning when it is missing, so that file is shipped and has to be rewritten rather than deleted
- `config.example.json`: still carries the old server address, port 25565 and an UpdateRepo pointing at the old product's repository

## Steps

- [ ] Branch off main, one fix on it, and do not fold the licence and notices work into the same branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/readme-is-thornswood origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Take the Google Drive link out first or in the same change, because redistribution is its own problem and it is the part that reaches strangers. (claude)
- [ ] Replace README.md with about thirty lines: what Thornswood is, that this repository is the launcher, the plugins, the site, the bot and the scripts, and links to SECOND-DEVELOPER.md and the site. (claude)
- [ ] Rewrite tools\READ ME FIRST.txt rather than deleting it, because Package-Thornswood.ps1:451-454 ships it to customers and warns when it is gone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 447 -First 10 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Remove SETUP.md and tools/Message to friends.txt, and take SETUP.md out of CLAUDE.md:97 and SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:319 in the same commit. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git rm SETUP.md "tools/Message to friends.txt"
  ```
- [ ] Either delete config.example.json or rewrite it with the current address and port and an empty update token, never a real one. (claude)
- [ ] Check the old product name, the em dashes and the Drive link are gone, then push and open the pull request and wait for a green build check. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path README.md -Pattern 'Skyrim Together' -SimpleMatch
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the documentation rewrite. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/readme-is-thornswood origin/main
  ```
- Finds the old product name in the README. Expect nothing when this is done. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path README.md -Pattern 'Skyrim Together' -SimpleMatch
  ```
- Finds every em dash, which the repo's own wording rules forbid. There are seven in README.md and one in SETUP.md today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path README.md,SETUP.md -Pattern ([string][char]0x2014) -SimpleMatch
  ```
- Finds the Google Drive link anywhere it still survives. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path . -Recurse -File -Include *.md,*.txt,*.json,*.ps1 | Select-String -Pattern 'drive.google.com'
  ```
- Removes the two superseded documents. Note that tools/READ ME FIRST.txt is not in this list because it ships. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git rm SETUP.md "tools/Message to friends.txt"
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub for the build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/readme-is-thornswood
  ```

## Done when

The old product name returns nothing from README.md, the em dash search returns nothing, the Drive link returns nothing anywhere outside the gitignored scratch folder, tools\READ ME FIRST.txt has been rewritten rather than removed, SETUP.md is gone from the tree and from both documents that listed it, and the build check on the pull request is green.

## Traps

tools/READ ME FIRST.txt is not a leftover: Package-Thornswood.ps1:451-454 copies it into the customer installer and prints a warning when it is missing, so deleting it silently ships an installer with no read me. SETUP.md has the same problem more quietly, being listed in CLAUDE.md:97 and SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:319. Documentation reaches strangers on the next push rather than with a release, so it does not need a coordinated client and server release. _to_delete/ holds stale copies of some of these files and is gitignored; do not edit those. One fix per pull request.

## Links

- https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-readmes what a README is for and where GitHub renders it, which is the audience this rewrite is aimed at
- https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rm git rm, including how to quote a path with a space in it
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases the public repository, whose two line README is the other document with no contact in it
- https://thornswood.net the site the new README should point at instead of repeating the install story

issues.title: The strip behind the title on the Play page moves: out in 1.1.51, left is a look by eye and the CPU check
issues.body:
**Order:** 220 · **Wave:** 5 What a stranger sees · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Djinn · **Old number:** new 19 Sep

## Where it lives

GitHub · pull request 74, branch djinn/launcher-header-video, one commit dd5b97b on top of main 2617295, build check passed · Your PC · tools\launcher-header.mp4 (new, 1,044,645 bytes) · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:159-162, 247 · tools\app\Art.cs:63-116 (HeaderVideo) · tools\app\Shell.cs:750-848 (StartHeaderVideo), called at :920 · tools\ui.xaml:527-531 (HeaderArtVideo) · worktree C:\Users\Ken\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo-headervideo

## What is known

Out in 1.1.51 on 19 September: pull request 74 merged as 06110a5, released in 0f0ef73. On Djinn's machine the 1.1.51 launcher wrote header-beb03d90.mp4 (1,044,645 bytes) beside the exe at 16:19, and launcher.log has no "Title band: the video did not play" line. What is left is looking at it in the real launcher and the CPU check while minimised. Built and measured on 19 September. Djinn pushed the branch and opened pull request 74 the same day, and its build check passed. What is left is Patrick's review and a release. The strip behind the title (pull request 70) now plays a 24 second loop, with the still JPG underneath as the fallback. It is a MediaPlayer painted through a brush, not a MediaElement, because a MediaElement pushed the band from 135 to 195.5 high. It loops on a MediaTimeline, which held one picture for 61 to 78 ms at the join, against 94 to 111 ms for MediaEnded then Position 0; ordinary frames are 33 ms apart. It is stopped, not paused, while the window is minimised or another page is open: a paused timeline still used up to 6.9% of one core, and stopped it measured 0.0 to 0.5%. While playing it uses 3 to 14% of one core. The exe grows by about 1 MB, from 2,163 KB to 3,184 KB. If the build has no video, or the video will not play, the still picture shows exactly as before and one line goes in launcher.log. All of this was measured in a test window that loads the real ui.xaml and calls the real Art and Shell code, not in the launcher itself. NOT TESTED: the real launcher looked at by eye, a Windows N machine, and any theme other than Forge. WORTH DECIDING: with Keep Launcher Open on, the launcher is not minimised while the game runs, so the video keeps playing behind the game and nothing pauses it. The clip's own join is not perfect either: last frame to first measures 40.0 dB PSNR against 47 to 50 between ordinary frames, in the banner at the far left and the mist on the right, both under the heavy side veils. Fixing that means re-encoding the clip. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #293. WHAT CHANGED: The video behind the title on the Play page now stops while the game runs, the same way the menu music does. This settles the entry's WORTH DECIDING point, where the entry says "with Keep Launcher Open on, the launcher is not minimised while the game runs, so the video keeps playing behind the game and nothing pauses it". In StartHeaderVideo, the check for whether the video can be seen now also requires !playing. That check is also stored in a new static field, headerVideoDecide, which does nothing until the video has started. The three places that change playing once the window is up call it straight after: the game starting, the game closing, and a failed start. When the game closes, the video carries on from where it stopped, using the same Begin and Seek the minimise path already uses. The code part of the entry is done. The status is partial because the entry is only finished once a person has watched it in the real launcher. MEASURED: Read in C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log: 42 "Starting the game" lines since 19 Sep, 41 "Ready." lines and exactly one title band failure, at line 3186: "2026-09-21 20:48:00 Title band: the video did not play (MILAVERR_UNEXPECTEDWMPFAILURE (Exception from HRESULT: 0x8898050C))". That came one second after "Starting the game on launcher 1.1.75 ... borderless" at 20:47:59. C:\Thornswood\Launcher\header-beb03d90.mp4 is 1,044,645 bytes, dated 19 Sep 14:16. Before this change, the check at Shell.cs:812 (now :826) looked only at page.IsVisible and whether the window was minimised, so nothing stopped the video while the game ran. MusicDecide (Shell.cs:946) already checked !playing. Wire() runs at Shell.cs:250, before playing = Checks.GameRunning() at :294, but the window is not shown until app.Run. The first check that can start the video comes when the page becomes visible (IsVisibleChanged) or the file opens (MediaOpened), and both happen after :294 has run, so the startup case needs no call. The new harness tools/test-header-video.js takes the check's code straight out of Shell.cs and runs it against a stand-in clock, window and page, then checks that a headerVideoDecide() call follows every assignment to playing in the Shell class (6 files). It gives 37 passed, 0 failed on the new code. On the old Shell.cs (copied into a scratch folder) it gives 24 passed, 13 failed, exit 1. Not measured: whether stopping the video during play prevents that MILAVERR failure. ClockController.Stop takes effect on the next timing tick, and the Play handler holds the UI thread through Process.Start and Thread.Sleep(1200) at Shell.cs:3964, so the video may still decode for the first second or so of a game start. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick: land it (push, pull request, merge) and do a dev Ship: .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "The moving picture behind the title stops while the game runs and picks up again when it closes". After that, a person has to look at the real dev launcher. (1) Open the Play page and watch the band through at least one full 24 second loop. It should move and loop with no black flash. (2) Minimise the launcher: Task Manager should show Thornswood near 0% CPU. (3) Tick Keep Launcher Open in Settings, press Play, and look at the band while the game runs. It should hold still and show a picture, not black. (A stopped WPF MediaClock's frame has not been seen with the launcher's real rendering. That is the one thing this change makes visible that nobody has looked at yet.) Task Manager should show the launcher near 0% CPU during the session. (4) Quit the game: the band should move again from where it stopped. Still open on the entry and not touched here: Patrick decides whether to re-encode the clip so the loop joins cleanly (40.0 dB PSNR from last frame to first, against 47 to 50 between ordinary frames). Djinn removes the worktree ..\Thornswood-Repo-headervideo and the untracked tools\launcher-header.mp4 copy on his own machine. Found here and not fixed (a separate defect for the To Do List): the failed-start catch in Play (Shell.cs:3979-3981 now) sets playing = false but never calls MusicDecide. After Process.Start throws, the music stays paused until the window is next minimised and restored, or the Settings music controls change. Also possible later: a video that fails while the game is running (drop() sets gone) could try once more after the game closes, instead of showing the still picture until the launcher is restarted.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Shell.cs:750-848`: StartHeaderVideo and its summary comment, which carries every measured number and why it is a brush, a timeline and a stop rather than a pause
- `tools\app\Art.cs:63-116`: HeaderVideo writes the video beside the exe as header-<hash>.mp4, the way the icon is written, and removes older ones
- `tools\ui.xaml:527-531`: the one new element, between the still picture and the veils

## Steps

- [x] Push the branch and open the pull request. Done 19 September: pull request 74, one commit, opened by Djinn. (patrick)
- [x] Wait for the build check on the pull request. Done 19 September: it passed. It runs Build-Launcher.ps1, so the video is embedded there too. (claude)
  ```powershell
  gh pr checks 74
  ```
- [x] Patrick reads pull request 74 and merges it from GitHub. Shell.cs needs a line in #dev before anyone edits it; Djinn posted that line on 19 September. Done 19 September: merged as 06110a5. (patrick)
- [x] It goes out in the next complete release, run by Ship.ps1 on Patrick's machine. Done 19 September: 1.1.51, commit 0f0ef73. (patrick)
- [ ] Once it is live, open the Play page and watch the band through at least one 24 second loop. Then minimise the launcher and check that Task Manager shows it near 0% CPU. (patrick)
- [ ] After it is merged, delete the untracked copy of tools\launcher-header.mp4 from the main folder before that folder pulls or checks out main, then remove the worktree. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git worktree remove ..\Thornswood-Repo-headervideo
  ```

## Commands

- where the pull request stands, read only (claude)
  ```powershell
  gh pr view 74 --json state,mergeable,statusCheckRollup
  ```

## Done when

Pull request 74 is merged and a release carrying it is out. The band has been seen moving and looping in the real launcher, and the launcher sits near 0% CPU while minimised.

## Traps

Do not try it with Build-Launcher.ps1 on Djinn's machine. That script repoints the Desktop Thornswood shortcut, can restart Explorer, and builds into C:\Thornswood-DevBuild, which does not exist there, so the exe would run as a fresh install on the Steam copy. The main folder C:\Users\Ken\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo also holds an untracked copy of tools\launcher-header.mp4; once main carries that file, checking out or pulling main in that folder refuses until the copy is deleted. The launcher is C# 5 only.

## Links

- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/pull/74 the pull request, with the measured numbers in its description (private repo, sign in)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.media.mediatimeline the timeline the loop runs on
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.media.videodrawing painting a video through a brush, which is what keeps the band at 135
