issues.title: A release is a diff against one machine's memory, not against the last release
issues.body:
**Order:** 228 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Old number:** 100

## Where it lives

Your PC · the baseline in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood · tools\Publish-Update.ps1:168-202, 378-447, 1214; tools\Ship.ps1:365-406

## What is known

This is the manifest entry the earlier rows point at. Publish a manifest per release, every shipped path with size and hash, committed to the releases repo beside version.json. Publish-Update already computes exactly that; switch it to SHA-256 and commit it. Then any machine can produce the same release, Djinn can ship, a dry run needs no copy-aside, and both 17 September incidents become impossible MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Nothing has changed yet. Publish-Update.ps1:475 still stores '{size}:{LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks}' per file. SHA-256 is used only for the two profile lists (:487) and the launcher source (:499). The baseline lives in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood (:215-229): published.json is 84,357 bytes (23 Sep 21:37), published-dev.json 84,368 bytes (22:46), and published.json.bak 693,679 bytes (15 Sep). Save-State is at :509-513 and runs at :1647, after the push. Ship.ps1:543-600 still copies version.json and the baseline aside for a dry run and unbumps. No manifest is written anywhere. Measured the cost the entry warns about with a read-only scratchpad script: SHA-256 of every file published.json lists (891 files, 661.9 MB, none missing) in C:\Thornswood\Game took 13.9 s with Get-FileHash under pwsh 7.6.6. The full walk the scan already does is 30,697 files in 2.6 s. So hashing adds about 14 seconds to a Ship. NEXT STEP: After #dev agrees: (1) Publish-Update.ps1:475: store size:sha256, hashing only the files that survive the filters (891 today). Teach the $prev read to accept old size:ticks entries (compare size, then hash), or the first release after the switch would see all 662 MB as changed. (2) At the version.json step (:1056-1090), write manifest-<Id>.json (sorted path, size, sha256) into $ReleaseDir, add a manifest pointer to version.json, and commit both in the same push. (3) A harness that runs the manifest writer twice over a temp tree and asserts byte-identical output. (4) Keep Ship.ps1's dry run copy-aside until the manifest replaces the baseline. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: This needs a #dev agreement between Patrick and Djinn, because it changes what a release is. Publish-Update.ps1 is shared, and 'any machine can produce the same release, Djinn can ship' touches the settled 'Only Patrick's machine ships main'. The done-when also needs Patrick's shipping machine: two Ship -DryRun runs, then a real Ship whose releases commit carries a manifest. SEEN AGAIN 24 September on hotfix 1.1.93: the live pack carried 21 files (17.4 MB, 12.5 MB zipped) that were byte for byte what testers already had, checked by hash against the live source and the launcher's own saved copies. Something rewrote them in place at 14:47 with the same content, and the baseline compares timestamps, so they went out again. Harmless to people, and a 12.5 MB download for nothing; a content hash in the baseline is what this entry already proposes.

## Read first

- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:168-203`: the comment and the lines that put the baseline in the local app data folder, including why it was moved out of _dist; :177 is the state directory, :178 the published.json beside it and :183-190 the dev baseline
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:378-447`: the scan and the diff; the loop at :381-389 stores size and LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks, only :400 and :412 use SHA-256, and the diff is at :439-442
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:1214`: Save-State, which runs after the push, so a failed push and a saved state are two different things
- `tools\Ship.ps1:355-406`: the dry run copy aside, which exists only because the baseline is mutable local state and an earlier dry run left it looking exactly like a broken release

## Steps

- [ ] Put this in #dev first: Publish-Update.ps1 is on the shared file list and this changes what a release is. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/manifest-per-release origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Change the value stored at :388 from size and ticks to the file's SHA-256, which this script already computes twice elsewhere at :400 and :412. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Publish-Update.ps1 -Pattern 'LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks|Get-FileHash'
  ```
- [ ] Measure the cost before making it the default, because hashing every file in the build runs on every Ship and reading sizes and times does not. (claude)
- [ ] Write that map out as a manifest file, every shipped path with its size and hash, and commit it beside version.json in the same push around :1180-1205. (claude)
- [ ] Keep the dry run copy aside at Ship.ps1:365-406 working until the manifest replaces the baseline entirely. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 361 -First 48 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Confirm two dry runs over an unchanged tree produce an identical manifest and that its entry count equals the mod files number the scan prints at :390. (patrick)

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the per release manifest. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/manifest-per-release origin/main
  ```
- Shows the one place size and time are used and the two places a hash already is, which is the change in one view. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Publish-Update.ps1 -Pattern 'LastWriteTimeUtc.Ticks|Get-FileHash'
  ```
- Shows the baseline state on this machine, the mutable local memory a release is currently diffed against. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem $env:LOCALAPPDATA\Thornswood | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime
  ```
- Runs the build check's parse gate on the publisher. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Publish-Update.ps1).Path,[ref]$null,[ref]$e); $e
  ```
- Produces a manifest without publishing anything. Run it twice over an unchanged tree and compare. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  pwsh -NoProfile -File .\tools\Ship.ps1 -DryRun -NoPause -Notes "manifest dry run"
  ```

## Done when

Two dry runs over an unchanged tree produce an identical manifest, and the releases commit contains a manifest whose entry count equals the mod files number the scan prints at :390.

## Traps

Hashing every file in the build is far slower than reading sizes and times and this runs on every Ship, so measure before making it the default. The dry run copy aside exists because an earlier dry run left the baseline and the feed changed and looked exactly like a broken release; keep it working until the manifest replaces the baseline. Publish-Update.ps1 needs a line in #dev before it is edited, and only Patrick's machine ships main. Entries 88 and 88 both depend on this one.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/get-filehash Get-FileHash, the cmdlet the script already uses twice, and what it costs per file
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases the releases API a manifest would be committed beside, one document per release
- https://semver.org/ why a release needs an identity of its own rather than being a diff against one machine's memory
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases/blob/main/version.json the feed the manifest would sit next to, so both are fetched from one place

issues.title: The feed is an append-only chain of 192 deltas with no rollback and no known-good state
issues.body:
**Order:** 229 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** replace it, rewrite · **Old number:** 101

## Where it lives

GitHub · version.json · Your PC · tools\Publish-Update.ps1:516, 798-813 · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Updater.cs:346-354, 450-462

## What is known

With entry 87 in place the client syncs to a complete manifest instead of replaying history. Rollback becomes publishing the previous manifest as current: one commit, one minute, no rebuild. Install, update, repair and rollback collapse into one code path, old assets can be deleted without breaking anything, and entry 86 stops mattering MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The feed is still append-only. Publish-Update.ps1:1074-1087 appends $chunks to $doc.packs and nothing ever removes one. Updater.cs:357-364 Pending() is the only selector, and ApplyPack replays the chain. There is no per-release manifest (entry 199 has not started: Publish-Update.ps1:475 still stores size:ticks). The live feed has 227 packs in 111,122 bytes. Measured under entry 198: the 164 oldest assets have already been deleted from GitHub (the private repo has 0 releases and the assets answer 404 even with a token). So old assets being deleted has already happened, by accident, and only the applied.txt seeding keeps installs working. NEXT STEP: After 199: Updater.cs reads a manifest pointer from version.json, fetches the manifest, compares it with local files (size, then hash) and fetches only what differs. It reads the old packs shape for one more release. Publish-Update.ps1 writes the manifest together with a way to fetch each file, and version.json shrinks to the launcher, server and manifest fields. Rollback means pointing at the previous manifest. Compile with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root temp, then a dev Ship. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Entry 199 (a per-release manifest) has to exist first. Patrick and Djinn need a #dev agreement on the feed shape, because Updater.cs and Publish-Update.ps1 are shared. Patrick also has a design question the entry does not answer: the assets are zips of deltas and a manifest lists files, so a client cannot sync to a manifest until each file has its own source (files stored by hash as assets, or a map from each file to the pack holding its current version).

## Read first

- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:795-813`: where packs are appended and never pruned; $packs starts at :799, one is added at :804 and the property is set at :812, with no removal anywhere
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:346-354 and :440-462`: Pending() and ApplyPack(), the client end that replays the chain, and Pending() is the only selector there is
- `entry 86 in this list`: this cannot start until a per release manifest is being committed; the manifest is the thing the client would sync to
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:455-500`: the applied.txt seeding that keeps fresh installs off the dead assets, which must stay until the manifest path is live

## Steps

- [ ] Do entry 87 first; nothing here starts until a per release manifest exists. (claude)
- [ ] Put it in #dev: Updater.cs and Publish-Update.ps1 both need a line first, and entry 89 touches the same file. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/sync-to-a-manifest origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Change Updater.cs to fetch the manifest the feed names and sync to it, instead of walking the packs array and replaying history. (claude)
- [ ] Cut version.json down to launcherVersion, launcherUrl, launcherSha256, the server fields and a pointer to the current manifest. (claude)
- [ ] Keep the old shape readable for one release, because launchers already installed must still be able to read the feed. (claude)
- [ ] Do not remove the applied.txt seeding before the manifest path is live, or a fresh install starts replaying assets that 404. (claude)
- [ ] Confirm the launcher compiles and that a fresh install with no applied.txt would reach the current build without touching a private asset url. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the manifest sync. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/sync-to-a-manifest origin/main
  ```
- Shows the client end that replays the chain, which is what gets replaced. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern 'Pending|ApplyPack' -Context 0,6
  ```
- Counts the pack urls pointing at the private repository, in the live feed entry 85 fetches into the scratch folder. The target is zero. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node -e "const v=require(process.env.TEMP+'/live-version.json'); console.log(v.packs.filter(p=>/\/repos\/EvilPatrick06\/Thornswood\//.test(p.url||'')).length)"
  ```
- Compiles the launcher under the .NET Framework 4 csc after the Updater change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub for the build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/sync-to-a-manifest
  ```

## Done when

version.json drops to a few hundred bytes, the count of pack urls matching the private repository in the published feed is zero, a fresh install with no applied.txt reaches the current build, and the launcher still compiles under the .NET Framework 4 csc.

## Traps

C# 5 only in the launcher: no string interpolation, no ?., no nameof, no expression bodied members, no out var. Package-Thornswood seeds applied.txt precisely so fresh installs never replay the dead assets; do not remove that seeding before the manifest path is live. Launchers already installed must still be able to read the feed, so the old shape cannot simply be deleted in one release. Updater.cs is a shared file needing a #dev line, and the self update inside it is being rewritten by another row at the same time.

## Links

- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases releases as the unit a manifest belongs to, which is what makes rollback one commit
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/contents the contents API the launcher fetches both the feed and the manifest through
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases/blob/main/version.json the feed as it is today, the append only chain this replaces
- https://semver.org/ why naming a known good state beats replaying a chain of deltas to reach it

issues.title: The update feed only ever grows, and every launcher downloads all of it on every check
issues.body:
**Order:** 230 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 59

## Where it lives

GitHub · version.json, 59,496 bytes, 192 pack entries · Your PC · tools\Publish-Update.ps1:898 (appended, never pruned) · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Updater.cs:141-160

## What is known

A feed describes the current state, not the archive: a few hundred bytes naming the latest version and what is needed to reach it, served with an ETag. History belongs in release notes. The manifest-per-release entry further down does this properly; this is the interim MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The live feed is now 111,122 bytes with 227 packs, not the 84,588 bytes and 192 packs in the entry. It also carries 40 news items (19,621 bytes) and 32,019 bytes of pack notes. Updater.cs:152-209 Check() fetches api.github.com/repos/<repo>/contents/version.json with Accept vnd.github.raw (:53), and there is no If-None-Match anywhere (grep). Measured with curl: the contents API returns an ETag with Cache-Control public, max-age=60, and a repeat with If-None-Match got 304 Not Modified. But X-RateLimit-Remaining went from 55 to 54 on that 304. Customer launchers have no token (Updater.cs:57-67, and this machine's config.json UpdateToken is empty), so for them a conditional request saves the 111 KB and does not save the rate limit. The rate limit is the bigger problem. Shell.cs:1430-1447 runs CheckUpdatesInPlay every 15 ticks of 2 s, so every 30 seconds while the game runs. That is 120 API calls an hour against GitHub's 60 an hour for an unauthenticated address. Failures are swallowed there (Shell.cs:4518 catch {}), so after about half an hour of play the in-play update countdown stops seeing releases without saying so, and the next launcher start from that address gets the 403 message. raw.githubusercontent.com serves the same file with its own ETag and max-age=300 and has no API rate limit. The prune in entry 198 alone halves the document. NEXT STEP: Now: (1) Updater.cs Check(): keep the last ETag and body in Profile, send If-None-Match, and on 304 parse the cached body. C# 5, compile with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root temp. (2) Once Patrick picks the in-play fix, apply it in Shell.cs:1447 and CheckUpdatesInPlay. Later, after 199 and 200: the small document naming the current release, keeping the fields old launchers and the Mods page read. The finding that the in-play poll runs over the rate limit probably deserves its own To Do entry. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides how the in-play poll stays under GitHub's 60 calls an hour with no token. The options: poll less often, poll raw.githubusercontent.com (no rate limit but up to five minutes of CDN delay), or rely on the server's own countdown broadcast. The document shape waits on entries 199 and 200 and a #dev agreement on Updater.cs and Publish-Update.ps1.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Updater.cs:141-205`: Check(), which downloads the whole document at :156 and holds the rate limit handling; :42 sets the Accept header to the raw media type and :157 passes octet false, so the transfer is the raw file and not a base64 envelope
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:790-815`: where a pack is appended and nothing is ever removed, so there is no prune and no notion of a baseline
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:346-354`: Pending(), the only selector: every pack whose id is not in applied.txt, with no catch up path, which is why trimming the feed to the newest few silently drops mod files
- `version.json in the repo root`: the stale 59,496 byte copy with 164 packs; the live feed is 84,588 bytes with 192, so measure against the live one

## Steps

- [ ] Agree the shape of this row and the two related feed rows in #dev together before writing any of them; they are the same file and the same trip to GitHub. (patrick)
- [ ] Do not publish a small document carrying only the newest few packs: Pending() is the only selector, so any install further behind than that never receives the skipped packs, and packs carry plugins.txt and loadorder.txt, so that machine ends up with a load order naming plugins it does not have on disk. (claude)
- [ ] If an interim document is still wanted, it must carry either every pack id or an explicit baseline, and it must keep the optional field the Mods page reads. (claude)
- [ ] Branch off main. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/feed-etag-and-shape origin/main
  ```
- [ ] Serve the document with an ETag and store the returned ETag in Config so the next check sends If-None-Match and usually gets a 304, which is where the real saving is. (claude)
- [ ] Keep version.json readable in the same release, because an old launcher reading a new feed and a new launcher reading an old feed both have to work. (claude)
- [ ] Confirm the launcher still compiles and measure the new document against the live feed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node -e "const v=require('./version.json'); console.log(JSON.stringify(v).length, v.packs.length)"
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch for the feed shape and the conditional request. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git checkout -b patrick/feed-etag-and-shape origin/main
  ```
- Measures the repository copy: 59,496 bytes and 164 packs. The live feed is larger. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node -e "const v=require('./version.json'); console.log(JSON.stringify(v).length, v.packs.length)"
  ```
- Fetches the live feed and shows what caching headers it already answers with. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  curl.exe -s -D $env:TEMP\feed-headers.txt -o $env:TEMP\live-version.json https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases/main/version.json; Get-Content $env:TEMP\feed-headers.txt
  ```
- Shows what the launcher asks for and proves there is no conditional request today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern 'vnd.github.raw|DownloadData|If-None-Match'
  ```
- Compiles the launcher under the .NET Framework 4 csc after the Check() change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

The launcher compiles under the .NET Framework 4 csc, the new document measures a few kilobytes against the live feed's 84,588 bytes, a repeat check answers 304 rather than downloading the document again, and a machine many packs behind still receives every pack it is missing.

## Traps

Trimming the feed to the newest few packs breaks the only selector there is and silently moves the Skyrim load order on any machine further behind than that, which with 192 packs live is the normal case. It also drops the optional field the Mods page reads. Launcher code is C# 5 only. Updater.cs and Publish-Update.ps1 are both on the do not edit without a #dev line list and this change touches both. Anything that changes what the feed looks like ships as one complete release, because an old launcher reading a new feed and a new launcher reading an old feed both have to work.

## Links

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Caching conditional requests end to end, which is where the saving actually comes from
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/ETag ETag and If-None-Match, the pair that turns the repeat check into a 304
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/contents the contents API and its raw media type, which is what Updater.cs already asks for
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases/blob/main/version.json the live feed every launcher downloads on every check

issues.title: Three unrelated identifiers per release, no tags, and dev builds published as public releases with no prerelease flag
issues.body:
**Order:** 232 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 27

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Ship.ps1:170-216; tools\Publish-Update.ps1:516, 710 · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Updater.cs:13 · GitHub · 62 releases, 0 marked prerelease, Latest is a dev build

## What is known

One version per release, a tag at the commit, a release named for it, assets named with it, dev builds flagged prerelease so Latest is always stable, and a minimum version in the feed so a bad launcher can be withdrawn. The prerelease flag is one argument and fixes the public page today PART DONE 24 September, pull request #250. WHAT CHANGED: Dev builds now go up to GitHub marked prerelease. The public releases page's Latest can then only point at a main build. Publish-Update.ps1 passes --prerelease to gh release create when the channel is dev. When the upload fallback is the path that worked (a resumed release, or a create GitHub answered 500 after it had in fact made the release), the release is marked with gh release edit --prerelease. If that edit fails, the script says so and the release still goes out. The upload line itself is unchanged: gh release upload has no --prerelease flag, so the entry's step to add it there would have broken every fallback. Main releases are untouched. The single identifier, the tag and the minimum version are not done. MEASURED: gh 2.100.0 run locally: `gh release upload none-such no-such-file.zip --prerelease --repo example/none-such` answered "unknown flag: --prerelease" and exited 1 at flag parsing. So the entry's plan to put the flag on the upload line would make every fallback upload fail. `gh release edit --help` lists --prerelease and --latest, and `gh release create --help` lists -p/--prerelease. New tools/test-release-prerelease.ps1 lifts the block between the new markers at tools/Publish-Update.ps1:963 and :1010 and runs it against a fake gh that refuses any flag the real one does not take for that command. It passes 33 of 33 under pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. Run against the old code (with only the markers added) 11 checks fail. Run against the entry's plan (flag on both create and upload) 14 checks fail, all on the upload path. The flag lines are Publish-Update.ps1:972 ($pre), the create call at :985 and the edit call at :998. The PowerShell parser finds 0 errors in both changed files. Nothing that updates anybody reads Latest: the launcher, site and bot go by version.json and asset ids. The only releases/latest reads in tools are in Bootstrap-VPS.ps1:92 and :115, and they are for PowerShell and git. The clone has one tag, v1.1.47, not the none the entry says. The 156/59/0 counts and the Latest=20260923-2246-dev reading come from the triage pass's gh release list. I did not contact GitHub again. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick: (1) Push the branch, open the pull request, then run a dev Ship, `.\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "..."`, and check the new release shows Pre-release on Thornswood-Releases. (2) One-off backfill on GitHub, which this run was not allowed to do because it contacts a live service: for each of the 59 existing -dev releases, `gh release edit <tag> --repo EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases --prerelease`, then `gh release edit 20260923-2137 --repo EvilPatrick06/Thornswood-Releases --latest`. Without it, Latest stays on 20260923-2246-dev until the next main release, which GitHub makes Latest by default. (3) Still needs a decision from Patrick, together with entry 11's feed rewrite, because it changes every asset url: one identifier per release instead of the launcher version, the timestamp pack id and the -dev suffix; a git tag at the shipped commit; releases and assets named for that identifier; a minimumVersion field in version.json so a bad launcher can be withdrawn. Collapsing the identifiers must keep the dev fourth-number scheme in Ship.ps1 working (IsNewer compares part by part). The To Do List entry should be corrected on two points. The upload line cannot carry --prerelease, so doneWhen's "on both the create and the upload lines" is impossible as written: it should say the create line and the gh release edit after an upload. And the clone has one tag (v1.1.47), not none.

## Read first

- `tools\Ship.ps1:169-216`: the version block: the constant is read out of Updater.cs at :174, bumped, and written back at :214, and the dev fourth-number scheme is explained in the comment at :185-189

- [ ] Branch for the one-line win only, keeping the identifier question separate. (claude)

- [ ] Leave the single identifier, the tag at the commit and the minimumVersion field in version.json for a second branch, decided with entry 11's feed rewrite, because both change asset urls. (patrick)
- [ ] Push the branch and open the pull request. (patrick)

## Commands

  ```

  ```

issues.title: Every launcher spends half the GitHub hourly quota checking for updates, and two people on one connection spend all of it
issues.body:
**Order:** 236 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Packaging · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 31

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Shell.cs:1198-1210 (a two second timer, checking every two minutes) calling tools\app\Updater.cs:141-205 (the Contents API, sixty an hour per address)

## What is known

Serve the feed from the site or a CDN rather than an API with a quota, check on the order of every fifteen to thirty minutes with a cached ETag, and take downloads through the browser download url, which is already an allowed host and has no limit. Two people in one house currently exhaust the budget between them. Entry 89 shrinks what each check downloads; this row is about how often and from where MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: It is worse than the entry says. Shell.cs:1447 now checks every 15 two-second ticks (every 30 s). Commit 0d5c5e9 on 20 Sep changed that from 60 ticks. That is 120 Contents API calls an hour per launcher in play, against GitHub's 60 an hour per unauthenticated address, so one person alone runs out after about 30 minutes. Updater.cs:163 still asks api.github.com contents/version.json. The start-up check (Shell.cs:4286) and ClientRuntime.cs:253 call Updater.Check too. GitHub's REST best-practices page says a 304 is free only when the request carries an Authorization header, and launchers send none, so an ETag alone saves nothing. The entry's trap is wrong about downloads: Publish-Update.ps1:999 writes https://api.github.com/repos/.../releases/assets/<id>, and version.json's launcherUrl, all 227 packs and clientRuntime point there, so every download spends the same quota. Shell.cs:4518 'catch { }' swallows a failed in-play check without logging it, so launcher.log (0 matches for 'too many update checks') cannot show whether it happened. AllowedHosts (Updater.cs:386-392) already holds github.com, objects/release-assets.githubusercontent.com and thornswood.net. WebClient follows redirects, and the sha256 check in Download (:425-446) covers integrity. NEXT STEP: Can be done now: (a) Publish-Update.ps1:999 writes each asset's browser_download_url for new releases. Those hosts are already allowed, so downloads stop spending the quota. Old packs keep their old urls. (b) Log a failed in-play check once per session (Shell.cs:4518), so a rate limit shows in launcher.log. Compile under a scratch root. Leave the 30 s interval alone, because the countdown depends on it. Left for Patrick: where the feed lives. The options are the site (scp'd by Ship the way Publish-News already does), raw.githubusercontent (its roughly 5-minute CDN cache breaks the 30 s countdown), or a flag the game server already publishes on its resource port. Moving the feed off GitHub moves the trust anchor for launcherSha256 onto the VPS while signing is off, so that is a security decision. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick chooses the feed host (site, CDN, or the game server's resource port) and accepts the trust change while code signing is off. Until then only the download urls and the logging can move.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Shell.cs:1198-1210`: the two second DispatcherTimer and if (++inPlayTicks >= 60), with the if (!playing) return; and Checks.GameRunning() guards above it that scope the polling to a live session
- `tools\app\Shell.cs:4163-4211`: CheckUpdatesInPlay: the first check only records updateSeenAt at :4206 and logs the five minute warning at :4207, and a second, later check at :4210 is what actually closes the game
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:141-205`: Check(): the Contents API url at :152-153, the repo-candidate fallback that can double the call, and the 403/429 handling at :184-196 whose own comment names the shared-address problem
- `tools\app\Updater.cs:375-381`: AllowedHosts, which already contains thornswood.net, so moving the feed to the site needs no change to the pinned list

## Steps

- [ ] Put a line in #dev first: Shell.cs and Updater.cs are both on CLAUDE.md's shared-file list. (patrick)
- [ ] Do not raise the 60 at tools\app\Shell.cs:1210. Read Shell.cs:4203-4210 and confirm the countdown needs a second check inside the server's five minute window, which Ship.ps1:44 sets as $AnnounceMinutes = 5. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern 'inPlayTicks|updateSeenAt'
  ```
- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/update-feed-off-the-github-quota
  ```
- [ ] Serve version.json from the site out of tools\docs-app and point Updater.Check at that url instead of api.github.com, which needs no host-list change because thornswood.net is already pinned. (claude)
- [ ] Leave the Accept header at Updater.cs:42 and VersionDoc.Parse at Config.cs:424-432 alone: the launcher already asks for and parses raw JSON with a byte order mark stripped, so nothing on the parse side changes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 38 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Store the last ETag in Config, send If-None-Match on the next check and treat 304 as no change. (claude)
- [ ] Build the launcher, which is the same gate the GitHub build check runs. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] After a session, read the launcher log and confirm the check lines name the new host and none of them go to api.github.com. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Content C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log -Tail 200
  ```

## Commands

- shows the tick counter and the five minute clock together, so you can see why raising the interval breaks the countdown. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern 'inPlayTicks|updateSeenAt'
  ```
- shows the endpoint and the pinned host list in one output. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\app\Updater.cs -Pattern 'api.github.com|AllowedHosts|thornswood.net'
  ```
- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/update-feed-off-the-github-quota
  ```
- reads the launcher's own log so the check rate can be counted against wall clock time; it does not start anything. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-Content C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log -Tail 200
  ```
- compiles the launcher into a scratch root; it also stops running Thornswood processes and restarts Explorer, which is why a person runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

The launcher compiles and the GitHub build check is green, and after a session C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log shows the update check going to the new host with nothing against api.github.com, while the five minute warning and the game close still happen inside the server's announced window.

## Traps

Raising the interval is not one digit and it defeats the countdown. Shell.cs:4169-4175 is a written comment about this exact failure class, where a check that did not come back wiped the five minute clock every two minutes. At 450 ticks somebody is not told for up to fifteen minutes and the game does not close for up to thirty, long after the server has already put them back. The download path is separate and already fine: assets go through browser_download_url, which has no quota. A 304 still counts against the REST quota, which is the other reason to move off it.

## Links

- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api sixty unauthenticated requests an hour, counted per IP address, in GitHub's own words
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/contents the Contents API endpoint the launcher polls for version.json
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/ETag the ETag response header to store
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/If-None-Match If-None-Match and the 304 answer a cached check should treat as no change

issues.title: A failed publish deletes the live server before it checks the new one, and there is no rollback for the server, the site or the bot
issues.body:
**Order:** 237 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** replace it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 18

## Where it lives

VPS · game server, site and bot · tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:84-86, 120-136; tools\Publish-Server.ps1:149; tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:135-179; tools\Install-Bot.ps1:156-198

## What is known

Unpack into a stamped releases folder, validate there, stop, repoint a current junction, start, health-check the port, swap back on failure. Keep the last three of each. Rollback becomes one rename. Today the fix meant to help takes the whole server away for the evening and tells the person nothing changed MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:143-178 stops node under the root and deletes the whole root (Remove-Item at :157). :181-182 recreates it and expands the archive. Only after that, at :236-250, does it strip the BOM and run the load order check that throws, so a bad payload leaves no server at all. Publish-Server.ps1:303-304 then says 'Nothing local was changed'. There is no releases folder or junction anywhere in tools. The loadOrder paths in server-settings.json are absolute under the root, so a check against a staged copy has to remap the prefix. Deploy-Docs.ps1 (the 'Opening the port and starting it' block) stops node and restarts it in place with no previous copy. Install-Bot.ps1 does the same. The script refuses to run on this PC because of the C:\Thornswood\Game\SkyrimSE.exe guard at :26. NEXT STEP: A step that can be taken now, for the game server only and without a junction: expand into "$Root.stage-<stamp>". Strip the BOM and run the load order check against the staged copy with the root prefix remapped, and throw before anything is stopped. Only then stop the server, rename $Root to "$Root.prev-<stamp>", put world, private and data back as the script does today, rename the stage to $Root, start, and poll the resources port the way Publish-Server.ps1:377-388 does. On failure, stop, rename back and start again. Keep the last three prev folders. Add a switch that lifts the gaming-PC guard for a harness. tools/test-install-server.ps1 runs the script with -NoTask against a scratch root and a scratch zip: a zip with a plugin missing from the load order must leave the old root byte for byte as it was. Left for Patrick: the junction-plus-releases layout on the VPS, which vps-dev-instance, backups, Watch-Services and Deploy-Server all touch; a rehearsal through Publish-Server -Channel dev; and the site and bot halves. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn agree the swap layout in #dev (junction or rename, and one shape shared with 209). A rehearsal on the dev root needs a person, because ssh from a session is refused. The site and bot rollbacks need the same decision.

## Read first

- `tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:70-95`: the world and data folders are set aside at :70-82, then :84 deletes the whole live root, :85 recreates it and :86 expands the archive into it
- `tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:118-138`: the byte order mark strip and the load order resolution check that throws, both of which run after the live folder has already been deleted
- `tools\Publish-Server.ps1:140-166`: the caller: the install at :148, the Die at :149 that says nothing local was changed while the remote server is in pieces, and the 3000 health check at :152-166 that a rollback should reuse
- `tools\MOVING-THE-SERVER.md`: what lives where on the VPS, which is what any rollback plan has to preserve

## Steps

- [ ] Agree the staging-and-swap shape with Patrick and Djinn in #dev, together with entry 97, so there is one shape for both scripts rather than two. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/server-installs-into-a-stamped-folder
  ```
- [ ] In tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1, replace the Remove-Item at :84 with an unpack into C:\Thornswood-Server-releases\<stamp>, leaving the live root untouched. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 80 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Move the existing validation at :118-138 so it runs against the stamped folder, and let its throw abort before anything is stopped. (claude)
- [ ] Only after the validation passes, stop the task, remove the old junction, create a new one with New-Item -ItemType Junction pointing at the stamp, start, and poll the resources port the way Publish-Server.ps1:152-166 already does, repointing the junction back on a failed check. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Publish-Server.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 148 -First 21 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Keep the world and data folders outside the junction so nothing has to be copied on a swap, and keep the last three stamps. (claude)
- [ ] Check specifically that server-settings.json's absolute plugin paths still resolve through the junction, because vps-dev-instance.ps1:49-54 shows those paths are written out in full. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\vps-dev-instance.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 45 -First 12 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Parse both scripts and open the pull request. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/server-installs-into-a-stamped-folder
  ```
- prints the destroy, the unpack and the validation in order, which is the whole finding. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 -Pattern 'Remove-Item|Expand-Archive|loadOrder'
  ```
- parses the edited installer, the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- on the VPS, names the stamp the junction currently points at. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-Item C:\Thornswood-Server | Select-Object LinkTarget
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

On a throwaway box, two installs leave two stamped folders; a second install broken on purpose by removing a plugin from the load order makes the check at :128-138 throw, the junction never moves, the old server still answers on the resources port, and Get-Item C:\Thornswood-Server | Select-Object LinkTarget still names the previous stamp.

## Traps

Moving the world folder by accident loses everything, so make the world and data paths explicit and outside the junction before anything else. server-settings.json holds absolute plugin paths under the server root, so a junction that changes the real path may break load order resolution; test that specifically rather than assuming. Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 and Publish-Server.ps1 both reach the VPS, so a person runs them, never a Claude.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/mklink mklink /j, what a directory junction is
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/new-item New-Item -ItemType Junction, and the note that -Force can overwrite an existing junction from PowerShell 7.4
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask Register-ScheduledTask, the task definition the server root runs under and that a swap must leave intact
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/nettcpip/get-netudpendpoint Get-NetUDPEndpoint -LocalPort and OwningProcess, the narrow stop this script already does

issues.title: Nothing tells a person when anything dies, and every check runs on the box being checked
issues.body:
**Order:** 240 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 20

## Where it lives

VPS · tools\Watch-Services.ps1:72-92, 124-141 (writes to a log on the same box; the checks target 127.0.0.1); tools\Check-Site.ps1:29-31

## What is known

A webhook into a private alerts channel, which this repo already has the machinery for, plus an outside monitor polling the public endpoints from elsewhere on the internet. The watchdog's three-strikes rule is good and should stay; the sentence it writes when it gives up currently goes to a file on the box that may itself be the thing that is gone SEEN 18 September: the live game server had written nothing to server.log for nearly three hours and had not touched online.json for over eight, while its scheduled task reported Running the whole time. That turned out to be an idle server rather than a dead one, but nothing on the box could tell the difference, which is exactly what this entry is about. A watchdog that only asks whether the task says Running would have reported everything fine through a real outage. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: In the watcher, Note() (Watch-Services.ps1:121) only appends to watch.log on the box. The give-up lines at :205 ('still down after ... needs a look'), :215 ('could not be started') and :223 ('did not come back in time') go nowhere else. Answers() (:126) is a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1. The kernel completes that handshake even when node's event loop is hung, so it cannot tell a hung server from an idle one, which is the 18 Sep case. Caddy is watched now (abd4d70 #176, 43bce3d #177), so entry 100 is done. The bot already posts to the staff channel by id: watch_site at bot.py:1050-1098 (site only), and watch_trouble at bot.py:1101 reads a file on the same box. That pattern can carry the watcher's give-ups with no new webhook secret. Nothing outside the VPS watches anything. Check-Site.ps1 runs by hand only. A branch exists, patrick/todo-211-watch-log-to-staff, not merged: Still open on entry 211, as the branch author said: (b) Watch-Services.ps1's game and dev game checks should fetch the manifest over HTTP with a timeout instead of a bare TCP connect to 127.0.0.1. That needs its own branch. An outside uptime monitor for https://thornswood.net and the resources endpoint. Patrick signs it up. Only this covers the whole box going down, because the bot goes down with the box. After merge, .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly puts bot.py on the VPS. There is no dev bot, so this reaches the live bot. The doneWhen test needs a person on the VPS: stop a service and see the message in the staff channel. The To Do List was not edited. The entry should record that part (a) is on this branch. NEXT STEP: Can be done now: (a) Add a watch_services loop to bot.py that tails C:\Thornswood-Watch\watch.log and posts each 'needs a look', 'could not be started' and 'did not come back' line once to the staff channel. It remembers what it has said the way watch_trouble does, and a python harness goes beside the existing bot harnesses. (b) In the watcher, the game and dev game checks become an HTTP GET of /api/servers/thornswood/manifest.json with a timeout rather than a bare TCP connect. The three-strikes rule is untouched. Parse Watch-Services.ps1. Left for Patrick: sign up an outside monitor (healthchecks.io or UptimeRobot) for https://thornswood.net and the resources endpoint, and run Install-Bot -CodeOnly and Watch-Services -Install, both on the live VPS. If he prefers a webhook to the bot, he creates it in Discord and places its file on the VPS, named by path only. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick signs up the outside uptime monitor, an outside account. Installing the watcher and the bot touches the live VPS, and ssh from a session is refused. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #283. I merged origin/main (5a9ba5c) into patrick/todo-211-watch-log-to-staff. The only conflicts were in tools/discord/bot.py, three places where main's public report watcher (report_text, report_say, watch_reports) and this branch's watchdog reader had been added side by side. Both are kept. The docstring lists Services and then Reports, the watchdog block comes before the report block, and on_ready starts both watch_services() and watch_reports(). Main's changes to tools/Watch-Services.ps1 (the disk check from #267) merged without conflict next to this branch's header comment. Main has nothing ... STILL TO GO OUT: Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly (the live bot). Left: Unchanged from the author's list: - Part (b), a separate branch: the game and dev game checks in Watch-Services.ps1 should fetch manifest.json over HTTP with a timeout instead of making a bare TCP connect to 127.0.0.1. - Patrick signs up an outside uptime monitor for https://thornswood.net and the resources endpoint. - After the merge, Patrick runs .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly. That reaches the live VPS and restarts the live bot, because there is no dev bot. - The doneWhen test, stopping a service on the dev instance and seeing the message in the staff channel, needs a person on the VPS. ...

## Read first

- `tools\Watch-Services.ps1:66-103`: the watcher heredoc: Note() at :72-75 appends to watch.log on the same box, and Answers() at :77-85 opens a TcpClient to 127.0.0.1, so every check is a loopback check
- `tools\Watch-Services.ps1:109-145`: the $checks array, the three-strikes give-up at :121-126 and the 'did not come back' branch at :141, which are the two places an alert belongs
- `tools\Check-Site.ps1`: the existing outside check, read-only and safe to run, and the shape a scheduled outside monitor would follow
- `tools\Publish-News.ps1`: the webhook machinery this project already has, to be reused rather than rewritten

## Steps

- [ ] Branch, and plan this with entry 100 and entry 101 because all three are changes to the same short watcher. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-watchdog-tells-somebody
  ```
- [ ] Add a Post function inside the watcher heredoc in tools\Watch-Services.ps1 that sends the same sentence Note writes, to a webhook url read from a file on the VPS named by path only. (claude)
- [ ] Call Post from the give-up branch at :123-126 and from the 'did not come back' branch at :141, and leave the three-strikes rule itself untouched. (claude)

issues.title: Nothing outside the project is watched at all
issues.body:
**Order:** 243 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 144

## Where it lives

VPS · tools\Watch-Services.ps1 checks only local ports · GitHub · the workflow has no schedule, so nothing ever runs unprompted

## What is known

A nightly job that walks the first-run path: fetch the feed, resolve every asset URL, resolve the pinned depot manifests, check the store's current build, and go red when one of them moves. For a project this size that is one scheduled workflow, and it is how entry 86 would have been caught the day it happened PART DONE 24 September, pull request #232. WHAT CHANGED: This adds part (1) only: tools/Check-Outside.ps1, a read-only check that makes anonymous GET requests along the path a first install takes through services this project does not run. It reads the feed the same way Updater.Check does. It checks every pack, the launcher and the client runtime against the launcher's own rules: https, a host on AllowedHosts (read out of Updater.cs), and a checksum. Each asset is also checked against its repository's public release listing, which costs one listing per repository, not one request per pack. It downloads the first byte of the launcher, the client runtime and the newest pack. It compares Steam's public build (from api.steamcmd.net) with a new tools/steam-build.json and reports on the Nexus collection page. It never sends a token. It never requests thornswood.net or the game server, and it prints only the host of GitHub's signed redirect address. The depot manifest pins cannot be checked without an account that owns the game, so they are listed as unchecked. A new harness, tools/test-check-outside.ps1, runs the real logic against a table of fake answers and never uses the network. MEASURED: Live run on 24 Sep, anonymous, from this machine, in both pwsh 7.6.6 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. Each run used 7 GitHub API calls: 58 left before, 51 after. Exit 1, for one reason: 164 of the 227 packs point at EvilPatrick06/Thornswood, whose release listing gives a stranger 404 (packs 20260910-2345 to 20260914-1917). All the other 63 packs, the launcher (asset 585078234, 302 to release-assets.githubusercontent.com, 3,292,160 bytes) and the client runtime (583111894, 6,538,349 bytes, which matches the feed) are listed in Thornswood-Releases, across 156 releases on two pages. The newest pack, 20260923-2137, downloads (90,471 bytes). Steam's public build is 24914197 (Steam changed it on 27 Aug 2026), now recorded in tools/steam-build.json. Nexus answered 403, so that is reported as unchecked. With -FeedUrl pointed at a file that does not exist on raw.githubusercontent.com the result was 404 and exit 1. Steam and Nexus were still asked. Two dead ends I tried along the way: the Nexus GraphQL endpoint answers GET with 404, and a GET of Steam's app info shows only the public branch. Harness: tools/test-check-outside.ps1, 60 passed and 0 failed in both shells. It fails without the script (0 passed, 1 failed). It also fails on each of three planted mutations: the server guard in Ask removed (2 failed), the signed address printed (1 failed), and the listing's second page dropped (14 failed). Found while building it: @() over a System.Collections.Generic.List[object] throws "Argument types do not match" in both PS 5.1 and 7, so the script enumerates through the pipeline instead (Check-Outside.ps1:267-269). WHAT IS LEFT: Parts (2) and (3), for Patrick. (2) The scheduled workflow .github/workflows/watch-outside.yml: cron plus workflow_dispatch, one windows-latest pwsh step that runs tools\Check-Outside.ps1, actions/checkout pinned to a full SHA, and no token. Before it can be written, Patrick has to decide three things. (a) The check is red on day one because of the 164 private-repo packs (entry 198). Should the nightly job wait for 198, or report those packs as a known list without failing on them? The script fails on them today, on purpose. (b) Is it acceptable to depend on api.steamcmd.net, a third party? The script already treats it as unchecked when it does not answer. (c) Should a Nexus API key be created and stored as a repository secret? Without one, the collection's revision cannot be checked, because Nexus answers a bare GET with 403 and its GraphQL endpoint answers GET with 404. Once merged, the schedule only starts from main, and GitHub turns scheduled workflows off after 60 days with no activity. (3) The doneWhen line "exits 0 today" cannot hold until entry 198 moves or rewrites those packs. The To Do List entry should be updated to say part (1) is done on this branch, with these measurements. Whenever Steam's public build moves, a person tries the downgrade on one machine and then writes the new build into tools\steam-build.json. The script says so when it goes red.

## Read first

- `.github\workflows\build.yml`: all 46 lines: on pull_request and push to main, no schedule key, so nothing ever runs unprompted; it is also the template for the new file
- `tools\Watch-Services.ps1:109-114`: the $checks array, four local port and task pairs and nothing that leaves the box
- `tools\app\Downgrade.cs:38-47`: the three Steam depot manifest ids, one of the outside things worth watching
- `tools\app\Config.cs:36-37`: the Nexus collection url, the other outside thing a nightly job would resolve

## Steps

- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/nightly-watch-outside
  ```
- [ ] Write .github\workflows\watch-outside.yml with on: schedule: - cron: '0 6 * * *' plus workflow_dispatch:, one job on windows-latest, in pwsh steps so it matches build.yml's style. (claude)
- [ ] Give the job steps that fetch the live version.json from the Thornswood-Releases raw url and fail on anything but 200, then HEAD every entry in packs[] and launcherUrl and fail on anything but 200. (claude)
- [ ] Resolve the collection url from tools\app\Config.cs:37 and say in the job output that a 200 from Nexus is weak evidence, because Nexus rate limits and may answer a bare HEAD with a challenge page. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Config.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 33 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Leave the three depot manifest ids from tools\app\Downgrade.cs:42-44 as a documented manual step unless an anonymous steamcmd session genuinely works, and put no credential in the YAML. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Downgrade.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 38 -First 9 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Prove the check logic locally before GitHub ever sees it, because a workflow_dispatch button does not appear until the file is on the default branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $r = Invoke-WebRequest -Method Head -Uri 'https://thornswood.net' -UseBasicParsing; $r.StatusCode
  ```
- [ ] Pin runs-on to a dated image and pin actions/checkout to a commit SHA while the file is new, so it does not inherit build.yml's floating pins. (claude)
- [ ] Open the pull request; the scheduled run only begins once the file is merged to main. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/nightly-watch-outside
  ```
- shows what triggers exist today and how the actions are pinned. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\.github\workflows\build.yml -Pattern 'on:|schedule|runs-on|uses:'
  ```
- runs the same shape of check the job would, from this machine, and prints the status code. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $r = Invoke-WebRequest -Method Head -Uri 'https://thornswood.net' -UseBasicParsing; $r.StatusCode
  ```
- reads the recent runs of the only workflow there is, for comparison once the second one exists. (claude)
  ```powershell
  gh run list --workflow build.yml --limit 10
  ```
- opens the pull request; the schedule starts after the merge, not before. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

The same pwsh block run in a terminal exits 0 today and exits 1 when pointed at a deliberately wrong url, and once the file is merged to main the Actions tab shows a Run workflow button for it and a dispatched run goes green.

## Traps

A scheduled workflow only starts running once the file is on the default branch, and GitHub only shows the Run workflow button for a workflow present there, so the doneWhen cannot be 'dispatch it from the branch'. This repo merges to main from GitHub and never pushes over it, so the honest test before merge is a local run of the same fetch and HEAD steps. GitHub disables scheduled workflows on a repository with no activity for sixty days. Put no token, key or webhook in the YAML. This runs on GitHub, not the VPS, so it is not a replacement for Watch-Services.ps1 and must not be wired to restart anything.

## Links

- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows schedule and workflow_dispatch, and the sentence that scheduled workflows only run on the default branch
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax workflow syntax: on, jobs, runs-on, the keys a second workflow file needs
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use why a full-length commit SHA is the only immutable way to pin an action
- https://thornswood.net the live site, the thing behind Caddy that a real check has to fetch

issues.title: Nothing tells anyone when the bot is down, and the panel is the first thing a stranger touches
issues.body:
**Order:** 244 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 69

## Where it lives

VPS · bot · tools\Install-Bot.ps1:360-388 (a fifteen second restart loop with no failure count); tools\discord\bot.py:851-862

## What is known

A heartbeat to a free uptime monitor every minute, a webhook post from the wrapper's failure branch, and give up after a few fast failures instead of looping. This is the bot's own wrapper loop, not the watchdog's three-strikes rule in entry 99, which is right and should stay PART DONE 24 September, pull request #233. WHAT CHANGED: The bot's run.ps1 wrapper, which Install-Bot.ps1 writes on the VPS, now times each run. It used to restart the bot 15 seconds after every exit, forever. Now, if three runs in a row end within 30 seconds, it writes one [run] line into bot.log with the last exit code and exits 0. A run of 30 seconds or more resets the count. The watchdog's three-strikes rule in Watch-Services.ps1 (entry 99) is unchanged, and it is now what starts the bot again after the wrapper gives up. A new harness, tools/test-bot-wrapper.ps1, checks both the installer and the script it sends, then runs the generated run.ps1 for real with a stand-in in place of python. MEASURED: The change is at tools/Install-Bot.ps1:415-448, inside the run.ps1 here-string: the comment at :415, `$fastSeconds = 30 at :432, and the give-up at :444. The harness parses Install-Bot.ps1. It checks that the block that writes run.ps1 fills in only rootWin and Task (13 variables found, no strays), so a missed backtick cannot pass just because the file parses. It expands that block the same way the installer does, parses the script that gets sent, and parses the run.ps1 inside it. It then runs that run.ps1 under Windows PowerShell 5.1 from a temp folder. python is replaced by a batch file that exits with code 7. The 30-second threshold and the 15-second pause are checked at their real values first, then shortened to 3 s and 100 ms so the run is quick. On this branch the wrapper started the stand-in 3 times, stopped after about 2 s and exited 0. Its line in bot.log names exit code 7 and passes the installer's own read-back filter ^\s*\[(thornswood-bot|run)\]. Fast, fast, slow (6 s), fast, fast, fast made 6 starts, then it gave up. Result: 20 of 20 checks pass under pwsh 7 and under powershell 5.1. Against main's Install-Bot.ps1 (git show HEAD:), the same run started the stand-in 230 times in 45 s and never stopped, and 10 of 20 checks fail. From reading Watch-Services.ps1:160-230, not measured on the VPS: after the wrapper gives up, the watchdog starts the task at most 3 times an hour, and each start gets 3 quick tries. The worst case drops from about 4 starts a minute to about 9 to 12 an hour. WHAT IS LEFT: Three parts, for Patrick. (1) The alert from the wrapper's failure branch to a private channel: a webhook has to exist on the VPS first. He either lets dev-webhook.txt go up to the box, which reverses the rule in the comment at Install-Bot.ps1:167-174, or makes a separate webhook in a private channel and puts it in bot.env.json himself. Until then, doneWhen's "a deliberately rejected token produces one message in the private alerts channel" is not met; today the only trace is the [run] line in bot.log and the watchdog's note in C:\Thornswood-Watch\watch.log. (2) The one-minute heartbeat in bot.py to an outside monitor: he needs an account (for example healthchecks.io) and has to put its ping url in bot.env.json on the VPS. (3) Deploy: this reaches the box only through a full .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -NoToken -NoPause run, which re-registers the Thornswood Bot task and restarts the live bot. The entry's own deploy line, Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly -NoToken -NoPause, would not send the new wrapper, because -CodeOnly exits at :252, before the runner section. The To Do List entry needs that line corrected. After the deploy, confirm with a look at C:\Thornswood-Bot\run.ps1 on the VPS (read over RDP; ssh is refused from here).

## Read first

- `tools\Install-Bot.ps1:360-370`: the generated run.ps1 wrapper: while ($true) { & cmd /c "python bot.py >> bot.log 2>&1"; Start-Sleep -Seconds 15 }, with no failure counter and no ceiling
- `tools\Install-Bot.ps1:380-388`: the scheduled task registration: RestartCount 999 at :385, -ExecutionTimeLimit ([TimeSpan]::Zero) at :386, and SYSTEM with RunLevel Highest at :388
- `tools\discord\bot.py:851-862`: the client.run(TOKEN) block whose PrivilegedIntentsRequired and LoginFailure handlers print advice and raise SystemExit(1), which the wrapper retries forever
- `tools\Watch-Services.ps1:72-141`: the three-strikes rule this row says to copy the spirit of and not to duplicate

## Steps

- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-bot-stops-spinning-and-says-so
  ```
- [ ] In the generated run.ps1 inside tools\Install-Bot.ps1:360-368, capture $LASTEXITCODE and the run's elapsed time, and count consecutive exits under thirty seconds. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 356 -First 15 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] After three such fast exits, post to the alerts webhook whose url is read from the bot's config file on the VPS, named by path only, and break the loop instead of spinning. (claude)
- [ ] Add a one minute heartbeat in tools\discord\bot.py that GETs a monitor url read from the same config, so a silent bot raises an alarm from outside the box. (claude)
- [ ] Check every dollar sign that belongs to the generated file is still escaped with a backtick, because the script is a here-string that writes another script and a mistake there parses fine and misbehaves at runtime. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -Pattern 'LASTEXITCODE|Start-Sleep -Seconds 15|while'
  ```
- [ ] Parse the installer and parse the bot. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-Bot.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- [ ] Test the wrapper in isolation: write the run.ps1 body to a temp file with python bot.py replaced by a command that exits immediately, run it, and confirm it stops after three fast exits. (claude)
- [ ] Deploy the changed installer to the VPS. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly -NoToken -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] Push the branch and open the pull request, one fix to a pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-bot-stops-spinning-and-says-so
  ```
- shows that nothing in the installer tells anyone anything today; it should find nothing before the change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -Pattern 'webhook|heartbeat|alert'
  ```
- parses the installer, the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-Bot.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- parses every Python file in the bot without writing bytecode anywhere. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import ast, pathlib; [ast.parse(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'), str(p)) for p in pathlib.Path(r'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\discord').rglob('*.py')]; print('every bot file parses')"
  ```
- sends the bot code and the new wrapper to the VPS without touching the token; it reaches the box, so a person runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly -NoToken -NoPause
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

The parser reports no errors on tools\Install-Bot.ps1 and every file under tools\discord parses, the run.ps1 body tested in isolation with a command that exits at once stops after three fast exits instead of looping, and a deliberately rejected token produces one message in the private alerts channel rather than a wrapper spinning every fifteen seconds.

## Traps

Install-Bot.ps1 writes files on the VPS and registers a scheduled task, so it is the person's to run. The script is a here-string that generates another script, so every dollar sign belonging to the generated file is escaped with a backtick; get that wrong and the parse check still passes while the wrapper misbehaves at runtime. Entry 99's three-strikes rule is explicitly correct and is to be left alone, so do not fold this into Watch-Services.ps1. Name the webhook by its location in the VPS config; never paste it into a script in the repo.

## Links

- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html the discord.py reference, including LoginFailure, the failure that is permanent
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/gateway the Discord gateway, disconnecting and resuming, so you know which bot failures are worth a retry
- https://healthchecks.io/docs/ an outside heartbeat monitor that alerts when the ping stops, which is the part the VPS cannot do for itself
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/webhook Execute Webhook, the endpoint an alerts post goes to

issues.title: The VPS is driven as Administrator with host key checking off in eleven scripts, password login never disabled, every service as SYSTEM, RDP open to the internet
issues.body:
**Order:** 245 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Security · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 22

## Where it lives

Your PC · StrictHostKeyChecking=no in Deploy-Server, Install-Bot, Deploy-Docs, Setup-Domain, Request-Restart, Get-Logs, Backup-Server, Watch-Services, Deploy-DevGamemode, Set-DiscordLogin, Check-* → VPS

## What is known

accept-new everywhere through one shared helper rather than eleven copies, key-only ssh once both keys are proven, one low privilege account per service, and RDP behind a VPN or an allowlist since keys already work. Setup-SshKey already does the right thing, so the shape is in the repo. On a hostile network today a machine answering as the VPS receives the Discord secret and the bot token MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Measured: 30 scripts under tools carry StrictHostKeyChecking=no (Backup-Server, Chargen-Log, Check-Chargen, Check-LiveGamemode, Check-Load, Check-Manifest, Check-Roster, Check-ShipReady, Clean-Everything, Deploy-DevGamemode, Deploy-Docs, Deploy-Server, Fetch-Backups, Fix-Voice, Get-Logs, Go, Install-Backup, Install-Bot, Publish-Installer, Publish-News, Remote, Request-Restart, Restart-Server, Rotate-ServerPassword, Set-DiscordLogin, Set-Door, Setup-Domain, Show-BotLog, Watch-Services, Wipe-Saves). The entry says eleven and its commands say 22, and both are out of date. Three use accept-new: Add-VpsKey.ps1:91, Check-Site.ps1:244, Setup-SshKey.ps1:60 and :180. tools/Ssh-Common.ps1 does not exist. SYSTEM tasks are registered in 8 files: Deploy-Docs:283-284, Fix-Voice:94, Install-Backup:150, Install-Bot:443, Install-ThornswoodServer:277, Install-Voice:280, Setup-Domain:230-231, Watch-Services:269 (/ru SYSTEM). On this machine ~/.ssh/known_hosts already holds the VPS's ed25519, ecdsa and rsa host keys (3 lines for 192.135.112.23), and ~/.ssh/config has a Host block for it with no StrictHostKeyChecking setting. accept-new would therefore behave the same here as today, while =no on the command line overrides anything in config. Djinn's known_hosts, sshd PasswordAuthentication and RDP exposure were not checked, because the VPS is off limits in this pass. NEXT STEP: Doable now, on two branches: (1) tools\Ssh-Common.ps1 exporting one option array (BatchMode=yes, StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new) and one Remote function. Copy the Remote from Deploy-Docs.ps1:84-110, keeping the 6000/8191 limit and the send-as-file path. Dot-source it the way Package-Thornswood.ps1:215 dot-sources Ship-Rules.ps1. (2) Migrate Install-Bot.ps1 and Set-DiscordLogin.ps1 first, because they carry the bot token and the Discord client secret, then the other 28 in reviewable batches. If Patrick prefers the smallest safe step, a single PR that only swaps =no for accept-new in all 30 lines takes away the exposure without the refactor. Gate: every .ps1 parses (the CI step), plus a harness asserting that no tools\*.ps1 contains StrictHostKeyChecking=no. Scripts run on Patrick's machine, so there is nothing to deploy. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn: agree the helper's shape in #dev once, together with entry 217, since both change the same Remote. Djinn runs .\tools\Setup-SshKey.ps1 -Test from his machine on a trusted network so his known_hosts holds the key. Production, Patrick only: set PasswordAuthentication no in the VPS sshd_config once both keys are proven; one low-privilege account per service (entries 219 and 249); and RDP behind an allowlist, either in the host's VirtFusion/BisectHosting firewall (an outside account) or in the Windows firewall rule scope on the box. FIXED 25 September as #362: every script under tools and scripts uses StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new (42 places), MOVING-THE-SERVER.md says what a rebuilt box on the same address does, and tools\test-ssh-host-keys.ps1 fails on the old option. Still open from this entry: Administrator as the only account, password login, and RDP.

## Read first

- `tools\Setup-SshKey.ps1:55-62`: the one script that does it correctly: StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new at :60, inside a BatchMode test that gives a real answer about the key rather than a prompt
- `tools\Setup-SshKey.ps1:176-181`: accept-new again at :180, on the call that installs the key, which is the shape to extract into a shared helper
- `tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:58, 84-110`: the $ssh option array at :58 and the Remote helper at :84-110, the most complete copy of the pattern and the one carrying the 8,191 character comment any replacement must respect
- `tools\Package-Thornswood.ps1:215`: how a shared file is already dot-sourced here, the precedent for a tools\Ssh-Common.ps1

## Steps

- [ ] Count the real spread before you plan anything, because the entry says eleven scripts and the working tree says otherwise. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\*.ps1 -Pattern 'StrictHostKeyChecking=no' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path -Unique
  ```
- [ ] Agree the helper's shape in #dev once, covering both this and entry 105, so the host key and the secret channel are designed together rather than twice. (patrick)
