issues.title: Secrets travel inside ssh command lines
issues.body:
**Order:** 246 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 23

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1:91-99; tools\Install-Bot.ps1:241-249; tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:219-226 → VPS

## What is known

Over stdin, or scp into an ACL-locked file the remote script reads and deletes. Never as an argument. The same shared helper as entry 104, so the host key and the secret channel are fixed in one place rather than in eleven copies MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Still as described, and one script wider than the entry says. Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1:124 base64s the password and :132 decodes it inside a Remote block. Install-Bot.ps1:296-297 base64s {token, key} and :304 decodes it inside the settings Remote block. Deploy-Docs.ps1:221-224 does the same, and its comment at :219-220 says the value is 'not sitting in a command line on either machine'. Set-DiscordLogin.ps1:289 and :302 do the same with the Discord client secret and bot token, with the comment 'Base64 so neither secret is ever a word on a command line on either machine'. That is a fourth script the entry does not name. Every Remote() builds `powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand <base64 of the whole script>` (Deploy-Docs.ps1:84-86). Under 6000 characters that goes onto the ssh command line, so it lands in the remote powershell process's command line. Over that limit it is written with Set-Content to a local temp file and scp'd to C:/Windows/Temp/thornswood-remote.ps1 on the VPS (:99-107), so the secret sits in a file on both machines for the length of the call. This machine has sshd installed but Disabled (Get-Service sshd), so there is no local remote to prove against. NEXT STEP: Doable now: add a RemoteWithSecret($script, $value) beside Remote (or in the tools\Ssh-Common.ps1 of entry 216). It pipes the value on ssh's stdin (`$value | & ssh @ssh host "powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand <script only>"`) and the remote script reads it with [Console]::In.ReadToEnd(). The script stays under the 6000 limit, and if it ever goes over, only the script goes by file, never the value. Change the four callers: Rotate-ServerPassword, Install-Bot, Deploy-Docs -Password, Set-DiscordLogin. Correct the two false comments. Prove the PowerShell half locally: pipe a dummy value into a local powershell.exe -EncodedCommand, read Win32_Process CommandLine during the call, and assert the value is absent. Add a harness asserting no Remote here-string in those four files interpolates '$b64'. Parse every script. Scripts run on Patrick's machine, so there is nothing to deploy. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick: agree the helper with entry 216 in #dev. Then the proof over real ssh needs a remote: either he turns on this machine's sshd for a test (it is installed and Disabled), or he runs one of the four against the VPS with a throwaway value while reading Win32_Process there. Neither can be done from a read-only session.

## Read first

- `tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:84-110`: Remote(): it builds powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand $e and hands it to ssh as the command, and its comment at :88-99 records the 8,191 character cmd limit measured on 17 Sep, which any replacement has to respect
- `tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:216-227`: the -Password branch, including the comment at :219-220 claiming the value is 'not sitting in a command line on either machine', which is false and needs correcting with the code
- `tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1:88-112`: the clearest single example of a secret making the trip: base64 at :91, the Remote block at :97, reconstituted on the remote at :99
- `tools\Install-Bot.ps1:241-246`: the JSON payload holding the bot token and the new key, base64d and passed to Remote

## Steps

- [ ] Agree the helper's shape in #dev with entry 104, once rather than twice, since both fixes live in the same place. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/secrets-travel-on-stdin
  ```
- [ ] Change the three calls so the remote script reads the value with [Console]::In.ReadLine() or ReadToEnd, and the local side pipes it into ssh, leaving only the script in the EncodedCommand. (claude)
- [ ] Where a script is too long for stdin to be convenient, scp the value into a file whose ACL is locked to the service account and have the remote script read and delete it, never passing it as an argument. (claude)
- [ ] Correct the comment at tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1:219-220 in the same change, because the next reader will otherwise trust it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 215 -First 8 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Confirm no base64 value is still being interpolated into a Remote block that becomes an argument. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-Bot.ps1,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Pattern 'b64|ToBase64String'
  ```
- [ ] Parse the three edited scripts. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools -Filter *.ps1 -Recurse -File | ForEach-Object { $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($_.FullName, [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Name, $e[0].Message } }
  ```
- [ ] Test against a throwaway remote or localhost and read the remote process list during the call; the value must not appear in any command line. (patrick)
- [ ] Push the branch and open the pull request, one fix to a pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/secrets-travel-on-stdin
  ```
- shows every place a value is encoded into a block that becomes an ssh argument. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Install-Bot.ps1,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Pattern 'b64|ToBase64String'
  ```
- puts the mechanism and the misleading comment side by side. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Pattern 'EncodedCommand|8,191|not sitting in a command line'
  ```
- parses every script under tools, the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools -Filter *.ps1 -Recurse -File | ForEach-Object { $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($_.FullName, [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Name, $e[0].Message } }
  ```
- on the remote box during a test call, shows whether the value is visible in a process command line; run it against a throwaway machine, never against the live VPS with a live secret. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'powershell.exe' } | Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

During a test call against a throwaway remote, the secret appears in no process command line on either machine; Select-String no longer shows a base64 value interpolated into a Remote block; the comment at Deploy-Docs.ps1:219-220 says what the code now does; and every script still parses.

## Traps

The 8,191 character cmd limit is real and dated in the comment at Deploy-Docs.ps1:88-99: a naive rewrite that makes the script longer reintroduces the truncation that produced "Missing closing '}' in statement block" on every deploy. Base64 is transport encoding, not protection, and the code's own comment says otherwise; fix both together. Never print the value while testing, including in an error message you add. These scripts all reach the VPS, so a person runs them.

## Links

- https://man.openbsd.org/ssh.1 ssh, and the fact that the remote command reads the local stdin, which is the channel a secret should travel on
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_pwsh -EncodedCommand and -NoProfile, what Remote() builds and hands to ssh as an argument today
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/cimcmdlets/get-ciminstance Get-CimInstance and Win32_Process, how you read a command line back to prove the value is not in it
- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html OWASP on secrets in process arguments, and why base64 is transport encoding rather than protection

STILL TO GO OUT: Deploy-Docs.ps1 (the live site; see the entry for which switches). Left: - The site's account on the VPS has not changed; nothing here touched the VPS. issues.title: Nothing rotates, so last night's crash is at the end of a file that grows forever
issues.body:
**Order:** 249 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Operations · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 131

## Where it lives

VPS · tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:152; tools\Install-Voice.ps1:167; tools\Install-Bot.ps1:366; tools\gamemode.js:85; tools\Watch-Services.ps1:146-154

## What is known

Size-based rotation with a few kept, so reading last night's crash means opening a file you can actually open. The gamemode's own log also gives up permanently on the first failed write, which should raise something rather than silently disabling logging  THE SITE ROLLS ITSELF NOW, 23 September, entry 64: server.js owns its own handle and rolls at 4 MB keeping five. THE OTHER THREE DO NOT. server.log, voice.log and bot.log are all written by cmd >> from a scheduled task, and a log held open that way cannot be moved or truncated on Windows, measured on 23 September. So they need rolling AT START rather than on a timer, or the same in-process treatment where the service is ours (voice-server.js is). MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The site is done (#178, in-process roll). The rest is unchanged: Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:265-266 starts the server as cmd /c node ... >> server.log and :285-286 deletes server.log on -StartNow. Install-Voice.ps1:172 and :184 build voice.log the same way and :283 deletes it. vps-dev-instance.ps1:85 builds dev voice's voice.log the same way. Install-Bot.ps1:415-423 appends bot.log forever from the run.ps1 loop. gamemode.js:63-96 appends thornswood.log with appendFileSync forever, and when a write fails it sets logBroken and says so once on the console, which lands in server.log, and nothing else. Watch-Services.ps1:229-236 keeps the last 1000 lines past 2000, which discards rather than rotates. Measured tonight in the scratchpad: with `cmd /c "ping ... >> held.log"` running, Rename-Item, Clear-Content and FileStream SetLength(0) are all refused ('being used by another process'), Copy-Item works, and Rename-Item works as soon as the holder exits. So the entry's 'copy then truncate on a timer' step cannot work, and rolling at start, or in process, is the only way. A branch exists, patrick/todo-220-log-rotation, not merged: Nothing is live yet; it all needs Patrick's deploys, dev first. (1) Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 for the thornswood.log roll and /thornswood-log.json. Then check http://192.135.112.23:7788/thornswood-log.json reads ok:true. (2) Publish-Server.ps1 -Channel dev puts roll-log.ps1 and the new task line on the dev server. Deploy-Server alone does not re-register the task. So live gets the server roll only on its next Publish-Server run on the main channel. (3) Install-Voice.ps1 for dev voice (-Root C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev -Port 7789 -TaskName 'Thornswood Dev Voice'), then live. (4) Install-Bot.ps1 -NoToken, a full run, because -CodeOnly copies roll-log.ps1 but does not rewrite run.ps1. There is only one bot, so this goes straight to live. (5) The entry's done-when test on the box has not been done: grow a large dummy voice.log, restart the service, and check voice.log.1 appears and the service keeps writing voice.log. One wording point for Patrick: the done-when says 'at most five files', but this keeps the live file plus five rolled ones (six files), to match the site. Open items for the To Do List: Get-Logs.ps1 fetches only the current file, not .1; watch.log still discards rather than rolls (this is documented in MOVING-THE-SERVER.md, not fixed); roll-at-start bounds each file per run, so a service up for days still grows one file until it restarts. The entry's step 1, a #dev line agreeing who owns rotation against entries 107 and 129, is Patrick's to send or waive. NEXT STEP: One fix per PR, dev first. (1) Bot: in the run.ps1 loop (Install-Bot.ps1:415-423), before each `cmd /c python`, roll bot.log if it is over 4 MB (.4 to .5 and so on up to .log to .1, keeping five). Python has exited at that point, so nothing holds the file. (2) Game server: Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1 writes a small roll-log.ps1 beside the server, and the task action becomes cmd /c "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File roll-log.ps1 server.log & node ... >> server.log 2>&1". The Remove-Item at :286 goes, since the roll does its job. (3) Voice: either the same roll-at-start in Install-Voice.ps1:184 and vps-dev-instance.ps1:85 with :283's Remove-Item gone, or voice-server.js owning its own log the way server.js now does. (4) gamemode.js: roll thornswood.log in process (appendFileSync opens per write, so a rename works), and when logBroken is set, write a 'log: broken' status file beside the published manifest (gamemode.js:10881-11035) so it can be read over HTTP on 3000 and 7788. (5) One sentence in the runbook that watch.log keeps only the last 1000 lines. Harnesses: tools/test-roll-log.ps1 driving roll-log.ps1 against a file held by a cmd >> child (five kept, the sixth dropped, the service writing to a fresh file after restart), and a node harness for the gamemode roll and the broken flag in the style of test-sitelog.js. node --check, and parse every script. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: None for the code. The entry's #dev line about who owns rotation is Patrick's to waive or send. Deploys: Deploy-DevGamemode for gamemode.js; Publish-Server -Channel dev for the server task; Install-Voice for dev voice, then live; Install-Bot -NoToken for the bot. The live server and live voice halves go only after dev has run on them. 24 SEPTEMBER: built and reviewed on patrick/todo-220-log-rotation, pull request #332 open, not merged yet. I fixed the one blocker from the review, and it was real. The /sessions page (serverLogSlice in tools/docs-app/server.js) read only the last 4 MB of server.log. On this branch, roll-log.ps1 runs before every start, so a restart with server.log at 4 MB or more moved the previous run, crash session included, to server.log.1, and the page lost it. Now, when server.log is shorter than 4 MB, the slice fills the rest of the 4 MB from the end of server.log.1, then .2, and so on up to the five the ...

## Read first

- `tools\Install-ThornswoodServer.ps1:145-152`: the comment at :145-150 saying redirecting is the whole reason cmd is in the chain, and the cmd redirection at :152 that builds server.log, so whatever replaces >> must keep stdout and stderr captured
- `tools\Watch-Services.ps1:146-154`: the one place that does bound its files, by rewriting with the last 1000 lines past 2000; it discards rather than rotates, which is a different and smaller problem
- `tools\gamemode.js:77-92`: the log function: the logBroken guard at :81, the append at :85, and logBroken = true at :88 with its comment at :87, the one part of this entry that is a code change rather than a hosting change
- `tools\Install-Voice.ps1:167`: voice.log built the same way, one of the four logs that grow forever

## Steps

- [ ] Agree in #dev who owns this, because entry 107 and entry 129 both claim part of the same rotation and three people should not write three rotators. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/logs-roll-rather-than-grow
  ```
- [ ] Write one tools\Roll-Logs.ps1 that, for server.log, voice.log, bot.log and the site's log, checks the size and past a threshold renames x.log to x.log.1 and so on, keeping five. (claude)
- [ ] Copy then truncate rather than rename, because on Windows you cannot rename a file that a cmd redirection holds open for append, which is why naive rotation silently does nothing. (claude)
- [ ] Have the existing five minute watchdog task run it, so nothing about how the processes are started has to change. (claude)
- [ ] In tools\gamemode.js, keep the logBroken flag but make the give-up path at :88 set a state the health or manifest route reports, so a server logging nothing is visible from outside. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Parse the new script. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Roll-Logs.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- [ ] Test the roll against a running service on the VPS, not a cold one, because that is what catches the file-handle trap. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Thornswood-Voice\voice.log*
  ```
- [ ] Push the branch and open the pull request, one fix to a pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/logs-roll-rather-than-grow
  ```
- shows the cmd redirections that create the four append-forever logs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\*.ps1 -Pattern '>>'
  ```
- syntax checks the gamemode after the logBroken change, without deploying it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- parses the new script once you have written it; tools\Roll-Logs.ps1 does not exist yet, so this fails until it does. It is the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Roll-Logs.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- on the VPS, shows at most five generations after the roll has run. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Thornswood-Voice\voice.log*
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

On the box, a large dummy voice.log rolls to voice.log.1, voice.log comes back empty, the voice service is still writing to voice.log afterwards, and Get-ChildItem shows at most five files. In the repo, the gamemode with an unwritable log path prints the carrying-on message once and sets the state you added rather than going silent with no trace.

## Traps

The cmd redirection is deliberate and its comment says why: a previous version piped through PowerShell and Out-File, which re-encoded the text and left the file unreadable past a point, and could hold the bot's own print() calls on its event loop. Do not put a pipeline back. On Windows you cannot rename a file another process holds open for append, so test the roll against a running service. Watch-Services.ps1:146-154 discards rather than rotates; either fix it or say plainly in the runbook that it keeps only the last 1000 lines. Roll, never delete: deleting a log is how the evidence for the last crash disappeared in the first place.

## Links

- https://12factor.net/logs why a process should not be managing its own log files at all
- https://github.com/winsw/winsw WinSW, a service wrapper whose log mode roll does the rotation for you
- https://nssm.cc/usage NSSM, the other wrapper, with I/O redirection and file rotation built in
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/clear-content Clear-Content, the truncate half of copy then truncate, which is what works on a file another process holds open

issues.title: The new-box runbook does not survive being followed, and there is no restore script at all
issues.body:
**Order:** 251 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Operations · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 134

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\MOVING-THE-SERVER.md:96-138 is the only restore instruction in the repository; tools\Backup-Server.ps1 has no counterpart; its capacity numbers contradict what the box reports

## What is known

A restore runbook beside the backup one, with a stated recovery time, executed once against a throwaway box so the gaps found that way are written back into it. Until it has been run it is a plan, not a runbook. Entry 8 is the backup half; this is the half that proves the backup is worth having MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The title is out of date. A restore runbook and restore script already exist: tools/RESTORING.md (116 lines) and tools/Restore-Backup.ps1 (157 lines) landed in 2761d47 on 18 Sep, together with vps-nightly-backup.ps1, Install-Backup.ps1 and Fetch-Backups.ps1. Backup-Server.ps1 now takes world and private (its lines 160-170) and, since f7db06e, exports every task whose name starts with Thornswood rather than four hand-named ones. RESTORING.md:113 says 'Last rehearsed: never', and that is the real gap. I checked RESTORING.md against the code and found these errors: (1) :40 names tools\Characters.ps1, which was deleted in afb1ad9 (Install-Voice.ps1:126 records it). (2) :22-24 and step 4 restore voice\owners.json, which the nightly backup stopped taking (vps-nightly-backup.ps1:119-124). (3) Step 4 restores bot\config.json, but the backup holds bot\bot.env.json (vps-nightly-backup.ps1:118). (4) Step 4 never puts web\Caddyfile back, although the backup takes it (:129). (5) Step 5 says Ship.ps1 brings back the server, the gamemode and the site. Ship calls only Build-Launcher, Go, Package-Thornswood, Publish-Discord, Publish-News, Publish-Update, Request-Restart and Sync-Client, so it restores none of those three. (6) The nightly backup only lists task names in NOTES.txt (:133-136) and exports no task XML, so a restore from a nightly backup has no tasks to import. (7) No recovery time is stated. MOVING-THE-SERVER.md:98 still says 'about 18 GB' and :126 says 'three services'. The scripts register nine Thornswood tasks: Server, Voice, Docs, Web, Watch, Bot, Backup, Dev Server and Dev Voice. Every script MOVING-THE-SERVER names exists (Bootstrap-VPS, Install-ThornswoodServer, Set-Server, Setup-SshKey, Check-Load, Set-Vps). I could not read the capacity numbers at :7-13 off the box, because ssh is refused from this session. A branch exists, patrick/todo-222-restoring-doc, not merged: For Patrick: the entry's done condition. Book an afternoon, order a throwaway box and follow "The box is gone" without improvising. Record that the site returns 200 over HTTPS, the game port answers, voice health answers, the bot is online in a test Discord, and the accounts and documents are present. Then write every gap, the date and the elapsed time into the "Rehearsing it" section, and destroy the box, because the backup holds live secrets. Until then the page says it is a plan, "Last rehearsed: never" and "Recovery time: not measured". A session cannot do this. tools/Restore-Server.ps1 is not written. The entry's version of it imports the task XMLs, which only the hand-run Backup-Server.ps1 zip has. The nightly zip, the one that holds the world every night, has none, and the page rebuilds each task from its install script instead. Two things need deciding before that script exists: which backup a restore uses, and whether an imported `Thornswood Watch` may be allowed to start the server before its world is in place. The rehearsal is where to find out, so it belongs to Patrick after the box run. When 255 lands, a bullet for `Thornswood Load` beside `.\tools\Watch-Load.ps1 -Install` in RESTORING.md step 7 is still better than the catch-all. The harness prints a NOTE saying so, but no longer fails. For the To Do List (not edited here): the header of Backup-Server.ps1 still says "the three scheduled tasks" and "the installer ... is the big one", although its own code enumerates every Thornswood task. Publish-Installer.ps1's header says the payload is "about a gigabyte" and the build is 385 MB. Neither is in this entry's scope. NEXT STEP: tools/RESTORING.md: fix the six errors above. Point step 1 of the one-character procedure at the file names in the unpacked world folder instead of Characters.ps1. Map bot\bot.env.json and web\Caddyfile to their roots and drop owners.json. Replace step 5 with Deploy-Server.ps1, Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 and Deploy-Docs.ps1 (never -SeedDocs), Install-Bot.ps1 and Install-Voice.ps1. Add a task step that uses the tasks folder from a Backup-Server.ps1 zip, and say that the nightly zip has none. Add a target recovery time labelled as a guess until rehearsed. tools/MOVING-THE-SERVER.md: fix :98 and :126 (nine tasks, named). New tools/Restore-Server.ps1, run on the new box against an unpacked backup folder: it refuses while any Thornswood task is running, copies each piece to its root, imports every tasks\*.xml with Register-ScheduledTask -Xml when present, and prints what it placed and what was missing. Verify with the ParseFile check and a scratch harness that runs it with -Root against a fake unpacked tree. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: The done condition is a person following the document end to end on a throwaway box. Patrick has to order and pay for that box with the hosting provider, handle live secrets on it, and destroy it afterwards. The capacity lines at MOVING-THE-SERVER.md:7-13 and the 16GB-plan decision at :38-40 need Check-Load run against the box from Patrick's machine. A BRANCH EXISTS AND WAS HELD BACK ON PURPOSE, 24 September: patrick/todo-222-restoring-doc. Its review found that the rewritten 'The box is gone' section reads as a literal sequence that is not safe to follow as written during a rehearsal. It was not merged. Read the review before using it. 25 SEPTEMBER, found reviewing #342: RESTORING.md's sentence and its step 4 (line 92) still list the voice service's owners.json, which the nightly backup stopped taking on 23 September, and step 4 never restores voice\choices.json. #342 fixed the bot's line in the same sentence (config.json to bot.env.json) and left these.

## Read first

- `tools\MOVING-THE-SERVER.md:96-138`: the only restore instruction in the repository, fourteen numbered steps, with line 98 read as a known-stale sentence and step 9 read as wrong about how many tasks there are
- `tools\Backup-Server.ps1`: all of it, because a restore runbook is written against exactly what the zip contains, and today that is four config files, four task XMLs and no world folder
- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:168-181`: the secrets table, since a restore has to put every one of those back
- `tools\Restore-KzlContent.ps1`: the only Restore-* script in the repo, which is about Keizaal content and is not a counterpart to Backup-Server.ps1

## Steps

- [ ] Land entry 8 first, because the 15 September zip holds nothing under the world folder and a restore rehearsed today proves you can bring back a server with no characters in it. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/restoring-the-server-runbook
  ```
- [ ] Write tools\RESTORING-THE-SERVER.md with a stated recovery time, a prerequisites list naming the machine, the backup zip, the ssh key, the DNS access and the Discord developer portal, then numbered steps that each name the script and what proves it worked. (claude)
- [ ] Reuse MOVING-THE-SERVER.md:96-138 as the skeleton but fix what is wrong there: step 9 says three services and there are six tasks, and line 98 still says the installer is about 18 GB against a 527 MB payload. (claude)

  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\MOVING-THE-SERVER.md -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 92 -First 49 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```

- [ ] Add tools\Restore-Server.ps1 doing the mechanical parts: unpack the zip, put the four config files back, import every task XML in the tasks folder, and report what it restored and what was missing. (claude)
- [ ] Parse the new script. (claude)

  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Restore-Server.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- [ ] Confirm every command named in the new document exists as a script in tools. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools -Filter *.ps1 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
  ```
- [ ] Book an afternoon, order a throwaway box, follow the document without improvising, write every gap back into it, then destroy the box. (patrick)

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/restoring-the-server-runbook
  ```
- prints the two sentences in the existing runbook that are now wrong. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\MOVING-THE-SERVER.md -Pattern '18 GB|three services'
  ```
- lists every script, so no command in the new document names one that does not exist. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools -Filter *.ps1 | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name
  ```
- parses the new script once you have written it; tools\Restore-Server.ps1 does not exist yet, so this fails until it does. It is the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Restore-Server.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- the end-of-restore proof that the site answers over HTTPS on its own hostname, run from outside the new box. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Site.ps1 -NoSsh -NoPause
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

The document has been followed end to end by a person against a throwaway box, and the result answers: the site returns 200 over HTTPS on its own hostname, the game server's port answers, the voice service's health route answers, the bot appears online in a test Discord, and the linked accounts and documents from the site's data folder are present. The elapsed time is recorded in the document, and everything worked out on the day is written into it before the box is destroyed.

## Traps

Until that run has happened the document is a plan, not a runbook, and it should say so at the top. The backup zip holds the bot token, the Discord client secret and the server password, so the rehearsal box handles live secrets and must be destroyed afterwards; never print or paste any of them. Deploy-Docs.ps1 -SeedDocs during a restore flattens every document with the repo copy, which its own header warns has already thrown away an evening of edits, and MOVING-THE-SERVER.md step 7 says not to use it; keep that warning. Check the box before writing capacity numbers into the new document, because the decision at MOVING-THE-SERVER.md:38-40 to buy the 16GB plan may or may not have happened.

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask Register-ScheduledTask, including the -Xml form a restore uses

issues.title: The bot is invited with Administrator and keeps it
issues.body:
**Order:** 252 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 70

## Where it lives

Discord · tools\Setup-Discord.ps1:24-26; tools\discord\Build-Discord.py:33-34

## What is known

Print the reduced-permission invite at the end of a successful build and untick Administrator on the bot role afterwards. With it, the blast radius of either token file or a backup zip is the whole server PART DONE 24 September, pull request #254. WHAT CHANGED: Merged origin/main into patrick/todo-223-bot-overwrites twice, because main moved while the first merge was being checked (aec3d24 merged 52472ed, then 4fb61f6 merged 89d3fd8). Then one fix commit, b042534. Build-Discord.py conflicted with #203 ("Build-Discord keeps the gate"). Kept from main: the public, open, membersread and hold modes, HOLD_STAFF, _named, the category mode map and the system channel guard. Kept from this branch: with_bot and keep_bot, the call in ensure_channel's else branch, keep_bot on categories that are already there, and the pass over channels made by hand. The merge left this entry's change not holding: main now shuts @everyone out of nearly every channel, but the branch only named the bot in read, staff and pathfind. So the fix commit does three things. (1) overwrites() names the bot in every mode except public. (2) keep_bot(ch) now checks @everyone's actual overwrite on the channel instead of the mode in PLAN, and writes only where one of View Channel, Send Messages or Read Message History is denied. Main's own comment says the modes only apply to channels the builder makes and the live gate was set by hand, so the channel's real state is what matters. It also means a channel open to everybody is never written, including one made by hand inside a gated category. (3) The call sites no longer pass mode. test-bot-overwrites.py now models the live server behind the gate (main's modes, #say-hello, the Applications category, #choose-your-hold, the holds), plus the hand-made staff #news and a hand-made channel left open inside the Thornswood category. It checks that neither a Member nor somebody not yet approved gains anything. The rest of entry 223 is still open, as the author said: the reduced invite URL printed at the end of a build, the untick-Administrator line, and correcting Setup-Discord.ps1:24-26 and Build-Discord.py:33-34. MEASURED: The harness on the merged branch passes 92 of 92. The bot's overwrite is still allow 68608, deny 0: 1<<10 View Channel + 1<<11 Send Messages + 1<<16 Read Message History, taken from Discord's permission bit numbers, not from discord.py's names. The modelled live server has 50 channels and categories. Before the run, without Administrator, the bot cannot get into 47 of them: every channel and category except #say-hello, the Applications category and the hand-made open channel. That includes #staff-general, the staff #news, #news and #choose-your-hold. One run writes exactly those 47, once each, and nothing else. The only thing written is the bot's own overwrite. -Check writes nothing, a second run writes nothing, and a Forbidden goes into failed while the build carries on. The same harness against main's builder (copied to a scratch folder and run from there; Build-Discord.py is identical at c1557b1 and 89d3fd8) gives 16 passed, 102 failed, exit 1. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick, on the live Discord, and a Claude must not do this: run .\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Check first. On the gated server it should list about 47 "would change ... lets the bot in without Administrator" lines. Then run it for real once, while the bot still has Administrator. Then the rest of entry 223, unchanged from the author's list: settle the reduced role permissions and print that invite URL plus the untick-Administrator line at the end of a successful build; give Setup-Discord.ps1:24-26 and Build-Discord.py:33-34 two permission sets, Administrator for a full build and the reduced set for running; before unticking, check channels outside the plan's categories (for example #welcome-travelers and any top-level channel made by hand) that shut out @everyone and that the bot relies on. New finding: on main, #tickets-and-applications is mode 'read', and read_only denies @everyone Send Messages in Threads. A build that makes that channel fresh would stop applicants, and a bot without Administrator, from writing in the private ticket threads bot.py opens there. The live channel was set by hand, so check its @everyone overwrite before Administrator comes off. Either the reduced set gives the bot Send Messages in Threads there, or the mode should not deny it. This belongs on the To Do List under entry 223 or next to it.

## Read first

- `tools\discord\Build-Discord.py:28-41`: the setup instructions asking for Administrator at :33-34, and the note at :40-41 that the bot must sit above the roles it creates, which is why it was written that way
- `tools\discord\Build-Discord.py:100-215`: ROLES from :100 and PLAN from :143, the full list of what the builder creates and therefore what permissions it genuinely needs
- `tools\discord\bot.py:100-110`: discord.Intents(guilds=True, members=True), the running bot's actual footprint, which is far less than the builder's
- `tools\Setup-Discord.ps1:20-30`: the same Administrator instruction in the same words, so both places need the same correction

## Steps

- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/reduced-bot-invite
  ```
- [ ] Work the real permission set out from ROLES and PLAN: manage roles, manage channels, view channels, send messages, create public and private threads, send messages in threads, manage messages, manage threads, embed links, attach files, read message history. (claude)
- [ ] Check each channel kind in PLAN against the permissions page, because Discord's community features, forum channels, announcement channels and the rules screen, may need bits the reduced set drops. (claude)
- [ ] Sum those bit values into one integer and, at the end of a successful Build-Discord.py run, print the reduced invite url with that integer plus scope=bot. (claude)
- [ ] Print one line after it telling the person to untick Administrator on the bot's role now the build is done. (claude)
- [ ] Decode the integer back against the documented bit values before anybody uses it. (claude)
- [ ] Parse the builder without running it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import ast; ast.parse(open(r'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\discord\Build-Discord.py', encoding='utf-8').read()); print('the builder parses')"
  ```
- [ ] Open the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/reduced-bot-invite
  ```
- shows both places that ask for Administrator and nothing anywhere that takes it back. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\discord\Build-Discord.py,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Setup-Discord.ps1 -Pattern 'Administrator'
  ```
- parses the builder without running it, because running it rewrites a live Discord server. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -c "import ast; ast.parse(open(r'C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\discord\Build-Discord.py', encoding='utf-8').read()); print('the builder parses')"
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

The builder parses, and its help or dry path prints an invite url whose permissions parameter is a specific integer rather than 8, followed by the line telling the person to untick Administrator now the build is done. The integer decodes back to the intended bit list against the documented values.

## Traps

Do not run Build-Discord.py or Setup-Discord.ps1: they rewrite a live Discord server's roles, channels and channel content. Reducing permissions on a live bot can break the next build, because the builder needs more than the runtime does, so the honest shape is two permission sets with a note saying which is which. Entry 104 is the same blast-radius argument for the VPS and names the bot token among what a backup zip would expose, so the two share a threat model.

## Links

- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/permissions every permission bit and its value, which is what the reduced integer is summed from
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/oauth2 the bot invite URL, scope=bot and the permissions integer
- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/intents.html privileged intents, including the members intent the bot is set up with
- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html the discord.py reference, including LoginFailure, the failure that is permanent

issues.title: Two pull requests that were each green turned main red together, because main does not ask for a branch to be up to date
issues.body:
**Order:** 254 · **Wave:** 6 Release and operations · **Category:** GitHub & CI · **Effort:** decide it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

GitHub branch protection on main (required_status_checks.strict) · Claude outputs/todo-run/land.js

## What is known

FOUND 24 September. #328 (entry 197) added a check that the six client files ship by record; #306 (entry 128) made a client file ours only by its bytes. Each passed its own build and they merged an hour apart. Together the check failed, main was red from ac9df44, and every pull request after it went red for a change it never made. Fixed by #338, which asks the six by their bytes. WHY IT COULD HAPPEN: branch protection has strict off (read with gh api on 24 September), so a pull request merges on a build that ran against an older main. Two answers, and Patrick picks. (a) Turn strict on: every pull request has to be brought up to date and built again after each merge, which is safe and slow when twenty land in a row. (b) Leave strict off and have the landing helper bring each branch up to date and wait for a fresh build before it merges. (a) is one setting; (b) is code nobody else runs.

## Done when

Patrick has chosen, and the choice is in place.

## Traps

With strict on, a batch of twenty takes twenty builds in a row rather than twenty at once.

issues.title: The shipped exe is compiled on your desktop while CI compiles the same source and throws it away
issues.body:
**Order:** 255 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** GitHub & CI · **Effort:** replace it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 102

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 · GitHub · .github\workflows\build.yml:33-46, artefact kept seven days and never used

## What is known

A release job on a tag: clean checkout, build, record the commit in the assembly version, sign from a secret, scan with Defender on the runner, attach to the release with a checksums file. The person shipping never compiles the shipped binary. This is also the only place the signing key from entry 2 can be used safely, so the two go together MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: build.yml is still one job, and its 'Keep the exe from this build' step uploads with retention-days 7 and nothing downloads it. It is now on actions/checkout@v7 and upload-artifact@v7, so the entry's '@v4' is stale. Ship still builds the shipped exe locally: Ship.ps1:401 calls Build-Launcher.ps1, and signing runs only where the gitignored tools/signing.json exists (Build-Launcher.ps1:361-376, Sign-Artifact.ps1, Azure Artifact Signing). I measured the done condition itself. I compiled a one-line program twice with the same Framework csc Build-Launcher uses (C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe, 'version 4.8.9221.0 for C# 5'). The hashes differ: 9C31E5D4... and 3A040101..., with 20 of 3584 bytes different (timestamp and MVID). The same compiler rejects the switch that would fix this with 'CS2007: Unrecognized option: /deterministic'. So 'the same SHA-256 as a local build of the same commit' can never be met with this compiler. NEXT STEP: After the #dev agreement: add .github/workflows/release.yml on tags v*. Pin runs-on and every action to a full commit SHA. Build with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root under RUNNER_TEMP, write SHA256SUMS, and attach both to a draft release. Change Ship.ps1 around :385-420 to download that asset and check it against SHA256SUMS instead of compiling. Rewrite the done condition, because byte-identical local and runner builds are impossible here. The choices: Ship publishes only the runner's exe, verified by its checksum file; or the compiler moves to Roslyn with /deterministic /langversion:5, which changes 'built with the .NET Framework 4 csc'. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: The entry's own first step is a #dev agreement between Patrick and Djinn on where the shipped binary comes from. Two more things are needed: an Azure Artifact Signing identity usable from a GitHub runner (an outside account and a repository secret), and Patrick's choice between the two replacement done conditions, because the one written is impossible with this compiler (measured).

## Read first

- `.github\workflows\build.yml`: all 46 lines: one job on windows-latest, a parse step, a build step calling Build-Launcher.ps1, and actions/upload-artifact@v4 with retention-days 7 that nothing ever downloads
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:224-269`: the csc invocation a runner build has to reproduce, including /noconfig at :232 and the hand-listed references at :267
- `tools\Ship.ps1:253`: where the shipped exe is actually built today, on the shipping machine
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:163-171, 332-365, 390-412`: the install work CI is also running: Stop-Game and Stop-Launcher at :169-170, a Desktop shortcut at :350-365 and an Explorer restart at :396-412, which is harmless on a runner and ugly anywhere else

## Steps

- [ ] Agree in #dev before code: this changes where the shipped binary comes from, Ship.ps1 is shared, and only Patrick's machine ships main. (patrick)
- [ ] Branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/ci-builds-the-shipped-exe
  ```
- [ ] Add .github\workflows\release.yml on push: tags: ['v*'] that checks out, runs tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 with an explicit -Root, and attaches the exe plus a checksums file to the release. (claude)
- [ ] Pin runs-on to a dated image and pin every action to a full-length commit SHA in the new file, rather than inheriting build.yml's floating @v4. (claude)
- [ ] Change tools\Ship.ps1:253 to consume that asset instead of building locally, so the person shipping never compiles the shipped binary. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 249 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Compare the two builds of the same commit by hash, which is the only evidence they agree until a signing identity exists. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe -Algorithm SHA256
  ```
- [ ] Parse the edited scripts and open the pull request. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Ship.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- [ ] Push the branch and open the pull request, one fix to a pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/ci-builds-the-shipped-exe
  ```
- shows the floating pins and the artifact nobody downloads. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\.github\workflows\build.yml -Pattern 'uses:|runs-on|retention-days'
  ```
- shows the one line where the shipped exe is built today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern 'Build-Launcher'
  ```
- parses the edited script, the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile('C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Ship.ps1', [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- builds locally for the hash comparison; it stops running Thornswood processes and restarts Explorer, which is why a person runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- prints the local build's hash, to compare against the runner's. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe -Algorithm SHA256
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

A tag push produces a release whose exe has the same SHA-256 as a local build of the same commit, compared with Get-FileHash, and Ship.ps1 attaches that asset rather than one it compiled itself.

## Traps

Signing and this go together: the key must only ever touch the runner, which means the local build has to stop being the shipping build in the same change. CI runs tools\Build-Launcher.ps1, which kills running Thornswood and game processes and writes Thornswood.lnk to the Desktop, so never copy that step onto a real machine. The launcher is C# 5 compiled by the .NET Framework 4 csc, so do not add a job that builds it with a modern SDK. Only Patrick's machine ships main and Ship refuses a main release that is not on main or is behind origin, so a CI-built artifact still has to reach that machine or the rule has to change deliberately.

## Links

- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflow-artifacts what a workflow artifact is and why one nobody downloads is thrown away
- https://github.com/softprops/action-gh-release an action that creates a release and uploads assets from a tag, with a prerelease input
- https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases the Releases REST API and the prerelease field the flag sets
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use why a full-length commit SHA is the only immutable way to pin an action
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax workflow syntax: on, jobs, runs-on, the keys a second workflow file needs

issues.title: If your machine dies, the source survives and the release process does not
issues.body:
**Order:** 256 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Release · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 103

## Where it lives

Your PC · the baseline, the news webhook, the update token and the shipping role all live here · SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:47-70, 150-166

## What is known

The sum of 100, 101, 102 and 104: the release definition in the repository, the build in CI, the installer as a bootstrap, tags on main, and the secrets in a secret store rather than one person's profile. Then a release can be cut from any machine with a checkout and the credentials, which is the whole point MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: This is a roll-up; the entry says it cannot be picked up alone. Some of it has moved. Ship no longer commits or pushes the source: Ship.ps1:338-356 and :891-900, f917dd8, with Bump-Version.ps1 as its own commit. A ship-readiness preflight exists as tools/Check-ShipReady.ps1 (870f77e), so 'Ship's preflight passes there' has a concrete command. What is still machine-local, named by location: the baseline at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json and published-dev.json (Publish-Update.ps1:215-224; Publish-Update.ps1 -Baseline rebuilds it on a new machine, per SECOND-DEVELOPER.md). tools/discord/news-webhook.txt and dev-webhook.txt (.gitignore:20, :40). tools/signing.json (.gitignore:46) and the Azure signing account behind it. The fork's build tree. The done condition asks for the same exe hash for the same commit on a second machine. I measured that the Framework csc 4.8.9221.0 produces different bytes on every compile and rejects /deterministic (see entry 224), so that can never be met as written. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change in the repo on its own. When 224 and the vault decision are settled, rewrite the done condition. Replace the exe hash comparison with: Check-ShipReady.ps1 -Channel dev and then main report no gaps on the second machine, and a dev Ship from there publishes. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides where the shared credentials live, which vault and who holds each. Patrick and Djinn agree in #dev on whether a second machine may ship main, which is settled-design territory. Entry 224 (CI builds the shipped exe) has to be decided first. The written done condition is impossible with the current compiler and needs replacing.

## Read first

- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:47-70`: the release path, naming Ship.ps1 and the baseline at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thornswood\published.json at :58
- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:163-166`: the sentence that the #news webhook lives in tools\discord\news-webhook.txt and is handed over only to somebody who will ship main releases
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:177-191`: where the baseline state file lives and how the dev channel gets its own, so you can see exactly which piece is machine-local
- `.gitignore`: which of these four things are deliberately absent from the repository

## Steps

- [ ] Treat this as the acceptance test for entries 112, 114, 115 and 117 rather than a task of its own, and say so in #dev so nobody picks it up alone. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm what is actually machine-local before planning anything: the baseline, the news webhook, the update token and the shipping role. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\.gitignore -Pattern 'webhook|published'
  ```
- [ ] Branch for the two pieces that belong only here. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/two-holders-for-the-release-credentials
  ```
- [ ] Move the #news webhook and the update token into a shared vault both people can reach, naming them by location in the repo and never by value. (patrick)
- [ ] Write into SECOND-DEVELOPER.md which machine may ship and exactly what the second machine needs to take over, in plain sentences. (claude)
- [ ] Prove it: a checkout on the second machine plus the credentials produces the same exe hash for the same commit, and Ship's preflight passes there. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe -Algorithm SHA256
  ```
- [ ] Open the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- shows which release-critical files are deliberately kept out of the repository. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\.gitignore -Pattern 'webhook|published'
  ```
- names the baseline's location without reading its contents. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\Publish-Update.ps1 -Pattern 'StateDir|published.json'
  ```
- starts the branch for the documentation half. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/two-holders-for-the-release-credentials
  ```
- the comparison that proves the second machine produces the same artifact. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-FileHash C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe -Algorithm SHA256
  ```
- opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

A checkout on the second machine, plus the credentials, produces the same release artifact as the first: the same exe hash for the same commit, and Ship's preflight passes there.

## Traps

This is a roll-up and cannot be picked up alone; do entries 112, 114, 115 and 117 first. Secrets are named by location only, never printed, pasted, committed or logged. news-webhook.txt and dev-webhook.txt sit in the working tree and are gitignored, so a careless git add -A on this branch publishes credentials. Changing who may ship main is settled-design territory and belongs in #dev first.

## Links

- https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create gh pr create and what --fill takes from the commits
- https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore gitignore, which is why news-webhook.txt and dev-webhook.txt sit in the tree and not in the repository
- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html OWASP on storing credentials somewhere two people can reach rather than in one person's profile

issues.title: Deploys are one laptop, one hardcoded address, and no versioned artifact
issues.body:
**Order:** 258 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Server · **Effort:** change it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 104

## Where it lives

Your PC · the VPS address written into 22 files; tools\Set-Vps.ps1:11-17; tools\Deploy-Server.ps1:33 and 46 → VPS

## What is known

CI builds the server payload from a tag and uploads it with its hash; a deploy job installs it into a versioned folder and swaps. The address and the ports in one config file rather than twenty-two. Both known incidents in this area came from what ships depending on the state of one person's disk MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The address is in more places than the entry says: 39 files among tools/*.ps1 and tools/app/*.cs (grep -l), and 52 tracked files repo-wide (git grep -l). Set-Vps.ps1:11 says 'twenty three'. There is no tools/vps.json. Deploy-Server.ps1:34 still defaults $Vps to the literal address, and Backup-Server.ps1 does the same. The sources that are meant to carry the address are Config.cs, the five ts-plugins and version.json; Publish-Update.ps1 and Ship.ps1 do not carry it. A helper pattern already exists: 15 scripts dot-source Close-Launcher.ps1. 30 scripts carry StrictHostKeyChecking=no, which is the separate host-key entry. The server binary is built from the fork on Patrick's machine (Build-Server.ps1, Publish-Server.ps1), so a runner cannot build the server payload without that toolchain. NEXT STEP: The cheap half, one pull request. Add tools/vps.json (address, user, live and dev ports) and tools/Vps.ps1, which reads it. In each script that defaults $Vps to the literal, make the parameter default empty and fill it from Vps.ps1 after the param block, so an explicit -Vps still wins. Leave the address in Config.cs, the plugins, version.json and the docs, where Set-Vps.ps1 rewrites it (it walks every text file, vps.json included). Fix Set-Vps.ps1:11 to state the measured count. Verify: ParseFile over every script, the grep count falls to the baked set plus vps.json, and a harness dot-sources Vps.ps1 and checks every changed script resolves the same address with and without -Vps. Keep host keys and the secret channel on their own branches, as the entry says. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick splits this entry from entries 104 and 105, as the entry's own step says. The other half is production work: CI building a versioned server payload from a tag, and a deploy job that installs into a versioned folder and swaps. That needs a runner that can reach the VPS (a deploy key as a GitHub secret) and a server build that is not tied to the fork build tree on Patrick's machine.

## Read first

- `tools\Set-Vps.ps1:1-110`: what already exists for exactly this problem: it walks the whole repo skipping .git, node_modules, bin, obj, _dist and packages, rewrites every text file carrying the old address, previews first, and adds a redirect so installed launchers move themselves
- `tools\Set-Vps.ps1:11`: the header's own count, twenty three files, which is itself stale
- `tools\Deploy-Server.ps1:33-47`: the three machine-specific defaults in one param block: the dist tree at :33, the address at :34 and the Steam Data path at :46
- `tools\MOVING-THE-SERVER.md`: the written procedure a shared defaults file would be replacing

## Steps

- [ ] Count what is really there before planning, because the entry says twenty two files and the header says twenty three. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\*.ps1,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\app\*.cs -Pattern '192\.135\.112\.23' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path -Unique).Count
  ```

- [ ] Leave Set-Vps.ps1 as the migration path for the sources that legitimately bake the address in: the plugins, Config.cs and version.json. (claude)
- [ ] Split the shared-helper work deliberately: this row, entry 104's host key and entry 105's secret channel all want the same home, and one pull request for all three is too big under the one-fix-per-pull-request rule. (patrick)
- [ ] Parse every script. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools -Filter *.ps1 -Recurse -File | ForEach-Object { $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($_.FullName, [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Name, $e[0].Message } }
  ```

- [ ] Have Patrick run the preview to see exactly which files still embed the address. (patrick)


## Commands

- counts the scripts and launcher sources carrying the address today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Select-String -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\*.ps1,C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools\app\*.cs -Pattern '192\.135\.112\.23' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path -Unique).Count
  ```

- parses every script under tools after the defaults change, the same check CI runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users\evilp\Downloads\Thornswood-Repo\tools -Filter *.ps1 -Recurse -File | ForEach-Object { $e = $null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile($_.FullName, [ref]$null, [ref]$e); if ($e) { '{0}: {1}' -f $_.Name, $e[0].Message } }
  ```

## Done when

The count of files carrying the address falls to the handful that genuinely embed it, the rest read tools\vps.json through the shared helper, .\tools\Set-Vps.ps1 -Preview lists only those, and every script parses.

Never hand-edit the address anywhere: Set-Vps.ps1 exists because a partial edit left the site deploying to a dead box for two days. Many of these scripts also carry StrictHostKeyChecking=no and three put secrets on ssh command lines, and a shared helper is the natural home for all three, which is exactly why the work has to be split into separate branches.

issues.title: The repo's own writing rules are written down and nothing enforces them
issues.body:
**Order:** 268 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Testing · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 156

## Where it lives

Your PC · CLAUDE.md's Words section, against tools\app\Help.cs, tools\ui.xaml, tools\discord\content.py and the site pages

In .github/workflows/build.yml the two new steps sit side by side: main's "Check the launcher window" step and this branch's "Check the writing rules" step, both inside the one required "Launcher builds" job. - [ ] Send it out: Deploy-Docs.ps1 (the live site; see the entry for which switches). (patrick)

## Commands

- Counts em dashes in README.md by code point; reads 7 before the fix and 0 after. (claude)
