issues.title: Two thirds of catch blocks are silent, so a broken button looks like nothing happened
issues.body:
**Order:** 270 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Launcher code · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 115

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · 367 of 581 catch clauses are empty across tools\app\*.cs; worst in Shell.cs, OwnGame.cs, Checks.cs, Voice.cs and Uninstall.cs; the global handler at Shell.cs:436-444 swallows the rest

## What is known

A one line helper that logs the exception at debug level, which is mechanical and carries no behaviour risk, and never swallowing at all in Config.Save, Swap.Restore, Hold.Release or Keep.Unpark. Make it a lint rule with a frozen baseline so the count stops growing while the rest is worked through. A tester says the Save button did nothing; a stranger closes the window PART DONE 24 September, pull request #311. WHAT CHANGED: The branch is brought up to date with main and nothing else on it changed. When this run started it already held main (8d4fbdb) from its own third merge, so the first git merge said "Already up to date". Main then moved three times while the checks ran, so the branch got three more merges, each with the required trailers. 8a6bfe7 brings in #289 and #290 (#290 is the fix for three harnesses main itself had broken: test-door, test-journal-key, test-mold-key). fb2570b brings in #291, #292 and #294 to #298. 66b4cb3 brings in #293, which changes Shell.cs (the header video stops while the game runs) and adds no catch. None of the merges conflicted. None needed a fix commit, and the baseline was never raised. What the branch does is unchanged from its author's report. tools\app\Swallow.cs adds Swallow.Note, which writes one line to Paths.LogFile and never calls Shell.Log or touches a control. Config.Save, Swap.Restore (with DropLink), Hold.Release and Keep.Unpark now log what they catch through it, with the same return values as before. tools\Check-Swallow.ps1 and tools\swallow-baseline.txt freeze the count at 376, and build.yml runs the checker inside the required Launcher builds job. Earlier merges on the branch already dealt with the twelve new empty catches main had brought in: they log through Swallow.Note, or they explain themselves in a comment inside the braces where the harness compiles the class on its own (SteamUpdates.cs, SelfSwap.cs, and the log write in the ShellUninstall fault handler). That is one consistent version. Main has not done this work, so the branch is still needed. MEASURED: Measured on the final tree 66b4cb3: Check-Swallow.ps1 counts 376 silent catches in 54 source files against a baseline of 376. It exits 0 with "Nothing rose, and the baseline matches" under both pwsh 7 and PowerShell 5.1. I planted one empty catch in a scratch copy of tools\app, passed in with -AppDir, and the checker exited 1 naming Swap.cs at 7 against 6. Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root %TEMP%\ts-build-239 -NoPause compiled the final tree with exit 0 (Thornswood.exe 3,245 KB). The only warnings were the four CS0649 in Verify.cs, which is unchanged, and it printed "a throwaway build, so the Desktop is left alone entirely". The PowerShell parser found 0 errors in Check-Swallow.ps1, test-swallow.ps1 and test-feed-notice.ps1. The full sweep ran 135 harnesses: every tools\test-*.js, every tools\voice\test-*.js and every tools\test-*.ps1 under pwsh. test-swallow.ps1 passed 65/65, test-feed-notice.ps1 138/138, test-self-update.ps1 68/68 and test-steam-updates.ps1 96/96. On the last full pass 134 passed. test-command-ack.js failed there with EADDRINUSE on 127.0.0.1:7912 and then passed 49/49 run alone straight after. An earlier pass also hit port contention: test-chat-limit.js got EADDRINUSE on 7907, and test-auth, test-cull and test-ice also failed on that pass. Run alone, all five passed (8/8, 17/17, 25/25, 15/15, 49/49). Other worktrees tonight run the same harnesses on the same fixed ports. None of those harnesses reads a file this branch changes. On the untouched 8d4fbdb, test-door.js, test-journal-key.js and test-mold-key.js failed because of main itself. #290 fixed them, and they pass after the merge. No added line says "player" or has an em dash. No added C# line uses $", ?., nameof, => or out var. WHAT IS LEFT: Still open, for the To Do List entry. Recording it is not this run's job. (1) Config.Save, Swap.Restore, Hold.Release and Keep.Unpark only log. The entry wants them to stop swallowing: return false or rethrow, and have the Save button say so. That changes behaviour and was left out on purpose. (2) The other 376 silent catches are not converted yet. Each file converted should lower its line in tools\swallow-baseline.txt in the same pull request. (3) Config.Load still swallows a parse failure, and its own comment says that would silently turn updates off. It is the next one to log. (4) The entry's trap about a temp-root build repointing the Desktop shortcut is out of date: the build says it leaves the Desktop alone. (5) Entry 128 (line numbers in stack traces) would make these log lines more useful. (6) Check-Swallow.ps1 could go on the read-only list in Allow-Claude.ps1. Also for whoever lands this: once it is on main, any branch that adds an empty catch in tools\app turns the required check red. Run .\tools\Check-Swallow.ps1 on main after each merge tonight. The launcher change needs a dev Ship once it merges. The fixed ports in the voice harnesses (7907, 7912) collide when several worktrees run the sweep at once. That is worth its own entry.

## Read first

- `tools/app/Shell.cs:440-451`: the real global handler: it logs the type and message and appends the full ToString to Paths.LogFile, so do not re-add logging that is already there
- `tools/app/Shell.cs:708-714`: Log is private and its second line sets txtStatus.Text, which is why no helper may call it, least of all from a pool thread
- `tools/app/Config.cs:257-280`: Save with its silent catch at 274 and its finally, the single highest-value place to stop swallowing
- `CLAUDE.md:45-46`: the C# 5 restriction, before you write a helper

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line: Shell.cs, Checks.cs, Keep.cs and Hold.cs are four of the six protected files and four of the worst offenders, so this cannot be done quietly. (patrick)
- [ ] Get today's number and the per-file order yourself; the command below prints 373 with Shell.cs at 78, OwnGame.cs 22, Icons.cs 21, then Updater.cs, Checks.cs and Voice.cs at 20 each. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern 'catch\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*\{\s*\}' -AllMatches | Group-Object Filename | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Count, Name
  ```
- [ ] Write the counting rule at the top of tools/swallow-baseline.txt, in particular whether a comment-only body counts as empty, because that is the whole difference between two honest counts. (claude)
- [ ] Add tools/app/Swallow.cs with a static Note(string where, Exception e) that appends to Paths.LogFile with File.AppendAllText inside its own try and never touches Shell.Log or any control, in C# 5 syntax only. (claude)
- [ ] Replace empty catches file by file, smallest first, with catch (Exception e) { Swallow.Note("Config.Save", e); }, and leave the deliberate swallows that carry a comment beside them, for example Shell.cs:474, as swallows that merely log. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 470 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] In Config.Save (Config.cs:257), Swap.Restore (Swap.cs:40), Hold.Release (Hold.cs:105) and Keep.Unpark (Keep.cs:407), let the caller see the failure by returning false or rethrowing, and have the button that called it say something. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Config.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 253 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Write tools/Check-Swallow.ps1 that counts empty catches per file, compares against the checked-in baseline and exits 1 when any file's count rises, then add it as a job in build.yml. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Swallow.ps1
  ```
- [ ] Compile with the Framework csc, which is the whole risk of a mechanical change like this, then add one deliberate empty catch and confirm the checker goes red. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Counts single-line empty catch clauses per file; 373 today, Shell.cs worst at 78. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern 'catch\s*(\([^)]*\))?\s*\{\s*\}' -AllMatches | Group-Object Filename | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Count, Name
  ```
- Compares today's per-file counts against the checked-in baseline and exits 1 on a rise. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Swallow.ps1
  ```
- Compile check with the .NET Framework 4 csc. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

The count command prints the same per-file numbers as tools\swallow-baseline.txt, Check-Swallow.ps1 exits 1 the moment one deliberate empty catch is added and 0 when it is removed, and Build-Launcher.ps1 compiles clean. No game start is needed for any of it.

## Traps

Shell.Log is private and its second line sets txtStatus.Text, so a helper that calls it will not compile, and if it did it would throw on a pool thread and swallow that too: write to Paths.LogFile directly. Build-Launcher.ps1 writes Thornswood.lnk to the Desktop and can kill and restart Explorer when the artwork hash changes, so a temp-root build repoints the customer-facing shortcut and the real build has to be run afterwards to put it back. C# 5 only, and this is worth shipping with entry 128, because a logged exception with no line number is much less useful than one with it.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.application.dispatcherunhandledexception the handler Shell.cs already wires up, so you can see what is genuinely covered
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/exceptions/best-practices-for-exceptions when swallowing is defensible and what to log instead
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/errors-warnings the compiler switches that decide whether a mechanical change fails loudly
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/utility-modules/psscriptanalyzer/overview a static rule checker for PowerShell scripts with rules you include or exclude, the shape Check-Swallow.ps1 borrows

issues.title: No symbols are built, so the log the whole diagnostic story depends on can never name a line
issues.body:
**Order:** 271 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Launcher code · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 116

## Where it lives

Your PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:231-236, no debug switch at all · no .pdb beside the shipped exe

## What is known

One switch beside the optimiser, and the pdb shipped or kept with the release. Optimisation is unaffected. From the next release every fault names the file and line, which with entry 127 turns one report from one stranger into a fix without a conversation. Cheap enough to pull forward if you want it sooner MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Not done: Build-Launcher.ps1:239-243 has no /debug switch, and the stub compile at 327 has none either. The pdb is already filtered out downstream: Publish-Update.ps1:474 and Package-Thornswood.ps1:375 skip any .pdb, so a pdb never rides in a pack or the installer. The launcher travels as exactly one asset: Updater.SelfUpdate at Updater.cs:942 downloads v.launcherUrl and replaces one file, and Build-Launcher.ps1's WebView2 comment explains why sidecar files were avoided. That changes the entry's assumption. A pdb kept on the shipping machine never sits beside a customer's Thornswood.exe, so their Exception.ToString in launcher.log still names no file or line. The payoff the entry describes needs the pdb on the customer's machine, which means a second launcher asset (version.json, Publish-Update and Updater.cs, all protected) and publishing symbols. The legacy Framework csc has no /pathmap and no /debug:embedded. A published pdb therefore carries the build machine's absolute source paths, which include the Windows account folder, and an embedded pdb cannot be built. NEXT STEP: Claude can do now: add '/debug:pdbonly' to the cscArgs array at Build-Launcher.ps1:240, and check that Thornswood.pdb lands beside Thornswood.exe in a temp-root build. Run the throwaway throw.cs comparison from the entry to show file and line appear only with the pdb present. Upload the pdb as a CI artifact next to the exe in build.yml. Copy each release's pdb into a gitignored per-version folder on the shipping machine in Ship.ps1, and give the pdb an explicit line in Ship-Rules.ps1. Optional, and it needs no disclosure decision: have the fault handler at Shell.cs:451-456 also log each frame's method and IL offset (StackFrame.GetILOffset), so a pdb kept on Patrick's machine can map a customer's report to a line later. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides, with Djinn in #dev, whether the pdb ships to customers as a second launcher asset (a disclosure decision, plus an updater change across protected files) or is kept only on the shipping machine with IL offsets logged. Only the first gives file and line directly in a customer's log.

## Read first

- `tools/Build-Launcher.ps1:231-236`: the $cscArgs array: /noconfig, /nologo, /target:winexe, /platform:anycpu, /optimize+, /out, /win32icon and /resource, and no debug switch anywhere
- `tools/app/Shell.cs:445-451`: the fault handler that writes Exception.ToString() to Paths.LogFile, the string that gains file and line the moment a pdb exists
- `tools/Ship-Rules.ps1`: what is allowed to leave the machine in a release, read before deciding whether the pdb ships or is only kept

## Steps

- [ ] Add '/debug:pdbonly' to the $cscArgs array at tools/Build-Launcher.ps1:232, beside '/optimize+', because pdbonly emits the symbol file without changing code generation. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 228 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Build to a temp root and confirm Thornswood.pdb lands beside Thornswood.exe. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] List the output folder and read the two file sizes rather than comparing byte length against an older build, because pdbonly adds a DEBUG directory entry and embeds the pdb's absolute path, so a length difference is expected. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher | Select-Object Name, Length
  ```
- [ ] Prove the payoff without starting anything: write a four line C# file at $env:TEMP\throw.cs whose Main throws, then compile it with the same csc this build uses and the new switch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  & "$env:WINDIR\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe" /nologo /debug:pdbonly /out:$env:TEMP\throw.exe $env:TEMP\throw.cs
  ```
- [ ] Compile the same file again without the switch, so the two ToString() outputs can be read side by side and only the pdb build names a file and line. (claude)
  ```powershell
  & "$env:WINDIR\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe" /nologo /out:$env:TEMP\throw-nopdb.exe $env:TEMP\throw.cs
  ```
- [ ] Read the path csc embedded in the exe and decide whether that build folder is something that should leave the machine, since it will travel with any published pdb. (claude)
- [ ] Decide in #dev whether the pdb ships as a release asset or is only kept per version on the shipping machine, because that is a disclosure decision rather than a build detail. (patrick)
- [ ] Add an explicit rule to tools/Ship-Rules.ps1 either way, then wire the chosen route into tools/Ship.ps1 so the symbols are versioned with the release rather than left loose in a folder. (claude)

## Commands

- Builds the launcher to a temp root with the new switch in place. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- Shows Thornswood.pdb sitting beside Thornswood.exe. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher | Select-Object Name, Length
  ```
- Compiles a throwaway thrower with symbols, to see file and line appear in ToString(). (claude)
  ```powershell
  & "$env:WINDIR\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe" /nologo /debug:pdbonly /out:$env:TEMP\throw.exe $env:TEMP\throw.cs
  ```
- The same throwaway file with no symbols, which is the half of the comparison that must name no line. (claude)
  ```powershell
  & "$env:WINDIR\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe" /nologo /out:$env:TEMP\throw-nopdb.exe $env:TEMP\throw.cs
  ```

## Done when

Get-ChildItem on the temp Launcher folder lists Thornswood.pdb beside Thornswood.exe, and the throwaway exe compiled with /debug:pdbonly names a file and line in its exception ToString() while the one compiled without it does not. Ship-Rules.ps1 names the pdb one way or the other, and Ship.ps1 puts it where that rule says.

## Traps

Do not use the exe's byte length as proof that optimisation is untouched: pdbonly adds a DEBUG directory entry and embeds the pdb path, so the two builds differ on purpose and the test reads as a failure when nothing is wrong. /debug:full would change code generation; pdbonly does not. A pdb reveals source paths and method names, so publishing it publicly is a decision for #dev. The pdb must match the exact exe, so version it with the release, and a pdb that exists on the shipping machine but is not wired into Ship.ps1 is half a change.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/code-generation DebugType and Optimize, including what pdbonly means for a pre-C#-6 compiler like this one
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/advanced PdbFile, for moving the symbol file somewhere other than beside the exe
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/errors-warnings the warning switches, so a manifest or symbol problem is not silent
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.application.dispatcherunhandledexception the handler whose ToString() output the symbols improve

issues.title: No application manifest: the window is blurry on mixed DPI and the exe declares no identity
issues.body:
**Order:** 272 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Launcher code · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 117

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:231-242; the DPI is worked around by hand at tools\app\Downgrade.cs:540-552

## What is known

A twenty line manifest with per-monitor awareness, the supported Windows entries and run-as-invoker, plus one compiler switch. A blurry window is one of the first things a stranger notices and the last thing anybody reports, and the declared identity is what Windows shows in the file's properties and in the SmartScreen prompt MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The title is partly wrong. I measured a scratch copy of the shipped 1.1.92 exe (C:/Thornswood/Launcher/Thornswood.exe) and it already carries csc's default manifest: assemblyIdentity name='MyApplication.app' version='1.0.0.0', requestedExecutionLevel asInvoker, uiAccess false. It has no dpiAware and no supportedOS. So run-as-invoker is already declared, and the missing parts are per-monitor DPI and the supportedOS GUIDs. WPF on the Framework makes itself system DPI aware on its own, which matches the assumption behind the Downgrade.cs offset. The identity claim is also wrong: the file Properties dialog reads the version resource the build already generates (Build-Launcher.ps1:181-216), and SmartScreen shows the Authenticode signer (entry 14), not assemblyIdentity. There is a trap the entry misses. The build sets no TargetFrameworkAttribute (grep finds none in tools/app or Build-Launcher.ps1), and on the Framework, WPF's reaction to WM_DPICHANGED is governed by Switch.System.Windows.DoNotScaleForDpiChanges, whose default depends on the targeted framework. A PerMonitorV2 manifest on its own may leave the window unscaled on the second monitor rather than sharp. That has to be measured on a real mixed-DPI desktop. Downgrade.cs ClickCommandLine at 578-597 scales its offset by GetDpiForWindow over GetDpiForSystem (declared at 796-797) and still drives Steam's console, so the DPI mode change moves a synthesised click into Valve's window. NEXT STEP: Claude can do now: write tools/app/Thornswood.manifest (assemblyIdentity Thornswood.Launcher.Thornswood with a four-part version, asInvoker, supportedOS GUIDs through Windows 10/11, dpiAwareness PerMonitorV2 and legacy dpiAware true). Pass /win32manifest in the cscArgs array at Build-Launcher.ps1:240; /win32icon can stay, only /win32res conflicts. Add the AppContext handling so WPF actually rescales: set Switch.System.Windows.DoNotScaleForDpiChanges=false before the Application is created in Shell.cs, or emit a TargetFramework attribute in the generated info file. Work out whether the Downgrade.cs ratio becomes 1 under PerMonitorV2 and change it to match. Compile to a temp root and confirm the embedded manifest text with the same byte probe used here. Leave the visual check to a person. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Needs the #dev line between Patrick and Djinn, because it changes DPI behaviour for the whole launcher and for the Steam console click. After that a person has to confirm on a mixed-DPI desktop that the window is sharp and correctly sized on both monitors, and that the Downgrade click still lands in Steam's console. Nobody here starts the launcher.

## Read first

- `tools/Build-Launcher.ps1:231-236`: no /win32manifest anywhere, and /win32icon is already passed at 234, which is what the manifest and resource switches conflict around
- `tools/app/Downgrade.cs:532-563`: ClickCommandLine, which scales a 72 pixel offset by GetDpiForWindow divided by GetDpiForSystem, an assumption that only holds while this process is system DPI aware
- `tools/app/Shell.cs:460-475`: the window placement maths against SystemParameters.WorkArea, the other thing a DPI mode change moves

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line and say exactly what it touches: this changes the DPI contract for the whole process, and Downgrade.cs types a synthesised click into Valve's own window at a measured pixel offset. (patrick)
- [ ] Write down what scale means in Downgrade.cs:535-556 today, GetDpiForWindow(steamWindow) over GetDpiForSystem(), and note the comment saying a Windows before 10.0.1607 gets the ratio 1. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Downgrade.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 531 -First 28 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Create tools/app/Thornswood.manifest with an assemblyIdentity carrying type="win32", a name in the Organization.Division.Name form such as Thornswood.Launcher.Thornswood and a four part version, all three of which the schema requires, a trustInfo requestedExecutionLevel of asInvoker with uiAccess false, a compatibility block carrying the supportedOS GUIDs including {8e0f7a12-bfb3-4fe8-b9a5-48fd50a15a9a} for Windows 10 and 11, and a windowsSettings block with dpiAwareness PerMonitorV2. (claude)
- [ ] Set the legacy dpiAware to true, which is system aware, and not to true/pm, because true/pm makes the process per-monitor aware on Windows 8.1 and on Windows 10 before 1607, where WPF on the Framework does not handle WM_DPICHANGED and the window comes out the wrong size rather than merely blurry. (claude)
- [ ] Add one entry to the $cscArgs array at tools/Build-Launcher.ps1:236 pointing /win32manifest at the new file, and do not also set awareness from code, because a manifest and an API call fight each other and the manifest wins. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 232 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Re-read Downgrade.cs:535-556 and decide whether the ratio must become 1 under PerMonitorV2, or whether entry 39's DepotDownloader replacement has landed and removed the coupling altogether. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Downgrade.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 531 -First 28 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Build and confirm csc emitted no manifest warning and that the exe grew by roughly the manifest's size. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] Hand the visual half over: the person checks a mixed-DPI desktop for a sharp window and confirms the Steam console click in the downgrade still lands, because nobody here starts the launcher. (patrick)

## Commands

- Builds with /win32manifest and shows any csc manifest warning. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- Reads the exe size, which should grow by roughly the manifest's size. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe | Select-Object Name, Length
  ```
- Shows which Win32 resource switches the compile passes, since only one manifest is allowed and /win32res conflicts. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Pattern 'win32manifest|win32res|win32icon'
  ```

## Done when

The build compiles with no manifest error or warning out of csc, the exe grows by roughly the manifest's size, and the person confirms on a mixed-DPI desktop that the window is sharp and that the Steam console click in the downgrade still lands.

## Traps

Do not use (Get-Item ...).VersionInfo as the proof: the version resource is generated from assembly attributes at Build-Launcher.ps1:188-216, so /win32manifest cannot displace it and that test cannot fail. PerMonitorV2 moves this process into unvirtualised coordinates, which is exactly what Downgrade.cs's 72 pixel offset assumes it is not, so getting the manifest right and the offset wrong types into the wrong place in somebody else's application. csc accepts one /win32manifest and it conflicts with /win32res, and this build already passes /win32icon. The declared identity is what Windows shows in the file's properties and in the SmartScreen prompt, which ties it to entry 14's signing identity.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/application-manifests every element the manifest needs: assemblyIdentity, trustInfo, compatibility and the supportedOS GUIDs
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/hidpi/setting-the-default-dpi-awareness-for-a-process the dpiAwareness and dpiAware table, including what true/pm actually means
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sbscs/manifest-file-schema the full schema, for getting the namespaces right first time
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setprocessdpiawarenesscontext the API the manifest replaces, and why the two must not both be used
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/resources the csc Win32Manifest, Win32Icon and Win32Resource switches and how they conflict

issues.title: Installed apps lists Thornswood only after the first launch, and without a size
issues.body:
**Order:** 276 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Packaging · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 121

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Register.cs:78-126 · Your PC · tools\Setup-Thornswood.ps1 writes no registry entry

## What is known

The installer writes the same key at install time with the size of the payload it just moved, under the same hashed name so the launcher updates that row rather than adding a second. Somebody who installs and does not launch has a program Windows cannot see MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The first half is mostly closed already. Setup-Thornswood.ps1:608-677 opens the launcher itself at the end of a successful install (Open-Launcher). tools/Setup.bat never passes -NoOpen, and neither does Bootstrap.cs:1020-1026, so Register.Ensure writes the key seconds after install. The key is missing only when the install's own checks failed (:655-659). That window is the one that asks for a screenshot, and the install is broken at that point anyway. Setup-Thornswood.ps1 writes no Uninstall key (grep: no HKCU or Uninstall writes). Register.cs:118-122 still deliberately omits EstimatedSize. The entry's fix rests on a premise that no longer holds under the own-game-folder layout: the installer's payload is not Thornswood's footprint. I measured this machine read-only from C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\files.txt: - C (copied) lines: 7,957 files, 1,093.4 MB. - L (hard linked to Vortex's copy) lines: 22,696 files, 40,433.5 MB. - du: Launcher 5 MB, Profile 48 MB. OwnGame.cs:235-283 already adds up copyBytes when it builds the folder, and made.txt (:875) is written at that moment. So a real number is available with no walk at launch. It is roughly 1.15 GB of Thornswood's own bytes against 41 GB that Explorer would show for the Game folder. NEXT STEP: What can be done now, pending Patrick's call on which number to show: 1. tools/app/OwnGame.cs: where it writes made.txt (:875) after a build, also write copied=<copyBytes>. It already has that value at :235-240 and :311-350. 2. tools/app/Register.cs Ensure: read copied= from Profile\OwnGame\made.txt if present. Add the launcher exe size and write EstimatedSize as a DWord in KB. When the record is absent, write nothing, which keeps the 'no invented number' rule at :118-122. Update that comment to say the number comes from OwnGame's build record, not a walk. 3. Drop the installer-side key write the entry proposes. The installer opens the launcher, the launcher writes the key within seconds, and a second writer with its own copy of the FNV hash (Register.cs:40-55) is the double-row risk the entry itself warns about. 4. Compile and ship on the dev channel. After a person has launched once, read EstimatedSize with Get-ItemProperty and check there is exactly one row. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick has to decide what Windows should show as Thornswood's size: the copied bytes OwnGame measured, or nothing, as Register.cs:118-122 decided. He also has to confirm the installer-side key write can be dropped, since the installer already opens the launcher. The registry result is only visible after a person runs the launcher.

## Read first

- `tools/app/Register.cs:40 and 78-126`: KeyName() and the subkey Ensure creates at 88, which is the exact name the installer has to match
- `tools/app/Register.cs:118-122`: the written decision against inventing EstimatedSize, which is an argument against the obvious fix unless the number comes from the installer
- `tools/Setup-Thornswood.ps1`: the section that moves the payload into place, the one moment a true size is known for free
- `tools/setup/Bootstrap.cs:716-812 and 979-1026`: the stub that downloads and unpacks the payload, the other candidate for writing the key

## Steps

- [ ] Print Register.cs's KeyName() logic and the name your installer code builds side by side and confirm they are identical for the same root, before writing a single value. (claude)
- [ ] Have whichever half finishes the install write the same values the launcher writes: DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallLocation, DisplayIcon, UninstallString, and NoModify and NoRepair as DWords. (claude)
- [ ] Add EstimatedSize as a DWord in KB taken from the size of the payload the installer has just moved, which it already knows and does not have to walk for. (claude)
- [ ] Change Register.Ensure only so it writes EstimatedSize when the value is absent, so the launcher never overwrites the installer's honest number with nothing. (claude)
- [ ] Leave the reasoning at Register.cs:118-122 intact and do not add a file walk to the launcher's startup path. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Register.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 114 -First 11 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Check there is exactly one row, before the installer change and after it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Where-Object DisplayName -eq 'Thornswood' | Select-Object DisplayName, EstimatedSize, UninstallString
  ```
- [ ] Ship it in the same release as entry 132's UninstallString change, or the second one rewrites the first. (patrick)

## Commands

- Shows how many rows Windows has for Thornswood and whether a size is set. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Where-Object DisplayName -eq 'Thornswood' | Select-Object DisplayName, EstimatedSize, UninstallString
  ```
- Pulls up the subkey name logic and the deliberate omission in one view. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Register.cs -Pattern 'KeyName|CreateSubKey|EstimatedSize'
  ```
- Compile check after the one change to Register.Ensure. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

On a throwaway machine or a copy, after the installer runs the Uninstall query returns exactly one row with a non-zero EstimatedSize and a working UninstallString, and launching the launcher afterwards still leaves exactly one row.

## Traps

The same hashed name is the whole risk: get it wrong and Windows lists Thornswood twice, one row from the installer and one from the launcher, which is worse than today. Register.cs:118-122 is a written decision against inventing a size, so the only defensible number is one the installer measured. Register.cs is not on the protected list but Shell.cs, which calls it at 244, is. An installer that writes a key the launcher's KeyName() does not agree with is a half change, and halves do not ship.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/uninstall-registry-key the value names Windows reads, including EstimatedSize and InstallLocation
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/registry-value-types REG_DWORD against REG_SZ, the difference EstimatedSize depends on
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/get-itemproperty reading the subkeys back to prove there is one row and not two

issues.title: The bot runs as SYSTEM under a hand-written loop, stopped by matching a command line, with a log that never rotates
issues.body:
**Order:** 280 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 125

## Where it lives

VPS · bot · tools\Install-Bot.ps1:166-171, 360-388; tools\Show-BotLog.ps1

## What is known

A service through NSSM or WinSW as a dedicated low-privilege account, with backoff and log rotation, stopped properly rather than by name matching. An image decoder bug in the card renderer should not run as the highest account on the box that holds every secret. The install script gets shorter, not longer PART DONE 24 September, pull request #302. WHAT CHANGED: I merged origin/main into the branch twice, because main moved during the work: first 29496f8 (commit 017aaa0), then 4e529eb (commit d7456aa). Neither merge conflicted. I fixed the reviewer's one major problem, which is real. patrick/todo-220-log-rotation already rolls bot.log before each start, in the same run.ps1 loop, through Roll-Log.ps1: 4 MB limit, five files kept, and the same check that nothing else has the file open. It also makes the same shorter-log fix to both read-backs, in Fresh and in -CodeOnly. Keeping both branches would put two rollers back to back and cause three conflicts in Install-Bot.ps1. Commit e0f97f6 therefore puts tools/Install-Bot.ps1 back exactly as it is on main and deletes the 381-line roll harness tools/test-bot-log-roll.ps1. The one part 220 does not do stays: tools/Show-BotLog.ps1 reads bot.log.1 before bot.log. Right after a roll, the lines that say why the bot restarted are in bot.log.1. Its comment now says the roll comes from entry 220's roll-log.ps1. A new, smaller harness, tools/test-show-botlog.ps1 (13 checks), covers it. It runs Show-BotLog's own script against a temp folder through powershell.exe -EncodedCommand, which is how the VPS runs it. It checks that bot.log.1's lines come before bot.log's, that the bot-only filter still drops discord.py noise from both files, that -All lets it through, that -Lines 3 keeps the newest three across both files in order, that with no bot.log.1 it shows bot.log and no error, and that with no bot.log it still says so. I also looked at the earlier fix agent's leftover diff (249-leftover.diff). It had begun the same two things, taking out the roll and renaming the harness to test-show-botlog.ps1, and this finishes them. The branch now changes two files against main: tools/Show-BotLog.ps1 and the new harness. MEASURED: tools/test-show-botlog.ps1: 13 passed, 0 failed under pwsh and under Windows PowerShell 5.1. Run against main's Show-BotLog.ps1 (-ShowBotLogPath pointing at the output of git show origin/main:tools/Show-BotLog.ps1), it scores 9 passed, 4 failed: bot.log.1 lines missing, the order check, the -All check, and -Lines 3 across both files. The PowerShell parser reports 0 errors on Show-BotLog.ps1, test-show-botlog.ps1 and Install-Bot.ps1. git diff origin/main -- tools/Install-Bot.ps1 is empty. On the final merged tree (d7456aa), the full sweep ran 134 harnesses (every tools/test-*.js, tools/voice/test-*.js and tools/test-*.ps1 under pwsh, test-source-bytes included) with 0 failed. The same sweep before the second merge ran 127 with 0 failed. git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD patrick/todo-220-log-rotation now reports no conflict; before this fix it conflicted in three hunks. Nothing in .js, .py or tools/app changed, so there was no node --check, no ast.parse, no launcher build and no discord harness to run. WHAT IS LEFT: Entry 249's real work has not started and needs Patrick's decisions: choose NSSM or WinSW; create the low-privilege service account and keep its password where the other VPS credentials are, named by location only; move the bot.env.json ACL from SYSTEM to that account in the same step; and replace the scheduled task and the stop-by-command-line with Stop-Service plus a one-off sweep for a copy started by hand. Neither this branch nor 220 rolls the log while the bot is running. Only a service's roll-by-size log does that. The interim roll of bot.log itself belongs to entry 220's branch (patrick/todo-220-log-rotation). That branch is not on origin and has no pull request yet. Show-BotLog reading bot.log.1 is harmless before 220 lands (no bot.log.1 exists, and the harness checks that case) and useful once it has. Get-Logs.ps1 still fetches only bot.log and not bot.log.1; that belongs with 220's rotation or a later entry. The To Do List was not edited. The previous author's note that entry 220 'should be updated to say the bot is done here' is wrong and should not be followed: 220 does the bot roll and 249 does not. Nothing goes to the VPS from this branch until someone runs Show-BotLog.ps1. It only reads, and it needs no install.

## Read first

- `tools/Install-Bot.ps1:164-171`: the stop by command line and the comment saying why it is done that way, because a bot started by hand still holds the token
- `tools/Install-Bot.ps1:358-368`: the wrapper loop: cmd redirection at 366, a flat 15 second sleep, no failure count and a log that only ever grows
- `tools/Install-Bot.ps1:380-388`: Unregister and Register-ScheduledTask running as SYSTEM at RunLevel Highest
- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:168-178`: the secrets table, because moving the bot to a low-privilege account moves the ACL on bot.env.json with it

## Steps

- [ ] Agree in #dev which entry owns this loop before anybody starts, because entries 71 and 133 want a failure count and rotation on the same lines and a service does all three at once. (patrick)
- [ ] Choose one supervisor and write its configuration: with WinSW an XML carrying executable, arguments, workingdirectory, a roll-by-size log with a sizeThreshold and keepFiles, onfailure restart entries with growing delays and a serviceaccount, or the same shape from nssm set. (claude)
- [ ] Create a dedicated low-privilege local account for the service, with its password kept where the other VPS credentials are and named by location only. (patrick)
- [ ] In tools/Install-Bot.ps1, delete the run.ps1 heredoc and the Register-ScheduledTask block, replace the stop at 166-168 with Stop-Service, and keep a one-off sweep for a copy somebody started by hand. (claude)
- [ ] Change the ACL block in the same step as the account, granting the service account read on bot.env.json instead of SYSTEM, because taking SYSTEM off that file is how the bot once started with no token and exited immediately. (claude)
- [ ] Parse the edited script the way CI does before it goes anywhere near the VPS. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; $t=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1).Path, [ref]$t, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- [ ] Install on the box and check all four things: the service runs, it runs as the new account, it restarts the process when it is killed, and the log rolls. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-Service ThornswoodBot
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the file permissions moved with the account. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-Acl C:\Thornswood-Bot\bot.env.json | Format-List
  ```

## Commands

- Parses the edited script exactly as the build check does, printing any error. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; $t=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1).Path, [ref]$t, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- On the box: shows the service and its status. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-Service ThornswoodBot
  ```
- On the box: shows which account the bot actually runs as. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-Process python -IncludeUserName | Select-Object Id, UserName
  ```
- On the box: shows whether a rolled log file has appeared past the size threshold. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Thornswood-Bot\*.log*
  ```
- On the box: shows who can read the file that holds the token, by location only. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  Get-Acl C:\Thornswood-Bot\bot.env.json | Format-List
  ```

## Done when

On the VPS the service reports Running, the python process runs as the new account and not as SYSTEM, killing it shows the service restarting it with the restart in the Windows event log, a rolled log file appears past the threshold, and the ACL lists the service account. In the repo, the edited Install-Bot.ps1 parses with no errors.

## Traps

Install-Bot.ps1 talks to the VPS, so the person runs it. The cmd redirection at 366 is itself a fix: piping through PowerShell re-encoded the text and left the log unreadable past a point, and a slow pipeline could hold the bot's own print() calls on its event loop, so whatever replaces it must not reintroduce a pipeline. Stop-Service alone will not catch a copy started by hand, so keep the sweep. The token and the site's key are both written by this script, so never print either while testing.

## Links

- https://nssm.cc/usage nssm install and the set commands for AppStdout, AppRotateFiles, AppThrottle and ObjectName
- https://github.com/winsw/winsw the XML service definition with log modes and failure actions, the other option
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/scheduledtasks/register-scheduledtask what the current scheduled task does, so nothing is lost when it is removed
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-security-and-access-rights why a card renderer should not run as the highest account on the box
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/get-acl reading the permissions on the file that holds the token

issues.title: One bot token lives in two files and a backup zip, and rotating it is two scripts nothing ties together
issues.body:
**Order:** 281 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 126

## Where it lives

VPS · bot and site · tools\Install-Bot.ps1:219-303; tools\Set-DiscordLogin.ps1:244, 270-273; tools\Backup-Server.ps1:33, 246-248

## What is known

One rotation command that updates every consumer and restarts them. Install-Bot already writes the bot key into the site's config, so writing the token there too makes it one command with no second half to forget. Keep the webhook files and the backup zips outside the repository folder so a zip-it-and-send-it never carries them MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: There are still two writers for the token: - Install-Bot.ps1:272-296 prompts with Read-Host -AsSecureString, base64s the token into bot.env.json as DISCORD_TOKEN, and writes only botKey into the site's config.json (:360-369). - Set-DiscordLogin.ps1:176-290 writes discord.botToken into the site's config.json the same base64 way. There is no tools/Rotate-BotToken.ps1 (ls: no such file). Part of the entry is already true: - The backup zips land outside the repo: Backup-Server.ps1:28 sets $To to $env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\Thornswood-Backups, a sibling of the repo folder. - The webhook files are not tracked: `git ls-files tools/discord` lists no webhook file, and news-webhook.txt and dev-webhook.txt are gitignored (.gitignore:20, :40). They do still sit in the repo folder: Publish-Discord.ps1, Set-DevNews.ps1, Setup-Discord.ps1 and Build-Discord.py read them from tools/discord. tools/thornswood-front.zip (5.5 MB, gitignored by *.zip) is also in the repo folder. All three scripts pass StrictHostKeyChecking=no (Install-Bot.ps1:62, Backup-Server.ps1:47). NEXT STEP: Doable now: 1. Make Install-Bot the one rotation command rather than adding a third writer. In its settings block (:360-369), where it already reads, sets and writes the site's config.json for botKey, also merge the token into discord.botToken when one was given. Then restart the site task when the key or token changed. 2. Move the shared write into one function both scripts use, so Set-DiscordLogin's token write and Install-Bot's cannot drift. Or have Set-DiscordLogin hand the token to the same code. 3. Check statically with `Select-String -Path tools\Install-Bot.ps1,tools\Set-DiscordLogin.ps1 -Pattern '\$token|\$botToken'` that every use sits inside the base64 payload. Parse both scripts with the Parser API. 4. Correct SECOND-DEVELOPER.md's secrets table so it says which files hold the token and that one command updates both. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Rotating the token needs Patrick: - Reset Token in the Discord developer portal (an outside account). - Run it against the VPS. There is no dev bot instance to try it on first. - Decide in #dev how long backup zips are kept. - Decide whether the webhook files move out of tools\discord and where to, since four scripts read them from there. None of this can be proven without that live run.

## Read first

- `tools/Install-Bot.ps1:215-320`: the SecureString prompt, the base64 payload, the ACL on bot.env.json, and the block at 310-318 that already reaches into the site's config.json
- `tools/Set-DiscordLogin.ps1:241-256 and 265-276`: the second writer, and the base64 pattern with the comment saying why neither secret is ever a word on a command line
- `tools/Backup-Server.ps1:33-35`: the header saying the zip deliberately holds the token, the client secret and the server password, which is the third copy
- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:168-178`: the secrets table, the document that has to end up telling the truth

## Steps

- [ ] Write tools/Rotate-BotToken.ps1 that prompts for the new token as a SecureString, never as a parameter and never as a word on a command line. (claude)
- [ ] Have it base64 the payload exactly as both existing scripts already do, write bot.env.json on the VPS, then merge the token into the site's config.json with the read-set-write that Set-DiscordLogin.ps1 uses at 265-276. (claude)
- [ ] Have it restart the bot and the site and report which consumers were updated, naming each by location and never by value. (claude)
- [ ] Pull the write into one shared helper that Install-Bot.ps1 and Set-DiscordLogin.ps1 both call, rather than leaving a third copy. (claude)
- [ ] Move tools/discord/news-webhook.txt, dev-webhook.txt and the backup zips out of the repository folder to a path named in the secrets table, so a zip-it-and-send-it can never carry them. (patrick)
- [ ] Prove the no-secrets-on-the-wire property statically: the token should appear only inside the base64 payload and never in an ssh argument. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Rotate-BotToken.ps1 -Pattern '\$token'
  ```
- [ ] Confirm no webhook file is tracked, then run the new script against the dev instance first and the live one afterwards. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git ls-files tools/discord
  ```

## Commands

- Shows every place the token variable is used, which must all be inside the base64 payload. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Rotate-BotToken.ps1 -Pattern '\$token'
  ```
- Shows what is tracked in that folder, which must include no webhook file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git ls-files tools/discord
  ```
- Parses the new script the way the build check does. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; $t=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Rotate-BotToken.ps1).Path, [ref]$t, [ref]$e); $e
  ```

## Done when

After a dev run: the bot's log shows it reconnecting as the same application, the site's config.json parses and has the token present (presence only, never the value), and the site's Discord-dependent routes answer. In the repo, git ls-files lists no webhook file and the new script parses with no errors.

## Traps

Rotating a token is a live operation against Discord and the VPS, so the person runs it, and secrets are named by location only and never printed, pasted, committed or logged. A token that reaches bot.env.json but not the site's config.json leaves the site's Discord lookups failing, which is exactly the shape of entry 64, so rotate both or neither. Install-Bot.ps1 restarts the bot as part of its run, so a rotation during an evening throws whoever is mid-ticket. Every older backup zip becomes a copy of a dead token and a live client secret, so decide in #dev how long zips are kept. These scripts use StrictHostKeyChecking=no, so fix the ssh helper in entry 23 first.

## Links

- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html what a rotation procedure has to cover so no consumer is left behind
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits the per-route and global HTTP limits the bot meets when it reconnects and re-registers after a rotation
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/get-acl checking who can read the file the new token lands in
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-security-and-access-rights the account model the ACL on that file depends on

issues.title: The stranger waits on the site's timeout after pressing Submit
issues.body:
**Order:** 284 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Discord · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 129

## Where it lives

VPS · bot · tools\discord\bot.py:564-580, 112-135

## What is known

Acknowledge as soon as the thing they asked for exists and do the bookkeeping afterwards. Two blocks swapped. A spinner that sits for ten seconds reads as broken to somebody who has never used the server, and the site copy still lands MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Read tools/discord/bot.py on main at 29beece. TicketModal.on_submit is at 562 and its first line (563) is interaction.response.defer(ephemeral=True, thinking=True), so Discord's three second deadline is already met. At 703-704 the handler waits on push_async(...) before any of the three followup.send calls at 706-721. push() (222-245) calls urlopen with timeout=12 at 242, and push_async (248-252) runs it in an executor and already logs 'site push failed' itself. asyncio is already imported (create_task is used at 1318-1319). Nothing in git log -250 touches this ordering. tools/discord/test-ready.py and test-watch.py import the real bot.py with the outside world stubbed, and build.yml's 'Run the bot harnesses' step runs every tools/discord/test-*.py, so a new harness gets picked up with no CI change. The fall-back rewrite this entry's trap warns about is entry 154 (old 63). It changes bot.py:678-701, not the push line. A branch exists, patrick/todo-253-submit-wait, not merged: Patrick: after merge, deploy the bot with .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly (the only deploy this needs). Optionally, test on a dev Discord with the site pointed at a port nothing listens on: the ephemeral reply should appear at once, and bot.log should still get a "site push failed" line. The entry's trap still applies: entry 154 (old 63) rewrites the fallback block just above this one (bot.py:678-701 before the change), so whichever lands second rebases. This diff does not touch that block. Known limit, accepted in the triage: if the bot restarts in the moment between the reply and the push finishing, that one ticket's site copy is lost. The Discord thread is still the record. NEXT STEP: tools/discord/bot.py: delete the awaited push_async call at 703-704. Below the if/elif/else of acknowledgements (ends at 721), start it with asyncio.create_task(push_async(same args)), add the task to a module-level set _pushes, and give it add_done_callback(_pushes.discard) so it is not garbage collected. The DM branch, posted, fell_back and the message text stay as they are. New tools/discord/test-ticket.py, built like test-watch.py: import bot, set bot.push to a stub that sleeps 3 s and records its arguments, then call TicketModal.on_submit with a fake interaction, guild, channel and thread. Three cases: thread opens; thread refused so it falls back to the channel; no channel at all. Each case asserts that followup.send is recorded before the push stub returns and that push is still called once with the same five arguments. Then run py -m compileall -q tools\discord and py tools\discord\test-ticket.py. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #331. Merged origin/main (5a9ba5c) into patrick/todo-253-submit-wait with no conflicts. Main has not done this entry's change. The site push in TicketModal.on_submit was still awaited on main. On this branch it is still a background asyncio task, held in _pushes and started before the replies. Main's entry 154 (#308) changed the block just above it: a ticket whose thread will not open now goes to the staff-only log channel (checked by its permissions through log_channel and private_channel_ok) and no longer to the panel channel. The merge kept that and left the push change untouched. After the ... STILL TO GO OUT: Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly (the live bot). Left: Patrick, after merge: .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly is the only deploy this needs. Optionally, test on a dev Discord with the site pointed at a port nothing listens on: the ephemeral reply should appear at once, and bot.log should still get a "site push failed" line. Known limit, accepted in the triage: if the bot restarts between the reply and the push finishing, that ticket's site copy is lost. The Discord thread or the staff channel is still the record.

## Read first

- `tools/discord/bot.py:500-582`: the whole submission path: the thread creation, the fall-back to the channel at 540-551, the push at 564-565 and the three acknowledgements at 567-580
- `tools/discord/bot.py:112-141`: push with its 12 second urlopen timeout at 132, push_async at 138-140, and the comment at 113-115 saying the Discord thread is the record and the site push is the convenience
- `tools/discord/bot.py:423-424`: TicketModal.on_submit and its first line, interaction.response.defer(ephemeral=True, thinking=True), so the three second deadline is already met and the twelve seconds are the follow-up arriving late

## Steps

- [ ] Confirm the handler is already deferred before changing the order: bot.py:424 is interaction.response.defer(ephemeral=True, thinking=True), so the wait a tester feels is the follow-up at 567-580 and not the acknowledgement. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\discord\bot.py -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 420 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Move the await push_async(...) at 564-565 to after the if/elif/else block that ends at 580, so the acknowledgement goes out as soon as the thread or the channel message exists. (claude)
- [ ] Better still, do not await it at all: use asyncio.create_task(push_async(...)) and keep a reference so the task is not garbage collected, because push_async already swallows and logs its own errors. (claude)
- [ ] Leave the ordering of posted, fell_back and the direct message fallback exactly as it is, and change nothing else in the function. (claude)
- [ ] Compile-check the folder. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -m compileall -q tools\discord
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the diff is the moved block and nothing more. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff --stat tools/discord/bot.py
  ```
- [ ] Test on a dev Discord with the site pointed at a port nothing listens on, and time the reply with a stopwatch if you want a number. (patrick)
- [ ] Send it out: Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly (the live bot). (patrick)

## Commands

- Byte-compiles the bot sources to catch a syntax error before any deploy. (claude)
  ```powershell
  py -m compileall -q tools\discord
  ```
- Shows that only the moved block changed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff --stat tools/discord/bot.py
  ```
- Puts the push, the three acknowledgements and any defer call in one view. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\discord\bot.py -Pattern 'push_async|followup.send|defer'
  ```

## Done when

With the site deliberately unreachable, the ephemeral reply appears at once rather than after twelve seconds, and bot.log still carries a site push failed line, which proves the push ran and reported. The diff shows only the moved block.

## Traps

Entry 65 rewrites the same fall-back region to fail closed into the staff-only log channel instead of the public tickets channel, and that is a safety fix with higher priority, so agree in #dev which lands first or one will silently revert part of the other. The comment at bot.py:113-115 is the design statement that the Discord thread and not the site is the record, so do not invert it while reordering. Discord's three second acknowledgement deadline means moving work around can expose a handler that was never deferred. bot.py is deployed by Install-Bot.ps1, which the person runs.

## Links

- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/interactions/api.html Interaction.followup and InteractionResponse.defer, the two things the timing depends on
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/interactions/receiving-and-responding the three second deadline and what a deferred response buys you
- https://discordpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api.html the client and event model, for where a background task may safely live
- https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rate-limits what a burst of follow-up messages costs if the reordering changes the pattern

issues.title: The secrets table says the game server has a password; the script that manages it says it does not
issues.body:
**Order:** 289 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Handover · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 138

## Where it lives

Your PC · SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:172 against tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1:36-44

## What is known

A secrets inventory lists each credential, where it lives, what it actually protects and who can reissue it, and says not enforced where a control does not exist rather than listing it as though it did. Entry 4 is the same confusion in code; this is it in the documentation PART DONE 24 September, pull request #207. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 207, "The retired register secret gets its own row, and the VPS key row says to move the old key aside". SECOND-DEVELOPER.md's table said the game server had a password, sPassword in server-settings.json, handed to the launcher by the site at check in. tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1, the script that manages it, says in its own header that SkyMP has no join password and that it stopped touching the game server "because there was nothing to write there". The door key row named data\door.json; the gamemode reads private\door.json. The heading said none of them was in the repo, over a row naming a file in tools\discord. From the To Do List: "A secrets inventory lists each credential, where it lives, what it actually protects and who can reissue it, and says not enforced where a control does not exist rather than listing it as though it did." So every row now answers those four, and the rule is written under the table. Measured before writing each row, never reading a value: - The join password MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

## Read first

- `SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:168-178`: the whole secrets table, seven rows under a heading that claims none of them is in the repo while the #news webhook row names a file inside tools\discord
- `tools/Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1:30-40`: what the script actually does now, and the sentence at 35-36 saying there was nothing to write on the game server
- `tools/app/Config.cs:72-76 and tools/docs-app/server.js:1292`: the same value surviving as a dead field in the launcher and in the join reply, which entry 3 deletes

## Steps

- [ ] Wait for entry 3 to replace the four digit value before rewriting the row, or you document a compromised value as though it were fine. (patrick)
- [ ] Rewrite every row to answer four questions: the name, where it lives by location only, what it actually protects, and who can reissue it. (claude)
- [ ] Replace the first row with the truth: the game server does not enforce a password, offlineMode is set by Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:185, and the field survives in the launcher and the join reply as dead weight. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 181 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Introduce the phrase not enforced and use it, then add a one line rule under the table saying a control that does not exist is listed as not enforced rather than omitted. (claude)
- [ ] Add the rows the table is missing while you are there: the voice service's secret file and the dev webhook. Do not add an ssh key row, because VPS access already has one; make that row say what it protects instead. (claude)
- [ ] Record that a launcher older than 1.0.197 reads the password out of version.json rather than the site, so old installs keep whatever they last read, which is another not-enforced fact. (claude)
- [ ] Walk all seven existing rows against the machine, confirming presence and never printing a value, and record the result. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path SECOND-DEVELOPER.md -Pattern 'Server password'
  ```

## Commands

- Shows the row before and after the rewrite. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path SECOND-DEVELOPER.md -Pattern 'Server password'
  ```
- Pulls up the sentence in the script that contradicts the table. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1 -Pattern 'nothing to write'
  ```
- Shows the dead field in the launcher that the row should stop describing as a control. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Config.cs -Pattern 'ServerPassword'
  ```

## Done when

Every one of the seven rows can be checked by a person against the machine in under a minute: the file exists at the named path, the thing it claims to protect refuses without it, and the named script reissues it. For the first row, either the game server now refuses a connection without the credential, in which case the row is true, or the row says not enforced, in which case it is honest.

## Traps

Secrets are named by location only and never printed, pasted, committed or logged, and that applies to verifying a row as much as to writing one: confirm presence, never print the value. Entry 3 is a hard prerequisite, because the value in that first row is simultaneously a dead join password, a live register secret and in public history on the releases repo. Rotate-ServerPassword.ps1 reaches the VPS and the person runs it. Entry 138 wants one rotation command for the bot token, so the table and that entry have to agree on who reissues what.

## Links

- https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html what an inventory row should record: owner, location, rotation and blast radius
- https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/secret-security/secret-scanning the automated half that keeps the inventory honest once it is written
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.security/get-acl checking who can read each named file, which is half of what a row claims

issues.title: The Skyrim build number and the depot ids are compiled into the exe rather than carried in the feed
issues.body:
**Order:** 294 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 145

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Config.cs:77 and 206 (an expected file size); tools\app\Downgrade.cs:41-46 (three depot and manifest ids, and the newer build's size)

## What is known

The pinned build, its file signature and the manifests that produce it are data in the feed, not constants in the binary, so everyone can be moved to a new pin without shipping code. The project already applies this principle correctly elsewhere; the downgrade is the one place it did not MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The pin is still compiled in and nothing in the last 250 commits touches it. Downgrade.cs:38 AppId 489830, :48-52 the three depot/manifest pairs, :54 NewerExeBytes; Config.cs:122 ExpectedExeBytes = 37157144 and :273 the migration default (the entry's :77/:206 have moved). VersionDoc (Config.cs:461-541) has no pin fields; OnVersionDoc (Shell.cs:4333-4357) adopts serverAddress, collectionUrl, serverPort, maxOnline and collectionRevision only. Setup-Thornswood.ps1:40 (exe size) and :46-51 (depots) duplicate it, and that script still ships in the installer (Package-Thornswood.ps1:527). The premise does not hold, though: the build number lives in far more places than the entry names. Checks.cs:620 and Pages.cs:181 test skse64_1_6_1170.dll by name; Downgrade.cs:122-124, Shell.cs:1831-1832 and :1869, and Pages.cs:179 say 1.6.1170 in text; Package-Thornswood.ps1:183 packs skse64_1_6_1170.dll; Add-Bodies/Add-Characters/Add-JContainers pick the 1170/AE1170 builds. So putting the exe size and depots in the feed cannot move the pin without a launcher release. A pin move also needs a new script extender and collection revision, and CLAUDE.md already makes every change one complete release, launcher included. NEXT STEP: Now: the inventory above is the correction to this entry. If Patrick wants the plumbing anyway: (1) Config.cs VersionDoc gets optional expectedExeBytes (long), newerExeBytes (long) and depots ([{id, manifest}]), all defaulting to zero or null. (2) Shell.cs OnVersionDoc, beside the maxOnline line at :4344, adopts each value only when it is non-zero, and the existing cfg.Save writes it. (3) Downgrade.cs reads the depots and newer size from cfg and keeps the array at :48-52 as a clearly labelled fallback. (4) Publish-Update.ps1 writes the values from one record (for example a new tools/skyrim-pin.json), and Setup-Thornswood.ps1 reads the same record out of the installer stage in place of its own :40/:46-51 copy. (5) Compile with Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root <scratch> -NoPause and grep for 8442952117333549665 and expectedExeBytes. Otherwise close the entry, and fix only the duplication between Downgrade.cs and Setup-Thornswood.ps1. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides whether the pin should be feed data at all, given that the script extender dll name and the launcher's text are compiled in and a pin move is always a full release. If yes, he also decides which single record holds the pin.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Downgrade.cs:36-47`: AppId 489830, the three depot and manifest pairs in the static readonly Depots array, and NewerExeBytes at :47; the comment at :39-40 says the same ids are duplicated in Setup-Thornswood.ps1
- `tools\app\Config.cs:70-80 and 195-215`: ExpectedExeBytes at :77 and the migration default at :206, the exact shape a feed-supplied value with a compiled fallback already uses
- `tools\app\Config.cs:380-422`: VersionDoc, the real feed class; Updater.cs has no DataContract in it at all
- `tools\Setup-Thornswood.ps1:47-52`: the second copy of the same three depot and manifest ids, which silently disagrees the first time the pin moves

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line first: Shell.cs is on CLAUDE.md's protected list at line 79 and both machines touch it. (patrick)
- [ ] Cut the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-pin-comes-from-the-feed
  ```
- [ ] Add three optional fields to VersionDoc in tools\app\Config.cs:380-422: expectedExeBytes (long), newerExeBytes (long) and a depots array of id and manifest pairs, each defaulted so a feed without them still deserialises. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Config.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 376 -First 49 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Adopt them in the feed handler in tools\app\Shell.cs beside the maxOnline line at :4030, only when present and non-zero, then let the existing cfg.Save at :4058 write them. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 4026 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Change tools\app\Downgrade.cs to read the depot list and the two sizes from cfg first and fall back to the compiled Depots array at :41-45 when the feed has supplied nothing, marking that block clearly as the fallback. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Downgrade.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 37 -First 11 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Make tools\Setup-Thornswood.ps1:47-52 read the same feed, or say in the pull request why it is being left, because a fresh install pinned to script constants while the launcher follows the feed is the split this entry exists to remove. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Setup-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 43 -First 12 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Compile and prove the plumbing with two greps, then push and open the pull request. (claude)
  ```powershell
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher | Out-Null; .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-pin-comes-from-the-feed
  ```
- Compiles the launcher with the .NET Framework csc and drops Thornswood.exe in the scratch Launcher folder, the same gate the pull request build check runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher | Out-Null; .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- After the change this should only hit inside the marked fallback block. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Downgrade.cs -Pattern '8442952117333549665'
  ```
- Must hit inside the feed handler around line 4030. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern 'expectedExeBytes'
  ```
- Shows whether the script still carries its own copy of the depot ids. (claude)
