  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Setup-Thornswood.ps1 -Pattern '489831|489832|489833'
  ```
- Puts the branch on GitHub for the build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  git push -u origin patrick/the-pin-comes-from-the-feed
  ```
- Opens the pull request. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

Thornswood.exe comes out of the build, Select-String finds expectedExeBytes in Shell.cs's feed handler, and the depot id 8442952117333549665 appears in Downgrade.cs only inside a block that is plainly labelled as the fallback for a launcher that has never reached the site.

## Traps

Shell.cs is on the #dev-first list. C# 5 only: no string interpolation, no ?., no nameof, no expression-bodied members, no out var. Every launcher already installed reads the same version.json, so the new fields must be optional and an older exe must ignore them rather than fail to deserialise. Moving the pin is one coordinated act: the exe size, the depot manifests and the collection all describe one build of Skyrim, so changing one without the others hands people a game the checks call wrong. Do not run Downgrade or anything that talks to Steam from here.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.serialization.datacontractattribute the attribute VersionDoc is built with
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.serialization.datamemberattribute how to add an optional field an older exe will ignore
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.serialization.json.datacontractjsonserializer the serialiser that reads version.json, and what it does with members it does not know
- https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/SteamCMD Valve's own description of app, depot and manifest ids, the three things being moved into the feed

issues.title: Caddy and Node are fetched latest, with no version and no checksum, and the bot's libraries are unpinned
issues.body:
**Order:** 297 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 148

## Where it lives

VPS · tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:86-92 (downloads whatever the vendor serves, guarded only by whether a file already exists); tools\Install-Bot.ps1:210 (pip install with no versions)

## What is known

Pin to an exact version with a published checksum, recorded in the provisioning script and bumped deliberately. A requirements file with equality pins installed into a virtual environment. The next full install otherwise takes whatever the next major release turns out to be PART DONE 24 September, pull request #210. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 210, "A fresh VPS gets one exact Caddy, Node and set of bot libraries, checked against the published checksums". Entry 266 on the To Do List. Setup-Domain.ps1 fetched Caddy from the download API on caddyserver.com, whatever build it served that day, guarded only by whether caddy.exe was already there. Bootstrap-VPS.ps1 read nodejs.org/dist/index.json and took the newest v24 with Select-Object -First 1. Install-Bot.ps1 ran pip install discord.py pillow certifi by name. None of them checked a checksum. In the entry's words: "The next full install otherwise takes whatever the next major release turns out to be." Caddy is pinned to 2.11.4 with the SHA-512 from Caddy's own caddy_2.11.4_checksums.txt. The remote block downloads the release zip from GitHub, compares Get-FileHash SHA512 before unpacking, deletes the zip and throws on a mismatch, and keeps only caddy.exe. A box that already has caddy keeps it and now says which version it is. Node is pinned to v24.21.0 with the SHA-256 from nodejs.org/dist/ MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

## Read first

- `tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:84-94`: the Caddy block; the URL at :90 is https://caddyserver.com/api/download?os=windows&arch=amd64, guarded only by the caddy.exe existence test at :86, and the whole block is inside a here-string run on the VPS, so backticks are escapes
- `tools\Bootstrap-VPS.ps1:28-35 and 75-86`: $NodeMajor = 'v24' at :32 and the Node block that reads nodejs.org/dist/index.json and takes Select-Object -First 1 at :83; :18-19 records why the major is pinned at all
- `tools\Install-Bot.ps1:200-214`: line 210 is the pip install of discord.py, pillow and certifi with no versions, and the comment above it explains why certifi is there
- `tools\discord`: there is no requirements.txt in this folder today, which is the file the fix creates

## Steps

- [ ] Read the quoting in both here-strings before changing a character: a stray backtick or an unescaped dollar sign silently changes what runs on the VPS. (claude)
- [ ] Cut the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/pin-caddy-node-and-the-bot-libraries
  ```
- [ ] Replace the api/download URL at tools\Setup-Domain.ps1:90 with a pinned caddy_<version>_windows_amd64.zip release asset, add $CaddyVersion and $CaddySha256 parameters at the top of the script, and after the download compare (Get-FileHash $file -Algorithm SHA256).Hash against the expected value and throw on a mismatch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Setup-Domain.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 86 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add a $NodeVersion parameter beside $NodeMajor in tools\Bootstrap-VPS.ps1, select that exact entry from index.json instead of the Select-Object -First 1 at :83, and verify the msi against the SHASUMS256.txt nodejs.org publishes for that release directory. (claude)
- [ ] Create tools\discord\requirements.txt with discord.py, pillow and certifi pinned with == to the versions on the VPS today, create a virtual environment in the install script, and change tools\Install-Bot.ps1:210 to install with -r requirements.txt. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 206 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Copy each edited here-string body into a scratch .ps1 under the scratchpad and parse that file too, because ParseFile over the outer script treats the whole remote block as one string literal and cannot see a syntax error inside it. (claude)
- [ ] Let Patrick push the bot code to the VPS once the pull request is merged. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/pin-caddy-node-and-the-bot-libraries
  ```
- Parses the outer script, the same check the pull request build runs; empty output means it parses. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Setup-Domain.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- Same parse check for the bot installer. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- Parses the script that installs Node, which the Node half of this fix edits; empty output means it parses. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Bootstrap-VPS.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- Shows the newest-v24 pick in the Node block; after the change it must no longer sit there. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Bootstrap-VPS.ps1 -Pattern 'Select-Object -First 1' -Context 3,1
  ```
- Must return nothing once Caddy is pinned to a release asset. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Setup-Domain.ps1 -Pattern 'api/download'
  ```
- The file must exist and every line must carry an equality pin. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Test-Path tools\discord\requirements.txt; Select-String -Path tools\discord\requirements.txt -Pattern '=='
  ```
- Pushes the bot code and the new requirements file to the VPS. This one leaves the machine, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Bot.ps1 -CodeOnly -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

All three edited scripts parse, the extracted remote blocks parse as well, Select-String finds no api/download in Setup-Domain.ps1, the Node block no longer picks with Select-Object -First 1, and tools\discord\requirements.txt exists with == on every line.

## Traps

The parse check cannot see inside the here-strings, so a green build.yml proves nothing about the new Caddy or pip code; extract and parse the block separately. Both scripts handle VPS credentials: name them by location, never print or log a value. Pinning Node has a hard constraint recorded at Bootstrap-VPS.ps1:18-19, the voice server's native addon is Node-API, so do not pin below what the build machine runs. Bootstrap-VPS.ps1 also carries the broken guard from entry 166 of the wider list, so do not make that harder while you are in the file.

## Links

- https://caddyserver.com/docs/install Caddy's own install page, including the release downloads that replace the api/download call
- https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases the pinned release assets and the checksums published with each one
- https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json the index the Node block already reads, so you can pick an exact version rather than the newest
- https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/reference/requirements-file-format/ the requirements file format, including what == means
- https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html the virtual environment the bot's libraries should be installed into
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/get-filehash Get-FileHash, the checksum comparison after the download

issues.title: A Steam library on a second drive silently disqualifies the own game folder
issues.body:
**Order:** 298 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 149

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\OwnGame.cs:147-150, which refuses because hard links only work inside one volume

## What is known

Ask where to install on the volume it needs, during setup, before anything is written. Failing that, offer to move, or fall back to copies with the disk cost stated. Plenty of people keep games on a second drive, and today they meet a refusal rather than a choice MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: OwnGame.cs:147-149 still returns the flat 'has to be installed on the same drive' sentence. Since 20-21 Sep this blocks more than a feature: OwnGameRequired (ShellOwnGame.cs:158 onward) refuses Play outright, with a MessageBox, whenever WhyNot names a reason. So somebody with Skyrim on D: and Thornswood on C: cannot play at all. Place() (OwnGame.cs:785-791) already falls back to File.Copy when CreateHardLink fails, so the copy path exists mechanically. The installer (tools/setup/Bootstrap.cs:108 defaults to C:\Thornswood; BuildDrives :146-192) offers every fixed drive with no hint which one Skyrim is on, and its intro text at :411 still describes the old shape ('puts Thornswood into the Skyrim you already have on Steam... does not make a second copy'). The entry's trap that djinn/own-game-folder is not on main is out of date: 56af203 (1.1.75) and 5dcc6b5 put it on main, the branch no longer exists, and CLAUDE.md says so. Measured here: C:\Thornswood\Game is 41 GB apparent and its Data folder 26 GB, roughly what a copy fallback would cost. NEXT STEP: Doable now, inside the settled design: (1) Bootstrap.cs finds Skyrim's Steam library (the same libraryfolders.vdf walk as Steam.SkyrimPath, Steam.cs:107-130), preselects that drive, and says on screen when a different drive is picked that Thornswood has to share Skyrim's drive. Rewrite the stale text at :411 while there. (2) OwnGame.cs:147-149 names the exact way out: reinstall Thornswood to <Skyrim drive>\Thornswood, or move the Skyrim library to <Thornswood drive> in Steam's Storage settings. Compile the launcher and the setup stub. Left for #dev: whether the launcher may fall back to copies (about 26 to 41 GB, never silently) or move an install itself. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn in #dev: a copy fallback or a launcher-driven move both change the hard-link design. The installer steering and the clearer refusal need no decision.

## Read first

- `tools\app\OwnGame.cs:120-150`: the whole precondition method: the Vortex deployment test first, then the volume test at :147-149, which returns a flat refusal sentence and offers nothing
- `CLAUDE.md:24-35`: the settled design: the own game folder is built from Vortex's deployment with the big files as hard links, which is the reason the same-volume rule exists, and djinn/own-game-folder is not on main
- `tools\New-GameFolder.ps1`: the script that does the same job for Keizaal and Daedric, so you can see whether the restriction and any fix have to be mirrored
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:116-117`: the note saying OwnGame.cs and the foreign-file rules change together

## Steps

- [ ] Take this to #dev before writing code. CLAUDE.md names the own game folder as settled design, djinn/own-game-folder is not on main, and the two shapes must not be mixed in one release, so what the refusal should become is Patrick and Djinn's call. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm the branch really is still unmerged before arguing about it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git branch -a | Select-String 'own-game-folder'
  ```
- [ ] Cut the branch once the approach is agreed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/a-second-drive-is-a-choice-not-a-refusal
  ```
- [ ] Replace the sentence at tools\app\OwnGame.cs:147-149 with a structured result the caller can act on: same volume is fine, or offer to move the Thornswood folder to Skyrim's volume, or fall back to real copies with the disk cost stated. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\OwnGame.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 143 -First 9 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Compute that cost from the deployed Data folder with DirectoryInfo and show the number in GB on screen before anybody agrees to it, because copies double the collection on disk, which is the exact cost the hard-link design exists to avoid. (claude)
- [ ] Check the size the new code would show on a machine with two drives. (claude)
  ```powershell
  '{0:N1} GB' -f ((Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data' -Recurse -File | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum / 1GB)
  ```
- [ ] Compile, then confirm the dead end is gone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\OwnGame.cs -Pattern 'has to be installed on the same drive'
  ```

## Commands

- Shows whether djinn/own-game-folder is still unmerged, which decides whether any of this can ship. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch origin; git branch -a | Select-String 'own-game-folder'
  ```
- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/a-second-drive-is-a-choice-not-a-refusal
  ```
- Measures what a copy fallback would actually cost on disk, read-only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  '{0:N1} GB' -f ((Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data' -Recurse -File | Measure-Object Length -Sum).Sum / 1GB)
  ```
- Compiles the launcher with the .NET Framework csc and drops Thornswood.exe in the scratch Launcher folder, the same gate the pull request build check runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher | Out-Null; .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- The flat refusal sentence should no longer be the end of the path. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\OwnGame.cs -Pattern 'has to be installed on the same drive'
  ```
- Opens the pull request once the approach is agreed in #dev. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

Thornswood.exe comes out of the build, OwnGame.cs's volume test returns a choice rather than a sentence that ends the road, and the copy fallback prints a real size in GB computed from the deployed Data folder.

## Traps

This is settled design. Until djinn/own-game-folder is on main, what ships is the Steam copy with Vortex and the two shapes must not be mixed in one release, so steering the install drive from the installer is exactly that mix and needs the #dev line first. Hard links genuinely cannot cross volumes, so do not try to make them; the choice is move, or copy, or stay. Copies must never be a silent default. OwnGame.cs mirrors the foreign-file rules in Ship-Rules.ps1:116-117, so check whether your edit touches that pairing. C# 5 only.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/hard-links-and-junctions why a hard link cannot cross a volume, which is the constraint the refusal is built on
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-createhardlinkw the call the own game folder is built with and its same-volume requirement
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.driveinfo DriveInfo, for naming the two volumes and their free space in the choice
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.directoryinfo DirectoryInfo, for computing the size the copy fallback has to state
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/creating-symbolic-links the alternative link type, and why it is not what this design uses

issues.title: Which browser the in-game interface uses is inferred from another server's file, and recorded nowhere
issues.body:
**Order:** 299 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Compatibility · **Effort:** change it, small · **Old number:** 150

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Chars.cs:723-830; the reasoning at tools\app\Checks.cs:56-90

## What is known

Record which of the two it chose and show it where a person can see it, so a report about the interface says which one was running. The inference itself is correct and hard-won and should stay; what is missing is that nothing afterwards knows what it decided PART DONE 24 September, pull request #206. WHAT CHANGED: This branch fixes only the leftover the triage named. It is comments only. Two comments in tools/app/Checks.cs said NirnLab was "the browser backend this build runs on", "this build's own browser", "not another server's file" and "not foreign either", which contradicts OwnGame.Foreign and Test-ShipOtherServer. Those comments now say that which backend runs is not decided in Checks.cs. They point at Chars.WriteBrowserBackend, which chooses the backend on every Play, and at the line thornswood-front.js writes to Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log. They say that OwnGame.Foreign keeps NirnLab out of the own folder. The warning that NirnLabUIPlugin.dll must never go back on ForeignNames is kept, with its history. No code in Checks.cs changed. A new harness, tools/test-browser-backend.js, proves the change. MEASURED: Measured on this machine on 24 Sep. C:\Thornswood\Game\Data has no NirnLabUIPlatform folder. C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins\SkyrimPlatform.ini line 35 reads "BackendName = tilted" (file last written 18 Sep). issues.body:
**Order:** 300 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Moderation · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 151

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js: the complete set is death at 1581, respawn at 1618, reading a book at 1627 and activation at 1789

## What is known

Establish what the client is allowed to ask the server to do and block the rest at the handler level, then log what was allowed. Item creation is admin-only and audited on every server that has an economy. The consent rules the world runs on currently have nothing behind them but people keeping their word PART DONE 24 September, pull request #285. WHAT CHANGED: I merged origin/main into patrick/todo-269-audit-handlers. Main had gained seven pull requests since the branch's last merge: #253, #254 and #256 through #260. Git merged them with no conflicts. Main still has no onTakeItem or onDropItem, so the branch's change stands and main has not already done it. That change is three things in tools/gamemode.js: the list of what a client can ask the server, the two new handlers (mp.onTakeItem and mp.onDropItem), both built with guard(), that only log, and the three older comments about spell casts, corrected. The branch also adds tools/test-audit-handlers.js. Two of the merged pull requests change handlers that the list describes. #258 means a door that is a way out is never locked. #260 means a craft that matches no recipe is still asked race, profession and rank. One fix commit (58a5237) updates two rows of the list. The onActivate row now says a way-out door is never refused. The onCraft row now names every refusal the handler actually makes: the recipe gate, a key with no stamped mold, a hafted item with no handle, a brew or an enchantment made at the wrong trade's bench, and #260's craft that matches no recipe (tempering still goes through). Only the comment changed. When I started, the worktree already had the branch checked out with uncommitted edits to two comments, left by an interrupted earlier run. Those comments sit inside the ==== blocks for property and chat commands. I discarded the edits under the rule against hand-editing inside ==== markers; a copy is saved as scratchpad/269-uncommitted.diff. The merge commit f92ba1e carries the required trailer; I changed only its message, before anything was pushed. HEAD is detached, so the branch is free for the next worktree. Nothing was pushed. Status is partial because the entry itself is only partly done: the refusing half waits on Patrick's decision. MEASURED: - **Commits on main since the last merge:** `git log f4a2d6a..origin/main` lists 7 (#253, #254, #256, #257, #258, #259, #260). - **Merge:** clean. The branch's diff against origin/main is still only `tools/gamemode.js` (+289/-10) and `tools/test-audit-handlers.js` (+595). - **Handlers after the merge:** 7 registrations, all built with guard(): - onDeath :4781 - onRespawn :4914 - onActivate :6830 - onCraft :10000 - onPutItem :20202 - onTakeItem :20457 (new) - onDropItem :20462 (new) - **Where the list sits:** at :20209, between `end thornswood chat commands` (:20188) and `thornswood needs` (:20474). It is outside every ==== block. - **Refusals the onCraft row now names**, each read in the merged file: - `recipelessCraft` refuses a brew or an enchantment at :9967. - #260's owned-item refusal is at about :9866. - The recipe gate is at :10040. - The key mold check is at :10080. - The handle check is at :10131. - **Checks:** - `node --check` passes on `tools/gamemode.js` and `tools/test-audit-handlers.js`. - `tools/test-audit-handlers.js`: 70 passed, 0 failed. - Full sweep over every `tools/test-*.js`, every `tools/voice/test-*.js` and every `tools/test-*.ps1` under pwsh: 98 harnesses. - 95 passed on the first run. - `tools/voice/test-cull.js`, `test-ice.js` and `test-keepalive.js` failed on that run. The keepalive log shows EADDRINUSE on port 7903, and test-cull could not open its socket, which fits other worktrees running sweeps on the same ports. All three passed when I ran them again alone. - `test-source-bytes.js` passes after the commit. - **Checks on what the merge brought in:** - PowerShell parser: all 8 .ps1 files main changed parse. - Python `ast.parse` on the 3 .py files passes. - All 4 `tools/discord/test-*.py` pass (discord.py 2.7.1). - `Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root %TEMP%\ts-build-269 -NoPause` builds Thornswood.exe, exit 0. WHAT IS LEFT: **Patrick: the decision.** Which take the consent rules should refuse: a box inside somebody else's claim, another person's body, or a claimed house while its holder is offline (rule 4). Then onTakeItem returns false on that one named path. **Patrick: deploy and test.** After the pull request merges, run `.\tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1`, then a dev session to check three things: - ordinary doors, chests and items still work; - the `take:` and `drop:` lines appear in thornswood.log; - how many lines an evening produces. Nobody has measured that yet. **Still for the To Do List (this run cannot edit it):** 1. A likely defect. onDeath treats only a profileId of 0 as "not a person", but an NPC's profileId is -1 (MpChangeForms.h). If so, NPC deaths get a spawnPoint and a death line, and a warrior's kill credit never fires. This is read from the fork's source and has not been confirmed while the game runs. 2. Two comments inside ==== blocks are now stale and were left alone under the marker rule: - The property block says "no take handler". - The /ate note in the chat block says "there is no eat hook". The discarded draft that fixed both is at scratchpad/269-uncommitted.diff.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:1786-1800`: mp.onActivate, the one handler that makes an allow or deny decision; the comment records that an explicit false counts as a block and falling off the end is the safe answer

- `tools\docs-app\data\site\rules.md`: what the world's consent rules actually say, since the point of the work is to put something behind them

## Steps

- [ ] Say in #dev first what is actually being claimed, because the premise needs correcting: the four mp.on handlers are right, but chat and administrative actions are already handled and allow-listed server-side, and additem and placeatme cannot be reached by any mp.on handler. (patrick)
- [ ] Cut the branch. (claude)

- [ ] Log every action that was allowed, by name and quantity, through the existing log() helper rather than a new mechanism, because the audit trail is the point. (claude)
- [ ] Confirm what the shipped client can even forward before writing a handler for something that never fires. (claude)

- [ ] Parse the file and count the handlers, then let Patrick try it on the dev channel after saying in #dev that he has taken the dev feed. (claude)


## Commands

- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/server-side-watches-what-is-asked-of-it
  ```
- Parses the gamemode without running a server. (claude)

- Lists the registered handlers; it reads four today and must read more after the change, each wrapped in guard(). (claude)

- Confirms in the shipped client bundle which console commands are forwarded at all. (claude)

## Done when

node --check passes, Select-String lists more than four mp.on handlers with every one of them wrapped in guard(), each new handler has an explicit deny on its named path and nothing else, and a dev-channel run shows ordinary doors, chests and items still working.

## Traps

A handler that returns false too eagerly blocks ordinary doors, chests and items for everybody at once, which is exactly what the comment at gamemode.js:1786-1788 warns about. Item creation does not arrive as an mp.on event, so do not promise that a handler closes it. gamemode.js has no version, no lint and no tests, so add near the other handlers rather than at the end under a new banner. Deploying is Deploy-Gamemode.ps1, which is Patrick's to run. In any message text say customers, people or testers, never the other word.

issues.title: The Nexus collection carries the plugin order from revision 5, and what is left is proving a clean install matches the server
issues.body:
**Order:** 305 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 38

## Where it lives

Nexus collection ombo2a revision 5 · collection.json pluginRules, 51 rules over 52 full plugins · %APPDATA%\Vortex\skyrimse\userlist.yaml · revisions 2 to 4 carried no rules at all

## What is known

Re-upload the collection with its load order included, which Vortex supports and which costs minutes. Or ship only the own-folder shape, which makes the reference list authoritative everywhere. Today a first-time person installs, presses Play, is refused, and presses Fix DONE IN REVISION 5, 22 SEPTEMBER. The order is pinned as LOOT after rules in Vortex's userlist, one chain over the 52 full plugins from Water for ENB.esm to Playable Rieklings.esp, and revision 5's collection.json carries them: 51 plugin rules where revisions 2 to 4 had none. It is the order this machine deployed from revision 5, and the server takes the same list through Deploy-Gamemode -Vortex -NewOrder in entry 46, so both come from one source. THE MCM HELPER STEP IS ALREADY TRUE: revision 5 installs MCM Helper 1.6.2, and its MCMHelper.esp carries the light flag (header flags 0x200), checked in Vortex's copy and in the game folder. DOES LOOT STILL MOVE THINGS: not the chained plugins. LOOT treats an after rule as a hard constraint, so a sort can put other plugins between them but cannot reorder them. Light plugins and anything outside the chain can still move, and the server does not count those by position. What can still break it is somebody dragging plugins by hand, which the install instructions now tell people not to do. LEFT: the proof this entry asked for, a clean profile install compared line for line with the reference list. It can only be done after the release in entry 46, because until then the reference list on this machine is revision 4's. The 97 plugins, one listed twice and 48 of 55 were never checked and no longer matter. MEASURED ON THE MACHINE, 22 SEPTEMBER, after revision 5 published the order. LOOT treats the collection's "load after" rules as hard constraints and puts them ahead of its own masterlist. All 52 full plugins are chained one after another, so autosort cannot swap any two of them, and after a Sort Now all 52 landed in exactly the server's order. That is the fix working. THREE LIMITS, and the second one is maintenance nobody will remember without this line. ONE, light plugins are not chained. LOOT can still move an esl around, and that is fine, because the server's position check skips light plugins entirely. TWO, A PLUGIN ADDED LATER IS NOT PINNED UNTIL SOMEBODY GIVES IT A RULE. The chain covers what was in the collection when the rules were written and nothing after it. Every future plugin needs one rule putting it after the current last one in the chain, which as of revision 5 is Playable Rieklings.esp. Forget that and the new plugin floats, which is the same load order mismatch this entry exists to stop, arriving one revision later with nobody connecting the two. THREE, a conflicting masterlist rule stops LOOT rather than winning. If a future masterlist update ever contradicts one of these rules, LOOT reports a cycle and refuses to sort. The order stays where it is and the person gets an error, which is the safe way for it to fail. AND IT IS STILL DEFEATABLE TWO WAYS. The collection install dialog has a "Skip plugin rules" switch, and anybody who turns it on gets no order at all; the launcher's Fix button is the fallback for them. And dragging plugins by hand in Vortex still breaks it, because nothing about this stops a person reordering the list themselves. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #217. WHAT CHANGED: Added tools/Check-CollectionRules.ps1, a read-only check that compares the plugin rules in the Nexus collection with a plugin list. It reads the newest collection revision Vortex has installed, one plugins.txt (Profile\Default\plugins.txt unless -List names another) and the plugin headers in one Data folder. It says NO and exits 1 in four cases: a full plugin that no rule names (the entry's "a plugin added later floats" trap, and it says which rule the next upload needs), a rule the list breaks, two neighbouring full plugins that no chain of rules keeps in order, and a full plugin that a rule names but the list does not enable. Light plugins and the five base masters are left out, the same as the server's position check leaves them out. With no collection in Vortex it says SKIP and exits 0. tools/test-collection-rules.ps1 proves all of this with its own test files and runs the real script as a child process. MEASURED: Measured on this machine against revision 5 (collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z\collection.json: 51 rules naming 52 plugins). HELD, exit 0, for three lists: - the dev server's list: the 22:46 dev pack's profile\plugins.txt. Its SHA256 (A3FFEB2C...) is the same as %LOCALAPPDATA%\Skyrim Special Edition\plugins.txt. - that live plugins.txt itself. - Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt. All three: 94 enabled, 52 full, 42 light, 52 of 52 named, 51 pairs held. NOT HELD, exit 1, for the reference C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt (written 23 Sep 22:39): - "Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary.esp (line 34) must load after Thornswood-Content.esp (line 95)". - "Playable Rieklings.esp (line 93) then Thornswood-Content.esp (line 95): the rules put them the other way round". This confirms the triage's finding: diff shows Thornswood-Content.esp at line 31 in the live list and line 95 in the reference. The Profile\Default\plugins.txt.rev4.bak list: 5 plugins that revision 5 dropped are reported as floating, and 2 plugins the rules name are missing from it. Where the logic is in the new script: - Check-CollectionRules.ps1:108 picks the revision through Get-CollectionRevision. - :110-112 is the SKIP path. - :224, :238, :248 and :287 are the four findings. - :252 is Test-Reaches, which follows chains of rules only through plugins the list enables. Both files are pure ASCII with no control bytes. WHAT IS LEFT: The code is complete. The entry stays open for Patrick. Its doneWhen needs him to install the current collection revision into a clean Vortex profile (his Nexus account, in Vortex). He then runs `.\tools\Check-CollectionRules.ps1 -List <the plugins.txt that install wrote>` and Compare-Object on that file against the server's order (the dev pack list, or the live manifest read over HTTP). Not done here, and each is his decision: - The check is not wired into Ship, Deploy-Gamemode or Check-ShipReady. Putting it there would change a release gate. - The reference Profile\Default\plugins.txt on the shipping machine is out of the chain today. Its cause is entry 275 (Install-ThornswoodContent.ps1:15 anchors on a plugin that is in none of the lists). - Every future plugin still needs a rule after Playable Rieklings.esp in the next Nexus upload. This check now says so when one is missing.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt`: the reference list the server expects, 98 lines with 96 starred and no duplicate entries, which is the comparison target for whatever the collection holds
- `tools\app\Verify.cs:112-133`: what the launcher does when the two disagree: the MCM Helper light-flag special case at :115-120 that the collection is known to get wrong, and the positional comparison at :121-131
- `CLAUDE.md:24-35`: the settled design; the own-folder shape this row names as the alternative is on djinn/own-game-folder and is explicitly not on main

## Steps

- [x] Get the facts before anybody decides anything: the repo holds no collection.json, so plugin rules empty, 97 plugins with one listed twice and differs at 48 of 55 positions are all statements about a file only Nexus and Vortex hold. (claude)
- [x] Open the Thornswood profile in Vortex, export the collection, and diff its plugin order against the reference list position by position. (patrick)
- [x] Read the reference list yourself so the diff has a fixed target. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt' | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\*' }).Count
  ```
- [x] Only then decide. The cheap fix is to re-upload the collection with its load order included, which Vortex supports through the collection's own rules; that is Patrick's action on Nexus, not a code change. (patrick)
- [x] Fix the MCM Helper light flag in the same re-upload, because Verify.cs:115-120 records that the collection installs its plugin without the flag, which shifts every index after it by one and leaves the symptom in place. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Verify.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 111 -First 12 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] After the release in entry 46: install revision 5 into a clean Vortex profile and compare the resulting list line for line against the reference. It is also the last step of entry 46. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Compare-Object (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt') (Get-Content 'C:\Users\evilp\AppData\Local\Skyrim Special Edition\plugins.txt')
  ```

## Commands

- Read-only: says what is enabled that should not be and what is missing, comparing the live load order against the reference this install shipped with. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Plugins.ps1
  ```
- Counts the enabled plugins in the reference list, which reads 96 today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt' | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\*' }).Count
  ```
- Compares the reference list against the one Skyrim actually reads; nothing returned means they agree. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Compare-Object (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt') (Get-Content 'C:\Users\evilp\AppData\Local\Skyrim Special Edition\plugins.txt')
  ```
- Finds the MCM Helper entry whose light flag the collection gets wrong, so the position is known before the re-upload. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt' -Pattern 'MCM'
  ```

## Done when

A real diff of the exported collection against C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt exists and has been quoted instead of the unverified numbers, and after a re-upload a clean Vortex profile install produces a plugins.txt that Compare-Object matches against the reference line for line, ignoring the leading asterisk.

## Traps

Do not quote 97 plugins, one listed twice or 48 of 55 until the export exists: the reference list on this machine is 98 lines with no duplicates, so whatever duplicate exists is in the collection. Do not reach for the own-folder shape as a shortcut; it is unmerged settled design and the two shapes must not be mixed in one release. A re-upload that does not also fix the MCM Helper light flag leaves the symptom. Anything on Nexus is Patrick's account and Patrick's action. THE MAINTENANCE TRAP: the chain covers the 52 plugins that existed when revision 5 was cut and nothing added afterwards. Any new plugin needs its own rule putting it after the last one in the chain, Playable Rieklings.esp as of revision 5, or it floats and the position check fails for everybody who installed cleanly.

## Links

- https://loot.github.io/ LOOT, which is what decides the order when the collection carries none
- https://loot.github.io/docs/help/Introduction-To-Load-Orders why position matters at all, in the terms the server's positional comparison uses
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/compare-object Compare-Object, the line for line check after a clean install

issues.title: Seven copies of the list on your machine, written by five tools, and nothing compares any two at Ship time
issues.body:
**Order:** 306 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 39

## Where it lives

Your PC · Profile\Default, Profile\OwnGame, Profile\LocalAppData, Vortex's own, _dist\server, and tools\Ship.ps1 which never mentions the manifest

## What is known

The shipping step derives the server list from the reference it is about to pack, using the header logic Deploy-Gamemode already has, and refuses when it does not equal the live manifest, naming the first position that differs. Ten lines. Today they agree because the steps happened to be run in the right order on one machine RE-READ 22 SEPTEMBER, and most of this is already built, in Publish-Update rather than in Ship. Publish-Update.ps1:251 dot-sources LoadOrder.ps1, fetches the live manifest, and Get-ReferenceInServerOrder DIES when the server does not answer, so a pack can no longer be built against an unverified order. It puts the reference list into the server's order before zipping, so position is enforced by construction rather than compared. At :1256-1290 it derives the game order with Get-LoadOrderGame and names any full plugin the list enables that the server does not have, with the two commands to put it right. SO THE REMAINING GAP IS SMALL AND WORTH STATING EXACTLY: that check is set membership, not position, and the reordering makes position true rather than proving it. The Get-LoadOrderGame call there passes an empty ccc list, which is correct for a reference list (the shipping machine's own Creation Club files are not what testers have, and the launcher does the per-machine check), but it is worth a comment saying so before somebody reads it as an omission and adds it. Ship.ps1 itself still never mentions the manifest, so the Select-String in this row's commands still returns nothing. Whether the gate belongs in Ship as well is now a judgement rather than a defect. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #218. WHAT CHANGED: This does step 1 of the triage plan and nothing more. The new tools/test-load-order.ps1 dot-sources tools/LoadOrder.ps1 and runs it with stub light and Data checks, so it needs no game folder, no Data and no server. It checks the Publish-Update path end to end: a stale list is found at the exact first position that differs, and after Get-LoadOrderReordered it agrees at every position. It also checks the edge cases: an extra full plugin found by position, a plugin enabled twice, a missing or switched-off plugin, light plugins keeping their lines, case and spacing, Skyrim.ccc, the manifest JSON, the manifest URL and port, and that the file round trip keeps its byte order mark and newlines. It also compiles tools/app/LoadOrder.cs and checks that the launcher and the publisher give the same answers. That makes the LoadOrder.ps1 header line "held to identical output by a test" true for the first time. No change to LoadOrder.ps1, because the harness found no bug in it. MEASURED: Harness: 127 passed, 0 failed under pwsh 7.6.6 and under Windows PowerShell 5.1. 47 of those checks compare the launcher with the publisher. To show the harness catches real breakage, I ran it against 11 deliberately broken copies (scratch script mutants.ps1, run with -LoadOrderPath / -LauncherPath). Every one exited 1. The breakages were: light plugins moved, case-sensitive compare, ccc after the list, a duplicate accepted, slots unsorted, BOM read as text, a missing plugin skipped, resources served on the game port, the Data check dropped, and in LoadOrder.cs light plugins moved and a case-sensitive compare. The first version of the harness let 3 of them through. I tightened it until none got through. Real data on this machine, read only: C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt has Thornswood-Content.esp on line 31 of 95. Profile\Default\plugins.txt (written 2026-09-23 22:39) has it on line 95 of 95, and Profile\LocalAppData\Plugins.txt on line 96 of 96. The built server's order in C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\build\dist\server\server-settings.json (written 23 Sep 11:37, 57 plugins) has it at index 23. I only read the loadOrder field from that file. Against that order, Default and LocalAppData first differ at index 23: the list has Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary.esp where the server has Thornswood-Content.esp. Get-LoadOrderReordered moves 34 lines, the first being Thornswood-Content.esp, and after that the mismatch is -1. OwnGame already matches. This was checked against the local build, not the live manifest; I did not contact any server. I also reproduced a separate bug with a probe script under both PowerShell versions. At tools/Publish-Update.ps1:1542, `Say '...' + $missing[0] + '"' 'Yellow'` is parsed in argument mode, so the colour argument becomes '+'. Write-Host then throws "Cannot bind parameter 'ForegroundColor'". WHAT IS LEFT: For Claude (steps 2 and 3 of the triage plan, each its own pull request), plus two decisions for Patrick. (a) tools/Publish-Update.ps1, which is on the shared list (Patrick waives the #dev line when he asks). Add a comment at about line 1531 saying the empty ccc list is deliberate. Have the yellow warning name the first differing index from Get-LoadOrderFirstMismatch; the harness already shows it returns 8 for the extra-plugin case. Fix the bug at line 1542 in the same file, which needs its own To Do entry. When the list enables a full plugin the server does not have, that line throws under $ErrorActionPreference Stop. That happens after the upload and after version.json is written, but before 'Pushing', so the feed is never pushed and Write-Pending never runs. Line 1618, in the branch for a machine with no git identity, has the same pattern. The fix is to wrap the concatenation in parentheses. (b) tools/Install-ThornswoodContent.ps1: when the plugin is already listed, keep its line where it is; when the anchor plugin is missing, refuse instead of appending. That script is what moved Thornswood-Content.esp to the end of Profile\Default and LocalAppData on 23 Sep, and it needs its own To Do entry. Decisions for Patrick: whether an extra full plugin should stop a publish before the upload rather than warn after it, and whether Ship.ps1 gets its own load order gate. The entry calls both a judgement. The entry's doneWhen ("a reordered copy makes the dry run stop") is out of date: Publish-Update puts a reordered copy back in order rather than refusing it.

## Read first

- `tools\Ship.ps1:296-322`: the existing plugin freshness gate: it hashes each source plugin against the one in the game folder and calls Unbump and Die naming what differs, which is the precedent a load order gate copies
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:215-222`: Get-ShipLoadOrderDir, which already owns the question of where the reference list is read from; this is the one answer, do not add a second
- `tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1:113-180`: the header logic that derives the server's list: light plugins dropped, the master cascade, the five implicit Bethesda masters prepended at :147, and $keep at :173
- `tools\app\OwnGame.cs:404-428`: SettleSettings, which already copies the reference plugins.txt and loadorder.txt into the live location, so you can see which copy is which

## Steps

- [ ] Cut the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/ship-compares-the-load-order
  ```
- [ ] Read the reference list through Get-ShipLoadOrderDir from tools\Ship-Rules.ps1, not a second lookup of your own: that helper exists because Publish-Update and Package-Thornswood each had their own list and a sign-in token fell through the gap. (claude)
- [ ] Derive the server's expected order from it with the same header logic tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 uses, including the light-plugin drop, the master cascade and the five implicit masters. (claude)
- [ ] Fetch the live manifest and compare position by position, then on the first difference call Unbump and Die naming the index and both names, in the style already used at Ship.ps1:311-318. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 307 -First 14 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Compare case-insensitively, because the file is Plugins.txt in _dist\stage\profile and plugins.txt everywhere else. (claude)
- [ ] Prove the gate fails before trusting a green run: build it against a deliberately reordered copy and confirm it names the first position that differs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Compare-Object (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt') (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt')
  ```
- [ ] Have Patrick run a dry run to see the new step without publishing anything. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -DryRun -NoPause 'check the load order gate'
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/ship-compares-the-load-order
  ```
- Returns nothing today, which is the whole finding; after the change it must hit. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern 'manifest|plugins\.txt'
  ```
- Compares two of the copies on this machine, which is exactly the comparison the gate automates. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Compare-Object (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt') (Get-Content 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt')
  ```
- Parses Ship.ps1, the same check the pull request build runs; empty output means it parses. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $e=$null; [void][System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile((Resolve-Path .\tools\Ship.ps1), [ref]$null, [ref]$e); $e
  ```
- Runs the shipping steps without publishing, so the new refusal can be seen. This one is Patrick's. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -DryRun -NoPause 'check the load order gate'
  ```

## Done when

Ship.ps1 parses, Select-String now finds the reference list being read inside it, a deliberately reordered copy makes the dry run stop and name the first index that differs, and an untouched tree passes.

## Traps

Do not add a second answer to where the reference list lives; Get-ShipLoadOrderDir is the one. Publish-Update.ps1 is on CLAUDE.md's protected list if the work spreads there. The filename case varies between copies, so compare case-insensitively without assuming the strings match. The seven copies agree today only because the steps happened to run in the right order on one machine, so the test you write must fail against a stale copy before a green run means anything.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.utility/compare-object Compare-Object, the comparison the gate is built on
- https://loot.github.io/docs/help/Introduction-To-Load-Orders what a position in the list actually means to the game
- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:Mod_File_Format the plugin header the server list is derived from
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/workflows what a GitHub Actions workflow is, which is the shape .github/workflows/build.yml takes

issues.title: Two mods you believe are already removed are still shipping
issues.body:
**Order:** 309 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 172

## Where it lives

Your PC · TavernGames.esp and Respawn - Death Overhaul.esp are starred at lines 86 and 48 of Profile\Default\plugins.txt, again in Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt, and both .esp files are present in Game\Data

## What is known

Verified on 17 September. Taking a plugin out moves the load order for every machine at once, so it is a release, not a tickbox: pull them from the collection, re-derive the server list, deploy the server and the client together. Do it in the same batch as any other removal. Entry 168 is the other two RE-MEASURED 22 SEPTEMBER and every word of this row is still true, which is worth recording because it has been open five days. Both mods are starred in Profile\Default\plugins.txt, in Profile\Default\loadorder.txt and in Profile\LocalAppData\plugins.txt. All four files are in Game\Data: TavernGames.esp, TavernGames.bsa, TavernGames - Textures.bsa and Respawn - Death Overhaul.esp. The repo still names them in four places: Links.cs:77, known.md:34 and mod-audit.json at 126, 128, 146 and 148. Nothing here can close this. It is a Vortex change, a Nexus re-upload and one complete release, and every part of that is Patrick's. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Both mods came out in collection revision 5 on 22 Sep. grep -i 'Tavern|Respawn|SunHelm' finds nothing in C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt, Profile\Default\loadorder.txt (101 lines, 0 hits), Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt, Profile\LocalAppData\plugins.txt or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Skyrim Special Edition\plugins.txt. ls C:\Thornswood\Game\Data | grep -i 'tavern|respawn|sunhelm' is empty, so the esp and both TavernGames BSAs are gone. The revision 5 collection.json (%APPDATA%\Vortex\skyrimse\mods\collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z) lists 103 mods and neither of these. diff of Profile\Default\plugins.txt.rev4.bak against the current list shows Respawn - Death Overhaul.esp and TavernGames.esp removed. The latest dev pack (pack-20260923-2246-dev.zip) ships a list without them. tools/Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1:38-41 records that on 22 Sep live handed out 57 plugins matching the game, and only the stale dev list still carried the four. Left in the repo are tools/app/Links.cs:77 A("TavernGames",1668), known.md:34-35, mod-audit.json:126-148, board.json rows r52-r53 and the obsolete Skyrim Together-era tools/Add-TempleRespawn.ps1. All are carried into entry 280, which owns the same cleanup. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: Most of the machine side is confirmed done. grep -i 'tavern|respawn' finds nothing in C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt, Default\loadorder.txt, OwnGame\plugins.txt, OwnGame\loadorder.txt, LocalAppData\plugins.txt or LocalAppData\loadorder.txt. ls C:\Thornswood\Game\Data | grep -i 'tavern|respawn' is empty. tools\Find-MissingMasters.ps1 -Data C:\Thornswood\Game\Data prints "No missing masters: 100 plugin(s), 94 of them enabled". One doneWhen clause is still not true on main, though. It says "the launcher no longer links to a mod that is not shipped". origin/main (c32b820) still has tools/app/Links.cs:77 A("TavernGames", 1668); in the gameplay block of the Nexus link table that Shell.cs:2104/2420 reads through Links.Target and Links.Exact. The entry's own step 5 cleanup never happened either. Links.cs:77 is still there. tools/Add-TempleRespawn.ps1 still exists. tools/docs-app/data/known.md:34-35 still lists "Respawn - Death Overhaul" and "Tavern Games" under "These are in the collection and do nothing useful", and that page is public at thornswood.net/known. board.json:394 still names Respawn, and mod-audit.json:126/128/146/148 still carry the TavernGames BSA rows. No commit in the recent log touches any of these. The reviewer says entry 280 carries this cleanup, but only in part. 280's doneWhen covers known.md and the load order lists. It says nothing about Links.cs or the launcher link, so that clause would be orphaned if 278 closed. I also could not confirm the last clause, that the server list the publisher wrote matches the client list in count. The one number for it is Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1:38-41, measured 22 Sep. That is a record, not a current measurement. The dev pack pack-20260923-2246-dev.zip was not found locally to re-check, and the VPS was off limits in this pass. What is left is a small repo change and one launcher release to dev. That would make 278 fixable rather than stale. NEXT STEP: Close this entry. The leftover references (Links.cs:77, known.md, Add-TempleRespawn.ps1) are handled under entry 280 so the cleanup is done once. mod-audit.json is regenerated by Audit-Mods.ps1, which Patrick runs. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: The machine side is done. grep for Tavern and Respawn finds nothing in C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt, Default\loadorder.txt or the OwnGame lists. The only OwnGame hits are unrelated tavern sound files and a font. ls C:\Thornswood\Game\Data shows no TavernGames or Respawn file. known.md on origin/main (c13ada9) now marks both mods as Out, at lines 43 and 44. One doneWhen clause is still not met: "the launcher no longer links to a mod that is not shipped". origin/main tools/app/Links.cs:77 still has A("TavernGames", 1668). Shell.cs:2134 and 2450 read that table through Links.Target and Links.Exact. The entry's own step 5 named this line for removal, and no commit has touched it. Entry 280 does not pick it up either: its doneWhen covers the lists, Game\Data, Find-MissingMasters and known.md, and never mentions Links.cs. Closing 278 would leave that clause with no entry. The last clause, a server list count equal to the client list, rests only on the 22 Sep note at tools/Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1:38-41. Nobody has taken a fresh reading. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: Triage hands the leftover repo references (Links.cs:77, Add-TempleRespawn.ps1, board.json, mod-audit.json rows) to entry 280. Entry 280's doneWhen covers none of them except known.md, so either 280 takes them on explicitly or 278 stays open for them.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt`: line 48 is *Respawn - Death Overhaul.esp and line 86 is *TavernGames.esp, both enabled; Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt carries the same two at 47 and 85
- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\loadorder.txt`: both mods are here too, at lines 53 and 91, and this is the file Publish-Update.ps1:1158 actually reads, so a check that only looks at plugins.txt passes while the server list still carries them
- `tools\app\Links.cs:77`: A("TavernGames", 1668), a Nexus link the launcher shows, which goes dead the moment the mod is removed
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:30-36`: both mods are already documented as not working, with the reason for each, so the page has to change in the same release

## Steps

- [ ] Decide the whole removal set once with Djinn in #dev, batching this with entries 167 and 166, because taking any plugin out moves the load order for every machine at the same moment. (patrick)
- [ ] See exactly what is shipping today before touching anything. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt','C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\loadorder.txt' -Pattern 'TavernGames|Respawn - Death'
  ```
- [ ] Pull both mods from the Nexus collection and let Vortex deploy; do not hand-edit plugins.txt, because it is derived from what Vortex deployed and an edit there is overwritten while the .esp stays on disk. (patrick)
- [ ] Rebuild so both lists are re-derived, then confirm the four files are gone from the game folder: TavernGames.esp, TavernGames.bsa, TavernGames - Textures.bsa and Respawn - Death Overhaul.esp. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data' | Where-Object Name -match 'TavernGames|Respawn'
  ```
- [ ] Clean up the four other places in the repo that name them: the Nexus link at tools\app\Links.cs:77, the one-shot installer tools\Add-TempleRespawn.ps1, the two documentation entries in tools\docs-app\data\known.md and tools\docs-app\data\board.json, and the BSA rows in tools\mod-audit.json. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Links.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 73 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Check no plugin is left mastering to something that has gone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Find-MissingMasters.ps1 -Data 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data'
  ```
- [ ] Ship the launcher, the game files and the server in one release, because one machine out of step gets a load order error and cannot connect. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 'two mods out of the collection'
  ```

## Commands

- Shows both mods in both lists; after the removal it must return nothing for either file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt','C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\loadorder.txt' -Pattern 'TavernGames|Respawn - Death'
  ```
- Lists the .esp and the two BSAs still on disk in the game folder. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data' | Where-Object Name -match 'TavernGames|Respawn'
  ```
- Read-only: reports any plugin whose master has gone, which is an instant crash at load. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Find-MissingMasters.ps1 -Data 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data'
  ```
- Finds the repo references that go stale with the removal. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Links.cs,tools\docs-app\data\known.md,tools\mod-audit.json -Pattern 'TavernGames|Respawn - Death'
  ```
- Ships launcher, game files and server together, which is the only safe way to move the order. Patrick's, from main. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 'two mods out of the collection'
  ```

## Done when

Neither mod appears in Profile\Default\plugins.txt, Profile\OwnGame\plugins.txt, either loadorder.txt or Game\Data, Find-MissingMasters reports nothing, the launcher no longer links to a mod that is not shipped, and the server list the publisher wrote has the same count as the client list.

## Traps

A check that only greps plugins.txt passes while the server is still desynced, because Publish-Update.ps1:1158 reads loadorder.txt. TavernGames carries two BSAs that have to come out with the esp. The Embers XD SunHelm patch at plugins.txt:78 belongs to SunHelm, not to either of these two, so do not pull it here. Nothing on Nexus is yours to upload. Do not hand-edit the derived lists.

## Links

- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:Mod_File_Format why removing a plugin shifts every index after it
- https://loot.github.io/ what re-sorts the order once two entries have gone
- https://thornswood.net/known the public known issues page that has to stop naming mods that are no longer shipped

issues.title: Strip the load order to Special Edition only, so Anniversary content is never required
issues.body:
**Order:** 310 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Load order · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** patrick · **Old number:** 190

## Where it lives

Your PC · the current list of 102 plugins, checked against what needs the Anniversary upgrade

## What is known

Requiring paid content means half the people who would join cannot. Audit the list once, drop or replace anything that needs it, and do it in the same batch as entries 168 and 164 since all three move the order. Then say on the download page which edition is needed, because that is a question people ask before they install anything THE CHECK THIS ROW ASKED FOR IS BUILT, 22 September, commit 40d49d7. tools\Check-Editions.ps1 reads the MAST records out of every enabled plugin's header and reports anything declaring a Creation Club master, and any Creation Club plugin the list itself enables. Read only. MEASURED: 96 enabled plugins read, 0 named but not in Data, nothing declaring a cc master and no cc plugin enabled, so it exits 0 today. That is what makes it a regression test rather than a cut list, and it means THERE IS NOTHING TO CUT for the declared-dependency half: Special Edition is already enough. It was proved to fail before it was trusted: fed a planted plugin whose header declares ccBGSSSE001-Fish.esm it exits 1 and names it. It exits 0 with a SKIP on a machine with no game folder, so a build runner can run it. _ResourcePack.esl is not treated as a cut candidate, because 1.6.1130 put it in every Data folder. LEFT, and the script says so itself rather than pretending otherwise: a plugin using a Creation Club form id without declaring the master, and a mesh or texture that only ships with the upgrade. Neither is visible to any header scan. That is an xEdit pass over the order and somebody looking. join.md already says Special Edition twice and is deliberately left alone. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: tools/Check-Editions.ps1 (commit 40d49d7, 7,624 bytes) was run read-only tonight: 94 enabled plugins read, 0 named but not in Data, no Creation Club plugin enabled, nothing declaring a cc master, exit 0. The count is now 94, not 96, because revision 5 removed plugins. The script itself prints the two things it cannot see: an undeclared cc form id reference, and upgrade-only meshes or textures. New fact: C:\Thornswood\Game\Data holds 0 cc* files (ls | grep -i '^cc' counts 0), although Game\Skyrim.ccc names them. So every playtest on this machine is already a Special Edition only environment. The script cannot see those two cases, and neither can any header scan. No xEdit install was found on the usual drives (the search timed out without a hit). NEXT STEP: Nothing more for code. What is left is a person running SSEEdit over the current order: load everything, run Check for Errors, and look for unresolved or invalid-master form ids. Separately, look in play for missing meshes or textures (red exclamation marks, invisible objects). This machine has no Creation Club files at all, which makes it the right place to do that. Record in the entry that Game\Data has 0 cc files, so the in-play check can happen during any ordinary playtest here. Any cut then goes through the collection on Nexus and one complete release. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick (or Djinn) has to run an xEdit error check over the load order, and a person has to watch for missing assets in play on this machine, which has no Creation Club content. Any plugin found has to come out through a Nexus collection upload and a full release.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt`: the 96 enabled entries in load order; Game\Data holds 102 plugin files, the difference being the five Bethesda masters and _ResourcePack.esl
- `tools\Publish-Update.ps1:325-340`: $vanillaDataFiles and $vanillaDataPatterns already enumerate the base game files and the cc* patterns, which is the list an audit should reuse rather than reinvent
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\join.md:1-12`: the download page already says Special Edition on build 1.6.1170 and that Anniversary Edition is not required and never will be, so the last part of this row is done
- `tools\Audit-Mods.ps1`: the existing read-only audit that writes tools\mod-audit.json, the natural home for a master scan

## Steps

- [ ] Write a read-only script in tools\ that prints, for each of the 96 enabled plugins, its declared masters, and exits non-zero if any master matches cc* or falls outside the base game set, reusing the patterns already at Publish-Update.ps1:325-340. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Publish-Update.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 321 -First 22 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Run it and confirm it exits 0 today, which is what makes it a regression test rather than a cut list. (claude)
- [ ] Check the declared masters with the tools already here before writing anything new. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Find-MissingMasters.ps1 -Data 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data'
  ```
- [ ] Do not stop at the master scan: a plugin can reference a Creation Club form id without declaring the master, so run an xEdit error check over the load order and look for unresolved references. (patrick)
- [ ] Check the third kind too: meshes or textures that only ship with the Anniversary upgrade, which no header scan can see. (patrick)
- [ ] Leave tools\docs-app\data\site\join.md alone; it already says it twice, and a third statement that drifts is worse than one that does not. (claude)
- [ ] Batch any drop or replacement with entries 166 and 166 so the order moves once, and ship it as one complete release. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 'Special Edition only load order'
  ```

## Commands

- Read-only: reads the TES4 header of every plugin and reports any master that is not present. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Find-MissingMasters.ps1 -Data 'C:\Thornswood\Game\Data'
  ```
- Returns nothing today, which is the quick version of the declared-master check. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt' -Pattern '^\*cc'
  ```
