issues.title: Nothing anywhere limits how many people can connect, and the only number that looks like a limit is decoration
issues.body:
**Order:** 312 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 53

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · server-settings.json has no such key · Everyone's PC · tools\app\Config.cs:70 (MaxOnline = 25 is a display string), Online.cs:42, 104-105

## What is known

A hard slot count on the server, a clear refusal past it, and a number chosen from a load test rather than a guess. How many does it hold is a question a product answers before it opens. The twenty-sixth person today is told twenty-six of twenty-five are awake PART DONE 24 September, pull request #219. WHAT CHANGED: Step 2 only, scripts only. The server cap now comes from a single place: MaxOnline in the launcher's config.json, which is where Publish-Update.ps1 already reads it for the feed. A new tools/MaxOnline.ps1 (Find-LauncherRoot, Get-MaxOnline, Set-MaxPlayers) reads that key by the same rule the feed uses. Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 writes it as the engine's maxPlayers into the built server's settings, and Deploy-Server.ps1 sends those settings. Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 sets it in place on the dev box. Live reads C:\Thornswood\config.json and dev reads C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\config.json, the same two files the live and dev feeds are published from, so the feed, the Play page and the engine show one number. If there is no number, maxPlayers is left alone. If the number is above the engine's ceiling of 1000, the deploy stops before anything is written. MEASURED: The engine does cap connections, so the entry's title is wrong on that point. ScampServer.cpp:205 requires maxPlayers, Networking.cpp:157-162 hands it to RakNet as the slot count, and Networking.cpp:148 throws "Current slots limit is 1000" at startup above MAX_PLAYERS=1000 (skymp5-server/cpp/CMakeLists.txt:46). Nothing in the repo ever wrote maxPlayers: a grep of tools finds no match. On 24 Sep, C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp\build\dist\server\server-settings.json had maxPlayers 100, and so did C:\Thornswood-Dev\server-settings-vps.json (16 Sep copy). MaxOnline is 25 in both C:\Thornswood\config.json and C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\config.json; only that key was read. A refused person gets RakNet's "No free incoming connections" (Networking.cpp:49-50), and the client only traces it (skympClient.ts:70-72). The dev remote settings block was 16,238 characters as a command line before this change and about 17,062 after. Both are well over Remote()'s 6000 limit, so both already went up as a file and nothing changes in how it is sent. tools/test-max-online.ps1 passes 82 of 82 under both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. Against the old deploy scripts with the new helper it fails 11. Against the old code with no helper it fails at the first check. WHAT IS LEFT: Patrick: say in #dev that this is a soft limit until identity is settled (step 1). Pick the number from a load test, with voice tested under the same load (step 6); today the number is 25 because that is what the launcher already tells people. Merge, then run .\tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 for dev, and .\tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 then .\tools\Deploy-Server.ps1 for live when he says so. The VPS's actual maxPlayers has to be read on the box. The first deploy prints "most online: 25, was N". Claude, later steps: the gamemode logs a named "door: full" line (step 3); the voice service refuses at the same number (step 4); the server announces its cap and the Play page takes it from there (step 5). A message the refused person can see needs the fork's client to show connectionDenied, which is an engine release. The To Do List entry should be corrected: the engine caps at maxPlayers (100 until deployed), and step 2 is done on this branch.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Config.cs:68-70`: MaxOnline = 25 with a comment calling it something the Play page can say, which is all it has ever been
- `tools\app\Online.cs:38-46 and 98-106`: got.Max copied from cfg at :42 and Line() rendering N of 25 awake or room for 25, so the number is a display string end to end
- `tools\gamemode.js:2274-2400`: the door: the access control that watches who turns up, starts in WATCH mode and kicks nobody, which is where a slot count has to be enforced
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:150-210`: the other service people connect to, which needs the same cap or the game cap is half a fix

## Steps

- [ ] Say in #dev first that this is a soft limit until identity is settled: a cap enforced on a profile id the client picks is not a cap, because one person can hold several slots and a refused person can choose a different number. (patrick)
- [ ] Read the number from the server's server-settings.json rather than baking it, so it can be changed without a code release. (claude)
- [ ] Enforce it in the gamemode's door path, refusing past the count with a named reason that appears in the server log, not a silent drop. (claude)
- [ ] Cap the voice service in the same change, because it is the load bottleneck and capping one without the other only moves where it breaks. (claude)
- [ ] Have the server announce its actual cap in the status the launcher already polls, and derive the Play page string from that rather than the baked 25; Shell.cs:4030 already adopts maxOnline from the feed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 4026 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Measure before choosing the number: run a load test, and test the voice service under the same load, because the unculled position broadcast in entry 170 falls over first. (patrick)
- [ ] Parse both server files and compile the launcher. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\gamemode.js; node --check tools\voice\voice-server.js
  ```

## Commands

- Parses both server-side files without starting anything. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\gamemode.js; node --check tools\voice\voice-server.js
  ```
- Shows every place the number lives today, which is display only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Config.cs,tools\app\Online.cs,tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern 'MaxOnline|maxOnline'
  ```
- Returns only the respawn slots today, which is the evidence that nothing caps connections. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'slot'
  ```
- Compiles the launcher with the .NET Framework csc and drops Thornswood.exe in the scratch Launcher folder, the same gate the pull request build check runs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:TEMP\tsbuild\Launcher | Out-Null; .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root $env:TEMP\tsbuild -NoPause
  ```
- Puts the cap on the dev server for a load test. Say in #dev first, because there is one dev feed. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev 'a real cap on the door'
  ```

## Done when

server-settings.json on the VPS carries the cap key, the gamemode refuses connection N plus one with a named message that appears in the server log, the voice service refuses at the same number, the launcher builds, and the Play page string is derived from the announced value rather than the compiled 25.

## Traps

Order this after the identity work or say plainly that it is a soft limit, because the gamemode's own comment calls the profile id a claim and not a fact. The clause that server-settings.json has no such key is unconfirmed from this machine; that file lives on the VPS, so read it there before quoting it. gamemode.js and server-settings.json are deployed by Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 and Deploy-Server.ps1, which are Patrick's to run. Config.cs is C# 5. Shell.cs is on the #dev-first list. The voice service is the bottleneck, not the game server.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp the SkyMP server the gamemode runs inside, and where a connection is accepted
- https://nodejs.org/api/http.html the server the voice service is built on, for refusing a connection with a reason
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.runtime.serialization.datamemberattribute the feed field the announced cap travels in
- https://thornswood.net/join the page that would have to say how many the world seats

issues.title: What the unculled position broadcast costs: 369 GB an evening at two hundred people, against an 8 TB monthly cap
issues.body:
**Order:** 313 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 55

## Where it lives

VPS · voice · tools\voice\voice-server.js:192-206 (every peer, every 200ms) · measured at 128 bytes a row: 1.5 MB/s at fifty, 24.5 MB/s at two hundred, against a box that measured 93 Mbit/s

## What is known

Cull by distance and cell on the server, so each person is told only about people who could possibly be audible. That is the privacy fix and the bandwidth fix in one change, and it is the reason entry 6 does not try to do it: twenty-one evenings would burn the monthly cap, and the link saturates long before that PART DONE 24 September, pull request #211. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 211, "The voice service tells each person only about people they could hear, and their party". Every peer was sent the whole position snapshot five times a second: every person's coordinates, facing, cell and name, wherever they were. That is entry 282. It told anybody holding a socket where everybody in the world was standing, and it grew with the square of the room: the entry measured 1.5 MB a second at fifty people and 24.5 MB a second at two hundred, 369 GB an evening, against an 8 TB monthly cap and a box that measured 93 Mbit/s. Now each person is sent their own row, everybody in the same cell within 100 m, and their own party wherever they are. 100 m is over the furthest any client hears, the overlay's yell at 85 m, so nobody is cut off before their own falloff would have silenced them. The party is there because the party strip (ts-ui/thornswood-party.js) draws an arrow and a distance to every member anywhere in the world off this same feed, and a cull by cell and distance MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:192-206`: snapshot() filters on staleness and nothing else, and the setInterval at :202-206 sends the whole snapshot to every peer five times a second, so every person is told every other person's coordinates, facing, cell and name
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js:837-849`: the client already computes gain from cell and distance, including the different cell means no sound rule; this is the culling rule the server should be applying
- `tools\gamemode.js:616-620`: the towns table and the cell descriptors, so you know what a cell comparison actually compares

## Steps

- [ ] Pull the deployed voice service and read it before writing a line: the running build answers /health as owners-4 with routes that do not exist in tools\voice\voice-server.js, so an edit against the repo copy may land nowhere. (patrick)
- [ ] Cut the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/cull-the-position-broadcast
  ```
- [ ] Replace the single const snap = snapshot() at voice-server.js:204 with a per-recipient view: for each peer, include a row only when the other person is in the same cell or within the largest voice range. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\voice\voice-server.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 200 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Bucket by cell first so the loop is not quadratic over raw distance: keep a Map from cell descriptor to the peers in it and do distance maths only inside a cell. (claude)
- [ ] Use the same constants as tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js:837-849, because culling tighter than the client's own range table makes people cut out mid-conversation. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 833 -First 19 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Send a small left-your-range row so the client tears the peer connection down instead of leaving a stale panner running. (claude)
- [ ] Measure it without a game: instrument the interval to log total bytes written per tick, drive it with 200 synthetic positions spread across ten cells, and assert a peer in a different cell never appears in another peer's view. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\voice\voice-server.js
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/cull-the-position-broadcast
  ```
- Parses the voice service without starting it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\voice\voice-server.js
  ```
- Shows the single shared snapshot and the fan-out that has to become per recipient. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\voice\voice-server.js -Pattern 'snapshot\(\)' -Context 2,4
  ```
- Finds the client's range constants, which the server cull has to match rather than invent. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-ui\thornswood-voice.js -Pattern 'UNITS_PER_METRE|setRange'
  ```
- Installs and restarts the voice service on the VPS. This one leaves the machine, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Voice.ps1 -Restart -NoPause
  ```

## Done when

node --check passes, a unit test over the snapshot path shows a peer in a different cell never appears in another peer's view, and the instrumented bytes-per-tick figure for 200 synthetic positions across ten cells falls from 200 rows per recipient to a handful.

## Traps

This is the same change as the voice privacy problem and the mesh problem, and doing it wrong breaks voice for people who should hear each other. Do not cull tighter than the client's own range table. The deployed service is not this file, so verify against the deployed copy first. The dev gamemode currently talks to the live voice service, so testing on dev touches live. Slowing the 200 ms tick is not a substitute for culling, because that tick also carries positions for the audio panner. Install-Voice.ps1 and anything else that reaches the VPS is Patrick's to run.

## Links

- https://nodejs.org/api/timers.html#setintervalcallback-delay-args the 200 ms interval that does the fan-out
- https://github.com/websockets/ws the WebSocket layer every one of those rows is written through
- https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Source_Multiplayer_Networking how a shipped multiplayer engine decides who is told about whom, which is the same problem
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/PannerNode what the client does with each position row, so you know what may be dropped
- https://nodejs.org/api/net.html the socket the per-tick byte count is measured on

issues.title: The voice service writes to sockets with no backpressure, so one slow connection grows server memory without limit
issues.body:
**Order:** 315 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Scale · **Effort:** change it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 58

## Where it lives

VPS · voice · tools\voice\voice-server.js:109-112, 175-178, 202-206, 383-390

## What is known

Check the write return and skip the tick for a backed-up socket, or keep a small bounded queue per connection and drop the oldest. For state that is superseded every tick, dropping is the correct answer and is what unreliable transport means MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Still open. Sock.send at tools/voice/voice-server.js:281-284 calls this.socket.write and ignores its return value. ping() at :276-279 does the same, there is no 'drain' listener, and nothing checks writableLength. There are more call sites than the entry's six: announce :388, denied :409, welcome :424, the position tick :443, /say :793, the sdp/ice relay :885, vmode :900 and chat :956. Measured with a scratch copy of the service on loopback port 17993, a preload that wraps net.Socket.write, and one websocket that joins and then never reads. At 1,500 synthetic rows (about 165 KB a message, 5 a second), write() returned false 91 times in 20 s, nothing reacted, and writableLength climbed linearly: 0.33, 1.98, 3.6, 5.3, 6.9, 8.4, 10.1, 11.7, 13.3, 15.0 MB, with RSS going from 58 to 87 MB. At 200 rows the Windows loopback buffers absorbed the first 2.4 MB, and writableLength stayed 0 for all 20 s, so a harness has to use a heavy feed or run longer. The entry's 'the deployed copy is owners-4' step is stale: 41fdc1a merged it and BUILD is 'chat-1' (:61). A branch exists, patrick/todo-284-voice-backpressure, not merged: 1. Push the branch and open the pull request. Nothing was pushed from here. 2. After the merge, Patrick installs the voice service on the dev service first, using the dev flags from the author's notes: Install-Voice.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-Voice-Dev -Port 7789 -TaskName "Thornswood Dev Voice". Then check that /health reports build cull-1-command-ack-1-backpressure-1 and the fields backed, largestQueueBytes, droppedPositions, skippedRosters and closedBacklogged. 3. For the To Do List (not edited here): - Entry 284's steps said the roster stays on the reliable send. It now keeps only the newest roster while a socket is backed up, for the reason above. Record that on the entry. - The entry's step saying the deployed build is owners-4 is out of date. - The entry names a branch patrick/voice-service-honours-backpressure. The real branch is patrick/todo-284-voice-backpressure. - Entry 282 is on main now (PR 211), so the "do them together" trap is handled by this merge. - Every join and leave still sends the whole roster to everyone, which grows with the square of the room. A roster sent as changes only is a possible follow-up. NEXT STEP: 1. tools/voice/voice-server.js, class Sock (:256-359): add this.backed = false, a socket.on('drain') that clears it, and have send() record a false return from write. Add sendLossy(obj) that returns straight away while backed. Add a ceiling: once socket.writableLength passes 1 MB, close() the socket so the client reconnects. 2. New harness tools/voice/test-backpressure.js, following the test-ice.js pattern: a copy in a temp directory on a spare port, one socket that never reads, 1,500 rows every 200 ms for 20 s. Assert that writableLength (read from /health) stays under the ceiling and that the socket is closed once it passes it. 5. node --check. 24 SEPTEMBER: merged as #275. The reviewer's blocker was real and was still on the branch; it is now fixed. Sock.write closes a socket as soon as its writableLength passes QUEUE_CEILING, and feed() kept looping over the frames left in that read. Those frames reached onmessage for a peer that onclose had already removed. Fix (a171600): `if (this.closed) return;` at the top of the for(;;) in feed(), so the loop stops the moment the socket closes, including a close made by a write inside onmessage. I added a harness section to tools/voice/test-backpressure.js that repeats the reviewer's probe. A third socket that never reads ... STILL TO GO OUT: Install-Voice.ps1 (live voice service). Left: Merging and installing are for Patrick, not this run: push the branch, open the pull request and merge it, then run .\tools\Install-Voice.ps1, which is his and talks to the VPS. First, compare with the deployed copy as the entry's first step says, because the running service answered /health with a different build. BUILD stays 'cull-1-command-ack-1-chat-limit-1-chat-local-1-turn-key-1-backpressure-1' because this work has not shipped; if a copy from this branch was ever installed before these two commits, change it to backpressure-2 so /health can tell the two apart. For the To Do List (this ...

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:105-112`: the minimal socket wrapper and send(obj), which calls this.socket.write inside a try and ignores the boolean it returns; this is the single choke point every broadcast goes through
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:192-206`: the snapshot and the 200 ms tick, the traffic that actually matters and the same code the culling work touches
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:177, 186, 205, 436, 483, 532`: the six send call sites: the roster, welcome, the position fan-out, the loopback broadcast, the signalling relay and chat

## Steps

- [ ] Add a dropping sendLossy() that returns early while backed, and use it only at :205, the position tick, because that state is superseded every 200 ms; leave the roster, welcome, the loopback broadcast, the signalling relay and chat on the reliable send. (claude)
- [ ] Add a hard ceiling: when writableLength passes about 1 MB, close the socket and let the client reconnect, which is better than growing without limit. (claude)

## Traps

The GET /choices route is a one-shot HTTP response and not a backpressure site; the real sixth site is chat, plus the loopback broadcast and the signalling relay the write-up misses. issues.title: The command channel between the plugins and the server has no acknowledgement, and drops the oldest on overflow
issues.body:
**Order:** 321 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 96

## Where it lives

VPS · voice · tools\voice\voice-server.js:495-534, 408-416 · VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:3333-3359, 2863-3067

## What is known

A command channel carries an authenticated sender, a message id, an acknowledgement and a bounded retry. A queue that overflows drops the newest and tells the sender, rather than silently discarding what it already accepted. Entry 7 is what happens when two servers share this channel; this is the channel itself PART DONE 24 September, pull request #212. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 212, "The acknowledged poll hands each line to dispatch(), and its test knows it". To Do entry 290, "The command channel between the plugins and the server has no acknowledgement, and drops the oldest on overflow". Every slash line and every plugin report (/face, a swing of the axe, a broken lockpick) waits in the voice service's queue for the gamemode to collect it over loopback every 1.5 seconds. Two ways that lost commands with nobody told: GET /commands emptied the queue in one splice before the gamemode read the answer, and poll() parsed it inside a catch that returned. A batch that failed to parse, or an answer lost to the two second timeout, was gone from both ends. A full queue (200) shifted the oldest off the front without a word, so a command already taken vanished to make room. The service now gives every command an id (a stamp made at start, then a counter). GET /commands?ack=1 hands out the queue without emptying it, POST /commands/ack (loopback only, like MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

## Read first

- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:405-416`: the loopback-gated GET /commands; :412 splices the whole queue out in one go, so it is emptied before the gamemode has seen anything
- `tools\voice\voice-server.js:495-534`: where a slash line is queued, and the overflow rule at :520 that drops the oldest silently
- `tools\gamemode.js:3333-3359`: poll(), the other end: an http.request to 127.0.0.1 every 1500 ms, and the parse at :3343 whose catch returns and silently discards a whole batch that has already been removed from the service

## Steps

- [ ] Do not test this on the dev channel until the dev gamemode stops polling the live service: it drains this very queue, so a dev test eats live commands. (patrick)
- [ ] Cut the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-command-channel-gets-an-acknowledgement
  ```
- [ ] Make the drain non-destructive: return the queue with an id per item instead of splicing it out at tools\voice\voice-server.js:412. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\voice\voice-server.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 408 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add a loopback-only POST /commands/ack that removes acknowledged ids, guarded by the same isLoopback test already used at :411 and :421. (claude)
- [ ] In tools\gamemode.js poll(), acknowledge only after handle() has succeeded, so the parse failure at :3343 no longer loses a batch that the service has already forgotten. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 3339 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Change the overflow rule at :520 to refuse the newest and tell the sender, rather than silently discarding what it already accepted. (claude)
- [ ] Parse both files, then run the loopback test: POST a chat line into a locally running copy, GET /commands twice and assert the second GET still returns it until an ack arrives. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\voice\voice-server.js; node --check tools\gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/the-command-channel-gets-an-acknowledgement
  ```
- Parses both ends of the channel. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\voice\voice-server.js; node --check tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Shows the drain, the loopback gate and the new ack route beside them. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\voice\voice-server.js -Pattern '/commands' -Context 2,4
  ```
- Shows the parse whose catch currently throws a whole batch away. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'JSON.parse\(body\)' -Context 2,3
  ```
- Installs and restarts the voice service on the VPS. Patrick's. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Install-Voice.ps1 -Restart -NoPause
  ```
- Rebuilds and deploys the gamemode end of the channel. Patrick's, and it goes in the same release as the service. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1
  ```

## Done when

node --check passes on both files, a local loopback test shows a command still returned by a second GET until an ack arrives, and an overflow now refuses the newest with a message to the sender rather than dropping the oldest without a word.

## Traps

The /commands and /say routes are already loopback-gated, so this is not the identity hole; the sender's profile id comes from the join message, which is a different entry. The deployed voice service is not this file. The dev gamemode currently polls the live service and drains this queue, so testing on dev eats live commands until that is fixed. Gamemode and service both change, so it is one complete release.

## Links

- https://nodejs.org/api/http.html the request and response model both ends of the channel are built on
- https://nodejs.org/api/net.html the loopback address the gate at :411 checks
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp the gamemode side, and what handle() is being asked to do
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket the socket the commands arrive on before they reach the queue

issues.title: The same thirty-four lines are copied verbatim into five plugins
issues.body:
**Order:** 324 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Gamemode · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 99

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-chargen.js:21-66, thornswood-emotes.js:31-76, thornswood-front.js:29-74, thornswood-mark.js:21-66, thornswood-voice.js (the same block)

## What is known

This is the whose-game gate, the thing that keeps the plugins idle unless the client is pointed at this server, so five copies of it is five places for one of them to drift. One plugin loads first and publishes a small named object, which is the pattern front.js already established for everything else PART DONE 24 September, pull request #235. WHAT CHANGED: I added one new harness, tools/test-whose-game-gate.js, and changed no runtime code. It reads every .js in tools/ts-plugins, the same set Ship.ps1 sends to Data/Platform/Plugins, so a sixth plugin would be checked too. For each one it checks four things: the gate is the first statement inside the plugin's wrapper; thornswoodGame() and the comment above it match front.js once indentation is set aside; every copy gives the same, correct answer in 15 cases run against a fake file system (no settings, another server, ours with a fresh, stale or missing note, a Thornswood.ini address, a byte order mark); and the one address in `ours` is the ServerAddress default in app\Config.cs, which is where Set-Vps.ps1 reads the address it moves. It also applies Set-Vps's replacement to each plugin and runs the gate again against the new address. The file header records why the entry's one-copy plan was not done: it fails open because of load order. MEASURED: All five copies of thornswoodGame() are 34 lines, and the gate is at chargen.js:50/53, emotes.js:50/51, front.js:40/41, mark.js:32/33 and voice.js:15/16. Today they are identical. front.js differs only by two-space indentation and the spacing before the trailing comment on `let when = Number(first);`. The harness gives 57 passed, 0 failed. To prove it catches drift, I made four edits by hand and then restored them with git checkout: emotes' note window 24h to 48h, mark's `ours` set to the old box 192.135.119.166, a statement put above voice's gate, and a word changed in chargen's gate comment. With those in place it gave 42 passed, 15 failed, and each failure named the file and the first line that differs. Set-Vps.ps1:70 takes the old address from Config.cs:13 (192.135.112.23). Its walk (skipDirs, extension list, 8MB limit) reaches all five plugins. Nothing in the repo writes a ServerAddress line into Thornswood.ini, so the ini override in the gate is only there for a hand-set ini. The dev server is on the same IP (58 references to 192.135.112.23 across tools). Load order: in the fork, skyrim-platform/src/platform_se/skyrim_platform/SkyrimPlatform.cpp:335-347 GetPathsToLoad uses std::filesystem::directory_iterator. NTFS returns names in order, so chargen.js and emotes.js load before front.js. That confirms the triage finding that the entry's stub plan, which returns true when front's object is missing, fails open. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick and Djinn in #dev, because the gate is settled design and a Claude does not decide this: pick one of (a) keep the five copies, held together by this check, which is now in place; (b) delete the retired thornswood-chargen.js together with its references in Install-Emotes.ps1:33,52, Install-Thornswood.ps1:109, Revert.ps1:69-92 and Check-Chargen.ps1:182, leaving four copies; (c) one copy that stays safe whatever the load order, where a plugin that loads before front.js and finds nothing published stays idle instead of carrying on (fails closed); (d) drop the gate now that Thornswood runs from its own folder and, by Patrick's 20 Sep decision, nothing here supports another server's install. The entry's own plan (stub returns true when globalThis.Thornswood.whoseGame is absent) must not be done as written. The entry's doneWhen (settings-file read in one file only) is not met and should not be until the #dev choice is made. The To Do List entry should be updated (not done by me, per limits): record that the check exists on this branch, give the corrected line numbers, and say that the stub plan fails open. Merging needs a normal PR. There is nothing to deploy.

## Read first

- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-chargen.js:18-24`: the comment explaining that plugins share one global scope, which is why everything is wrapped and why a shared object is delicate
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-chargen.js:40-74`: the gate itself: `if (!thornswoodGame()) { return; }` at 40 and the 34-line function under it. The same block is at emotes 50-84, front 40-74, mark 32-66, voice 15-49
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js:78-80`: `const T = (globalThis.Thornswood = globalThis.Thornswood || {});`, the publish point that already exists and does half the job
- `CLAUDE.md:36-42`: the settled-design line that the plugins idle unless the client points at our server and a fresh session note is there

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line first and get Patrick and Djinn to agree, because the whose-game gate is settled design in CLAUDE.md and a Claude does not settle it: say the problem, the approach and what it touches. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm the five copies yourself before editing, because the entry's line ranges are wrong: the guard and function are at chargen 40-74, emotes 50-84, front 40-74, mark 32-66 and voice 15-49. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-*.js -Pattern 'thornswoodGame'
  ```
- [ ] Keep the function body in front.js only and publish it as `T.whoseGame` on the object front.js already creates at line 79. (claude)
- [ ] Replace the body in the other four with a three-line stub that calls `globalThis.Thornswood && globalThis.Thornswood.whoseGame` when it is there and returns true when it is not, so nothing depends on load order. (claude)
- [ ] Move the hardcoded server address into that one copy while you are in there, and leave tools\Set-Vps.ps1 as the only thing that rewrites it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Set-Vps.ps1 -Preview
  ```
- [ ] Parse all five plugins and expect exit code 0 from each. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem tools\ts-plugins\*.js | ForEach-Object { node --check $_.FullName }
  ```
- [ ] Prove the body moved: the settings-file read should appear in one plugin and be gone from the other four. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-plugins\*.js -Pattern 'skymp5-client-settings.txt' | Group-Object Filename | Select-Object Name,Count
  ```

## Commands

- Shows the real line number of the guard and the function in each of the five plugins. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-*.js -Pattern 'thornswoodGame'
  ```
- Parses every plugin in the folder; silence means all five are sound. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem tools\ts-plugins\*.js | ForEach-Object { node --check $_.FullName }
  ```
- Counts the settings-file read per file, which is how you see the body is in one place. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\ts-plugins\*.js -Pattern 'skymp5-client-settings.txt' | Group-Object Filename | Select-Object Name,Count
  ```
- Lists every file that carries the server address without changing any of them. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Set-Vps.ps1 -Preview
  ```
- Starts the branch, after the #dev line is agreed and not before. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/one-copy-of-the-whose-game-gate
  ```

## Done when

`node --check` exits 0 on all five plugins, and the Select-String group count shows 'skymp5-client-settings.txt' read in one file with the other four holding only the three-line stub.

## Traps

Skyrim Platform loads every file in Data\Platform\Plugins in an order nobody controls, and a top-level function name is shared global state, which is exactly what the comment at chargen.js:20-23 is about. A naive front-publishes-it refactor fails silently for whichever plugin loads first, which is why each of the four keeps a stub that works when the object is absent. The address is in all five copies and in forty other files.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/tree/main/docs/skyrim_platform Skyrim Platform's documentation index, the pages that say what a plugin may call
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/cookbook.md Cookbook recipes, including how a plugin initialises itself across reloads
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/const Why a top-level const in two files stops one of them loading
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#-check node --check, run over each plugin as the done-when

issues.title: Mod settings menus reset every session, because a character lives on the server and there is no save for a mod to write into
issues.body:
**Order:** 330 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 180

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · no co-save exists under SkyMP · listed in the tester note as something not to report

## What is known

The server already stores per-character state, so mod settings can live there too: a small store keyed by character that the front plugin reads back at login and writes on change. Worth doing for the handful of settings people actually touch rather than all of them PART DONE 24 September, pull request #257. WHAT CHANGED: Merged origin/main (52472ed) into patrick/todo-299-mcm-inventory with no conflicts. The branch adds only two new files, tools/Audit-ModMenus.js and tools/test-mod-menus.js, and nothing on main touches them. Main does not already do this. Its nearest work, bsa.py and Audit-PapyrusEvents.py from #237, reads the same archives but answers a different question: which Papyrus events the blocker leaves alive. So the menu inventory is not a repeat. I added the session trailer to the merge commit. No fix commit was needed. The branch itself is still what its author described: step 1 of the entry only, a read-only count of the mod settings menus and where each one keeps its values. The per-character store, the doc corrections and the in-game check are not built, so the entry stays partial. The worktree is detached so the branch is free. MEASURED: After the merge, git diff origin/main HEAD shows only the two new files (792 + 432 lines). node --check passes on both. test-mod-menus.js: 54 passed, 0 failed, including the check that nothing in the folder was written, and the one that says the output never says "player". Neither file has an em dash. Full sweep on the merged tree: all 64 tools/test-*.js, all 7 tools/voice/test-*.js and all 18 tools/test-*.ps1 under pwsh, 89 in all, every one exit 0. test-source-bytes.js: 2 passed. discord.py 2.7.1 is present, so I also ran tools/discord/test-ready.py and test-watch.py; both exit 0, though this branch does not touch the bot. No .ps1, .py or tools/app file changed, so the PowerShell parser, python ast and launcher build checks do not apply. WHAT IS LEFT: Unchanged from the author's list. For Patrick: name the handful of settings people actually change (node tools\Audit-ModMenus.js -v lists them all), and decide whether the per-character store is still worth building. On the measured numbers, only the classic menus with GLOB records reset, plus SkyUI_SE's 3 script properties, which a store cannot reach. For a tester on the dev build: which menus open under SkyMP, whether an MCM Helper value survives quitting and coming back, and whether AHZmoreHUD or atlas act on a GLOB set from outside their menus. Still not done: correcting known.md, help.md, tests.md and board.json r40 so they say only classic menus reset, which must ride with entry 296 / 184's table move; and the store in gamemode.js with the login read in thornswood-front.js. Needs its own To Do entry: Data\MCM\Settings\Precision.ini and TrueDirectionalMovement.ini in C:\Thornswood\Game are another server's (Daedric Online) files, and they override those mods' defaults. The branch is not pushed, and it has no pull request.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:16-22`: the claim as written: 'Your character lives on the server rather than in a save file, so there is no co-save for a mod to write its settings into'
- `tools\docs-app\data\tests.md:162`: the 'Do not report these' sentence that repeats it, which has to change in the same release if this is built
- `tools\gamemode.js, the chargen state handling`: the server already keeps per-character state, and that is the store a settings feature extends rather than inventing a second one
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js`: the front plugin that would ask for the map at login and send a write when a value changes
- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt:65 and 82`: MCMHelper.esp and McmRecorder.esp are both enabled, so the machinery a fix hooks into is already present

## Steps

- [ ] Confirm the machinery is there before designing anything: MCMHelper.esp and McmRecorder.esp are in the load order and MCMHelper.dll is in the SKSE plugins folder. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt -Pattern 'MCMHelper|McmRecorder'
  ```
- [ ] Scope it deliberately small: pick the handful of settings people actually touch and write that list down, rather than trying to persist every menu. (patrick)
- [ ] Add a per-character key and value store to tools\gamemode.js beside the chargen state it already holds, keyed by the same character id. (claude)
- [ ] Have tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js ask for the map at login and apply it, and send a write when a value changes. (claude)
- [ ] Read McmRecorder first to see whether replaying a recorded menu walk is cheaper than intercepting individual settings, since it is already in the list. (claude)
- [ ] Round-trip the store server side with the game closed: write a value for a character id, restart the server, read it back and confirm it survived. (patrick)
- [ ] Parse both changed files. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\gamemode.js; node --check tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js
  ```

## Commands

- Confirms the two MCM mods a fix would hook into are enabled in the shipping load order. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt -Pattern 'MCMHelper|McmRecorder'
  ```
- Shows MCMHelper.dll is really on disk, not just its plugin record. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\SKSE\Plugins -Filter 'MCM*'
  ```
- Parses the server gamemode after the store is added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Parses the front plugin after the login read and the write path are added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js
  ```
- Puts the changed gamemode on the server; it leaves the machine, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1 -Gamemode tools\gamemode.js
  ```

## Done when

A value written for a character id through the gamemode path is still there after a server restart, and `node --check` exits 0 on both changed files. That proves the half that is actually missing; the in-game half needs the game and belongs to a tester.

## Traps

Every Papyrus event except OnUpdate is blocked, so a mod cannot be relied on to announce its own setting change through a script event; the change has to come through the interface layer or a poll. This is a server change plus a client plugin change, so it ships as one complete release. known.md:20 currently files this under 'not going to change', so entry 184's table move has to ride in the same release or the page will be telling people not to report a thing that now works.

## Links

- https://github.com/Exit-9B/MCM-Helper MCM Helper, the framework for mod configuration menus that the shipping load order already carries
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/papyrus.md The rule that Papyrus types and methods only work inside a hook or a Skyrim Platform event, which bounds the design
- https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html The file API the gamemode's own persistence already uses

issues.title: Killmoves and stagger do not show on other people, so a fight looks different to each person in it
issues.body:
**Order:** 331 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 181

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · those animation events are blanked

## What is known

Replicate the animation event rather than blanking it, which is the same shape as the position feed that already works. It matters more on a roleplay server than a co-op one, because a fight everybody saw differently is a fight nobody can agree about afterwards MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The entry's plan is obsolete. tools/Patch-Client.ps1 no longer exists, and per CLAUDE.md every client change now lives in the fork at C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp on thornswood/engine-changes (HEAD c8832519, the commit recorded in tools/client-build.json). In the fork, skymp5-client/src/services/services/deathService.ts:31-57 blanks 'KillMove*' and 'staggerStart' in a sendAnimationEvent hook limited to form ids 0xff000000-0xffffffff, which covers other people's actors and server-made actors only. Your own character's stagger already goes out: sync/animation.ts:258 forwards any event not in ignoredAnims (:296-304, which does not include staggerStart). The receiving machine applies it at animation.ts:180 with Debug.sendAnimationEvent on the remote actor, and DeathService's hook then blanks it. So stagger crosses the wire and is dropped on arrival. animation.ts:172-176 and :306-317 already hold the pattern needed to let a network-applied event through (the allowedAnims set used for attacks). Killmoves are paired animations between two actors whose owners are different machines, and death is server-owned, so they are a design problem, not a relay problem. NEXT STEP: Stagger only, as a prepared change. In the fork, add an allow set in animation.ts that marks formId:staggerStart just before Debug.sendAnimationEvent. Make deathService.ts hookDisableStagger let that one through and still blank a stagger the local game raises on someone else's actor. Build the client, record it with New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1 (tools/client-build.json changes), then Sync-Client.ps1 -Check and a dev Ship. No gamemode change is needed. Killmoves: write the analysis and a design note for #dev (who starts the pair, how the victim's machine and the server agree on death) and build nothing yet. known.md:22 changes in the same release if stagger lands. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A two-person playtest on dev: one staggers the other and both say what they saw. Killmoves need a design agreed between Patrick and Djinn in #dev before any code, since they touch server-owned death.

## Read first

- `tools\Patch-Client.ps1:1-40`: the header records why hand edits do not survive: on 16 Sep at 14:58 a fresh bundle landed, Keep took it as ours, the 15:23 pack shipped it, and the 14 Sep hand edits were gone
- `tools\Patch-Client.ps1:95-240`: the four existing blocks, each a Name, the exact expected text, the replacement and a marker, at lines 98, 129, 161 and 231. A fifth block copies this shape
- `C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js, class DeathService`: hookDisableKillMoves, hookDisableStagger and hookDisableBlockedAnims each set ctx.animEventName to empty, filtered on 'KillMove*' and 'staggerStart'
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-emotes.js:366-450`: a working example in this repo of applying a received animation event, including the try/catch that exists because the call throws in the wrong context

## Steps

- [ ] Accept the settled design before writing anything: skymp5-client.js is not built here, it is patched by Patch-Client.ps1 and shipped as is, so every change to it is a block in that script. (claude)
- [ ] Run the existing check first to see the four blocks pass against the bundle currently on disk, and expect exit code 0. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check
  ```
- [ ] Find the exact DeathService text to match on, so the new block's expected string is a copy rather than a paraphrase. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js -Pattern 'hookDisableKillMoves|hookDisableStagger|staggerStart'
  ```
- [ ] Add a fifth block to tools\Patch-Client.ps1 in the same shape as the four at 98, 129, 161 and 231: a Name, the expected text, the replacement and a marker so it is idempotent. (claude)
- [ ] In the replacement, leave ctx.animEventName alone locally and send the event name to the server instead of blanking it. (claude)
- [ ] Replicate it server side to nearby machines and apply it there with Debug.sendAnimationEvent on the remote actor, following the try/catch at thornswood-emotes.js:436-450. (claude)
- [ ] Re-run the check and confirm it names the new block and still exits 0, and that it exits 1 when the expected text is not found exactly once. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check
  ```

## Commands

- Checks every patch block against the bundle on disk without writing to it; this is what Ship runs before every publish. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check
  ```
- Locates the exact text in DeathService that the new block has to expect. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\skymp5-client.js -Pattern 'hookDisableKillMoves|hookDisableStagger|staggerStart'
  ```
- Lists the existing blocks so the fifth one is written in the same shape. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Pattern 'Name   ='
  ```
- Parses the server side of the replication after the forwarding handler is added. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Parses the patch script, the gate the GitHub build applies. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $null = [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile("$PWD\tools\Patch-Client.ps1", [ref]$null, [ref]$null); 'parsed'
  ```

## Done when

`.\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check` reports the new block and exits 0, and exits 1 if the expected text is not found exactly once. That is the read-only test and it catches the most likely failure, which is upstream changing DeathService under you. The visible result needs the game and belongs to a tester.

## Traps

The bundle in the game folder is another server's build, Keizaal's until 16 September and Daedric Online's since, so the expected text can change without notice; that is why each block fails the release rather than patching loosely. sendAnimationEvent hooks accept at most one wildcard in a filter. This is a client and a server change together, so one complete release, and known.md:22 currently calls it permanent, so entry 184's table move has to ride with it.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/events.md sp.hooks.sendAnimationEvent, its enter and leave callbacks, and the one-wildcard filter limit stated outright
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/native.md Calling Skyrim's own functions, which is what Debug.sendAnimationEvent on a remote actor is
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp The SkyMP source, for reading DeathService upstream when the expected text stops matching
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/papyrus.md The rule that Papyrus methods only work inside a hook or a Skyrim Platform event, which is why the call throws in the wrong context
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.management.automation.language.parser.parsefile Parser.ParseFile, for checking Patch-Client.ps1 still parses after the fifth block

issues.title: Start On Save is in the mod list and never loads a save, and pointing it at a character that does not exist crashed a fresh install
issues.body:
**Order:** 332 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 182

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · the launcher points it at a character that does not exist; an offline save cannot be loaded under Thornswood at all

## What is known

If it cannot do the one thing it is for, take it out of the collection rather than documenting it. It is also the sentinel entry 153 uses to decide the collection is out of date, so replace that check in the same change MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Parts of the entry are stale. The collection sentinel was already replaced: Shell.cs:4585-4618 CollectionProblem now compares Checks.CollectionRevision against Updater.FeedCollectionRevision (#96, f2f2da4), and tools/test-collection-revision.js:135-137 asserts nothing decides staleness from StartOnSave. tools/New-GameFolder.ps1 no longer exists. Chars.cs is right that sCharacterName = Thornswood-Nobody is the fix. The game folder's po3_StartOnSave.ini (23 Sep 10:19) carries it, and Chars.cs:846-922 WriteStartIni writes it on every Play. New findings: (a) the collection does carry the mod. %APPDATA%\Vortex\skyrimse\mods\collection_ombo2a_5_2026-09-22T22-26-11Z\collection.json lists 'Start On Save' (modId 50054, optional false), and the Steam copy's vortex.deployment.json deploys po3_StartOnSave.dll from 'Start On Save 50054 2.8.0'. That makes the comments at Shell.cs:4600-4603, Checks.cs:43-47 and Publish-Update.ps1:1219-1221 ('the collection has never carried it') wrong. (b) The Checks.cs:659-662 'Auto load' row reports 'walks past the main menu' when the DLL is present, which Chars.cs:846 contradicts, since the mod is told to stand still. When the DLL is absent it turns red with 'install it in Vortex'. Shell.cs:395 then logs 'Something needs attention before you can play', and Discord.cs:611 sends the row with the session. The installer zip does not contain the DLL (checked the Thornswood-Setup.zip entries). Other references remain at Run-Everything.ps1:43, Add-Characters.ps1, known.md:49 and help.md:120. NEXT STEP: Now, on one branch, as a dev launcher release: (1) delete the 'Auto load' row at Checks.cs:659-662 and StartOnSaveInstalled at :23-31 if nothing else uses it. (2) Correct the three wrong comments in Shell.cs, Checks.cs and Publish-Update.ps1. (3) Keep Chars.WriteStartIni. Vortex does not uninstall a mod that leaves a collection, so the DLL stays on most machines, and with a blank ini it loads the newest save, which caused the crash. (4) Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause, then run node tools/test-collection-revision.js. After Patrick's Nexus revision without Start On Save: drop Wants at Run-Everything.ps1:43, retire Add-Characters.ps1, and change known.md:49 and help.md:120 to say it is gone and left inert where it remains. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Taking Start On Save out of the collection is a new Nexus collection revision, which only Patrick can publish. It must come after the launcher release that removes the Auto load row. Patrick also decides whether it comes out at all, since it is harmless with the ini the launcher writes.

## Read first

- `tools\app\Chars.cs:636-715`: the comment block and WriteStartIni, the only honest account of this: sCharacterName = Thornswood-Nobody is the deliberate fix, and the comment names the two crash logs
- `tools\app\Checks.cs:23-27 and 452-461`: StartOnSaveInstalled tests for po3_StartOnSave.dll, and the 'Auto load' check uses it
- `tools\app\Shell.cs:4260-4266`: CollectionProblem returns 'stale' when StartOnSaveInstalled is false, which is the sentinel that has to be replaced before the DLL is removed
- `tools\Run-Everything.ps1:40-44 and tools\New-GameFolder.ps1:201`: the Wants entry naming the DLL and the special case naming po3_StartOnSave.ini, the two script references that go with it

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line first: Shell.cs and Checks.cs are both on CLAUDE.md's protected list because both machines touch them. (patrick)
- [ ] Read Chars.cs:636-715 and accept the correction before acting: the character name that does not exist is the fix, not the fault, and the crashes came from bStartNewGame true. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Chars.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 632 -First 86 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Replace the sentinel at Shell.cs:4264 first, pointing CollectionProblem at a file that is genuinely part of the current build and unlikely to be replaced. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 4260 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```

issues.title: Dull tinted hair, the colour of a bad dye job made with flowers
issues.body:
**Order:** 338 · **Wave:** 7 Everything else · **Category:** World · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 211

## Where it lives

Asked for in Discord 17 September · the build already ships RaceMenu and RaceMenuPlugin, which carry hair tint sliders

## What is known

Probably already possible rather than needing anything added: check whether the tint slider in the race menu is reachable and whether the result survives a login, given that the server owns appearance. If it does, this is a line in the help page rather than a build. If the tint is lost on login, that is a real bug in how appearance is stored and is worth more than the feature MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The entry's lead is misdirected. faceMark is now at tools/gamemode.js:3896-3906, not 820-841. It compares a.hairColor by value and only counts tints, and it is the chargen 'did the face change' check, not the persistence path. Hair colour travels on its own: in the fork, sync/appearance.ts:38-45 reads base.getHairColor().getColor() into an integer hairColor, appearance.ts:138 applies it with TESModPlatform.setNpcHairColor, and the server serialises and compares it (skymp5-server Appearance.h:50, 63, 75). So a hair colour that reaches the NPC's hair colour form round-trips as RGB, independent of tints. RaceMenu is enabled: plugins.txt:33 RaceMenuMorphsHIMBO, :52 RaceMenu, :53 RaceMenuPlugin and :54 RaceMenuMorphsCBBE, not lines 13 and 54-56. Nothing here can show whether RaceMenu's hair colour picker writes that form or an overlay SkyMP does not carry. Appearance is only taken while the race menu is open in the hall. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change until the test result is in. Record the correction in the entry: hair colour is compared by value, so a lost tint would not be caused by faceMark. If the colour survives a relog, add one line to tools/docs-app/data/help.md or the Bard/appearance area of tools/app/Help.cs saying where the slider is (RaceMenu, Hair, colour) and that it can only be set in the hall. If it is lost, trace RaceMenu's hair colour from appearance.ts:38 (what getHairColor returns after RaceMenu sets it), not from faceMark. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A person in the game: make a character, set a dull hair colour with the RaceMenu slider in the hall, finish, log out and back in, and say whether the colour held. Patrick decides whether 'dull tinted hair' means a creation-time colour, which this answers, or dyeing later, which is a new feature.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:820-841`: the faceMark doc comment and function: it records the bug it was written to fix, and its signature counts `(a.tints || []).length` rather than comparing tint values
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:38-42`: 'What the server owns', which confirms appearance is server owned, so a tint has to survive a round trip through the server and not just through the game
- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt:13 and 54-56`: RaceMenu.esp, RaceMenuPlugin.esp and both RaceMenuMorphs plugins are enabled, so the tint sliders ship already
- `tools\app\Help.cs`: the launcher Help page that would carry a line about where the slider is, if the cheap outcome is the right one

## Steps

  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt -Pattern 'RaceMenu'
  ```

- [ ] Have Patrick or a tester do the one test a Claude cannot: set a hair tint in the race menu, log out, log back in and say whether it survived. (patrick)
- [ ] If it survives, this is documentation: add a line to tools\docs-app\data\help.md or the launcher Help page saying where the tint slider is, written to C# 5 if it goes in Help.cs. (claude)
- [ ] If it is lost, treat it as an appearance persistence bug worth more than the feature: start at faceMark:830-840 and at whatever writes the appearance property back, and check whether tints are round-tripped at all or only counted. (claude)
- [ ] Verify whichever path you took: the launcher compiles for the documentation outcome, the gamemode parses for the bug outcome. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check tools\gamemode.js
  ```

## Commands

- Confirms RaceMenu and its plugins are enabled, so the sliders are already there. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt -Pattern 'RaceMenu'
  ```
- Shows the doc comment and the signature, including the tints-are-counted line. (claude)


- Compiles the launcher if the answer turns out to be a line of help text. (claude)
  ```powershell

  ```

## Done when

Either the help text exists and the launcher compiles with exit code 0, or faceMark compares tint values rather than counting them and `node --check tools\gamemode.js` exits 0. The login half of the test belongs to a person and is reported back in words.

## Traps

Do not change faceMark casually: its doc comment records a real bug where a client uploaded the previous character's face on connect and the server skipped creation entirely, so making it more sensitive could reintroduce a different version of that. Do not disable or reorder any RaceMenu plugin to test, because that moves the load order. Launcher help text is C# 5: no string interpolation, no ?., no nameof, no expression-bodied members, no out var.

Find the wait it depends on and make it not. THEN ON GITHUB, the same evening: tools/voice/test-local-chat.js failed two checks on #337 ('ON a whisper reaches only the one at the elbow', 'and arrives as a whisper') and tools/voice/test-backpressure.js one on #338 ('and stops growing rather than climbing with every tick'), neither touched by the pull request, and both passed every run here and on a re-run. A red build from a flaky test holds up every merge behind it, so each needs the wait it depends on found and made deterministic (a fake clock, or waiting on the event rather than on time). 25 SEPTEMBER, TWO OF THE THREE FIXED. test-backpressure.js turned main red on runs 827 and 828, after #332 and #334, and #337 on 826: 'and stops growing' subtracted two single 250 ms reads of a queue that sits at one 0.14 MB position message, and on the Windows runner the read a second in landed just after a drain (0.00 MB). #339, merged as c640ee2, reads the largest over 1,500 ms at each end and allows one message between them; the service from before #275 still fails it (1.70 MB growing to 4.55 MB). Then test-local-chat.js failed the whisper on #337 again at 01:20: say() read who had a line after a flat 350 ms, and the whisper came 25 ms after two sockets joined and was late, not lost (the next line reached the same person, and nothing in the service holds a line back). #344, MERGED as d50af66, waits for the people a line should reach, up to 3 s, then the old 350 ms; with delivery to a new joiner made 500 ms slow in a scratch copy of the service, main's harness fails 10 checks and #344's none, and a whisper that carries too far still fails and says who heard it. Client and server change together, as one release. The client runtime is built from the fork and recorded; never patched by text.
