NEXT STEP: On a branch, prepare but do not wire into Ship: tools/app/Thornswood.csproj in classic (non-SDK) format so BuildTools MSBuild builds it with no download. TargetFrameworkVersion v4.8.1. ui.xaml as EmbeddedResource with LogicalName ui.xaml (XamlReader.Parse at runtime stays). app.ico as ApplicationIcon. The art as EmbeddedResource under the names Art.cs expects. WebView2 as Reference HintPath to tools/lib/webview2 plus EmbeddedResource, with no PackageReference, so no loose DLLs. LangVersion 5 kept until #dev decides otherwise. Build it with BuildTools MSBuild into the scratchpad and Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root <scratch>, then compare AssemblyTitle, FileVersion, ProductVersion and size. Put the measured figures in the entry so the #dev conversation starts from facts. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Needs a #dev line agreed between Patrick and Djinn: it changes the build behind the settled C# 5 rule. Djinn's machine needs VS BuildTools or the SDK. The CI step and the Ship call change only after that.

## Read first

- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:1-30`: the header: the honest reason at 5-7 ('Uses csc.exe, which is part of the .NET Framework that ships inside Windows. Nothing to install.') and the dev-install default root at 21, which exists because a hand-run build once overwrote the real install
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:46-108`: the csc probe and the reference resolution, 55 lines of it, ending in the Die on missing assemblies at 108
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:110-134 and 235`: WebView2 vendored as three DLLs and both referenced and embedded, and /resource:ui.xaml, which is parsed at runtime by XamlReader.Parse rather than compiled
- `tools\Ship.ps1 around line 253`: the single call site, so the claim of two hundred and fifty lines of reference hunting does not survive contact with the file
- `.github\workflows\build.yml`: the runner that also compiles with csc and is what turns a pull request red

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line first: this removes the only stated reason for the C# 5 rule, which is settled design in CLAUDE.md, so it belongs in the same conversation as the language-version entry. (patrick)
- [ ] Correct the figures before arguing the case: the script is 421 lines, reference hunting is 55 of them, and Ship already calls it in one line. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Content tools\Build-Launcher.ps1).Count; Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern 'Build-Launcher'
  ```
- [ ] Add tools\app\Thornswood.csproj targeting net48 with UseWPF true, keeping the same framework the in-box compiler targets today. (claude)
- [ ] Bring ui.xaml in as an EmbeddedResource with the logical name ui.xaml rather than a Page, which is the smaller change and leaves Shell.cs:221-224 and XamlReader.Parse alone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 217 -First 10 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add app.ico as ApplicationIcon, logo.png and logo-192.png as EmbeddedResource with the logical names Art.cs expects, and WebView2 as a PackageReference, keeping it embedded in the single exe. (claude)
- [ ] Keep the generated AssemblyInfo step and reduce Build-Launcher.ps1 to argument handling plus one build line, retaining the dev-install default root and the Stop-Game and Stop-Launcher calls, which are safety rather than build. (claude)
- [ ] Build both ways into different roots and compare the two exes: same AssemblyTitle, AssemblyVersion and FileVersion, and a file size within a few percent. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the GitHub build check is green on the branch, because that runner is the second machine that has to compile it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr checks
  ```

## Commands

- Gives the real length of the build script, 421 lines, against the entry's figure. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Content tools\Build-Launcher.ps1).Count
  ```
- Shows the single call site in Ship, which is one line and not two hundred and fifty. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Ship.ps1 -Pattern 'Build-Launcher'
  ```
- Returns nothing today, which is the 'no project file' half of the entry confirmed. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Include *.csproj,*.sln
  ```
- Builds the current way into the dev install, which is the baseline the new project is compared against. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- Reads the version metadata off the built exe for the side-by-side comparison. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Item C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Launcher\Thornswood.exe).VersionInfo | Select-Object FileVersion,ProductVersion,FileDescription
  ```
- Shows whether the GitHub build check is green on the branch; it queries GitHub, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr checks
  ```

## Done when

The project and the old script both produce an exe, the two report the same AssemblyTitle, AssemblyVersion and FileVersion and are within a few percent in size, and the GitHub build check is green on the branch.

## Traps

The price named in the entry is real: the SDK or build tools have to exist on Patrick's machine, Djinn's machine and the GitHub runner, and today none of the three needs anything installed. WebView2 must stay embedded in the single exe, because the updater publishes exactly one asset and SelfUpdate replaces exactly one file, so a PackageReference that emits loose DLLs would break every launcher mid-upgrade. Ship must still build into the release root, not the dev one, and C:\Thornswood-dev is not a root this repo uses: the default is C:\Thornswood-DevBuild.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/compiler-options/ What the csc options in the current script actually do, before they are replaced
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/msbuild/msbuild MSBuild, which is what a project file hands the work to
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/frameworks Target framework monikers, for pinning net48 rather than drifting
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/consume-packages/package-references-in-project-files PackageReference, and the settings that decide whether a dependency lands as a loose DLL
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/ WebView2, the one package that must stay embedded in the single exe
- https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows GitHub Actions how-tos for writing workflows, which is what .github\workflows\build.yml is

issues.title: The rule banning modern C# is a rule about the compiler, not the framework, and it costs real code
issues.body:
**Order:** 353 · **Wave:** 8 Nice to have · **Category:** Launcher code · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Old number:** 170

## Where it lives

Your PC · CLAUDE.md, settled design · tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:5-7 gives the only reason for it

## What is known

The syntax is the small part. The real win is async and await in Play, the update check, the uninstall and the character sync, which removes the nested message pump and the reason the stall-detection file exists, and is the honest fix for Windows marking the launcher as not responding. Hot paths only, not a sweep. This is settled design, so it is a #dev conversation before it is a branch MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The entry's premise is false. The rule in CLAUDE.md lists interpolation, ?., nameof, expression bodies and out var. It does not ban async. I compiled a file using async/await and Task.Run with C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\csc.exe (it reports 'version 4.8.9221.0 for C# 5'): exit 0, and the exe ran and printed 5. `grep -E 'async|await' tools/app/*.cs` returns nothing, so no code uses it and nothing stops it. The nested pump now lives only in Waiting.cs:36 and :59; Creation.cs no longer has one. Shell.cs has 8 Waiting( call sites (1255, 1623, 1913, 3684, 3726, 3770, 4080, 4545). Waiting already runs the work on the pool and keeps the window pumping (Waiting.cs:30-75), so those waits are not what Windows calls not responding. Measured: C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log (17-23 Sep) holds exactly one stall report, '2026-09-21 20:07:27 ... not responded for 5 seconds. Nothing was marked as running', which means it was not inside Waiting. It came right after a voice loop that connected and disconnected every two seconds from 20:06:47 (log lines 2771-2790). Neither a rule change nor async removes a measured stall. Whether to allow newer syntax for its own sake is entry 316's decision. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: The first clause of doneWhen is still false at HEAD c32b820, which is also origin/main. The clause says "the named hot paths use await instead of the nested pump". `grep -nE '\basync\b|\bawait\b' tools/app/*.cs` returns nothing, and the reviewer measured the same. So none of the named hot paths awaits anything: - Play (Shell.cs:3698) - CheckUpdatesBackground (Shell.cs:4282) - CheckUpdatesInPlay (Shell.cs:4487) - Uninstall.cs - the character sync (Chars.cs; there is no CharSync.cs) The nested pump is still in use: - Waiting.cs:36 creates a DispatcherFrame and Waiting.cs:59 calls Dispatcher.PushFrame. - Shell.cs still calls Waiting( at 1255, 1623, 1913, 3684, 3726, 3770, 4080 and 4545. - Stall.cs (94 lines) still exists. The entry says await would remove the reason for it. The one thing that did land is that Creation.cs is gone (3aa37ef "Pick your character at the game's main menu"). That makes one baseline step out of date. It does not finish the work. No commit in the last 250 mentions async, await, the pump, a compiler or a change to the rule. No branch does either. CLAUDE.md:78, SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:32 and .github/workflows/build.yml:4 all still say C# 5 only. The "wrong premise" argument does not make the entry stale. The entry already corrects that premise itself (step 2, and traps: "async is already available"). Its finish line is the conversion, not a rule change. The reviewer says the Waiting calls cannot cause "not responding". Waiting.cs:60-63 shows otherwise: when PushFrame throws InvalidOperationException, the window thread blocks on done.WaitOne() with no message pump. That is a real way to freeze the window, and await would remove it. The third clause, no stall line across a session, is also not shown. C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log line 2813 (21 Sep 20:07:27) is a stall report, and no session has run on converted code, because no converted code exists. What remains is the #dev conversation between Patrick and Djinn, then the conversion itself. The entry is open work (progress or blocked on that decision), not stale. NEXT STEP: Close the entry, citing the compile proof and the log measurement. Record the real finding as its own entry: on 21 Sep the voice socket connected and disconnected every two seconds, and the only launcher stall of the week followed it with nothing marked as running (launcher.log 2771-2790). If anybody still wants async for the Waiting call sites, it can be written under the current rule. That would be a Shell.cs change with a #dev line, not a rule change. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: The first part of doneWhen is not met on origin/main (c13ada9): "the named hot paths use await instead of the nested pump". A git grep of tools/app/*.cs for async or await finds nothing. So Play, CheckUpdatesBackground, CheckUpdatesInPlay, Uninstall.cs and the character sync (Chars.cs) still run synchronously. The nested pump is still there: Waiting.cs:36 creates a DispatcherFrame and Waiting.cs:59 calls Dispatcher.PushFrame. Shell.cs still has 11 lines that match "Waiting(". Stall.cs is still in the tree. The third part, no stall line across a session, has not been measured on converted code, because no converted code exists. C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log line 2813 (21 Sep 20:07:27) is a stall report. The triage's own verdict is "progress" with low confidence, not closed. Its argument that the premise is wrong (async already works under C# 5) is a case for rewording the entry. It does not make the conversion done, and the entry already says async is available. The #dev conversation between Patrick and Djinn has also not happened. The only thing that has changed is that Creation.cs no longer holds a pump, so the baseline step naming it is out of date. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: The triage found that on 21 Sep the voice socket connected and disconnected every two seconds, and that the week's only launcher stall followed it with nothing marked as running (launcher.log 2771 to 2790). That needs its own entry. It also says the question of allowing newer syntax for its own sake belongs to entry 316.

## Read first

- `CLAUDE.md:45-46`: the exact rule: 'Launcher code is C# 5 only: no string interpolation, no ?., no nameof, no expression bodied members, no out var.' async and await are not on that list
- `tools\Build-Launcher.ps1:5-7 and 46-50`: the only reason given for the rule anywhere, and the probe that finds the in-box compiler which reports itself as supporting language versions up to C# 5
- `tools\app\Waiting.cs:36-59`: the shared nested message pump, with eight call sites in Shell.cs, which is why a scoped conversion cannot make the DispatcherFrame grep return zero
- `tools\app\Stall.cs`: 94 lines that exist purely to log when the window thread stops answering, which is what the pump costs
- `tools\app\Creation.cs:405-447`: a second, independent pump that a Waiting.cs-only conversion leaves behind

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line first and do not settle it here: this is settled design in CLAUDE.md, and Shell.cs, Checks.cs, Keep.cs, Hold.cs and Updater.cs each need a line of their own because both machines touch them. (patrick)
- [ ] Correct the premise before anybody spends a day on it: async and await are C# 5, the launcher already links the Task types, and it simply has no async code today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern '\basync\b|\bawait\b'
  ```
- [ ] Correct the second premise: the in-box csc cannot be raised with a flag, so a different compiler is required, which means doing the project-file entry first. (claude)
- [ ] Record the current baseline so the finish line is honest: the nested pump lives in exactly two files today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern 'DispatcherFrame|PushFrame'
  ```
- [ ] If it is agreed, convert only the named hot paths: Shell.Play at 3380, CheckUpdatesBackground at 3989, CheckUpdatesInPlay at 4163, Uninstall.cs and CharSync.cs. (claude)
- [ ] Set the finish line to match the scope: Waiting.cs still holds a DispatcherFrame while any of its eight call sites is synchronous, so do not promise zero matches for scoped work. (claude)
- [ ] Compile clean and confirm no stall line appears in the launcher log across a session, measuring by the grep and the compile rather than by starting anything. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Returns nothing today, which is the evidence that nothing is blocking async, only that none is written. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern '\basync\b|\bawait\b'
  ```
- Returns Waiting.cs and Creation.cs today; that count is the baseline the scoped work is measured against. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern 'DispatcherFrame|PushFrame'
  ```
- Counts the call sites that keep the nested pump alive, eight in Shell.cs today, which is why zero matches is the wrong finish line. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Select-String -Path tools\app\Shell.cs -Pattern 'Waiting\(' | Measure-Object).Count
  ```
- Compiles the launcher, which after this change requires the new compiler rather than the in-box csc. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- Reads the log for a stall line, which is the measurement CLAUDE.md asks for instead of a claim. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path C:\Thornswood\Profile\launcher.log -Pattern 'stall'
  ```

## Done when

The named hot paths use await instead of the nested pump, the launcher compiles with exit code 0, and Profile\launcher.log carries no stall line across a session. Do not use a zero-match DispatcherFrame grep as the finish line for scoped work: Waiting.cs keeps its frame while any of its eight call sites is still synchronous.

## Traps

This is settled design and CLAUDE.md is explicit that a Claude does not settle it, so get the #dev line first: the problem, the approach, what it touches. The entry's largest claimed benefit rests on a false premise, since async is already available. Converting string interpolation and ?. across the launcher is a large diff with no benefit and breaks the one-fix-per-pull-request rule, so keep it to the four hot paths. A launcher that will not compile on the runner stops the whole release at the build step.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/whats-new/csharp-version-history The version history that puts async and await in C# 5, which settles the premise
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/configure-language-version How a language version is actually selected, and why a flag alone does not raise the in-box compiler
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-scenarios The async patterns the hot paths would be rewritten into
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.threading.dispatcherframe DispatcherFrame, the nested pump in Waiting.cs that await replaces
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.windows.threading.dispatcher.pushframe Dispatcher.PushFrame, and why a nested pump makes Windows call a window unresponsive
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.tasks.task Task, which the launcher already links without using

issues.title: Shell.cs is a god object by any measure
issues.body:
**Order:** 354 · **Wave:** 8 Nice to have · **Category:** Launcher code · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 171

## Where it lives

Everyone's PC · tools\app\Shell.cs, 4,417 lines, about a hundred static fields, seventy-seven methods, one wiring method of 558 lines

## What is known

Split it, do not rewrite it. The seams are already visible: Play and its unwind are a session class, the update flow is another, the uninstall is most of the way out already, and the character cards, the news list and the pack rows are three page classes. One move per pull request, which fits the repo's own one-fix-per-request rule. It is already partial, so the first move costs almost nothing MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Shell.cs is 4,790 lines now (the entry says 4,417). The partial mechanism already exists: `static partial class Shell` in Pages.cs:18, ShellOwnGame.cs:17, Stall.cs:18 and Waiting.cs:9. The pack rows block is Shell.cs:2159 to about 2395: the BuildPackRows summary, BuildPackRows at 2167, Bytes, PackRow at 2228, both CollectionCard overloads, and PackAction at 2359, about 240 lines. Its one field, packBusy (Shell.cs:82), is used nowhere else (grep hits only 2256, 2361, 2369 and 2388), so it moves with the block cleanly. SafeLog, verifyCardVisible and LinkedRow after it are not pack code and stay. Build-Launcher.ps1 globs tools/app/*.cs, so a new file needs no build change. `gh pr list --state open` is empty and origin has no djinn/ branches, so no open branch conflicts with the move. NEXT STEP: New tools/app/ShellPacks.cs declaring `static partial class Shell` with the usings the block needs. Move Shell.cs:2159 through the end of PackAction, plus the packBusy field at :82, verbatim. Change nothing inside the method bodies. Compile with `.\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root <scratchpad folder> -NoPause`, not the dev root, because Build-Launcher.ps1:177-178 stops the game and launcher running from the root it builds into. Show it is a pure move with `git diff --color-moved=zebra` and `git diff --stat`. One pull request. Then update the entry to name the next slice (the update flow, then the character cards). The god object stays open until those land. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Shell.cs is on CLAUDE.md's protected list: a #dev line first, unless Patrick asks for it himself.

## Read first

- `tools\app\HOOKUP.md`: the launcher class map, the document that says what each file is for and where a new slice belongs
- `tools\app\Shell.cs:718-750`: the page constants, PageTitles and ShowPage: the cheapest seam and the one the Add-ons entry also wants
- `tools\app\Pages.cs`: an existing `partial class Shell` file, the worked example of how a slice looks when it is done
- `tools\app\Shell.cs:76-108`: the static fields, including lines 102-108 which declare thirty-three Buttons on their own; the fields are the hard part of a move, not the methods

## Steps

- [ ] Post the #dev line first, because Shell.cs is on CLAUDE.md's protected list and both machines touch it. (patrick)
- [ ] Record the starting size so the pull request can show the move, and expect 4,417 lines. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Content tools\app\Shell.cs).Count
  ```
- [ ] Read Pages.cs first as the template, since the splitting mechanism already exists: Shell is a static partial class extended by four other files. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern 'partial class Shell'
  ```
- [ ] Add one new file under tools\app declaring `static partial class Shell` and move exactly one group into it with its fields, changing nothing else. (claude)
- [ ] Pick the group deliberately: the pack rows (BuildPackRows at 1852, PackRow at 1913, PackAction at 2044) are the most self-contained first move, the update flow and the character cards are the next two. (claude)
- [ ] Move fields between the partials rather than making anything internal or public, because moving fields between partials of the same class is free. (claude)
- [ ] Compile and confirm the diff is a pure move: same method bodies, no changed lines inside them. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```

## Commands

- Gives the line count before and after, which is how the move is shown to be real. (claude)
  ```powershell
  (Get-Content tools\app\Shell.cs).Count
  ```
- Lists the files already extending Shell, which is the proof the mechanism exists and the template to copy. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\app\*.cs -Pattern 'partial class Shell'
  ```
- Should show only the two files and a balanced move, with the same method bodies on each side. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff --stat
  ```
- Compiles the launcher; Build-Launcher globs tools\app\*.cs so a new file needs no build change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause
  ```
- Starts the branch for one move, which is one pull request. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/shell-pack-rows-move-out
  ```

## Done when

Shell.cs is smaller by the size of the slice, the new file compiles, `git diff --stat` shows only moves with no changed lines inside the method bodies, and `.\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -Root C:\Thornswood-DevBuild -NoPause` exits 0.

## Traps

Do not rewrite, move. One move per pull request, which is the repo's own rule and also what keeps the diff readable as a move. The fields are the hard part: several static fields on lines 76-108 are shared across groups that look separate, so moving a method without its field leaves a compile error pointing at the wrong file. Launcher code is C# 5 only, so any refactor reaching for expression-bodied members, nameof or out var will not compile.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/partial-type partial class, the mechanism the launcher already uses across five files
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/whats-new/csharp-version-history What C# 5 allows, which bounds what the refactor may reach for
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/desktop/wpf/controls/ The WPF controls the moved page-building methods operate on
- https://git-scm.com/docs/git-mv Keeping a move readable in the diff rather than looking like a rewrite
- https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create gh pr create --fill, the form the one-move-per-request rule takes here

issues.title: Bethesda's guards are still standing in every hold, so nobody has a reason to deal with a person
issues.body:
**Order:** 357 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 189

## Where it lives

VPS · game server and the collection · the vanilla guard records are still in the load order

## What is known

Unblocked by entry 208's decision, and it is part of that one cut rather than a separate job. Guards go with everything else that is not a trader or a transport worker. Law being people is the premise the rules page is built on, so this only works alongside entry 210 and the staff commands in entry 32; taking the guards out first and leaving nobody able to act is the one sequence that makes the world worse than it is now. Deletion is irreversible, so the surviving cast list from 206 comes first MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt (95 lines) carries Guard Dialogue Overhaul at 27, Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary at 34, Immersive Patrols II at 45 and Skyrim Unbound - GDO Patch at 89. The entry's 28 and 94 have drifted. gamemode.js:276 is the only read of DATA.holds and only reports crimeFaction. Nothing anywhere suppresses or removes a guard. The mechanisms available are the same three as in entry 320: the fork's server isDisabled binding (IsDisabledBinding.h), the thornswood-front.js client route (5b7bc6f), and an esp edit through Nexus. tools/docs-app/data/site/rules.md already promises customers that law is people. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build until the decision. Once it is made: one hold first (Whiterun), keyed off DATA.holds. Done server side with isDisabled on a timer, it goes out with Deploy-DevGamemode and logs a per-hold count. Done in the esp, it is a Nexus upload and one complete release. It ships only in the same release as entries 210 and 32. The guard placement count per hold is the same load-order reader as entry 320's cast table and belongs there. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn decide in #dev on the mechanism and on whether Populated Cities and Immersive Patrols stay in the Nexus collection. It waits on entry 320's agreed cast list, and it lands in one release with entries 210 and 32. Whether it works can only be judged by people in the game.

## Read first

- `C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt`: all 98 lines: Guard Dialogue Overhaul and its Unbound patch change guards, Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary and Immersive Patrols II add people, so the collection is pulling the other way
- `tools\gamemode.js:23`: DATA.holds, the crimeFaction map for all nine holds plus Solstheim, the only crime-adjacent thing the server knows and the key any replacement builds on
- `tools\gamemode.js:170-190`: holdOfCell and nearestCapital, how the server already answers 'which hold is this' without any new plumbing
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\rules.md`: the public rules page is built on the premise that law is people, so this is a promise already made to customers

## Steps

- [ ] Post the mechanism choice in #dev and get it agreed with Djinn before code, because guards live in Skyrim.esm and cannot be removed by dropping a plugin, which makes this a world-shaping decision rather than a fix. (patrick)
- [ ] List what the live load order actually does to guards and crowds, so the conversation starts from the real list rather than memory. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt' -Pattern 'Guard|GDO|Populated|Patrols'
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the server has no NPC suppression today by finding every place the hold map is read and seeing that the single hit only reports a crime faction rather than acting on it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "DATA.holds" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Pick one of two mechanisms and write it down: a patch in Thornswood-Content.esp that empties the guard placements per hold, or server-side suppression in gamemode.js on the existing timer pattern at :1977. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 1973 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Do one hold first, Whiterun, keyed off DATA.holds WhiterunHoldLocation crimeFaction 0x0267EA, so the effect can be judged before nine holds are changed. (claude)
- [ ] Confirm the load order is still coherent after the change, and note that the manifest check has a known false mismatch so do not redeploy on its word alone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Plugins.ps1
  ```
- [ ] Hold the branch until entry 210 and the staff powers in entry 32 are ready, and ship all three in one release. (patrick)

## Commands

- Returns four lines with their numbers: Guard Dialogue Overhaul at 28, Populated Cities Towns Villages Legendary at 34, Immersive Patrols II at 45 and Skyrim Unbound - GDO Patch at 94. GDO is in the pattern because that patch does not carry the word Guard. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path 'C:\Thornswood\Profile\Default\plugins.txt' -Pattern 'Guard|GDO|Populated|Patrols'
  ```
- Returns one line, :234, the only place DATA.holds is read. Search the bare word crimeFaction instead and git prints the whole seventy-kilobyte generated blob on line 23. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "DATA.holds" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Compares the live load order against the reference this install shipped with. Read only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Plugins.ps1
  ```
- Answers what else would have to go if the server load order dropped every light plugin, reading only each plugin's TES4 header. Read only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Show-EslCascade.ps1
  ```

## Done when

For a plugin change: Check-Plugins.ps1 reports nothing enabled that should not be and nothing missing, and the client and server plugin lists match after the release. For a server-side change: the server log shows a count of guards suppressed per hold per cycle, readable from the VPS with nobody in the world.

## Traps

Doing this alone is worse than not doing it: taking law out while nobody can act in its place leaves the world with no law at all, so entries 210 and 32 land in the same release or none do. Any plugin change moves the load order and is one complete release across server and every machine. The collection currently carries two mods whose whole job is putting more people in the world, so this work and the collection are pulling in opposite directions and that needs settling in #dev before code.

## Links

- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Creating_a_Custom_Crime_Faction how a crime faction, its jail marker and its bounty settings are actually wired, which is what the hold map points at
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Faction the Faction record and its crime tab, for reading what 0x0267EA is

issues.title: Guards, bounties and cells run by people
issues.body:
**Order:** 358 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 196

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Next · with entry 193 taking the vanilla guards out and entry 16 giving staff something to act with

## What is known

Get caught and a person decides what happens to you rather than a script deciding for them. Three rows have to land together for this to work at all: the vanilla guards out, staff with in-world powers, and this. Doing any one alone makes the world worse than it is now MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: No bounty, cell or arrest code exists. grep -i 'bounty|jail|crimeFaction|arrest|prison' over tools/gamemode.js hits only DATA.holds crimeFaction at :23, its read at :276, and the warrior comment at :4784. The entry's line numbers are stale: admins()/isAdmin() are at :19198/:19207 now, not :3096. The staff gate is still keyed off a profile id. The comments at :18745-18760 and in the tier note above rolelist() say that id is a claim the page makes about itself, and the entry covering that hole (142, identity is a number the client picks) is still open. The prerequisite rows are open too: 145 (a moderator has no powers in the game), 321 (Bethesda's guards still stand) and 320 (the NPC cut). The repo has no surviving-cast list; git grep 'cast list|traders and transport' finds nothing outside board.json:1056. The public copy already promises this: home.html:592-596 'Law with people behind it' and board.json:1715 in 'Next'. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build until the decisions land. After that: (1) a guard office in the shape entry 96 built for stewards: a list beside claims in data/property.json, named by a jarl or captain, with an isX(profileId) check like isSteward at gamemode.js:14026. (2) A per-hold bounty ledger keyed by DATA.holds crimeFaction, persisted in the same register and not a Map. (3) A cell as an arrival record (cell, desc, pos, rot) like the CHARGEN.towns rows that /tp already uses. (4) Every action logged through the block's log function. (5) tools/test-bounty.js to prove restart persistence and hold scoping with a stubbed mp. Ship it together with 321 and 145 as one release. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn have to agree the three-row plan in #dev: guards out (321/320), staff powers (145) and this one. Patrick has to decide who may set a bounty and jail somebody (a guard office under the jarl, as the steward chain works, or staff) and where the nine cells are. Entry 142's verified identity should land before any new power is keyed off a profile id.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:23`: DATA.holds, the crimeFaction id for all nine holds plus Solstheim, which is the scoping key a bounty has to be stored against
- `tools\gamemode.js:3096-3108`: admins() and isAdmin(), the entire staff gate that exists today, keyed off a profile id list with a fallback
- `tools\gamemode.js:2955-2970`: the comment explaining that a profile id is a claim the page makes about itself, which is why /restart stopped being a chat command; read it before extending the admin surface
- `tools\gamemode.js:3042-3049`: the /help handler and the admin-only /tp, the one staff action in the world today and the proof a cell is reachable
- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json:1715`: the public roadmap row this closes, so the copy and the build agree on the day it ships

## Steps

- [ ] Post the three-row plan in #dev and get it agreed with Djinn before code, naming entry 209, entry 32 and this one as a single coordinated release, because any one alone makes the world worse than it is now. (patrick)
- [ ] Read the profile id warning at tools\gamemode.js:2955-2970 and decide there and then whether the admin surface you are about to widen is safe to key off a profile id at all. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "isAdmin" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Store a bounty per character per crime faction on a server property created in ensureProperties at :304-318, using SKILL_PROPERTY's visible pattern at :306-311, not a Map, so it survives a restart. (claude)
- [ ] Add the staff actions law needs beside the existing /tp handling at :3042-3049, gated by isAdmin, and log every one through the guard() wrapper at :95 so the server log records who did what. (claude)
- [ ] Make a cell a place the server can move somebody to and hold them in, reusing the arrival record shape CHARGEN.towns already uses at :616 (cell, descriptor, position, rotation). (claude)
- [ ] Add the bounty and cell counts to the load banner at :1858-1863 and confirm the file parses. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Split the work into several small pull requests, one fix each, but plan one release that carries all three rows. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Shows every place staff permission is checked, so nothing is widened by accident. (claude)

  ```
- Parses the gamemode after the bounty and cell code lands. (claude)

  ```
- Starts one of the several small branches this needs. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/bounty-per-hold
  ```
- Opens the pull request and triggers the GitHub build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

Checkable with nobody in the world: set a bounty on a character in one hold, restart the server, read it back, confirm it did not leak into another hold's crime faction, and confirm a staff action against it appears in the server log. That proves persistence and scoping, which is the part that cannot be judged by looking.

## Traps

Doing any one of the three rows alone makes the world worse than it is now, and that is the most important line on this entry. Most Papyrus events are blocked, so vanilla crime handling cannot be leaned on and the server has to own the whole thing. The admin gate is keyed off a profile id, and the comment at :2961 records that an earlier version let anybody who opened a socket claim one, so read that before widening the surface.

## Links

- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Creating_a_Custom_Crime_Faction what a crime faction, a jail marker and a bounty are in vanilla terms, which is the model being replaced
