issues.title: Most scripts never fire, mods and vanilla alike, so anything scripted is decoration until the server implements it
issues.body:
**Order:** 359 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** change it, large · **Old number:** 178

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · every script event except the timer one is blocked; records still work, scripted behaviour does not

## What is known

Unblocking events is a server change with real risk, so the practical version is to decide per event which ones the server can safely allow and let the rest stay blocked. In the meantime the collection should not contain mods that only work through the blocked ones, which is what entries 168, 166 and 23 are THIS IS THE ANSWER TO the report that a lot of the mods in our list are just straight up not present in the game, from Patrick on 20 September. It is not the load order: all 102 plugins load, and the 42 that look missing are light plugins the load order file cannot see, measured under entry 168. They are loaded and doing nothing, which from a chair is indistinguishable from not being installed. This entry is why. Worth saying plainly to anybody who reports it, because the obvious next move is to go digging through the collection and there is nothing wrong there to find. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #237. WHAT CHANGED: Added tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py, a read-only audit. It reads every VMAD in the load order and every .pex script, loose and in the archives. It then sorts each plugin by what the fork's event blocker (FridaHooks.cpp:43-72) leaves alive: works, partial, a timer only a blocked event starts, dead, fragments only, no events, or records only. It also lists which blocked events the most plugins wait on, which is the data the per-event decision needs. The event names come from the game's own native scripts, not from a hand-typed list. tools/bsa.py had to be fixed for this: it could not read any compressed archive Skyrim Special Edition makes, because those use LZ4 and not zlib, and it read every archive whole. It now decodes LZ4 in plain Python and memory-maps archives. tools/test-papyrus-events.js proves both, with 57 checks. MEASURED: On C:\Thornswood\Game\Data, 99 plugins: - 15,204 scripts parsed, 0 unreadable. Each one parses to exactly the end of its file (the check is at tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py:294). - 147 event names, from Form, ObjectReference, Quest, ReferenceAlias, ActiveMagicEffect, the PO3 event scripts, MCM Helper, one mod's own MCM script, and OnInit. No script anywhere declares OnInit. - Plugins by result: 1 works (SkyUI_SE), 24 partial, 23 dead, 6 with a timer only a blocked event starts (Odin, Gourmet, MoreCraftableEquipment, Solitude Arena, ZIA, Triumvirate), 2 fragments only, 3 no events, 40 records only. - Blocked events by how many plugins wait on them: OnInit 37 plugins / 189 scripts, OnLoad 25, OnActivate 24 / 803 scripts, OnDeath 20, OnCellLoad 19. - VMADs: a scan of every subrecord of every record finds 26,937, the same number as reading only the first two subrecords (tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py:406-418). - bsa.py: the archive data starts 04 22 4D 18, the LZ4 frame magic, after the 4-byte length. The old zlib path failed on 10 of the 25 archives that carry scripts, and on 23 of the 47 archives under 200 MB. Where the old code could read an archive (24 of them), the new code returns identical bytes. load_strings returns identical tables for Skyrim.esm (30,301 strings), Dawnguard.esm (3,662) and Dragonborn.esm (5,282). Looking for the scripts folder across all 63 archives took 80.4 s before and 1.8 s now (tools/bsa.py:53, 145, 183). - Caprica-built .pex files (QuickLootIE) carry an object size field in the billions, so the parser no longer trusts that field (tools/Audit-PapyrusEvents.py:248). - A full audit takes about 27 s with the disk cache warm and peaks at 289 MB of memory. - Output is the same under Python 3.9 and 3.12 (-W error). - Build-DoorTable.py --check still runs on the new bsa.py: 851 of 852 buildings named, from 6 string tables. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick and Djinn (a #dev decision, because the client runtime is settled design): which events, if any, the blocker should let through. The audit's list of blocked events and its JSON (--json) are the input for that. Narrowing the blocker afterwards is a change to FridaHooks.cpp in the fork, then a client rebuild, New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1, Sync-Client.ps1 and a dev Ship, followed by a check in the game. For Patrick (the Nexus collection): take out the mods the audit calls dead, once he has read the list. In particular IcePenguinWorldMap, Immersive Weapons, Cathedral Weathers, BetterContainerControls, atlas map markers, YokuWeapons and Playable Rieklings. Worth checking in the game before anyone trusts the premise: does TrueHUD's or Precision's MCM page appear at all? Their config scripts register through OnConfigManagerReady, a mod event the audit counts as blocked. If the page appears, mod events are getting through, and the audit overcounts dead mods. For the To Do List (this run could not edit it): 1. Entry 323's text points at the deleted Patch-Client.ps1. It should point at FridaHooks.cpp and at this tool, which is the triage's own correction. 2. known.md:30-36 lists five mods, but four of them (SunHelm Survival, SunHelm Diseases, Respawn, Tavern Games) are in neither plugins.txt nor Data. The fifth, Immersive Armors (Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation.esp), comes out dead. That table is stale. 3. Thornswood-Content.esp gives the furniture record ThornswoodExecutionerChoppingBlock the script KzlChop, and that script is nowhere in Data. 4. The triage asked to check the audit against SunHelm coming out timer-driven. That cannot be done, because SunHelm is not installed.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:16-22`: the rule as customers read it: all Papyrus events except OnUpdate are blocked, records still work, scripted behaviour does not
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:30-36`: the five mods listed there as not working as installed, which is the cheap half of this entry: stop shipping mods that only work through blocked events
- `tools\Patch-Client.ps1:1-52`: the header, which records exactly what happened on 14 to 17 September when the bundle was edited by hand instead, and why nothing is hand edited any more
- `tools\Patch-Client.ps1:98,129,161,231`: the four existing blocks, each a hashtable with a Name, the exact text it expects, the text it writes and a Marker; a narrowing of the event blocker is a fifth one in the same shape
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:38-42`: 'What the server owns': position, health, inventory, equipment, death, door state, harvest state and actor values are overwritten anyway, so unblocking those events makes mods fight the server

## Steps

- [ ] Post the per-event decision in #dev before touching the bundle, because CLAUDE.md names the client bundle as settled design: it is not built here, it is patched by Patch-Client.ps1 and shipped as is. (patrick)
- [ ] Run the read-only check first so you know the four existing blocks are all present before you add a fifth. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check
  ```
- [ ] Pick exactly one event with no server-owned side effect, checked against known.md:42, and prove the round trip with that one alone rather than unblocking wholesale. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\data\known.md -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 38 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Add a fifth block to tools\Patch-Client.ps1 in the shape of the four at :98, :129, :161 and :231, with a Name, the exact expected text, the replacement and a Marker so it is idempotent. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 94 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the new block reports cleanly and that the expected text is found exactly once, since a block whose text is not found exactly once exits 1 and stops the release. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check
  ```
- [ ] Do the cheap half in a separate branch: take the mods out of the collection that only work through blocked events, which is entries 168, 166 and 23. (patrick)
- [ ] Ship the bundle change with the server and the launcher as one complete release, never on its own, and say in #dev when you take the dev feed because the last dev Ship wins. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "narrowed the papyrus event blocker to one event"
  ```

## Commands

- Reports every block as present or absent without changing the bundle. Exactly what Ship runs before a publish. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check
  ```
- Shows whether anything in this repo touches the blocker, as opposed to the bundle that is not built here. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "blockPapyrusEvents" -- tools/
  ```
- Parses the server if the event decision also changes gamemode behaviour. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Tries the change on the dev server. Say in #dev when you take the dev feed, because the last dev Ship wins. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Ship.ps1 -Channel dev "narrowed the papyrus event blocker to one event"
  ```

## Done when

.\tools\Patch-Client.ps1 -Check reports the new block as present or absent and changes nothing, and the block's expected text is found exactly once so a wrong patch fails at build time rather than in the game.

## Traps

Never hand-edit skymp5-client.js. The header of Patch-Client.ps1 records what that cost: hand edits on 14 September, a fresh build written over them on 16 September at 14:58, Keep taking the new file as ours, the 15:23 pack carrying it to everybody, and doors unlocked again on the 17th with nobody noticing. Several events the server already owns will simply be overwritten if unblocked, so unblocking those makes mods fight the server rather than work.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/events.md the sendPapyrusEvent and sendAnimationEvent hooks, what a hook can and cannot catch
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/OnUpdate_-_Form the one event still alive here, and the fact it does not fire in menu mode
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/native.md how native game functions are reached from the client side, and the warning that form references can be lost across an await
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/Patch-Client.ps1 the patch script and its history header, for linking a block in a pull request (private repo, sign in)
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/ PowerShell reference for writing the fifth block in the same style as the four

issues.title: NPCs stand still when nobody is nearby, and behave differently for two people stood beside the same enemy
issues.body:
**Order:** 360 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** Known issue · **Effort:** replace it, rewrite · **Old number:** 177

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · SkyMP has no server-side AI; an NPC is simulated by a nearby machine or not at all, and hosting changes every two seconds

## What is known

Entry 208's decision shrinks this enormously and changes what it is for. With the cast cut to traders and transport workers, there is no crowd left to simulate, so this stops being a world-scale AI problem and becomes making a dozen named characters behave properly. Server-side routines for those, and nothing else. That is a different and much smaller build than the one this row originally described, and it is now worth doing rather than deferring. Correct the known issues page either way, because it currently tells people this is permanent PART DONE 24 September, pull request #295. WHAT CHANGED: The Known Issues page (tools/docs-app/data/known.md) now has its own section for the two NPC rows, "What is decided about NPCs". The rows are unchanged and keep their SkyMP reasons. The section says there are going to be fewer NPCs: the traders you buy from and sell to stay, and so do the carriage and ferry workers. Every other NPC is to be taken out or remade, neither roadmap item has a date, and it says what is still worth reporting. It does not mention routines, errands, jobs, quests or a date. The "Limits of a shared Skyrim" lead no longer talks about NPCs. A new harness, tools/test-known-npcs.js, checks all of this. It can also be pointed at another copy of the page through the KNOWN variable. MEASURED: Live page: fetched https://thornswood.net/api/page/known on 24 Sep (HTTP 200, 4679 bytes). With line endings stripped it matches the repo copy at fe66c8c (22 Sep) byte for byte, checked against every commit that touched known.md. So nobody edited it on the site and there was nothing live to merge in. The page just has not been deployed since 22 Sep. Live still says the first group "is not going to change", and the table over the NPC rows says "They are not going to change". Main had already removed that promise in 0cb16bc (#213, entry 296), so the doc half's done line was true in the repo but not on the site. What main still did was keep both NPC rows under "Limits of a shared Skyrim" (old known.md:20-21), with a lead (old :14-15) that named two roadmap titles and never said what was decided. tools/test-known-npcs.js runs 20 checks: 20/20 pass on the change, 7 fail on HEAD c13ada9 and 9 fail on the live copy. test-known-issues.js still passes 22/22 because the NPC section's lead names the roadmap and "NPCs with their own work" on one line (new known.md:24-30). WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick: deploy the page with `.\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Docs known`. Until that runs, customers still read "not going to change". The deploy also takes #213, #216 and #243 live on this page. The build half of entry 324 has not started and should not: server-side routines for the named traders and transport workers wait on entry 320's surviving-cast list, which is not in the repo, and on someone watching a server-driven NPC in the game. Two other places still promise routines and need a decision from Patrick. On board.json's roadmap, the "NPCs with their own work" row says "Jobs, routines and errands of their own, then quests". home.html:602-603 says the same; that page belongs to entry 186. The roadmap's Done row "The world kept its people: Nobody was deleted to make room" contradicts the 17 Sep cut. The hub's own copy of the table in board.json (admin only) still lists the NPC rows under "Engine and architecture". I left it alone, as #213 did. The To Do List was not edited.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:18-19`: the two claims as customers read them, including the two-second hosting handoff, which is where the 'this is permanent' wording that entry 208 changes actually lives
- `tools\gamemode.js:1977-1995`: the online writer, the working example of a guarded setInterval that clears its previous handle on a hot reload; a routine tick copies this exact shape
- `tools\gamemode.js:95-121`: the guard() wrapper every handler goes through, which is what puts a routine's moves in the server log
- `tools\gamemode.js:1789-1810`: mp.onActivate, the only place the server answers a button press, so the only way a routine can be interacted with
- `tools\gamemode.js:170-190`: holdOfCell and nearestCapital, how a routine decides where a character belongs without new plumbing

## Steps

- [ ] Post the reshaped scope in #dev first: with the cast cut to traders and transport workers this stops being world-scale AI and becomes a dozen named characters, which is a different agreement from the one on the board. (patrick)
- [ ] Correct the known issues page in its own branch before any build, because it currently tells customers this is permanent and entry 208 decided otherwise. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/known-issues-npc-routines
  ```
- [ ] Confirm for yourself that the server has no NPC control of any kind, so you are writing a system rather than turning one on. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -niw "routine\|schedule\|package" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Wait for the cut in entries 208 and 207 to land, because fewer characters is what makes server-driven routines affordable at all. (patrick)
- [ ] Pick one hold and one shape of routine, a shopkeeper in the shop by day and the inn by night, and drive it from a guarded setInterval in gamemode.js in the shape of the writer at :1977. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 1973 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Log every move through guard() so a routine moving N actors writes N lines per cycle, then confirm the file parses. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Keep the doc fix, the routine primitive and the cast changes as three pull requests, because the roadmap already treats this as two rows and a single one called 'NPCs' is the wrong shape. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the doc-only branch, the part that is testable today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/known-issues-npc-routines
  ```
- Returns nothing at all, which is the proof. Drop the -w and the same search returns respawn and spawnPoint lines that have nothing to do with NPC behaviour. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -niw "routine\|schedule\|package" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Finds the permanence wording that has to change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\docs-app\data\known.md -Pattern 'stand still|not going to change'
  ```
- Parses the server after the routine tick lands. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```

## Done when

The doc half is done when Select-String over tools\docs-app\data\known.md no longer returns a line calling this permanent. The build half is done when the server log shows a count of actors moved per cycle, readable from the VPS with nobody in the world, and node --check .\tools\gamemode.js exits 0.

## Traps

SkyMP has no server-side AI, so this is a system to write rather than a setting to turn on. Every Papyrus event except OnUpdate is blocked, so a routine cannot be a package or a quest script and has to run on the server timer. Do not build routines before the cast is cut: the tester notes already tell people not to report standing characters, so a routine for a crowd is work that nobody asked for and nobody will see.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/native.md what the native game API reaches from script, and why form references go stale across an await
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/events.md the hooks that survive, which is the whole toolbox a routine has
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/OnUpdate_-_Form the one surviving event, and its menu-mode caveat
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Map the per-actor bookkeeping a routine needs, and why it must not be the only home for state
- https://thornswood.net the landing page that tells customers what the world is meant to feel like

issues.title: An economy with a bottom: NPCs start with gold and only have what people have spent
issues.body:
**Order:** 362 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 207

## Where it lives

Design agreed in Discord 17 September · the server already owns inventory and container contents, so it can own a purse

## What is known

Each trader starts with a purse and buys and sells against it, so coin moves between people rather than appearing. Specific goods per trader rather than a universal shop. This is the single thing that makes crafting, mining and the professions worth doing, and it is also the thing that makes entry 225's trade ships possible. It needs entry 157 first, because an economy with a floor is only as good as the server's refusal to let anybody create items PART DONE 24 September, pull request #296. WHAT CHANGED: I added one read-only harness, tools/test-one-mint.js. It checks that coin enters the world in exactly one place, purse() in the spoils block (forty gold, once per character), and that everything else only moves gold or takes it away. It runs the real purse, takeGold and trade code against a fake mp, and it still refuses a second purse after a simulated restart. It lists every function that writes a pack with the reason each one cannot make a coin, parses every descriptor in the gamemode, pins every addItem caller to a table in the file, and reads tools/recipes.json for any recipe that makes gold. There is no gamemode change and no trader build, as the task limited it. MEASURED: Measured on 24 Sep against HEAD c13ada9. Writers: 13 functions write a pack, 14 writes in all (WRITERS list in tools/test-one-mint.js). Only spoils/purse and property/takeGold name gold. Descriptors: 27,778 in the gamemode and none is Gold001 (base 0xF in Skyrim.esm). Gold is written by number only in five places: gamemode.js:4298, 15314, 16356, 23077 and 23113. addItem: all 16 calls take their descriptor out of a table. Recipes: 4,529 in tools/recipes.json and none makes gold; 21 (Immersive Armors and Immersive Weapons) take gold as an input. Papyrus: the gamemode has no 'AddItem' Papyrus call. The entry's own check, Select-String 'f:Skyrim\.esm', matches 1,099 descriptors on 228 lines (frost salts 3ad5f among them) and none of them is gold, so its "four line numbers" were never gold lines. Proof that the harness catches a mint: it fails on gamemode.js from c87da23^ (class kits gave gold as "f:Skyrim.esm": 26 fails) and from 4dc2ccf^ (no purse: 14 fails). It also fails on six changed copies of today's file: a purse kept in a Map (fails the restart check), a new function writing gold into a pack, "f:Skyrim.esm" in ITEMS, moveById not taking the pile away, addItem(mp.getDescFromId(15)), and takeGold(-fee). Found and measured in a scratch run: moveById(A, A, 40 gold) turns 100 into 140, and trade.begin(A, A) returns '' and opens a trade. Two things block it today: the /trade command refuses yourself ("That is you.", gamemode.js:18991), and okB can never be set on a trade with one person on both sides, so swap() is never reached. The harness checks both. takeGold (gamemode.js:15814) does not refuse a negative amount; its only caller, gamemode.js:15847-15848, passes JOB_FEE or NOTICE_FEE (30 and 20), which the harness pins. WHAT IS LEFT: For Patrick with Djinn, before any code: the trader design in #dev (which NPCs trade, what each sells, starting purses, prices, and how a person buys, which has to be a Thornswood panel because the barter menu cannot be driven). Then for a Claude: a trader purse stored as a property on the trader, one function that moves coin and never creates it, per-trader stock keyed by base descriptor, and the trader count in the load banner. That code will change the WRITERS and ADD_FROM lists in tools/test-one-mint.js, which is the intended gate. To Do List corrections (not made; this run may not edit the list): the entry's readFirst is stale. CHARGEN.classes no longer carries 75/100/200/400 purses; the purse is PURSE=40 in the spoils block at gamemode.js:16597. The done-when check 'f:Skyrim\.esm' matches no gold at all; replace it with `node tools\test-one-mint.js`. New findings to record: trade.begin does not refuse a === b and moveById(a, a) doubles the pile it moves (safe today only because of the two guards above), and takeGold accepts a negative amount. Each is a one-line guard in gamemode.js if Patrick wants them closed.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:367-395`: addItem and takeItem, the two functions every coin and every good has to pass through; today they create and destroy with no ledger and no record of origin
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:38-42`: 'What the server owns', which is the authority that inventory and container contents really are server side, so a server-owned purse is possible at all
- `tools\gamemode.js:616`: CHARGEN.classes: every trade already hands out a starting purse, 75 gold for most, 100 for the smith, 200 for the bard, 400 for the merchant, and that is the money supply's only source today
- `tools\gamemode.js:302-333`: SKILL_PROPERTY, ensureProperties and getSkills, the per-character property pattern a purse must copy instead of a Map
- `tools\gamemode.js:351-352`: the lastUse Map, the pattern to avoid: in-memory state that resets on every restart, which for a purse is a money printer on a schedule

## Steps

- [ ] Post the economy design in #dev and get it agreed with Djinn before code, and settle there whether the starting purses at :616 stay, because they are the only mint in the world today. (patrick)
- [ ] Close entry 157 first, because an economy with a floor is only as good as the server's refusal to let anybody create items; see for yourself that addItem has no accounting. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "addItem\|takeItem" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Give each trader a purse as a per-reference number on a server property created in ensureProperties at :304-318, following SKILL_PROPERTY at :306-311 and never a Map. (claude)
- [ ] Route every buy and sell through one function that moves coin out of one side and into the other and never creates it, so there is exactly one mint and it has a name. (claude)
- [ ] Hold specific goods per trader as a table keyed by trader base descriptor in the same generated-constant style as STATIONS at :24, rather than a universal shop. (claude)
- [ ] Add the trader count to the load banner at :1858-1863, parse the file, then list the lines that mention the gold descriptor and confirm no code path outside the mint function hands gold out. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'f:Skyrim\.esm' | ForEach-Object { $_.LineNumber }
  ```
- [ ] Ship it as one complete release with the launcher and game files, and open the pull request for one fix at a time. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Lists every item movement so you can see which ones will need to go through the mint. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "addItem\|takeItem" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Prints four line numbers, 23, 26, 616 and 1690. Line 616 is CHARGEN.classes and the starting purses, the only mint today. It prints numbers rather than lines because three of the four are generated one-line blobs and line 23 alone is seventy kilobytes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern 'f:Skyrim\.esm' | ForEach-Object { $_.LineNumber }
  ```
- Parses the server after the purse property and the mint function land. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Starts the branch for the purse alone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/trader-purse
  ```
- Opens the pull request and triggers the GitHub build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

node --check .\tools\gamemode.js exits 0, the purse property appears in ensureProperties at tools\gamemode.js:304-318, the load banner at :1858-1863 prints the trader count, and git grep for the gold descriptor shows every call going through the one mint function.

## Traps

A purse held in a Map resets to full on every server update, which is a money printer on a schedule; store it on the actor property. The server owning inventory means a mod that hands out gold on somebody's own machine simply loses the gold, already documented for Tavern Games at known.md:35, so expect confused reports rather than exploits. This is a large build touching the file that ships to the VPS, so it goes out as one complete release and needs a line in #dev first.

## Links

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Map the Map type the cooldown uses, and why a purse must not live in one
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp the SkyMP project, for what the server owns and what it cannot reach
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Activator the record kind a trader stall or counter is, for the activation route a sale runs through
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html node --check, the parse gate before any deploy
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/docs-app/data/known.md the published list of what the server owns, for quoting in the pull request (private repo, sign in)

issues.title: Carriages and ferries are paid for, and the fare goes to the Hold's court
issues.body:
**Order:** 363 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Old number:** 208

## Where it lives

Design agreed in Discord 17 September · the driver is a worker of the Hold the carriage sits in

## What is known

The first piece of public money in the world, which is what makes a Keep's court a thing with a budget rather than a title. It also gives travel a cost, which is what stops the map feeling small. Needs the purse from entry 214 and a per-Hold treasury to pay into MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: No fare or travel code: grep -i 'carriage|ferry|fare' over tools/gamemode.js returns only data rows. The collection carries Carriage and Ferry Travel Overhaul (tools/news-public.json:27; tools/JKS-SKYRIM.md:16, CFTO-JK-Patch.esp). The per-hold treasury the entry says is missing now exists as the steward-designated drop box: a funds[hold] ledger (gamemode.js:15024) persisted beside claims, boxCmd :15073, putIn :15127, and test-coffers.js passes 38. So a fare into the court needs no NPC purse, and the three-entry chain the entry describes is shorter than it says. The comment at about :15080-15095 records an open decision on which one is the treasury, the ledger or the chest. The claim of nine towns against ten was not re-measured here because the entry is blocked on design. NEXT STEP: After the decisions: one function that takes the fare from the pack (never creating coin), credits funds[holdOfCell or nearestCapital] the way a notice fee is credited, and moves the person to an arrival record in the CHARGEN.towns shape. A route table in the load banner. tools/test-fare.js proves the coin arithmetic and hold resolution with a stubbed mp. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick has to decide whether the server owns carriage travel (replacing CFTO's driver) or charges alongside it, the fares and routes, and which hold's box gets the fare. The ledger-or-chest treasury question from entry 96 also needs his answer. A person has to try a CFTO carriage on dev to see what it does now under the event blocker and server-owned inventory.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:170-190`: holdOfCell and nearestCapital, which already answer 'whose court does this carriage belong to', so more than half the plumbing exists
- `tools\gamemode.js:255-292`: the death and respawn routing that uses those two, including the comment at :279-283 about interior cells being measured from the hold capital rather than the origin
- `tools\gamemode.js:367-395`: addItem and takeItem, since a fare is a coin movement and has to go the same route as everything else
- `tools\gamemode.js:616`: CHARGEN.towns, nine towns each with a cell, a descriptor, a position and a rotation: a carriage destination is exactly that shape of record
- `lore\accord.md`: a Hold's court is a lore object before it is a data structure, and the two should agree on the day this ships

## Steps

- [ ] Post the public-money design in #dev and get it agreed, because a Hold treasury is a new kind of thing in the world rather than a fix. (patrick)
- [ ] Wait for the purse in entry 214, which itself waits on entry 157; this is third in a chain of three and starting early means writing a fare that mints coin. (patrick)
- [ ] Count the towns yourself before sizing a route table, because the comment at :625 says ten towns and CHARGEN.towns holds nine. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '"town":"(\w+)"' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches } | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value } | Sort-Object -Unique
  ```
- [ ] Write one function that takes a fare with takeItem, adds it to a per-hold treasury number resolved with holdOfCell or nearestCapital, and moves the person using the CHARGEN.towns arrival shape. (claude)
- [ ] Store the treasury on a server property created in ensureProperties at :304-318, not in a Map, for the same restart reason as entry 214. (claude)
- [ ] Add the carriage route count and the hold count to the load banner at :1858-1863 and parse the file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Open the pull request for the fare function alone, with the treasury and the routes as separate reviews if they grow. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Returns the two function definitions at :170 and :180, the hold resolution a fare reuses. Searching holdToDestination instead prints the whole generated blob on line 23. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "function holdOfCell\|function nearestCapital" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Prints the nine town names actually in CHARGEN.towns, against the comment that claims ten. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '"town":"(\w+)"' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches } | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value } | Sort-Object -Unique
  ```
- Parses the server after the fare function lands. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Starts the branch for the fare alone. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/carriage-fare-to-the-court
  ```
- Opens the pull request and triggers the GitHub build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

node --check .\tools\gamemode.js exits 0 and the load banner at :1858-1863 prints the carriage route count and the hold count, so a deploy log line shows the table loaded with nobody in the world. The fare arithmetic can be checked offline by extracting the fare function into something callable, since it is pure coin movement.

## Traps

Nine towns exist in CHARGEN.towns, not ten, despite the comment at :625 saying ten, so do not size a carriage network off that comment. The hold mapping deliberately treats an interior cell's coordinates as local and measures from the hold capital instead, per the comment at :279-283; copy the routing without that and interior stops get measured against the origin. This depends on entry 214, which depends on entry 157, so it is third in a chain of three.

## Links

- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim:Carriage vanilla carriage routes and the 20 and 50 gold fares, a sane starting point for pricing
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Faction the hold factions the crime map already names, for keeping a treasury keyed the same way
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/lore/accord.md the Accord, which decides what a Hold's court is allowed to be (private repo, sign in)
- https://thornswood.net the public setting, so the lore and the fare land saying the same thing
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html node --check, the parse gate before any deploy

issues.title: Property you actually own
issues.body:
**Order:** 365 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 193

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Being built now · nothing in tools\gamemode.js for plots or a steward

## What is known

Buy it, furnish it, lock it, defend it, with land inside a hold meaning a steward you speak with rather than a menu you buy from. Needs entry 218 underneath it to be worth anything. The landing page already sells this, which is entry 74, so either this ships or that copy comes down MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Built, in the shape settled with Patrick on 21 Sep, and tracked for its playtest on entry 96 ('built and on dev, waiting on a test'). The property block starts at gamemode.js:13728. It has claim at the door (claim() :14251), the deed as the title (DEED 15493 named per instance, holdsDeed), a server register in data/property.json (:13959 writes claims, stewards and boxes), lapse, jarl and stewards (:13978-14030), /evict, rent (rentCmd :15212), the drop box (:15073) and boards. Commits 1100de7, 0a6eed0, ec61435, 7473e3b, f84506f. Harnesses all pass: test-deed-title 15/15, test-offices 26/26, test-coffers 38/38, test-boards 20/20. Two leftovers belong to other entries. home.html:586-588 still says 'Go to the hold's steward, pay for the plot', which contradicts free claiming (entry 186). board.json:1608-1609 says 'Buy it, furnish it' (roadmap copy, same fix). It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: The property code is on main, but the entry's doneWhen has never been shown true, and the entry's own condition about the landing page is still open. 1. doneWhen is a persistence check: set an owner through the gamemode path, restart the server, read it back, and confirm ownership and lock state survived. Nothing in the repo does that. The reviewer cites four harnesses (test-deed-title, test-offices, test-coffers, test-boards). Each one lifts a single decision out of the gamemode. None calls load() or save(), and none reads data/property.json after a reload. The same is true of test-locks, test-key-chain and test-cut-key. I ran all seven and they pass (15, 26, 38, 20, 16, 35 and 18), and node --check passes, but none of them covers this. The comment in load() at gamemode.js about lines 13903-13920 ("THREE FIELDS THAT WERE WRITTEN AND NEVER READ BACK, AND A RESTART ATE ALL THREE ... every deploy and every restart silently unlocked every locked house") shows that this exact failure shipped once. It was found by reading, not by a test. I wrote a throwaway script in the scratchpad that lifts registerPath/load/save, saves a claim with by=42 and locked=true, and loads it back. Both values come back, so the code half is probably right now. But no committed harness proves it, and nothing records a dev server restart with a claim on it, which is what doneWhen asks for. 2. It has not shipped past dev. Entry 96, "Property offices, rent, the drop box and the boards: built and on dev, waiting on a test", is still done:false. Its doneWhen needs somebody in the world: claim, lock, mold, thief with key, thief with deed, eviction, board fees. 3. The entry says "either this ships or that copy comes down", and step 6 says to do it in the same release. Neither has happened. home.html:587-588 still says "Go to the hold's steward, pay for the plot, then build it, furnish it and defend it". That contradicts the 21 Sep design (claiming costs nothing, done at the door). board.json:1608-1609 still has the roadmap row r4rm "done": false, "Buy it, furnish it, lock it...". Entry 186 does not cover this. It only moves the "Property worth owning" card into a being-built block, and its first step leaves that decision to Patrick. It does not rewrite the copy to match free claiming. 4. The deed is record 15493 (0x3C85) in Thornswood-Content.esp, added in 1100de7. That plugin reaches clients only through the Nexus collection. Commit 29beece (#200) confirms the plugin on main (141442 bytes, bb687a7) is not on the collection yet. Nothing here shows whether the deed record's own revision ever was. 5. Minor: the comment at gamemode.js:17284-17285 still says "A home and its farm are one claim in the design and they are two claims in the code today", which contradicts b3b46ba. What is left: a committed harness, or a dev restart check, that proves ownership and lock survive a reload. Entry 96's playtest. Patrick's decision on the home.html and roadmap copy, going out in the same release. NEXT STEP: Close as a duplicate of entry 96. Add a line to entry 186 that home.html:587 and board.json:1609 describe buying a plot while claiming is free. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: None for this entry. The playtest on dev is entry 96's. NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: The property code is on main (origin/main c13ada9), and load() in tools/gamemode.js now rebuilds the lock with `locked: !!c.locked` (about line 14186, inside the load() that starts near 14151, with the register at data/property.json, line 14139). But nobody has shown the doneWhen is true. It asks for this: set an owner on a plot through the gamemode path, restart the server, read it back, and confirm the owner and the lock survived. No committed harness does that. test-deed-title.js:54 and test-offices.js:72 start from an empty claims object in memory. test-locks.js:279 builds its claim by hand. None of the three calls load() or save(), and none reads property.json back after a second boot. The only harness that restarts is test-unpin.js, which covers the boards for entry 331. Its boot() at :132 sets `var claims = {};` and never reloads it, so it does not test claims. The load() comment at gamemode.js (about 14172-14181) records that this exact failure already shipped once: every restart unlocked every locked house. Nothing records a dev server restart with a claim on it either, and entry 96, where this is waiting on a playtest, is still open. The entry's own condition, "either this ships or that copy comes down, in the same release", is also still open. home.html:590-591 still says "Go to the hold's steward, pay for the plot", which contradicts the free claim at the door settled on 21 Sep. board.json:1608 still lists "Property you actually own" as not done. What is left: a committed restart harness for claims, like the one test-unpin does for notices, that saves a claim with an owner and locked set to true, boots again from disk, and checks both come back. Also Patrick's decision on the landing page and roadmap copy, going out with the release. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: The triage wants a line on entry 186 saying that home.html:590-591 and board.json:1608-1609 describe paying for a plot while claiming is free. Entry 186 only moves the card, so this copy fix belongs on entry 329 or on 186 as a new step. The comment at gamemode.js about line 17284 that says a home and its farm are two claims in the code is out of date since b3b46ba and should go on whichever entry covers home-and-farm claims.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json:1608`: the roadmap row 'Property you actually own' in the Being built now column, the promise as written
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:38-42`: the server already owns container contents, door open state and inventory, which is the half of a plot that is genuinely available
- `tools\gamemode.js:1789-1810`: mp.onActivate, because a steward cannot be a quest script and has to be a server answer to an activation
- `tools\gamemode.js:302-345`: the per-character property pattern, since a plot is an owner id and a lock state attached to a world reference and it has to survive a restart
- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html`: the landing page that already sells this, which is entry 74: either this ships or that copy comes down

## Steps

- [ ] Post the plot and steward design in #dev and get it agreed, because it adds records to Thornswood-Content.esp and therefore moves the load order for everybody. (patrick)
- [ ] Do not start before entry 218, because a plot without a real key is a menu with extra steps; confirm the gamemode has nothing for plots today. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -ni "plot\|steward\|deed" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Hold a plot server side as a world reference plus an owner character id plus a lock, on a property created in ensureProperties at :304-318 rather than in a Map. (claude)
- [ ] Make the steward a server answer to mp.onActivate at :1789 rather than a vanilla menu, since every Papyrus event except OnUpdate is blocked. (claude)
- [ ] Add the plot count to the load banner at :1858-1863 and parse the file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Either ship this or take the landing page copy down in the same release, because shipping half of it is the worst option: customers will go looking. (patrick)
- [ ] Open the pull request for the ownership property alone, and keep the Creation Kit records as a separate one. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Shows the server has nothing for plots or stewards to extend. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -ni "plot\|steward\|deed" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Returns :430, :480 and :481, the landing page copy that promises a steward and a plot. A looser pattern such as property or own returns fifty-three lines of markup. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\docs-app\public\home.html -Pattern 'steward|pay for the plot'
  ```
- Parses the server after the ownership property lands. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Checks the load order after any Thornswood-Content.esp change. Read only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Plugins.ps1
  ```

## Done when

Checkable with nobody in the world: set an owner on a plot reference through the gamemode path, restart the server, read it back, and confirm the ownership and the lock state survived. That proves the persistence half, which is the half that is actually hard.

## Traps

This needs entry 218 underneath it to be worth anything, and the internal board agrees by keeping them as one row. A steward cannot be a quest script because every Papyrus event except OnUpdate is blocked, so it has to be server side on activation. Adding plot and steward records to Thornswood-Content.esp moves that plugin's checksum and is one complete release across server and every machine.

## Links

- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Activator the record kind a steward's counter or a plot marker is, and what its activate text controls
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/OnActivate_-_ObjectReference what vanilla activation would have done, which the server now has to do itself
- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:Mod_File_Format the record and GRUP layout, for judging what adding plot records does to the plugin
- https://thornswood.net the landing page as a customer reads it, which already sells this feature
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/docs-app/public/home.html the source of that copy, for changing it in the same release (private repo, sign in)

issues.title: The climb through the ranks
issues.body:
**Order:** 368 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 197

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Next · the professions, halves and classes are in character creation and vanilla levelling is off; the server already zeroes skill experience

## What is known

Half-built and unreachable, which the roadmap does not say: gamemode.js has sixteen manual books mapped to four tracks at tiers one to four, tierOf() reads them, and the salt quarry and the charcoal kiln gate on them, but entry 20 establishes that nobody can obtain a manual, so every one of those gates refuses everybody. The tracks are also inherited from Keizaal and keyed on crafting verbs rather than on professions, halves or classes, so they cannot be pointed at this design without being re-keyed. What is missing is the other direction: nothing ties a track to the profession or the half you chose, and the other professions have no track at all. Levelling is switched off, so this replaces progression rather than fighting it. Somebody who plays for a month currently has nothing to show for it, which is the quietest reason people stop STALE IN PART, 21 September: this entry rests on the sixteen manual books and tierOf reading them, and the whole manual mechanic was removed tonight. What survives of it is the question of where a rank actually comes from, which is entry 33. Re-read it against the gamemode before working from it. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Everything this entry is built on has been removed. d1418f5 'Rank comes from working the trade, and no book moves it' took out MANUALS, mp.onReadBook, getSkills, setSkill and the manual ladder. 5d1f3f0 took the sixteen writs out of the plugin. git grep 'tierOf|MANUALS|"track":' on tools/gamemode.js returns nothing, and the four track literals are gone. Ranks are keyed on the five classes and the eight professions' halves (gamemode.js:11079-11107), not on crafting verbs. Work raises a rank: creditWork 12185 -> addWork 12120 -> rankUp 12036, which also gives tree points and mage spell points. Every class and half has a way to earn credit: mine 1974/3026, woodwright 3332, charburner 3409, a warrior's half on a kill 4807 (added by 6a417e8), harvest 5845, fish 5934, loot 6030/6716, any crafted half 9958, farm 13194/13376, and mage schools through feedSchools. Recipes are gated by rank at 9521. The K panel draws progress (16395-16409). Harnesses test-social 66/0 and test-recipeless-craft 26/0 pass. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: The reviewer is right about the code. On main (HEAD c32b820 = main = origin/main), `node --check tools/gamemode.js` exits 0. `git grep 'tierOf|MANUALS|"track":|onReadBook|getSkills|setSkill'` returns nothing. The literal track grep finds only `whatBench.indexOf('alchemy')` at gamemode.js:9723, which is a bench name and not a track. tools/thornswood-src is gone. Ranks are now earned by work: creditWork 12185 calls addWork 12120, which calls rankUp 12036, and each rank also gives a tree point and a mage spell point. Every class and half gets credit, including alchemist and enchanter through recipelessCraft at 9790-9803 and warrior through a kill at 4807. So the manual, track and tierOf clauses of doneWhen are superseded. The last clause of doneWhen is not true: "classes.md and the board row describe the same system". Step 7 gives its purpose: "so the page and the code stop disagreeing". That update never happened. (1) The board row this entry exists for is still unchanged. It is tools/docs-app/data/board.json:1705-1706, row r14rm, in the "Next" column (1636), with done:false. It still reads "What is missing is the climb: four ranks, and what each one opens inside your own half and nowhere else", which the code now contradicts. board.json was last committed in 6a4a212 at 11:08 on 20 Sep. That is before a96a22f (progression, 22:19 on 20 Sep) and before d1418f5 (rank from work, 21 Sep). No other To Do entry owns this row. (2) tools/docs-app/data/site/classes.md:396-400 still says "The ranks, the master perks, apprenticeship and spending points in the tree are being built now". Ranks earned by work and tree points to spend now exist in the code. classes.md was last committed in 077268f at 11:32 on 21 Sep, before d1418f5 at 12:16. (3) The master perks the page promises are still only names. Each perk key (masterchemist, grandchef, mastercraft, twinsouls, masterweaver, mastercarver, warlord) appears exactly once in gamemode.js, in the PROFESSIONS table at 11093-11107, and no code acts on any of them. So "what each rank opens" is not fully built, whatever the copy says. Minor: a stale comment is left at gamemode.js:12179 ("A manual read is worth several at once"). Not checked, because this pass may not contact the VPS: whether the rank-from-work gamemode is running on the live server, and whether the live site's board copy was edited there, since Deploy-Docs does not overwrite board.json without -Boards. What is left: rewrite or tick board row r14rm and the "While it is being built" section of classes.md so they match the code. Then run Deploy-Docs -Site, plus Deploy-Docs -Boards for board.json, which overwrites the live board. That is page work that can be done now, not a closed entry. NEXT STEP: Close it. Two things are left and belong elsewhere. (1) The eight Master perks are only names in PROFESSIONS (gamemode.js:11092-11107; each perk key appears once in the file), and apprenticeship beyond the sister-half Master check at 12044-12048 is not built. Both belong to the rulebook entry (54). (2) The public copy still says the climb is missing: the live roadmap row r14rm, and classes.md:394-400 ('The ranks ... are being built now'). classes.md is a repo edit plus Deploy-Docs -Site. r14rm has to be edited on the site board, not with Deploy-Docs -Boards. Put both under the public copy entries (184/186). NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: The code side is done or no longer applies. On origin/main (c13ada9), git grep for tierOf, MANUALS and "track": in tools/gamemode.js returns nothing, because the manual system was removed on 21 Sep, and rank now comes from work (creditWork, addWork, rankUp). So the clauses about the track grep and the load banner's track count no longer apply. The last clause of doneWhen is still not met: "classes.md and the board row describe the same system". Board row r14rm (tools/docs-app/data/board.json:1700-1706 on main) is still done:false and still reads "What is missing is the climb: four ranks, and what each one opens". tools/docs-app/data/site/classes.md:399-400 still says "The ranks, the master perks, apprenticeship and spending points in the tree are being built now". That contradicts classes.md:369 ("Rank comes from doing the work") and the code, which already earns ranks and hands out tree points. Master perks exist only as names in the PROFESSIONS table, and apprenticeship past the Master check is not built, so the page and the code still disagree. Nobody has changed the public copy since the rank-from-work commit d1418f5. The entry stays open as page work: rewrite r14rm and the "While it is being built" section, then Deploy-Docs -Site, with the board change made on the live board. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: The eight Master perks exist only as names in PROFESSIONS, and apprenticeship past the sister-half Master check is not built. Both belong on the rulebook entry (54). The stale comment at gamemode.js:12179 ("A manual read is worth several at once") can be fixed under the same entry.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:296-345`: the whole skill tracks section on two screens: MANUALS, SKILL_PROPERTY, ensureProperties, getSkills, setSkill at :334 and tierOf at :342
- `tools\gamemode.js:402-430`: mineSalt refusing at :404 on mining tier below one and burnCharcoal at :424 on woodcutter tier below one, the two gates that currently refuse everybody
- `tools\gamemode.js:616`: CHARGEN.classes, the sixteen trade keys a track has to be re-keyed onto: warrior, hunter, mage, smith, miner, woodworker, alchemist, bard, cook, enchanter, farmer, fisher, merchant, priest, scholar, thief
- `tools\thornswood-src\README.md:20-31`: MANUALS at gamemode.js:25 is generated from manuals.json, and the README tells a stranger to edit body.js, so a change made only in gamemode.js drifts from its source
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md`: the published promise of what professions, halves and classes do, which the build has to match or the page has to change

## Steps

- [ ] Post the re-key in #dev and get it agreed with Djinn before code, because this is a roadmap feature and CLAUDE.md requires the problem, the approach and what it touches to be agreed first. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm the tracks really are inherited rather than designed here by listing the four track names and comparing them against the sixteen trade keys. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '"track":"(\w+)"' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches } | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value } | Sort-Object -Unique
  ```
- [ ] Add a TRACK_OF_TRADE map beside MANUALS in tools\gamemode.js that names a track per trade key from CHARGEN.classes, so a track belongs to who somebody chose to be rather than to a crafting verb. (claude)
- [ ] Change tierOf(actorId, track) callers to resolve the track from the stored trade, keeping the literal form for mineSalt and burnCharcoal so nothing breaks in the same commit. (claude)
- [ ] Decide and write down the source of a tier: either keep manuals and make them obtainable, which is entry 20, or add one new award function beside setSkill at :334. (patrick)
- [ ] Add the track count to the load banner at :1858-1863, parse the file, then run the stubbed harness after repointing its hardcoded PLUGIN path at tools\thornswood-src\test.js:2. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Update tools\docs-app\data\site\classes.md and the board row in the same release so the page and the code stop disagreeing, and keep the re-key, the manual fix and any new professions as three pull requests. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Commands

- Lists the four track names inside the generated MANUALS blob: alchemy, mining, smithing, woodcutter. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '"track":"(\w+)"' -AllMatches | ForEach-Object { $_.Matches } | ForEach-Object { $_.Groups[1].Value } | Sort-Object -Unique
  ```
- Today this returns the two tierOf callers at :403 and :423. After the re-key it should return only the new map. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "'mining'\|'smithing'\|'woodcutter'\|'alchemy'" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Parses the server after the track map lands. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Drives the real gamemode against a stubbed mp. Repoint PLUGIN at test.js:2 first; it is a Linux path and the harness has not been touched since its only commit. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node .\tools\thornswood-src\test.js
  ```
- Opens the pull request and triggers the GitHub build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

node --check .\tools\gamemode.js exits 0, the load banner at tools\gamemode.js:1858-1863 prints the track count, the git grep for the four literal track names returns only the new map instead of today's two tierOf callers at :403 and :423, and classes.md and the board row describe the same system.

## Traps

Entry 20 is a hard prerequisite: every tier gate currently refuses everybody because no manual can be obtained, so a re-key alone changes nothing anybody can see. The recipe editor ids in Thornswood-Content.esp still carry the Kzl prefix, so anything here that looks deliberate may be another server's decision that nobody on this project ever made. node --check only proves the file parses, so use the stubbed harness for anything that matters, and do not touch tools\app\Creation.cs in the same branch without a line in #dev.

issues.title: A professions menu in game is a smaller build than it looks, and the client cannot currently see its own profession
issues.body:
**Order:** 370 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Old number:** 223

## Where it lives

VPS · game server · tools\gamemode.js:312-317 marks the chargen property not visible to its owner · Everyone's PC · the emote wheel already draws a ring and reports a click, and the authenticated socket, the loopback command queue and the reply-to-one-person route are all in production

## What is known

The transport and the renderer are done, so the menu itself is the easy half. What is missing is anything to show: entry 220 is the rank, entry 211 the crafting gates. Flip the property to visible and print the profession on login to prove the route, then build the menu once there is a system behind it. Building the menu first produces a screen that displays two words and a blank MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The client can already see its own profession, through a different property than the one the entry names. CHAR_PROPERTY 'thornswoodCharacter' (gamemode.js:16333) is created with isVisibleByOwner: true and an updateOwner script (16968-16974). That script pushes the panel view (profession, half, class, ranks, progress, recipe book) into window.thornswoodSkills.setData (16957-16963). The professions menu the entry calls future work already exists: the K panel, tools/ts-ui/thornswood-skills.js, header lines 1-30, with progress lines at :58-76. It was built in e46c14f and 077268f, and its progress fields are at gamemode.js:16373-16409. CHARGEN_PROPERTY (3465, made at 339-344 with isVisibleByOwner: false) holds creation-flow state, and nothing needs it on the client, so flipping it proves nothing new. The emote wheel is built: tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-emotes.js is deployed in C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins. It looked finished, and a second reader showed why it is not: The reviewer is right about the main point, but the entry is not fully closed. What checks out (on main at c32b820): - The client can see its own profession through a different property. CHAR_PROPERTY 'thornswoodCharacter' is at tools/gamemode.js:16333. It is registered with isVisibleByOwner: true and an updateOwner script at :16969-16974, and that script calls window.thornswoodSkills.setData at :16959. - forPanel at :16809-16881 sends the profession, class, half, ranks, work, progress and the recipe book. - The K panel, tools/ts-ui/thornswood-skills.js, is on main (last changed in 580f828, #117). It is also in C:\Thornswood\Game\Data\Platform\UI\thornswood-skills.js, dated Sep 22 22:29. The emote wheel is built and deployed. - The plan to flip CHARGEN_PROPERTY and add a login notify has been overtaken by this. The menu the entry deferred now exists. What is still not true: 1. The doneWhen, taken literally, is not met. CHARGEN_PROPERTY is still isVisibleByOwner: false at tools/gamemode.js:339-340, no notify prints the profession at login, and there is no diff for either. The doneWhen also names SKILL_PROPERTY, which no longer exists in the file (git grep finds nothing). It needs rewording, not a checkmark. 2. The follow-up the entry names was never done. Step 6 says to take the stale emote wheel row off tools/docs-app/data/board.json. That row is still there at :1751-1753: "c17rm": "Emote wheel", "c18rm": "Wanted since the start, never started". A second row at :228-229 says "Emote wheel" / "Not investigated". git log shows board.json has not changed since 6a4a212. 3. Some characters still cannot see their own trade. A character whose old trade was bard, merchant, priest, scholar or thief keeps it on the hidden chargen property: gamemode.js:16321-16326, and migrate() at :17054-17055 logs "left on the old property, nothing chosen here". Those clients see no profession. That decision belongs to entry 6. Suggested classification: - The profession-visibility part and the menu part are stale. - Removing the two board.json rows is fixable. It needs .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1, and possibly -Site depending on how the board is served; I did not check which. - Visibility for the old trades should go on entry 6. NEXT STEP: Close it. One piece of residue: the stale roadmap row 'Emote wheel: Wanted since the start, never started' (board.json Later r21rm, around line 1752). The Open row r27 'Emote wheel: Not investigated' at :228 needs a person to decide what it meant. Both live on the site's editable board, so the fix is a site edit and not a repo deploy. Deploy-Docs -Boards would overwrite everything typed into the board on the site (Deploy-Docs.ps1:18-19, 196-200). NOT CLOSED, 24 September. The triage said this could be closed; a second reader told to refute that found a part of doneWhen still unmet: The doneWhen is not met on main (c13ada9). CHARGEN_PROPERTY is still made with isVisibleByOwner: false at tools/gamemode.js:395-396. No notify at login prints the profession, and there is no diff for either change. SKILL_PROPERTY, the property the doneWhen compares against, no longer exists in the file. The triage is right that most of the purpose was reached another way. CHAR_PROPERTY 'thornswoodCharacter' (gamemode.js:16700) is registered with isVisibleByOwner: true and an updateOwner script at :17336-17340, which calls window.thornswoodSkills.setData (:17328), and the K panel exists. Even so, the title's claim that the client cannot see its own profession still holds for some characters. A character whose old trade has no home in the rulebook keeps it on the hidden chargen property: migrate() logs 'left on the old property, nothing chosen here' at :17422, and that client is shown no profession. Step 6 of the entry was never done either. tools/docs-app/data/board.json still has 'Emote wheel' / 'Not investigated' at :228-229 and 'Emote wheel' / 'Wanted since the start, never started' at :1752-1753, although the wheel is built. The entry should be rewritten, not closed: drop the chargen flip and add the board cleanup and the old trades. SEPARATE FROM THIS ENTRY: Entry 6 should get the characters whose old trade (bard, merchant, priest, scholar, thief) is left on the hidden chargen property and never reaches the client (gamemode.js:17422). The two stale 'Emote wheel' rows on the site's board (board.json:228 and :1752) should be removed by editing the board on the site, not by running Deploy-Docs -Boards, which would overwrite what people typed there.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:304-318`: ensureProperties: SKILL_PROPERTY at :306-311 is created with isVisibleByOwner: true and CHARGEN_PROPERTY at :312-317 with false, four lines apart, and the fix is that one word
- `tools\gamemode.js:122-160`: notify() at :122 is the reply-to-one-person route and say() at :140 posts over loopback to the chat socket at :148; the proof of the round trip uses notify
- `tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-emotes.js:127-131`: OPEN_KEY, PAGE_KEY, CLOSE_KEY and the rest: the wheel is real and built, so a professions menu is this renderer pointed at different data
- `tools\ts-ui\thornswood-bridge.js:138-150`: the CEF comment and the 400ms guard, the trap underneath both the chat and the wheel, which any new page inherits
- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json`: the Later column still carries an 'Emote wheel' row saying it was never started, which is stale and should come down in passing

## Steps

- [ ] Check in #dev that nothing in the chargen state is meant to stay hidden from the client before flipping its visibility, because the property carries character creation state. (patrick)
- [ ] Start the branch for the one-word change, then set isVisibleByOwner to true at tools\gamemode.js:313 so CHARGEN_PROPERTY matches SKILL_PROPERTY at :307, and change nothing else. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/chargen-property-visible-to-its-owner
  ```
- [ ] Add one notify() call where login is handled that prints the person's own profession back to them, so the round trip is proven without any UI work. (claude)
- [ ] Confirm the diff is the single word plus the notify call and that the file parses. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Budget for a full server restart rather than a hot reload, because mp.makeProperty sits in a try/catch at :304-318 that swallows the second call and keeps the old visibility. (patrick)
- [ ] Take the stale 'Emote wheel, never started' row off the Later column of tools\docs-app\data\board.json in the same pass, since the wheel is plainly built. (claude)
- [ ] Stop there. Build the menu only once entry 220 gives a rank worth showing and entry 211 gives crafting gates worth listing, or you ship a screen with two words and a blank. (patrick)

## Commands

- Starts the one-word branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/chargen-property-visible-to-its-owner
  ```
- Shows both makeProperty blocks side by side so the difference is the one word. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n "isVisibleByOwner" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Confirms the change is the single word plus the notify call and nothing else. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff
  ```
- Parses the server after the flag change. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Opens the pull request and triggers the GitHub build check. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  gh pr create --fill
  ```

## Done when

node --check .\tools\gamemode.js exits 0 and git diff shows the single word at tools\gamemode.js:313 plus the notify call. Offline, the property is now created with the same visibility as SKILL_PROPERTY at :307, which is the property the skill system already relies on reaching the client. The login message itself needs a tester in the game, which is not a Claude's to run.

## Traps

mp.makeProperty is wrapped in a try/catch at :304-318 with the comment 'already made, or made by a previous load. harmless.', so flipping the flag may not take effect until the server actually restarts and a hot reload will silently keep the old visibility. Do not conclude the change failed. Building the menu before entries 220 and 209 produces a screen showing two words and a blank, which is the entry's own warning and is worth taking literally.

## Links

- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp the SkyMP project, for what a server property's visibility flags actually control
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/events.md the hooks the client side has, for how the wheel and any new menu receive input
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON the shape the property is serialised as between server and client
- https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html node --check, the one offline gate on this change
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/gamemode.js the gamemode in the repo, for linking line 313 in the pull request (private repo, sign in)

issues.title: Dungeons worth going into
issues.body:
**Order:** 371 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 198

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Next

## What is known

Places built to be cleared by a group, with something at the end that was worth the walk. Worth holding until entry 212 is further along, because a dungeon full of NPCs that stand still when nobody is nearby is a corridor MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: There is nothing to extend: git grep -ni 'dungeon|encounter' on tools/gamemode.js finds only two comments about disconnects (19174, 19458) and the building-name table. Worse, Patrick's own later rules rule out the obvious design. b3b46ba: 'all weapons, armour, tools, and gold are not spawned in the world at all ... unless made by someone', so a reward at the end of a dungeon cannot be world loot. b133fa7: nothing comes back except things that grow, so a dungeon cannot reset through the engine. The NPC decision (entry 320) keeps only traders and transport. tools/docs-app/data/tests.md:222 tells testers not to report 'NPCs stand still when nobody is near them'. New dungeon cells would mean new plugin records, which only reach people through a Nexus upload. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build yet. The first step is Patrick's one-dungeon slice: which cell, who or what is in it given the NPC cut, what the reward is given that nothing spawns, and how it resets given that nothing comes back. After that, code goes through the routes that exist: mp.onActivate, addItem and takeItem at gamemode.js:1251/1265, and the load banner. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick has to design the slice (enemies, reward, reset) against his own rules in b3b46ba and b133fa7 and the NPC cut (entry 320). Standing NPCs need the NPC routine work. Anything that feels right in play needs a tester in the game.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json:1675`: the roadmap row 'Dungeons worth going into' in the Next column, the exact promise the public page makes
- `tools\docs-app\data\known.md:38-42`: the server owning position, inventory, container contents and door state decides what a dungeon can even be here
- `tools\gamemode.js:1789-1810`: mp.onActivate, the only place the server answers a button press, and therefore the shape every dungeon interaction has to take
- `tools\gamemode.js:367-395`: addItem and takeItem, the only route for anything handed over at the end of it
- `tools\docs-app\data\tests.md:162`: testers are already told not to report standing characters, so a dungeon built today would be a corridor of statues and they have been told that is expected

## Steps

- [ ] Write the one-dungeon vertical slice in #dev before a branch exists, naming the cell, the spawn source, the reward source and the reset rule, each pointing at an existing mechanism in tools\gamemode.js by line number. (patrick)
- [ ] Hold it until entry 212 is further along, because the cast cut and server-driven routines are what stop a dungeon being a corridor. (patrick)
- [ ] Confirm for yourself there is nothing to extend: the server has no dungeon, encounter or group content of any kind. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -ni "dungeon\|encounter\|loot" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] Keep the slice inside the two routes that work: mp.onActivate at :1789 for anything somebody presses, and the addItem and takeItem pair at :367-395 for anything handed over. (claude)
- [ ] Do not plan on vanilla dungeon scripts, levelled lists or quest stages, because known.md:32 records that a poll on a timer is the one script type still running here. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\docs-app\data\known.md -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 28 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] When code starts, add the dungeon count to the load banner at :1858-1863 and parse the file. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- [ ] If the slice needs new cells, check the load order after the plugin change and batch it with the other load order movers into one complete release. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Plugins.ps1
  ```

## Commands

- Shows the server has nothing for group content, so this is a build from zero. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -ni "dungeon\|encounter\|loot" -- tools/gamemode.js
  ```
- Shows what testers have already been told to expect, which the slice has to work around. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path .\tools\docs-app\data\tests.md -Pattern 'Do not report'
  ```
- Parses the server once the slice has code in it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  node --check .\tools\gamemode.js
  ```
- Checks the load order after any new dungeon plugin. Read only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Plugins.ps1
  ```

## Done when

Nothing is testable without the game until code exists, so the checkable milestone is the design: a written slice in #dev naming the cell, the spawn source, the reward source and the reset rule, each pointing at an existing mechanism in tools\gamemode.js by line number. When code starts, node --check .\tools\gamemode.js plus a new count in the load banner at :1858-1863 is the first proof the data loaded.

## Traps

Entry 212 is a real blocker: the tester notes already tell people not to report standing characters, so a dungeon built now is a corridor of statues and nobody will report it. Vanilla quest and dungeon scripts do not run, so anything built on them is dead on arrival. A new plugin for dungeon cells moves the load order, which makes every machine and the server mismatch at once, so it ships as one complete release batched with the other movers.

## Links

- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/Activator the record kind every pressable thing in a dungeon is
- https://ck.uesp.net/wiki/OnActivate_-_ObjectReference the vanilla event that does not fire here, so the server has to answer instead
- https://github.com/skyrim-multiplayer/skymp/blob/main/docs/skyrim_platform/native.md what the native API reaches for spawning and moving actors
- https://en.uesp.net/wiki/Skyrim_Mod:Mod_File_Format the record layout, for judging what new dungeon cells do to the plugin
- https://thornswood.net the public roadmap this row is promised on

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Next · Skyrim has a coastline and nothing on it

## What is known

Needs an economy that holds, which needs entry 157, because a cargo worth robbing is a cargo worth creating out of nothing while nobody is watching MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: git grep -niw 'cargo|ferry' on tools/gamemode.js finds nothing but the building-name table. 'Treasury' shows up only in the drop box comments (15071, 15092, 19655). addItem and takeItem (gamemode.js:1251, 1265; 23 call sites) keep no ledger. Patrick's rule in b3b46ba (nothing is spawned in the world unless someone made it) means a cargo cannot be created by the server, which is exactly the trap the entry names. The traders-with-purses entry and the NPC cut (320) are not built, so there is no trader to fill a ship and no sailor to crew one. NEXT STEP: Nothing to build yet. Patrick decides where a cargo's goods come from under the nothing-spawns rule, and who or what moves a ship given the NPC cut. After that, it follows the entry's shape: a server-owned container whose contents came out of someone's pack, a route between vanilla port cells so no plugin is needed, and robbing through the normal activate and inventory path. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's economy and NPC design first: traders' purses, the NPC cut (320), and a sourcing rule that fits b3b46ba. Whether a ship reads as a ship in play needs a person in the game.

## Read first

- `tools\gamemode.js:367-395`: addItem begins at :367 and takeItem at :381, ending at :395; any cargo worth robbing is created by these two and they have no ledger, no audit and no check on where a count came from

## Steps

- [ ] When the economy exists, shape a cargo as a container the server owns whose contents came out of somebody's purse, a ship as a scheduled move of that container between two named cells, and robbing as the ordinary activation and inventory route. (claude)
- [ ] Use vanilla port cells for the locations, because that needs no new plugin and no load order movement, which is the one thing in this row's favour. (claude)
- [ ] Add the route count to the load banner at :1858-1863 when code starts, and parse the file. (claude)

  ```
- [ ] If you do add a plugin for custom ship references, batch it with the other load order movers and ship one complete release. (claude)

  ```

The honest done-when today is that entry 214 has shipped and git grep -n "addItem\|takeItem" -- tools/gamemode.js shows every call going through a function that records where the coin or goods came from. Until that is true there is nothing here to test.

Building this before the economy has a floor writes exactly the bug the row warns about: cargo generated from nothing while nobody is watching.
