issues.title: The Free Skyrim Trading Company replaces the East Empire Company
issues.body:
**Order:** 374 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 209

## Where it lives

Design agreed in Discord 17 September · lore\ and the site's world page set the Empire as gone under the Accord

## What is known

An imperial trading company standing in a free Skyrim fifty years after the Empire left is the kind of detail people notice, and the fix is lore plus records rather than systems. It hangs off entry 214 for anything it trades, and it belongs in the world page and the lore folder on the same day it goes in game so the three do not drift MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The entry's first step is wrong: there IS an East Empire reference in this repo, just not in lore or on the site. git grep -in 'East Empire' -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site returns nothing (exit 1). But the server's generated BUILDING_NAME (gamemode.js:9217, built by tools/Build-DoorTable.py:417-422 from tools/doors.json:3344, :4653) names '16777:Skyrim.esm' 'East Empire Company', and two doors in The Great City of Solitude.esp 'EEC Warehouse West' (10574) and 'EEC Warehouse East' (fd2b). The server uses those names in claim and deed messages. The canon already makes room for a replacement. accord.md Article the Third (:33-38) allows the Empire one embassy at Solitude and 'no other house, fort, or station', so the EEC could not have kept its docks. Article the Second (:22-30) keeps the ports open. history.md:71, repeated at world.md:71, says 'The Empire wanted the province. It got a warehouse.' The new company has to be reconciled with that line. Patrick's 21 September drop box design already names 'Free Skyrim Trading Company payment' going into a hold's box (gamemode.js:14998-15001). NEXT STEP: Can do now: on a branch, draft a Free Skyrim Trading Company section in lore\history.md (or a new lore\ file) and the matching paragraph in tools\docs-app\data\site\world.md in the same commit. Build it on Articles 2 and 3 and on how history.md:71 reads. Check it with git grep -in 'Free Skyrim Trading' and a local render (THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL=1 node tools\docs-app\server.js). Leave it unmerged until Patrick confirms it matches what was agreed in Discord on 17 September; none of that agreement is in the repo. Keep the in-game half as a separate PR. Do not rename the three BUILDING_NAME entries on the server alone: the game's own door prompt would still say East Empire. Renaming the cells and factions is a plugin change and goes through a Nexus upload. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick confirms the 17 September Discord design: who founded the company, when, and what it took over. Then he or Claude runs Deploy-Docs -Site. In-game records need traders' purses and a Nexus upload of Thornswood-Content.esp.

## Read first

- `lore\accord.md`: the White Harbour Accord, which establishes what the Empire leaving actually means here; a replacement company has to be consistent with its nine articles
- `lore\history.md`: the fifty-year timeline the company's takeover has to sit on
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\world.md`: the public world page people read before they join, the second of the three places this has to be kept in step
- `tools\gamemode.js:616`: CHARGEN.classes already carries a merchant trade with a 400 gold purse, which is the only trading machinery in the world today

## Steps

- [ ] Do not go looking for an East Empire Company reference to change in this repo, because there is not one; the clash is with vanilla Skyrim content, so the work is entirely additive. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -in "East Empire" -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site
  ```
- [ ] Do the writing first and the records later, because the writing is the deliverable and the records depend on entry 214. (claude)

- [ ] Add the Free Skyrim Trading Company to lore\ as its own file or a section of an existing one, saying what it took over and from whom, written to the standard of what is already there. (claude)
- [ ] Add the matching paragraph to tools\docs-app\data\site\world.md in the same commit, so the two cannot drift. (claude)
- [ ] Read the result locally before it goes anywhere, binding to loopback so port 3001 does not become a plain HTTP way past the certificate. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL = '1'; node .\tools\docs-app\server.js
  ```
- [ ] Confirm both files changed in the same commit. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff --stat
  ```
- [ ] Hand the site deploy to Patrick, and leave in-game trader records until traders have purses. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Commands

- Returns nothing, which proves the work is additive rather than a correction. (claude)
  ```powershell

  ```
- Starts the lore and world page branch, one fix. (claude)

- Publishes the site pages to the VPS. This one talks to the box, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)

## Done when

git grep -in "Free Skyrim Trading" -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site returns hits in both places, git diff --stat shows both files changed in the same commit, and the local site run with THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL=1 renders the world page correctly with nothing deployed.

## Traps

Deploy-Docs.ps1 talks to the VPS, so a Claude shows the command and Patrick runs it. Nothing here moves the load order until in-game records appear, which is the one reason this can ship ahead of the systems it names; keep the lore and the records as two pull requests.

issues.title: The Thalmor never signed the Accord, so there is a war to have
issues.body:
**Order:** 375 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** World · **Effort:** build it, large · **Old number:** 210

## Where it lives

Design agreed in Discord 17 September · remnant roleplay plus staged war events, and outside forces that answer to what the Kingdom's people decide

## What is known

This is the thing that gives the world a direction that is not a person's own story, and events are the cheapest way to make a server feel run rather than hosted. It needs staff able to act in the world first, which is entry 32, and somewhere to announce it, which is entry 150. Write the lore before the systems, because the lore is the part that is already good here MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: git grep -in 'never signed' -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site returns nothing (exit 1). The canon already covers half of the idea. The Accord is between Skyrim and the Empire only (history.md:59-67), so the Thalmor never signed it simply because they were never a party. accord.md Article the Fifth (:59-66) makes the Aldmeri Dominion an enemy of both. history.md:43-55, repeated in world.md, already establishes the Remnant, which is the entry's 'remnant roleplay'. But history.md:50-51 (and world.md:50-51) says 'There is no Dominion order to retake it and no fleet coming', and a staged war against an outside force contradicts that unless it is reworded. The entry's accord.md:133 reference does not exist; the file is 128 lines. On the staff side, /tp, /give and /spawn exist since 648cf88, and 0c6eaef posts server changes to the news feed. NEXT STEP: Can do now: write a short analysis for the #dev post that names the conflict with history.md:50-51 and the two readings (the Dominion as the outside force, or the Remnant escalating). Once Patrick and Djinn pick one, draft the lore addition next to history.md:24-55 and the matching world.md paragraph in one commit, on a branch, checked with the grep and a local render, and left unmerged until they agree. Staged events stay a separate PR: they need event tooling for staff, beyond /tp and /give, and people in the game to run them. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick and Djinn choose the war's direction in #dev (the entry's own first step), including whether history.md:50-51 changes. Then comes the Deploy-Docs -Site run. Staged events need staff event tooling and people in the game.

## Read first

- `lore\accord.md`: the whole premise is that the Thalmor never signed it, so the text of the Accord's nine articles decides what that leaves open
- `lore\history.md`: the fifty-year timeline a war has to fit into
- `tools\docs-app\data\site\world.md`: the public version of the setting, which is what people read before they decide whether to join
- `tools\gamemode.js:122-160`: notify() at :122 and say() at :140 are the only two ways the server speaks to people, so they are the announcement route a staged event would eventually use

## Steps

- [ ] Post the direction in #dev and get it agreed with Djinn before any writing, because this sets where the world is going rather than fixing something. (patrick)
- [ ] Start the branch, then add the Thalmor position on the Accord to lore\ beside what is already written at lore\history.md:24-37 and lore\accord.md:133, saying plainly what they did not sign and what that leaves open. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/thalmor-never-signed
  ```
- [ ] Update tools\docs-app\data\site\world.md in the same commit so the public setting matches on the same day. (claude)
- [ ] Read the result locally, binding to loopback because server.js:35-38 says port 3001 otherwise stays open as a plain HTTP way past the certificate. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL = '1'; node .\tools\docs-app\server.js
  ```
- [ ] Confirm both files landed in one commit. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff --stat
  ```
- [ ] Do not build staged events before entry 32 gives staff in-world powers, because an event nobody can run is a promise the server cannot keep. (patrick)
- [ ] When events do come, use the routes that already exist, notify() at gamemode.js:122 and say() at :140, plus somewhere to announce it from entry 150. (claude)
  ```powershell
  Select-String -Path tools\gamemode.js -Pattern '^' | Select-Object -Skip 118 -First 7 | Format-Table LineNumber, Line -AutoSize
  ```
- [ ] Hand the site deploy to Patrick and keep lore and systems as separate pull requests. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Commands

- Starts the lore and world page branch. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git checkout -b patrick/thalmor-never-signed
  ```
- Shows the seven places the Thalmor are already written about, in lore\accord.md, lore\history.md and the world page, which the new document has to agree with rather than repeat. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -in "Thalmor" -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site
  ```
- Runs the site locally on 127.0.0.1 only, using the variable server.js asks for. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL = '1'; node .\tools\docs-app\server.js
  ```
- Returns nothing today, so it is a real before-and-after check: once the writing is in it should return hits in both the lore folder and the world page. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -in "never signed" -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site
  ```
- Confirms both files changed in the same commit. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff --stat
  ```
- Publishes the site pages to the VPS. This one talks to the box, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Done when

The Thalmor document exists under lore\, the world page paragraph exists, git grep -in "never signed" -- lore tools/docs-app/data/site returns hits in both places (it returns nothing today), and git diff --stat shows both files in the same commit. issues.title: Switch between servers from the launcher
issues.body:
**Order:** 376 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** Launcher · **Effort:** build it, large · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 201

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Later · the own-game-folder work, Keep, Hold and the parking of other servers' plugins are most of the machinery already

## What is known

One button for Thornswood, another roleplay server, or your own Skyrim, with nothing overwriting anything. This is further along than the roadmap suggests: the own folder design settled on 17 September is the hard half. It also makes the whole class of other-server contamination bugs go away rather than being defended against MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The entry's premise is out of date. djinn/own-game-folder merged as PR #1 (9c1629c) and went out as 1.1.75 (56af203 'Thornswood runs from its own Skyrim, never a shared one'). The branch no longer exists: `git branch -a` lists no origin/djinn/own-game-folder, so steps 1-2 (git log/diff of that branch) cannot run. What is left of the feature goes against a settled decision. CLAUDE.md:52 and SECOND-DEVELOPER.md:185 say 'nothing here supports another server's install' (Patrick, 20 Sep). tools/app/Keep.cs:36-42 already describes the switch the own folder gives: 'switching between servers is pressing Play in whichever launcher you want, with Vortex never touched', and the Steam copy is left alone. The public roadmap still promises it: tools/docs-app/data/board.json:1742, row r20rm, 'Switch between servers from the launcher' / 'One button for Thornswood, another RP server, or your own Skyrim'. Nothing in tools/app or tools/ui.xaml is a server selector; grep for select/switch/serverList found only the foreign-file machinery (Checks.cs:145-390, OwnGame.cs:671 Foreign). NEXT STEP: No code. Patrick picks one of two: (a) close it as superseded. The own folder already means nothing overwrites anything, and a button that starts another server's install is what the 20 Sep decision ruled out. Mark board.json row r20rm done or remove it, and correct the entry. (b) Re-scope it, which is a few lines in #dev between Patrick and Djinn before any code, because it would touch Keep.cs, Hold.cs, OwnGame.cs and the 20 Sep decision. If (b), the entry's steps need rewriting anyway: they point at a branch that no longer exists. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's decision: close as superseded by the own game folder and the 20 Sep decision, or re-scope through #dev with Djinn. The board row r20rm on the public roadmap changes either way.

## Read first

- `CLAUDE.md`: the 'Settled design, not up for a quiet rewrite' section: the own-game-folder decision, what is hard linked, what is copied, and the rule that the two shapes must not be mixed in one release
- `tools\New-GameFolder.ps1:1-40`: the whole built-folder machinery this feature would be a second caller of, including what is left out and why big files are hard links
- `tools\Ship-Rules.ps1:99-152`: how another server's files are classified: anything in Data\Platform\Plugins that is not thornswood-*.js or the patched skymp5-client.js is theirs, and OwnGame.Foreign is the launcher half to change alongside it
- `tools\app\Keep.cs`: how files are put back before Play and other servers' plugins are parked; on the do-not-edit-without-#dev list
- `tools\app\Hold.cs`: how Thornswood's files are held open read only while the game runs; also on the do-not-edit-without-#dev list

## Steps

- [ ] Read the open branch before writing anything, because the feature is a user interface over what that branch builds and cannot start until it is merged. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch && git log origin/djinn/own-game-folder --oneline
  ```
- [ ] See what that branch actually touches, so you know which files the selector would sit on top of. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff main...origin/djinn/own-game-folder --stat
  ```
- [ ] Post in #dev before any code, because CLAUDE.md is explicit that the two shapes must not be mixed in one release and a half-merged state is worse than either. (patrick)
- [ ] Once the branch is on main, build the feature as a per-server folder produced by New-GameFolder.ps1, a selector in tools\ui.xaml, and Keep and Hold pointed at whichever folder is selected. (claude)
- [ ] Do not write a wrapper script around the launcher and do not move anything by hand in Data\Platform: CLAUDE.md forbids both by name. (claude)
- [ ] Compile the launcher into the dev build the way the GitHub check does, and never start it. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- [ ] Check the controls wiring against the XAML after adding a selector, which is the read-only check for exactly that. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Controls.ps1
  ```

## Commands

- Shows what the open branch has done so far, which is the hard half of this feature. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git fetch && git log origin/djinn/own-game-folder --oneline
  ```
- Shows which files that branch touches, so the selector is designed onto real code. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git diff main...origin/djinn/own-game-folder --stat
  ```
- Compiles the launcher with the .NET Framework csc into C:\Thornswood-DevBuild. It does not start the launcher. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause
  ```
- Checks that every control named in tools\ui.xaml is wired in the app. Read only. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Controls.ps1
  ```
- Read-only report on what another server's launcher has done to the game folder, which is the problem this feature removes. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Why-Keizaal.ps1
  ```

## Done when

Before the branch lands, the checkable step is reading it: git diff main...origin/djinn/own-game-folder --stat prints a file list you have gone through. After it lands, .\tools\Build-Launcher.ps1 -NoPause produces Thornswood.exe, .\tools\Check-Controls.ps1 reports every control wired, and the GitHub build check on the pull request is green.

## Traps

This is blocked on a branch rather than on code. CLAUDE.md is explicit that until djinn/own-game-folder is on main what ships is the Steam copy with Vortex, and the two shapes must not be mixed in one release, so a half-merged state is worse than either. Keep.cs and Hold.cs both need a line in #dev before an edit, and launcher code is C# 5 only. Do not lean on Check-Manifest.ps1 as the verification step: it compares the server's filtered plugin list against the client's unfiltered one, so it reports a mismatch that is not there and ends by advising a redeploy of a server that is already correct.

## Links

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/ PowerShell reference for reading New-GameFolder.ps1 and Ship-Rules.ps1 before extending them
- https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rebase how to bring a long-running branch up to main without pushing over it
- https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create gh pr create and --fill, the form this repo opens reviews with
- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/whats-new/csharp-version-history what arrived after C# 5, the exact list the launcher may not use
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/New-GameFolder.ps1 the folder machinery this feature would be a second caller of (private repo, sign in)

issues.title: Site themes: colours, fonts and weight a person sets once and the site remembers
issues.body:
**Order:** 377 · **Wave:** 9 The world · **Category:** Website · **Effort:** build it, medium · **Needs:** server · **Old number:** 203

## Where it lives

Roadmap, Later

## What is known

Genuinely last. The site's design is already one of the best things the project has, and entries 134 and 133 change how it is served, so building a theme system first means building it twice MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Measured the surface. tools/docs-app/public/home.html:62 has a :root with 11 colour tokens and 4 font tokens. tools/docs-app/public/index.html:17 has its own :root with 16 colour tokens and 3 font tokens, and the names differ (--night/--page vs --ink/--text). Hex literals: 23 in home.html and 35 in index.html, so about 12 and 19 sit outside :root. There are also 18 and 15 rgba() literals. A theme that only redefines :root would leave all of those unthemed. index.html:665-671 already has remember(), a localStorage helper wrapped in try/catch that can be reused. There are two roadmap rows: board.json:1131 s7r7 'Site themes and a screenshot gallery' ('Your default stays the default') and board.json:1782 r25rm 'Make the site yours'. The entry waits on 'entries 134 and 133', and those numbers no longer mean anything: old 134 is now entry 222 (the new-box runbook, nothing to do with serving), and no current entry carries old 133. The entry's deploy command is also wrong. public\*.html goes with plain .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 (Deploy-Docs.ps1:137-145 sends everything in public\), and -Site covers data\site markdown. NEXT STEP: Once Patrick says build it: (1) move every hard-coded hex and rgba in home.html and index.html into :root tokens, a visual no-op, and check it by rendering locally under $env:THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL='1'. (2) Give each theme a small :root[data-theme=...] block that redefines only the tokens, including font and weight tokens. (3) Add a picker on both pages, stored through the existing remember() helper, and apply it before first paint so the page does not flash. (4) Fix the entry: deploy with .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 (no -Site), and drop the dead 133/134 dependency or re-point it. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick decides whether it is built now (the entry calls it 'genuinely last'), which row it closes (s7r7 bundles a screenshot gallery, r25rm does not), and which palettes, fonts and weights are offered. The design is his.

## Read first

- `tools\docs-app\public\home.html:33`: the :root block that holds the palette, plus the layout, the navigation and the roadmap renderer at :666-694, which is where a theme system would live
- `tools\docs-app\public\index.html:17`: a second :root block of its own, so a theme defined only in home.html leaves this page unthemed and the eighty-line estimate covers half the surface
- `tools\docs-app\server.js:34-43`: PORT, BIND and ROOT, including the comment that port 3001 stays open as a plain HTTP way past the certificate unless THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL is 1
- `tools\docs-app\data\board.json:1782`: the Later row is 'Make the site yours', not 'Site themes'; there is a separate string at board.json:1131 that also bundles a screenshot gallery, so decide which row you are closing

## Steps

- [ ] Do not build it yet. Settle in #dev which row this closes, because the Later column row is 'Make the site yours' and a separate string bundles a screenshot gallery with it. (patrick)
- [ ] Wait for entries 134 and 133, which change how the site is served, or the selector and the serving layer get written twice. (patrick)
- [ ] When it is time, define the palette as CSS custom properties on :root in both tools\docs-app\public\home.html:33 and tools\docs-app\public\index.html:17, not just one of them. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n ":root{" -- tools/docs-app/public
  ```
- [ ] Give each theme a small block that redefines those properties, and remember the choice in localStorage wrapped in try/catch so a browser with storage blocked still renders. (claude)
- [ ] Run the site locally with the loopback variable the file itself asks for, open it, switch theme, reload, and confirm the choice survived. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL = '1'; node .\tools\docs-app\server.js
  ```
- [ ] Confirm the working tree holds only the two public pages you meant to change, because the real publish is a VPS script and is not a Claude's to run. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git status
  ```
- [ ] Hand the deploy to Patrick when the change is agreed. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Commands

- Shows both root blocks, so a theme is not defined on half the site. (claude)
  ```powershell
  git grep -n ":root{" -- tools/docs-app/public
  ```
- Serves the site on 127.0.0.1 only. Without the variable, server.js binds 0.0.0.0 and port 3001 becomes a plain HTTP way past the certificate. (claude)
  ```powershell
  $env:THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL = '1'; node .\tools\docs-app\server.js
  ```
- Read-only site check that does not reach the box. (claude)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Check-Site.ps1 -NoSsh
  ```
- Publishes the site to the VPS. This one talks to the box, so Patrick runs it. (patrick)
  ```powershell
  .\tools\Deploy-Docs.ps1 -Site
  ```

## Done when

Testable entirely locally with no game and no VPS: the site runs under THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL=1, both public pages pick up the theme, switching and reloading keeps the choice, and git status shows nothing deployed. The real publish stays with Patrick.

## Traps

server.js binds 0.0.0.0 unless THORNSWOOD_DOCS_LOCAL is 1, and the comment at :35-37 says why that matters, so a local run without the variable opens the machine. A theme defined only in home.html leaves index.html unthemed, because each has its own :root block. The site's design is already one of the strongest things the project has, so a theme system that lets somebody pick a worse version of it is a real cost, not just a build cost.

## Links

- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Using_CSS_custom_properties how to declare and redefine custom properties on :root, which is the whole mechanism
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage localStorage and the SecurityError it throws when storage is blocked, which is why the read goes in a try/catch
- https://nodejs.org/api/http.html the module the site server is built on, for reading the bind logic before running it
- https://thornswood.net the live site, the design a theme system has to avoid making worse
- https://github.com/EvilPatrick06/Thornswood/blob/main/tools/docs-app/server.js the server source and its bind comment (private repo, sign in)

issues.title: Instruments, bows, arrows and fishing poles are listed at the forge, and the bench is in the plugin
issues.body:
**Order:** 381 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Mods · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

the COBJ records of Skyrim.esm and the collection · tools\recipes.json · Thornswood-Content.esp would carry the overrides

## What is known

PATRICK, 23 September: "Instruments are made at the forge for some reason when that’s supposed to be a woodworkers job", then "Same with fishing poles", "And bows and arrows", and "And not in the forge". MEASURED, and the ownership is already right: instruments are Woodworker/Woodwright (3 recipes), bows are Woodworker (76), arrows are Woodworker (21 of 23). A smith who tries one is refused by mp.onCraft today. WHAT IS WRONG IS WHERE THEY ARE LISTED: the bench is the BNAM keyword on the COBJ record, which is Bethesda’s CraftingSmithingForge, and no amount of server code moves a menu entry. Fixing it means override records in Thornswood-Content.esp pointing those recipes at a woodworking bench, which is plugin work in xEdit and a collection revision, not a script. THE SMALLER HALF THAT IS SCRIPT WORK: spears are owned by Smith today and Patrick said "Spears should also be woodworkers" (22 rows, e.g. Steel Nordic Spear, Iron Hunter’s Spear), and 22 plain-clothes rows are Smith/Platewright when he said "there are clothes in the forge as well which doesn’t make sense just regular tailor clothes". Both are rules in Build-RecipeTable.ps1.  MEASURED AGAIN 23 September, after the spears went out as pull request 192. The OWNERSHIP half of this is finished: a Steel Nordic Spear and an Iron Hunter’s Spear are Woodworker/Woodwright, and so is the Lute. THE LISTING HALF IS UNTOUCHED AND IS THE WHOLE OF what is left: every one of them still carries benchName CraftingSmithingForge, because the bench is the BNAM keyword on the COBJ record and no amount of server code moves a menu entry. So a woodworker still finds their spear in the forge menu and a smith still sees it there and is refused when they press it. Override records in Thornswood-Content.esp are the only thing that moves the listing, or this entry decides out loud that the listing stays and the refusal is the gate.  AND ONE MORE THING CAME OUT OF THE SAME BUCKET, 23 September. This entry said the ownership half was already right and listed instruments, bows and arrows. The FISHING POLES were not right and were not in that list: they were unowned, open to anybody, because the rule that gives the Woodwright a spear sits under WEAP and a fishing pole is a MISC record. Fixed with the house parts as pull request 197, so Fishing Pole Crude, Fine and Master are now Woodworker/Woodwright. The ownership half of this entry is finished for real now. What is left is unchanged and is the whole of it: every one of them still lists at the forge, because the bench is the BNAM keyword on the COBJ record and only an override record in Thornswood-Content.esp moves a menu entry. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The ownership half is done, checked against tools/recipes.json (rebuilt 23 Sep 22:46). Steel Nordic Spear and Iron Hunter's Spear (Immersive Weapons.esp), Flute and Drum (PlayFluteLuteDrum.esp) and Fishing Pole - Crude (FishingInSkyrim.esp) are all Woodworker/Woodwright (commits e09957d #192, 8a1cae5 #197; Build-RecipeTable.ps1:1404-1405 SPEAR_WORDS, :3051 and :3162). Plain clothes are no longer the Smith's: no Smith row has a clothing reason. The 16 'Other armour and clothing' Smith rows all carry ArmorHeavy/Light plus a clothing keyword. Clothing is 'Tailor/Haberdasher, clothing that is neither a robe nor faction dress' (216 rows). The listing half is untouched: 75 Woodworker rows still carry benchName CraftingSmithingForge (Immersive Weapons 34, Dawnguard 12, Playable Rieklings 8, Skyrim.esm 6, MoreCraftableEquipment 5, Dragonborn 4, FishingInSkyrim 3, PlayFluteLuteDrum 3), and so do 100 Tailor rows (Hothtrooper44_ArmorCompilation 54, Playable Rieklings 46). All 175 have fires=true, so the gate in mp.onCraft does refuse the wrong trade. No woodworking bench keyword exists anywhere in the load order's COBJ benches. Thornswood-Content.esp's header masters are only Skyrim, Update, Dawnguard, HearthFires, Dragonborn (read from the TES4 MAST subrecords), so overriding the 158 mod-sourced rows would add six mod masters. The gamemode already argues against exactly this at gamemode.js:9924 ('an override is a copy that goes stale silently'). NEXT STEP: This comes down to one decision. (a) The listing stays and the refusal is the gate. Then the entry closes with that sentence, no code, and doneWhen is already met for ownership. (b) Override records. That means choosing a bench (a new keyword plus furniture placed in towns, or an existing one such as the MCE loom for the Tailor rows), adding six mod masters to Thornswood-Content.esp, and writing ~175 COBJ overrides with a script in the style of Add-TempleRespawn.ps1 or Add-ContentRecords.py. It also needs a Nexus collection revision, the launcher's plugin-size check passed, and Deploy-DevGamemode -LoadOrder. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: Patrick's decision between 'listing stays, refusal is the gate' and plugin overrides. If overrides, he also picks the bench and uploads a new Thornswood-Content.esp to the Nexus collection before any server can carry it.

## Done when

A spear and a plain shirt come out of the generator owned by the Woodworker and the Tailor, and either the bench overrides are in the plugin or this entry says plainly that the listing stays and the refusal is the gate.

## Traps

Do not move ownership to fix a listing. The two are different fields and the owner is already correct for instruments, bows and arrows; changing it would break the gate that works in order to tidy a menu that needs a plugin edit.

issues.title: Crafted a helmet twice and got one
issues.body:
**Order:** 383 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, medium · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\gamemode.js mp.onCraft · the inventory sync in the fork

## What is known

PATRICK, 23 September, in the world: "Made a helmet twice only got one". Two crafts, one item. The shape to suspect first is the same one behind the naked arrivals: the client makes the thing and puts it in its own pack, the server is told afterwards, and an inventory write that crosses the two loses one of them. WHAT TO MEASURE: whether onCraft fired twice in the server log, whether the pack held two before the next sync, and whether the second craft consumed its materials. Those three answers separate "the craft was refused", "the item was made and then overwritten" and "the client never sent the second one". MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: Found in the log already on this machine, logs/dev/server.log (pulled 23 Sep 22:28). Lines 2303-2305: at 20:46:05 'User 1 tries to craft 0x38019f67 on workbench 0xc430a', then 'Recipe not found' with 13 reported inputs, including gold (baseId 15) x1 and x46, iron ingot 0x5ace4 x1+x12+x3 and 0x1be1a. The gamemode logged 'worked 38019f67 with no recipe ... tempering or the like. Allowed' (gamemode.js:9652 recipelessCraft, :9694-9697). Then '[error] Source inventory doesn't have enough 0x1be1a (1 is required while 0 present)'. So the craft was dropped server-side and the next inventory sync took the helmet back. Lines 2307-2309, 20:46:09: a phantom 'craft 0x5ace4 from 0x38019f67 x1' (the sync putting the ingots back and removing the helmet, misread as a craft) failed the same way. Lines 2312-2316, 20:46:22: the retry matched RecipeArmorRieklingHelmet3Alt (Playable Rieklings, index 56) and 'crafted -0x5ace4 x3 +0x38019f67 x1'. So two crafts, one helmet, which is what Patrick reported. The cause is in the fork. skymp5-client/src/services/services/craftService.ts builds each craft's inputs from every item that left the pack while the character was at that furniture (furnitureStreak), keyed per furniture and only cleared when a craft finishes. So the removals from the deploy respawn at 20:44 (entry 351: 'it was while looking in the forge'; log 20:44:52 'login ff000003 put 2 worn thing(s) back on') were still in that list when he crafted. CraftService.cpp RecipeItemsMatch requires GetItemCount == entry.count exactly (16 ingots reported vs 3 wanted), so FindRecipe failed. CraftEvent::OnFireSuccess removes the client's list and throws atomically (Inventory.cpp:106-147) when one entry is missing. NEXT STEP: Server side in the fork, C:\Thornswood-Dev\skymp on thornswood/engine-changes, as a THORNSWOOD PATCH in skymp5-server/cpp/server_guest_lib/CraftService.cpp. When the exact match finds nothing and the output is a plugin form (below 0xff000000), try again with a looser rule: a recipe matches if every one of its inputs is covered by (reported inputs that the server's own inventory actually holds), at the same bench keyword, with conditions met. Then UseCraftRecipe as normal, so only the recipe's own inputs are removed and the server never adds anything the client did not make. Filtering by what the server holds is what keeps the phantom out: at 20:46:09 the server did not hold the helmet, so 'ingot from helmet' matches nothing. Log a line whenever the loose match was used. Add cases to unit/CraftTest.cpp: a polluted list with extra stale entries crafts the recipe and removes only 3 ingots, and a reported input the server does not hold matches nothing. Build with tools\Build-Server.ps1, record with New-ServerBuildRecord.ps1, then Publish-Server -Channel dev. The client-side streak cleanup is optional and separate, because its timing cannot be observed from here. WORKED 24 September, and the cause is not what the entry first thought. See the new entry about the client craft streak: the list of inputs was polluted after a respawn, so no recipe matched. A server side resend was built, tested and reviewed, and it makes no visible difference because the client defers its own inventory correction while the crafting menu is open; it is kept unpushed on the fork branch thornswood/craft-resync as a record. Merged instead: pull request 221, which stops the gamemode log calling such a craft tempering. And the investigation turned up a real gap, now its own fix: a craft that matched no recipe skipped the whole craft gate.

## Done when

Two crafts of the same thing leave two of it in the pack, and the log shows both.

## Traps

Do not fix this by having the server add the item: the client already added it, and adding a second is how one craft becomes two of everything for anybody who notices.

issues.title: Standing in an interior pool reads as a dry room
issues.body:
**Order:** 385 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** find out, medium · **Needs:** server

## Where it lives

tools\ts-plugins\thornswood-front.js, the wading test · Cell.getWaterLevel

## What is known

PATRICK, 23 September: "Stood in the water in the temple in Whiterun temp stayed the same". MEASURED from his own client log: it reported `indoors` the whole time he was in that pool, so the server was never told about water and did the right thing with what it was told. Wading is the cell’s water level against where somebody is standing, and that is ALL there is: an Actor has isSwimming, a Cell has getWaterLevel, and Skyrim Platform exposes no submerged depth and no is-in-water anywhere. So either that cell answers a level nowhere near his feet or it answers nothing. The heartbeat line now carries the water level, where his feet are and the difference, so the next visit answers it. If the cell has no level, the fix is the same walk the fires use: find the water planes in the cell and measure against those. MEASURED 24 September, reading the code rather than the entry: The measurement is in place and has not been run yet. cd0a1ab (#188) added waterSaid to the heartbeat (tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js:2315, :2545-2553, :2674): the cell's water level, where the feet are and the depth, or 'the cell has no readable water level'. The dev game folder carries it: C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data\Platform\Plugins\thornswood-front.js contains waterSaid, modified 23 Sep 21:37. The dev front log C:\Thornswood-DevBuild\Game\Data\Platform\thornswood-front.log was last written 21:00, before that plugin landed. It has 0 'water level' or 'readable water' lines, and its last place lines are Whiterun outdoors/indoors with no water bracket at all. Nothing on this machine records a visit to the Temple of Kynareth pool with the new plugin. The next step depends on which of the two answers that visit gives: a level far from his feet, or no level at all. NEXT STEP: Nothing to change until the log answers. Next session, read the place: lines in the dev front log for the temple visit. (1) If the level is readable but far from his feet, measure the offset and decide whether interior pools need a different depth rule. (2) If there is no readable level, walk the cell's references for water planes (the walk the fire probe already does, gamemode and front at the fire bases) and measure against those, with a harness in the style of test-temp.js. Both branches are front-plugin work that ships with a dev Ship. WHAT IT IS WAITING ON: A person (Patrick) standing in the Temple of Kynareth pool in Whiterun on the dev server with the current dev build, long enough for two heartbeat lines, so the place: line reports what the cell said about water.

## Done when

Standing in the Temple of Kynareth pool reports shallow or water, and the temperature moves toward the water number.

## Traps

An exterior cell answers a sensible level and an interior one often does not, so testing this outdoors proves nothing about the case that was reported.

issues.title: A gamemode deploy respawns everybody who is playing, and nothing warns them
issues.body:
**Order:** 387 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Handover · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools\Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 · tools\Deploy-Gamemode.ps1

## What is known

FOUND 23 September by doing it to Patrick six times in an hour while he was testing. His words: "I randomly teleportes as I was typing this and I heard the noise of things equipping and the right hand side of my screen showed things going into my inventory that already were", and then "I did the teleport thing again, it was while looking in the forge". WHAT TO DO: the deploy should say who is online before it stops anything, and either refuse without a switch or announce it in game the way Ship does, with the same countdown. A deploy that lands on somebody mid-swing is the cheapest possible way to lose a tester’s evening. PART DONE 24 September, pull request #214. WHAT CHANGED: Merged as pull request 214, "A dev server that is down has nobody on it, and its stop leaves no warning behind". Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 went straight from the syntax check to stopping the dev server, with nobody told. Every stop drops everybody on it, and when it comes back each game reconnects and respawns. On 23 September that happened to Patrick six times in an hour while he was testing: "I randomly teleportes as I was typing this and I heard the noise of things equipping", and then "I did the teleport thing again, it was while looking in the forge". Measured in logs\dev\server.log: 'gamemode loaded' at 20:39:00.541 and 'login ff000003 put 2 worn thing(s) back on' at 20:39:47.177, the same pair at 20:44:04.992 and 20:44:52.111, and no restart request anywhere before either. Entry 351. Before anything stops, and after the load order is worked out so a missing plugin still stops the run before anybody is told, the script now reads the dev box in one ssh call: the port and the data folder from its MEASURED: Not measured again here; the pull request says what was run before it merged. WHAT IS LEFT: Nobody reviewed this branch independently before it merged: its reviewing agent died in the first wave on 24 September. Check the merged code against this entry's doneWhen, then close it.

Deploy-DevGamemode names who is online and will not stop a server with people in it unless it is told to, and what it does say reaches them in the game.

issues.title: The key mold and key recipes are in the plugin, and the plugin only reaches people through Nexus
issues.body:
**Order:** 390 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Content · **Effort:** run it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

tools/Thornswood-Content.esp (384 records, 141,442 bytes) · Profile/OwnGame/files.txt · tools/Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 -LoadOrder

## What is known

FOUND 24 September by the dev release that should have carried it. Pull request 199 added ThornswoodRecipeKeyMold and ThornswoodRecipeKey to tools/Thornswood-Content.esp, 382 records to 384, 141,234 bytes to 141,442, verified byte for byte against every other record. The dev release 1.1.92.2 that followed carried nothing for it: the pack was 0 MB. MEASURED: the plugin is listed in Profile/OwnGame/files.txt on both builds, which is the launcher's record of what Vortex deployed, and Publish-Update excludes every file in that record by path. So this plugin reaches people only through the Nexus collection, never in a pack. And the launcher compares every plugin's name and size with the server's and refuses Play on any difference, so putting the new plugin on a server before the collection carries it would lock out everybody who has the old one. Pull request 200 made /mold keep conjuring a mold until the blank mold's recipe record is actually loaded, so nothing is broken in the meantime: the key chain works the old way until the plugin arrives, and switches to the forged blank by itself the day it does. Pull request 198 already lets a smith cut a key to their own door with no mold at all.

## Done when

Thornswood Content on Nexus carries the 384-record plugin, a collection revision carries that, and the dev server has it through Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 -LoadOrder, after which a smith can forge a blank Key Mold and a Key at a forge.

## Traps

Do not run Deploy-DevGamemode.ps1 -LoadOrder, Deploy-Server.ps1, or anything else that sends plugins to a server before the collection revision is out: the size check refuses Play to every tester whose copy is older. The dev server running the new gamemode with the old plugin is fine and expected; that is what pull request 200 is for.

issues.title: This machine's C: drive is full: 952 GB used, and one night of parallel work filled the last few GB
issues.body:
**Order:** 391 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** Operations · **Effort:** run it, small · **Who:** Patrick · **Needs:** patrick

## Where it lives

C: on Patrick's machine · C:\Users\evilp\Downloads · tools/Measure-Reclaim.ps1

## What is known

MEASURED 24 September 05:15: 0.02 GB free on C, with 952 GB used. The night's To Do run had created 121 git worktrees of about 58 MB each under the repo's .claude/worktrees, plus scratch launcher builds in the temp folder, and agents began failing with No space left on device. Removing every finished worktree brought it back to 6.2 GB, and a cleanup every minute held it near 4 GB for the rest of the night. Nothing of Patrick's was deleted. The Downloads folder holds many large mod archives, installers and recordings.

C: has 20 GB or more free and stays there.

## Traps

Vortex's staging folder, the game folders and the release clones are not scratch: measure with tools/Measure-Reclaim.ps1 before removing anything, and never delete a collection file by hand.

issues.title: After a respawn the client's craft streak outlives the forge, so the next craft lists the wrong inputs and matches no recipe
issues.body:
**Order:** 392 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, medium · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

the fork, C:/Thornswood-Dev/skymp: skymp5-client/src/services/services/craftService.ts (furnitureStreak), remoteServer.ts (isBadMenuShown), sync/inventory.ts (applyInventory)

## What is known

FOUND 24 September working To Do 347, and it is the cause of "Made a helmet twice only got one". MEASURED from the dev server log of 23 September: after the respawn at 20:44, the helmet craft at 20:46:05 arrived listing thirteen input entries, sixteen iron ingots among them, where the recipe wants three. CraftService matches a recipe only when the list is exact, so none matched; the craft was then refused on the inventory check ("Source inventory doesn't have enough 0x1be1a"), while the client had already shown the helmet. The list was polluted by the client's furnitureStreak, which survived the respawn. A SERVER SIDE FIX WAS BUILT AND TESTED AND DOES NOT HELP, and it is kept only as a record: fork branch thornswood/craft-resync (fdb36279, 97ea907e), not pushed. It resends the inventory when a craft fails, but the client defers applying its own correction while the crafting menu is open (remoteServer.ts returns early while isBadMenuShown is true), and the menu was open for about 55 seconds, so the resend lands at the same moment the client's own correction would have. The fix belongs in the client: clear furnitureStreak when the character respawns and when a crafting menu opens. A second client symptom rides with it: the client reads its own inventory correction as a craft while the person is still seated, which usually produces a refused craft and can, through the no-recipe path, turn one real item into one material.

## Done when

A craft made right after a respawn lists exactly the recipe's inputs, and the client's inventory correction is never sent as a craft.

## Traps

This is a change to the client runtime, which is settled design: fork source, then New-ClientBuildRecord.ps1, Sync-Client.ps1, and a dev Ship, and the fork's own unit tests. The local server binary was put back to the recorded live build (sha256 de74c582) after the experiment; rebuild it only on purpose.

F shourtcut and mouse well only goes from 3rd to extremely close 3rd closer than over the shoulder. ... Tab not opening up the skills magick window". His screenshot shows a goblin character in the Creation Hall with the party window open. NOT MEASURED YET: nothing from his machine has been read. What the plugin already records settles it: every five seconds it logs "input: N keys in 5s, browser focus yes or no, menu yes or no [which menus], controls on or off". THREE CANDIDATES, in the order the evidence points: (1) a game menu left open after loading, which would stop Tab opening the Tween Menu and the camera switching to first person, and would also stand the controls watchdog down so it says nothing; (2) the party window opened by Shift P in the name box still holding the keyboard after the creation screen closed (the key guard for that is its own pull request); (3) the goblin race having no first person view, which would explain the camera but not Tab. The controls watchdog would have logged and fixed camera or menu controls switched off, so a plain controls problem is unlikely.

## Done when

Measure before fixing: read the log first. Session logs have only reached the site since dev 1.1.92.5 (the 401 fix, pull request 259), so a session from before that update is not there.

issues.title: The key mold prompt and the Controls page: five follow-ups from the review of the U key
issues.body:
**Order:** 398 · **Wave:** 1 Today · **Category:** In-game · **Effort:** change it, small · **Needs:** free

## Where it lives

tools/ts-plugins/thornswood-front.js (the mold section) · tools/gamemode.js holderNearby · tools/app/Keys.cs · tools/emotes/Thornswood.ini · the fork ScampServer::GetNeighborsByPosition

## What is known

FOUND 24 September by the review of pull request 287, none of them blocking. (1) The U prompt shows for anybody carrying any Key Mold, stamped ones included, and holders keep their stamped mold for good, so every holder sees it at every door and U only answers that there is no blank or already a mold. The plugin cannot tell a stamped mold from a blank yet. (2) holderNearby checks people nearby before the presser and counts a deed carrier the same as the holder, so somebody standing by with a stolen deed can receive the mold ahead of the real holder. (3) MoldKey has no Controls row, so the Controls page's clash check does not know U is taken. (4) The shipped Thornswood.ini template sets WheelKey = 34, which is G, the friend key, so a fresh install has both on G; the emote plugin and Keys.cs default the wheel to 48 (B), which is also the voice mode key. And Keys.cs WriteIni only rewrites a line already in the file, and PartyKey, JournalKey, FriendKey, TradeWithKey and MuteThemKey are not in the template, so their Controls rows fail with Could not write Thornswood.ini on every install. (5) In the fork, GetNeighborsByPosition makes an array of n and then appends at its length, so every caller gets n empty slots before the n ids.

## Done when

The prompt shows only for a blank, the holder gets the mold ahead of a deed carrier, every key in Thornswood.ini has a Controls row that can be written, no two defaults share a key, and the fork returns only the ids.
